title: feat(vgi-bridge): take git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 only, and answer trust-task-discovery (#92)
body:
feat(vgi-bridge): take git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 only, and answer trust-task-discovery (#92)

* feat(vgi-bridge): report the effective role map to the VTC (git-ns/bridge/event 0.3)

- The bridge now sends `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3 by default and, under it,
  `roleMapReported` for every bound namespace at start-up and right after a
  binding completes: the role map as the forge applies it (each right's
  configured role rounded onto the namespace's ladder), each configured
  repository whose map differs, and each managed repository whose roles
  were last projected under another map (`stale`), which the VTC
  re-projects. There is still no entry for git.ns.admin.
- RepoRecord keeps the map a fully successful projection applied
  (`roleMap`); a record without one is taken to be the default map.
- One outbox key per namespace, so a newer report replaces an
  unacknowledged one; sent after the start-up resend, so it is the last
  the VTC reads. The outside-namespace guard also covers `repos[].resource`
  and `stale`.
- BREAKING: `event_version` defaults to "0.3". A VTC that takes only 0.2
  needs `event_version = "0.2"` (or "0.1"), and is then told no role map.
- BridgeConfig::role_map_repos lists the repositories with a map layer.
- Docs: BRIDGE.md §6c and §7, RUNBOOK §8b and troubleshooting, the GitHub
  setup guide, the example config.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): report the role map whenever the bridge starts serving a namespace or its VTC link comes up

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 now asks for a roleMapReported whenever the
bridge starts serving a namespace, whenever its link to the VTC is
established or re-established, and whenever its map changes.

- Bridge::link_up: resend everything unacknowledged except earlier
  role-map reports, then report every bound namespace afresh (one per
  namespace per link-up; the per-namespace outbox key replaces an
  unacknowledged report). Called at start-up (restore), on every new
  mediator session (the DIDComm supervisor in run), and when a send
  succeeds after sends failed, which covers a transport that came back
  without a signal: every send to the VTC goes through send_doc, which
  tracks a link-down flag and raises the background loop on recovery. A
  transport-signalled link-up clears the flag first, so it is not counted
  twice.
- Bridge::started_serving: report a namespace that became this bridge's
  to serve (after bindCompleted); a restored store is covered by restore.
- Tests: a cut link that comes back reports once per namespace and is not
  counted twice; a newly served namespace is reported. The test harness's
  link can be cut.
- BRIDGE.md §6c and RUNBOOK §8b say when reports are sent.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): take git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 only, and answer trust-task-discovery

git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 (trust-tasks #635) sends a namespace admin with no
right of their own on a repository as git.ns.admin, which maps to no role,
never as the git.repo.own it implies. Before 0.4 the two could not be told
apart, so the bridge now takes 0.4 only:

- A job of 0.1, 0.2 or 0.3 is refused unsupportedVersion.
- projectRoles requires repo: there is no namespace-level role job, so one
  without repo is malformedRequest (it was notCapable).
- desiredRoles may name an account once, matched by forge and id.
- removeAccounts may name an account desiredRoles lists at git.ns.admin
  (no role either way); any other overlap is still malformedRequest.
- trust-task-discovery/0.2 from the VTC is answered with the 0.4 type URI,
  which is how the VTC learns it may send 0.4 (the spec forbids sending it
  to a bridge that has not shown it takes it).

0.4 payloads are read with the generated 0.3 types, which have the same
shape, until a trust-tasks-rs release carries 0.4's. The lockfile moves
trust-tasks-rs to 0.22.7 for job::v0_3.

No backwards compatibility: every deployment is a test instance.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vgi-bridge): mark the hand-written job 0.4 type for the trust-tasks release

JOB_TYPE and the job::v0_3 alias stand in for the generated job::v0_4
until a trust-tasks-rs release carries trust-tasks #635. Say so with a
TODO at both.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vgi-forge): only own may map to the forge admin role

A role map giving maintain or commit the admin role would let a member make
themselves a repository administrator on the forge by self-granting a
non-elevated right. RoleMap::new and deserialisation now refuse such a map,
so the bridge fails to start with an error naming the layer, and RoleMap's
fields are private so no map can be changed afterwards to one they refuse.
The docs and example config no longer suggest maintainers as admins.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): report the forge's ladder, and build every role-map report afresh

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #639):

- a roleMapReported event names the namespace's `ladder`, which the VTC
  holds every map to;
- a report is built afresh at each send, a resend of an unacknowledged
  one included, so a later `issuedAt` never carries an older map;
- a map that the adapter rounds unordered is logged and not reported,
  and not recorded as the map a repository was projected under;
- a pending report is dropped once the bridge speaks an event version
  below 0.3, rather than sent under a version without the type.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vgi-bridge): take trust-tasks-rs 0.23 for the published git-ns/bridge/event 0.3

git-ns/bridge/event 0.3 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639) is now
published, so the local trust-tasks-rs patch this branch developed
against is no longer needed: bump to the real 0.23 release.

trust-tasks-proof 0.23 also changed sign_trust_task's default
proofPurpose from assertionMethod to authentication (matching the
Trust Task spec's own examples). This bridge and the VTC-side checks
it faces still require assertionMethod on both sides of the wire, so
BridgeIdentity::sign now passes it explicitly instead of relying on
the library default.

trust-tasks-proof 0.23 also replaced VerificationMethodResolver with
a purpose-aware ProofPurposeResolver; the test-only Published resolver
in vta.rs moves onto it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vgi-bridge): take trust-tasks-rs 0.23 for the generated git-ns/bridge/job 0.4

git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#635) is now
published (trust-tasks-rs 0.23): the bridge takes the generated
specs::git_ns::bridge::job::v0_4 types in place of the generated 0.3
ones it read 0.4's wire-identical payload with, and JOB_TYPE is now
sourced from the generated Payload::TYPE_URI instead of hand-written.

trust-tasks-proof 0.23 also changed sign_trust_task's default
proofPurpose from assertionMethod to authentication (matching the
Trust Task spec's own examples). This bridge and the VTC-side checks
it faces still require assertionMethod on both sides of the wire, so

the library default.

trust-tasks-proof 0.23 also replaced VerificationMethodResolver with

in vta.rs moves onto it.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): separation of duties and break-glass for elevated git rights
body:
## What

This implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641, the 2026-09-25 decision. An **elevated** git right (`git.ns.admin`, `git.repo.create`, `git.repo.own`) must be granted by someone other than its recipient. If nobody else is available, the member uses **break-glass**: an explicit self-grant that takes effect immediately and never expires. It is gated by a passkey, requires a written justification, and stays flagged in front of every other administrator until one of them ratifies or revokes it.

### Server (`vtc-service`, `vti-common`)
- **Fixed rule 7:** an elevated self-grant is refused with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`, and the message names `cnm git break-glass …`. The rule applies to grant 0.3, to drift adopt (through `right_grant_via`), to `repo/adopt` when the adopter names themselves as owner, and to reseat to oneself. The actor is compared after console-key delegation. Self-grants of maintain and commit.sign still work. Bind is not a self-grant.
- **`git-ns/right/break-glass/0.1`** (`git_ns/break_glass.rs`):
  - **Who may use it:** someone with grant authority over the right, or a community admin taking `ns.admin` on a headless namespace (`notHeadless` otherwise).
  - **Passkey:** an **operation-bound passkey step-up is always required** (`acl::bound_step_up`, aal2 with user verification, the acting DID's own passkey). The spent mark now returns its evidence (credential id and bound digest) for the audit row.
  - **Admin gate:** it bypasses the `elevated_requires_admin` stand-in, because the real step-up applies.
  - **The record:** it takes effect immediately, has no expiry, and is flagged `breakGlass {by, at, justification, effectiveAt?, ratifiedBy?, ratifiedAt?}`.
  - **Audit failure:** if the critical audit row cannot be written, the break-glass is rolled back.
- **Ratify** (`git-ns/right/ratify/0.1`):
  - It is never allowed from the subject, and it is bound to the `breakGlassAt` the ratifier read.
  - A community admin can ratify, as can someone whose own grant authority is not itself an unratified break-glass.
  - It is gated like a grant of the same right.
- **Revoke:** any community admin may revoke an unratified break-glass, and no policy can refuse that. Unratified and expiring records never count toward the last-owner or last-admin invariants.
- **Visibility:**
  - `AuditEvent::GitNsBreakGlass` records the break-glass, and a new `AuditEvent::severity()` rates it as **Critical**. It carries the justification, the entitlement, the step-up evidence, the policy version and any notices that could not be delivered. The usual `GitNsOperation` row is still written.
  - Activity shows `gitNs.right.breakGlass`, `…BreakGlassRatified` and `…BreakGlassRevoked`.
  - A signed **`git-ns/right/break-glass-notice/0.1`** goes to every community admin and every live ns admin except the actor. It is sent through `AppState::send_to_member` (DIDComm through the VTC's mediator, guaranteed delivery), the same path as the removal notice.
  - `git-ns/view/0.4` returns the records, `GET /v1/git-ns/break-glass` is new, and the rights rows carry `breakGlass`. The registry projection is unchanged.
- **Policy** (`git_ns.rego` settings): `break_glass` (`enabled` by default, or `disabled`), `break_glass_delay_seconds` (up to a day, revocable meanwhile) and `break_glass_min_justification_chars`. The policy can also deny `right.breakGlass` or `right.ratify`. It cannot suppress the audit row, the notices or the surfaces.

- **`git-ns/repo/create/0.3`:** the creator owns the repository only when they hold `git.repo.create` **by explicit record**, either granted by someone else or recorded through break-glass. A `git.repo.create` that is only implied by `git.ns.admin` gives no creator ownership. That requester names another member in the new `owners`, or is refused `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` with a message that names break-glass. Naming other owners counts as granting `own` (`git-ns:escalation`). A single-admin community breaks the glass once for `git.repo.create` on the namespace, not once per repository.
- **Members only (fixed rule 5):** an elevated right (own, repo.create, ns.admin) goes only to a current member with an ACL entry, and only from an actor who is one. This applies to grant, create, repo/adopt (including the reservation path), transfer, drift adopt and break-glass, and policy cannot waive it. A throwaway `did:key` the actor controls cannot stand in for a second person.

### `cnm`
- `cnm git break-glass --right=… --resource=… --justification=…`. On a step-up refusal it prints `<vtc>/admin/step-up#request=…`, waits for Enter, and resends the **identical** signed document.
- `cnm git ratify --subject=… --right=… --resource=… --break-glass-at=… [--statement=…]` and `cnm git break-glass-list`.
- `cnm git create --owner=<did>` (repeatable) sends repo/create 0.3. The generic `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` help reads: "This would give you an elevated right (own, repo.create or ns.admin) on your own authority. Ask another community administrator to do it, or use break-glass (`cnm git break-glass`), which is audited and must be ratified."
- `cnm git view` shows a banner and flags each break-glass right. All printed commands are fish-safe.
- `grant` and `revoke` send 0.3 (`vtc-client`'s `git_ns_grant` and `git_ns_revoke` are now the 0.3 calls; the 0.1 methods and the `_v3` names are gone).

### Admin console
- A persistent banner on every page for every admin while anything is unratified or pending. It cannot be dismissed.
- **Repos → Break-glass grants**, with Ratify and Revoke. The grantee is never offered Ratify, and the page explains why.
- The flag chip next to every flagged right. The last-owner note follows the new invariants.
- Drift adopt never offers a viewer their own forge account as an elevated right: it hands the command to another administrator and names break-glass.
- The member page (`MemberGit.tsx`) flags a break-glass right with `BreakGlassChip`.
- When the viewer is the subject of an elevated grant, the grant and reseat forms don't offer it. They explain separation of duties and offer **Break glass…** instead, with the justification field and the consequences.
- `SignTaskDialog` answers a `stepUpRequest` refusal with the passkey and resends the same document. `/admin/step-up` finishes a step-up handed over from `cnm`.
- The create dialog takes an optional owner DID and sends repo/create 0.3. The hint explains that an empty owner makes the signer the owner, which works only on an explicit `git.repo.create`.
- Grant and revoke are sent as 0.3, and the `trust_task_manifest` census is updated. `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4` is allowlisted as a spine document.

## Deliberate breaks
- Self-grants of own, create and ns.admin that used to succeed are now refused, including drift adopts of your own forge role and reseating a namespace to yourself. A namespace admin creating a repository with no `owners`, on a `git.repo.create` that is only implied, is now refused as well.
- **repo/create is served at 0.3 only.** 0.1 is refused as an unknown task.
- Elevated rights to or from a DID with no ACL entry, which used to succeed for `own`, are now refused `git-ns:membersOnly`.
- **Grant and revoke are served at 0.3 only.** 0.1 is dropped with no compatibility window: a 0.1 client gets an unknown-task refusal. The pre-DID-core subject accommodation in revoke goes with it, because 0.3's schema holds every subject to DID-core. That is fine for test deployments, which are recreated rather than migrated. The openvtc TUI moves to 0.3 in OpenVTC/openvtc#384.
- A namespace admin with no passkey registered with the VTC cannot break the glass. They get the existing "register a passkey" refusal.

## Coordination
- #1729 (ns-admin projection): break-glass is how an ns admin gets an explicit `own`, and with it a forge role.
- The drift/resolve 0.3 recipient binding (trust-tasks #640) and reseat 0.3 (#635) should declare `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`.

## Merge order

**#1736 first, then #1735, then this PR.** This branch merges main and `feat/git-ns-reproject-role-map` (#1736). It does not depend on #1735. Where both touch drift adopt, the conflicts are small and in the same direction.

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

Built on main's trust-tasks-rs 0.23, which carries #641 (break-glass, ratify, break-glass-notice, grant/revoke 0.3, repo/create 0.3, view 0.4). The local `[patch.crates-io]` is discarded, and Cargo.lock has one trust-tasks-rs (0.23). Reseat uses the generated `reseat::v0_3` (from #1736). The console's reseat form uses the generic separation-of-duties refusal and offers break-glass.

## With #1736's role map

- **Fixed rule 7 now asks `rules::elevated_on`**, which is `Right::is_elevated_in` under the target namespace's map. So grant 0.3, drift adopt and repo/adopt refuse a self-grant of `git.repo.maintain` where the map projects it to forge `admin`. They fail closed (refuse it too) while a bridge-mode namespace's map is unknown. A manual-mode namespace projects no forge role, so its elevated rights stay ns.admin, repo.create and own.
- Reseat (always ns.admin), repo/create (always own) and break-glass (only the three) are unchanged. The refusal for a right elevated only by the map points to another owner or administrator, not to break-glass.
- The console's `adoptStanding` hands over a self-adopt that the map makes elevated, without offering break-glass. The docs describe the rule.
- Two #1729 drift tests were adjusted: a namespace admin's own forge `admin` is now adopted by someone else, and one fixture reports the default map so the adopt reaches rule 7.

Rebased onto main after #1726, #1727, #1728, #1732, #1741 and #1747, and later merged with main (#1729, #1764) and #1736.

Local results: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (139, including the repo/create 0.3 ownership and members-only sock-puppet tests, including the end-to-end drift-adopt self-grant refusal and a check that grant and revoke 0.1 and 0.2 are not served), `openapi_snapshot`, `trust_task_manifest`, the vti-common audit tests, the `cnm-cli` tests, and clippy `-D warnings` and fmt on the touched crates. Admin UI: `npx vitest run` (460) and `tsc -b`.

After the merges and 0.23: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (182; after the two drift-test fixes `git_ns::tests::` re-run, 141 pass), `--test trust_task_manifest` (8), `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::` (21), clippy `-D warnings` (vtc-service, cnm-cli, vtc-client), `cargo fmt --check`, admin-ui `npm run lint` and `vitest run` (471) all pass locally.

The openvtc TUI banner is in OpenVTC/openvtc#384. Step-up passkeys for members who are not console users are a stacked follow-up.

title: feat(git-ns): an adoption names the member who receives the right
body:
Spec first: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#640. Companion TUI change: OpenVTC/openvtc#382. (#1728, which this was stacked on, has merged.)

## Problem

A `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1 `adopt` does not name who receives the right. The VTC resolves the item's forge account to whoever has linked it **when the task runs**. If the account is relinked between the owner reading the item and signing, the owner's signed document grants a right, published to the Trust Registry, to someone the owner never saw.

## What changed

**Server (`vtc-service/src/git_ns`)**
- Serves `git-ns/drift/resolve` **0.3**. An adopt must carry `subject`, and a revert must not; either mistake is `malformedRequest`.
- Adopt step 3 refuses with the new **`git-ns/drift/resolve:subjectChanged`** when the account is linked to someone other than `subject`.
- **The link check is repeated in `right_grant_via`, under `store::write_lock`** (`GrantVia.linked_to`). Every link and unlink is written under that same lock: `bridge::handle_event` for `accountLinked`, and `lifecycle::sweep_departures`. So no relink can fall between the check and the write.
- 0.1 is still served for **revert**. A 0.1 **adopt** is refused with the framework's `unsupportedVersion` (new `OpError::UnsupportedVersion`), with a message naming 0.3. That follows the spec's SHOULD.

- **Adopt step 5 compares with the member's *projected* right** (`bridge::projected_repo_right`): the right the projector lists them at from rights in their own name, via `highest_repo_rights` with `git.ns.admin` rows left out. A namespace admin projects to no forge role, so one holding `maintain` can now have a forge `admin` adopted as `own`; before, their implied `own` made it unadoptable. The role-to-right side stays `drift::projected_right`, which #1736 generalises to the reported role map (no second implementation).
- **Adopt step 6, separation of duties** (trust-tasks #641 / #1745): an adoption that would record an elevated right (only `git.repo.own` is reachable here) for the resolver themselves is refused **`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`**, before policy, with a message pointing to `git-ns/right/break-glass`. The actor is the DID after console-key delegation (`tasks::acting_as`). Adopting `maintain`/`commit.sign` for oneself stays allowed. `Right::is_elevated` is added verbatim as #1745 defines it, so the two merge cleanly.

**Admin console:** sends 0.3. `projectedRepoRank` replaces `heldRepoRank` (ns.admin no longer counts), and an adoption that would make the viewer an owner is handed over, naming break-glass, rather than offered. An adopt carries, as `subject`, the member its dialog already names, and the hand-over command gains `--subject=<DID>`, fish-safe.

**`cnm git drift resolve`:**
- New `--subject`: required to adopt, refused on revert, and validated as a DID Core DID before signing.
- Sends 0.3 through the new `vtc-client` `git_ns_drift_resolve_v3`.
- Explains `subjectChanged`.

**`vtc-client`:** `git_ns_drift_resolve` (0.1) is `#[deprecated]`, not removed, so the published API stays additive.

The `trust_task_manifest` census lists drift/resolve 0.3.

## Merge order

**#1736 first, then this PR, then #1745.** This branch merges main and `feat/git-ns-reproject-role-map` (#1736). If #1736 lands first, this PR's diff shrinks to its own changes.

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

Built on main's trust-tasks-rs 0.23, which generates `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.3. A new commit reverts the `[patch.crates-io]` that 95f8f46c added. Cargo.lock has one trust-tasks-rs (0.23). 0.3 does not re-declare `git-ns:roleMapUnknown`, so `drift::ROLE_MAP_UNKNOWN` comes from 0.1's generated codes.

## With #1736's role map

- **Step 6 uses `Right::is_elevated_in(&ns, repo)`**, not `Right::is_elevated`. Where the bridge's map gives maintainers forge `admin`, adopting a forge `admin` as `git.repo.maintain` for oneself is refused `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`. The refusal points to another owner, not to break-glass, which does not carry `maintain`. The console mirrors this with `isElevatedIn(right, repo.roleMap)` in `adoptStanding`.
- Two #1729 tests asserted 0.2 behaviour and now test 0.3's:
  - A namespace admin's own forge `admin` is adopted by someone else. The self-adoption is refused.
  - A `roleChanged` over `maintain` is measured against the projected right, so it is a raise, and the self-adoption is refused by step 6.

## Behaviour changes (deliberate, per the standing security/usability rule)

- **A 0.1 adopt is refused.** Before, it granted to whoever held the link. This affects the openvtc TUI shipped in #379; #382 removes adopt there and says where to adopt instead.
- **`cnm git drift resolve … adopt` now requires `--subject`.**
- **Self-adopting `own` is refused** (`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`), even by a community administrator; another owner adopts it or the resolver breaks the glass. The same goes for `maintain` where the role map projects it to forge `admin`, without the break-glass option.
- **`subjectChanged` is a new refusal.** A relinked account adopts nothing and must be read again.

## Tests

- server:
  - `drift_resolve_adopts_only_for_the_member_it_names`: a wrong `subject` is refused; a relink after reading is refused with no right recorded for anyone; naming the member it is linked to now adopts.
  - `an_adopted_grant_rechecks_the_link_where_it_is_written`: `right_grant_via` refuses a mismatched link (`subjectChanged`) and a vanished one (`accountNotLinked`) under the lock.
  - `a_namespace_admin_adopts_a_raise_over_their_own_name_right`: an ns admin holding `maintain` has a forge `admin` adopted as `own` by another admin.
  - `a_namespace_admin_alone_has_no_projected_right`
  - `an_adoption_never_grants_the_resolver_an_elevated_right`: self-adopting `own` is refused, signed directly or through a console key, recording nothing; an owner adopts `maintain` for himself.
  - `drift_resolve_0_1_reverts_but_does_not_adopt`
  - malformed: an adopt without `subject`, and a revert with one.
  - 0.3 is served.
- console: projected rank (ns.admin counts for nothing); self-adopt of `own` handed over naming break-glass; adopt payload, command and document carry `subject`; `subject` is shell-safe.
- cnm: payload building, `--subject` rules, and the `subjectChanged` hint.

`cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (126 tests), `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest`, `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::`, `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli -p vtc-client --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and admin-ui `npm run lint` + vitest (`model.test.ts`, `RepoDetail.test.tsx`) pass locally.

After the merges and 0.23: `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (168 pass), `--test trust_task_manifest` (8), `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::` (20), clippy `-D warnings` (vtc-service, cnm-cli, vtc-client), `cargo fmt --check`, admin-ui `npm run lint` and `vitest run` (433) all pass locally.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): report the effective role map to the VTC (git-ns/bridge/event 0.3)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #84 (configurable role map): the VTC could only assume the default map, so its console showed forge roles the bridge did not give, drift adopt derived rights from the wrong map, and a map change reached a repository only at its next unrelated role projection.

- **`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3** (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639) is now the default. Under it the bridge sends `roleMapReported`, one per namespace, whenever it **starts serving** a namespace (at start-up — the only time its config, and so its map, can change — and right after a binding completes, `Bridge::started_serving`) and whenever its **link to the VTC comes up** (`Bridge::link_up`, see below):
  - `roleMap` — the map as the forge applies it: each right's configured role rounded onto the namespace's ladder (GitHub personal account: `write`/`write`/`none`; Forgejo's `maintain` is the adapter's own rung, `write` + merge allow-list);
  - `repos` — configured repositories whose map differs;
  - `stale` — managed repositories whose roles were last projected under another map. The VTC re-projects these itself (and `cnm git reproject` / console "Re-project roles" do it by hand).
  - No entry for `git.ns.admin`: a namespace admin still gets no forge role.
- `RepoRecord.roleMap` records the map a **fully** successful projection applied (a partly failed one leaves the repo stale); a record without one is taken to be the default map, the only one a released bridge applied.
- **Link-up triggers.** `Bridge::link_up` resends everything unacknowledged except earlier role-map reports, then reports every bound namespace afresh. It runs (1) at start-up from `restore`, (2) on every new mediator session in the DIDComm supervisor (`run`), and (3) when a send succeeds after sends had failed — every send to the VTC goes through `send_doc`, which keeps a link-down flag and wakes the background loop on recovery, covering a transport that comes back without a signal. Debounced to one report per namespace per link-up: a signalled link-up clears the flag before sending, so its own sends do not count as a second one.
- One outbox key per namespace (`event:roleMap:<ns>`), so a newer report replaces an unacknowledged one rather than piling up. `outside_namespace` also checks `repos[].resource` and `stale`.
- **Review follow-ups (#639 latest):**
  - every report carries `ladder`, the namespace's levels lowest first without `none` (GitHub org `read…admin`, personal account `write`, Forgejo `read`/`write`/`maintain`/`admin`); the VTC refuses a map off it;
  - **newest wins:** the VTC ignores a report issued before the one it holds, so every send of a report — a resend of an unacknowledged one included — is rebuilt from the map applied at that moment (`Bridge::send_outbox` → `refresh_role_map_entry`), never the content first queued under a new `issuedAt`;
  - a map the adapter rounds **unordered** is logged at error and not reported (`effective_for` returns `None`), and is not recorded as the map a repository was projected under;
  - a pending role-map outbox entry is **dropped** once `event_version` is below 0.3, rather than sent under a version without the type.
- Docs: BRIDGE.md §6c/§7, RUNBOOK §8b + troubleshooting, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC, example config.

## Breaking

- **`event_version` defaults to `"0.3"`.** A VTC that serves only `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2 refuses every event as an unsupported type until it is updated or the bridge is set to `event_version = "0.2"` (or `"0.1"`); under 0.1/0.2 no role map is reported (logged once at info).

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3 is now published (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639, trust-tasks-rs 0.23). The branch is off the local `[patch.crates-io]` it was built and tested against and takes the real release: `trust-tasks-rs` and `trust-tasks-proof` bumped to 0.23 in the workspace `Cargo.toml`, `cargo update`d, no other dependency changes.

Two things broke on the bump, both fixed:

- trust-tasks-proof 0.23 changed `sign_trust_task`'s default `proofPurpose` from `assertionMethod` to `authentication` (matching the Trust Task spec's own examples). This bridge and the VTC-side checks it faces still require `assertionMethod` on both sides of the wire (see **Follow-up** below), so `BridgeIdentity::sign` now passes it explicitly instead of relying on the library default — otherwise every event the bridge signs would have silently switched purpose and the VTC's own `assertionMethod` check would start refusing them.
- trust-tasks-proof 0.23 replaced `VerificationMethodResolver` with a purpose-aware `ProofPurposeResolver`; the test-only `Published` resolver in `vta.rs` moves onto it.

The rest of the workspace (`vta-sdk` 0.51, `verify-trust`, and `trql-client` below them) is still on the 0.22 and 0.21 lines respectively, so `cargo tree -i trust-tasks-rs` now shows three nodes rather than two — a wider but still bounded, `publish = false` split; see the comment above `trust-tasks-rs` in the root `Cargo.toml`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vgi-bridge`: a cut link that comes back reports once per namespace and is not counted twice by a signalled link-up; a newly served namespace is reported; new tests for the effective map (GitHub org default, personal account, Forgejo default and `maintain = "admin"`), repository overrides listed only when they differ, `stale` incl. a record with no map, a successful projection clearing it, one outbox entry per namespace, the start-up report, the report after `bindCompleted`, nothing sent under `event_version = "0.2"`, and the outside-namespace guard for `repos`/`stale`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] review follow-ups: a resend carries the map applied now; a pending report is dropped under `event_version = "0.2"`; an adapter that rounds unordered reports nothing; the ladder in every report
- [x] trust-tasks-rs 0.23: dependency bumped off the local patch, `cargo test -p vgi-bridge` green (82 lib + 17 + 2 integration tests), clippy and fmt clean
- [ ] Against a VTC with the matching change: restart the bridge with a changed `role_map` and see the VTC re-project the stale repositories

## Follow-up

- **`proofPurpose`.** The spec's examples sign bridge events with `proofPurpose: "authentication"`; this bridge still signs with `assertionMethod` and still requires `assertionMethod` on the jobs the VTC signs (`wire.rs`). Moving both sides together is left for a separate change, so neither refuses the other in between.

title: fix(vta-service)!: close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit
body:
Stacked on #1733 (base `fix/vta-key-export-authz`). Review that PR first.

## Summary

This PR fixes the follow-ups found while writing #1733.

1. **`keys/export-secret` returns the spec's own codes.**
   - An internal key is refused with `keys/export-secret:neverExportable`.
   - A key marked non-exportable is refused with `keys/export-secret:notExportable`. It used to return `permissionDenied` in both cases.
   - The refusals stay typed (`KeyExportRefusal`) from the operation up to the Trust-Task handler.
   - They are reached only after the `key-export` capability, the channel and the caller's scope have all passed, so an unentitled caller never sees them. This is the spec's "after establishing entitlement and before assembling a response".
   - REST, DIDComm and the other callers keep a 403 carrying the same message.
2. **`vault/release` writes a durable `vault.secret_release` audit row before the sealed secret leaves.** If the row cannot be written, the release is refused, as `key.secret_export` is.
   - This applies to every kind of vault secret, including passkey and SSH private keys.
   - The row names the holder, the entry id, the context, the transport (`trust-task/<binding>`) and `kind=<secretKind>`.
   - It never contains the secret, the entry's label or its site.
3. **The TEE mnemonic export is sealed to the requester, and a bearer token alone never releases it.**
   - **New Trust Task:** `spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0` (payload `{clientDid, nonce, label?}`). Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649. Until that ships in trust-tasks-rs, the URI is listed in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS`.
   - **Signed by the caller, on every path.** The request's proof is made for `authentication` and verifies as `issuer`. `issuer` is the session DID, `recipient` is this VTA's DID, and `issuedAt` is fresh. The caller is a super admin holding `key-export`.
   - **End-to-end path (DIDComm authcrypt, TSP).** `clientDid` is the requester's ephemeral key, from `pnm bootstrap request`.
   - **Signed first-boot path (Trust Tasks on HTTPS).** A freshly booted TEE VTA may have no DIDComm or TSP endpoint yet. Over HTTPS the export is allowed only when `clientDid` is **exactly** the signing caller's DID, so the words are sealed to a key only the caller holds. A TLS terminator holding the bearer JWT cannot sign as the caller, so it can neither make its own request nor change the seal recipient in the caller's. The spine's replay guard refuses a second use of the document `id`.
   - **Everything else over hop-by-hop is refused** with `permissionDenied`, including a `clientDid` that differs from the signer and an unsigned request. Every refusal happens before the guard is touched, so a refused request does not spend the one-time release.
   - **The replay guard never keeps a secret-bearing response.** A task classified `Discloses::Secret` has its duplicate absorbed with no body. So a replayed mnemonic export is never answered with the bundle, and the record never holds it.
   - **`POST /attestation/mnemonic` is refused** with 403 for every caller (after the `key-export` check), with a message naming the Trust Task. REST is hop-by-hop, and for a TEE, TLS terminates outside the enclave.
   - **Sealed answer:** an armored bundle carrying a new additive `SealedPayloadV1::SeedMnemonic` variant, sealed to `clientDid` under an `Attested` producer assertion. The quote binds `SHA256(client_ed25519 || nonce || producer_ed25519)`. The response also carries the bundle's digest. Open the bundle with `pnm bootstrap open --expect-digest`.
   - **Two-phase export:** `MnemonicExportGuard::reserve` and `commit` are the only way to read the words. The plaintext one-shot `MnemonicExportGuard::export()` and `MnemonicExportResponse` are removed from the public API. The entropy is zeroed only after the bundle is built and the audit row is written, so a failed seal cannot lose the root seed, and a concurrent second export is refused.
   - **`SeedMnemonicBundle` zeroizes its mnemonic on drop**, on every path: opened, sealed, or dropped on an error.
   - **Audit:** the `seed.mnemonic_export` row records the actor, the recipient `did:key`, the transport and the bundle digest.
4. **The VTA's own use of a key is recorded as `key.internal_use`.** `get_key_secret_internal` used to log it as `key.secret_export`, so every VC issuance and webvh publish looked like an export.
5. **Stored P-256 public keys are multicodec-prefixed (`p256-pub`).**
   - `create_key` and `import_key` stored a bare SEC1 point, which named no algorithm (VTI-KEY-012) and differed from what custody publishes for the same key on export. The same was true of imported X25519 keys and of the offline `vta keys` export.
   - No boot migration. These are test deployments, so a record written by an earlier build is recreated, not rewritten. (`migrate_unprefixed_public_keys` and its test are removed.)

The spec side of the capability is trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#643, which registers `keyExport` in the shared `Capability` enum.

## Breaking changes

- **`POST /attestation/mnemonic`** is refused (403). Use `spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0`: over DIDComm or TSP, or at first boot over HTTPS, signed by the caller with `clientDid` set to the caller's own DID. It returns `{bundle, digest, windowRemainingSecs}`. The request must carry the caller's `authentication` proof.
- **A duplicate of a secret-disclosing Trust Task** (for example `keys/export-secret`) is answered with an empty body rather than a replay of the first response.
- **`MnemonicExportGuard::export()` and `MnemonicExportResponse`** are removed. Use `reserve()` / `commit()`.
- **`SealedPayloadV1`** gains the variant `SeedMnemonic`. It is additive, but any exhaustive `match` must add an arm. Every in-tree match has been updated.
- **Audit consumers** that counted `key.secret_export` rows will see the VTA's internal loads move to `key.internal_use`.
- **Stored P-256 and imported X25519 key records** written by an earlier build keep the bare encoding. Recreate the deployment.
- **`vault/release`** fails when the audit sink is unavailable.

## Tests

- `refusals_about_the_key_carry_the_declared_codes` (trust task)
- `an_uncommitted_reservation_releases_the_export` (vta-tee)
- `seed_mnemonic_roundtrips_and_redacts` (vta-sdk)
- `internal_use_is_not_recorded_as_an_export`
- `p256_record_and_export_agree_on_the_multicodec_public_key`
- `a_mnemonic_export_over_an_end_to_end_channel_is_sealed_to_the_requester`: only the requester's key opens the bundle, it holds 24 words, the words are not in the response, and the release is one-time.
- `a_signed_first_boot_export_over_https_is_sealed_to_the_signer`: first boot over HTTPS, signed, `clientDid` == signer. The export is released, only the caller's key opens it, and it is one-time.
- `over_https_a_client_did_other_than_the_signer_is_refused`
- `an_unsigned_request_is_refused` (HTTPS and end-to-end)
- `a_request_signed_by_another_did_is_refused`
- `a_proof_made_for_another_purpose_is_refused`
- `a_non_super_admin_is_refused` (HTTPS and end-to-end)
- `a_replayed_first_boot_request_is_refused_the_bundle`: the same document is sent twice through the dispatch spine. The replay is not answered with the bundle.
- In each refusal test the guard is still available afterwards.
- `the_rest_mnemonic_export_is_refused`
- The existing export, vault and guard tests pass.
- Local: `cargo test -p vta-service --features tee --lib`: 1330 passed, 1 ignored. `cargo clippy -p vta-service --features tee --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: fix(vta-service)!: close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit (#1743)
body:
fix(vta-service)!: close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit (#1743)

* fix(vta-service): apply the key-export and sign capability checks on every transport

The KeyExport capability was checked only by the keys/export-secret
Trust-Task handler, so GET /keys/{id}/secret and DIDComm get-key-secret
released private keys to an admin whose entry was narrowed without
key-export. Capability::Sign was checked nowhere.

Both checks now live in the operation layer (VTI-VTA-003, VTI-VTA-007):

- get_key_secret requires key-export before any lookup, refuses a
  hop-by-hop channel (keys/export-secret/0.1 requires a channel
  confidential to the two parties), keeps the internal-key and
  non-exportable refusals, and writes the key.secret_export audit row
  durably before releasing the material, refusing if it cannot.
- The Trust-Task binding (https, didcomm, tsp) is recorded at the three
  entry points and named in the export's audit channel.
- vta/contexts/secrets and provision-integration use the same gate.
- sign_payload requires sign for opaque caller bytes; derive-and-sign
  and derive-and-sign-document require sign.
- The legacy REST and DIDComm key routes now consult the policy gate
  with the matching Trust-Task URI.
- The TEE mnemonic export writes a durable audit row before release.

BREAKING CHANGE: private keys are no longer released over REST or the
HTTPS Trust-Task binding; use DIDComm, TSP or the on-host CLI. Entries
narrowed without key-export or sign lose export, provisioning and
generic signing respectively.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: gate backup export on key-export and a confidential channel

A backup carries the seed, so it is an export of every key the VTA holds
(VTI-VTA-003).

- export_backup requires the key-export capability, read from the caller's
  ACL entry, on every path (REST, DIDComm, both initiate-export versions).
- The backup.export and backup.initiate-export audit rows are written
  durably before the envelope or descriptor is returned; a failed write
  refuses the export and aborts the bundle.
- POST /backup/export is refused, and initiate-export is refused over a
  hop-by-hop transport: the sealing password would exist in plaintext
  wherever TLS terminates, next to the bundle. DIDComm and TSP work.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic requires key-export.
- keys/export-secret and keys/sign check the caller's scope before they
  say whether a key exists, so an out-of-scope caller gets one refusal for
  both and learns neither the key's context nor its existence.
- Revoked keys are neither exported nor loaded with InternalAuthority.
- The non-exportable refusal message no longer carries a run of spaces.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the admin key-export gate test expects the scoped refusal

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: refuse backup import over REST and HTTPS Trust Tasks

The import carries the backup and the password that opens it, which
together are every key the backup holds. Over a hop-by-hop channel both
exist in plaintext wherever TLS terminates.

- POST /backup/import always answers 403.
- initiate-import and finalize-import (1.0 and 1.1) are refused over the
  HTTPS binding, after the super-admin check and before a slot is minted
  or the password is used. DIDComm and TSP still work, as does DIDComm
  backup-import.
- This implements the vta/backup Channel requirement proposed in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646, which also covers initiate-export.
- The pnm --use-rest-legacy help and the backup docs say DIDComm or TSP.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): close the key-material follow-ups from the export audit

- keys/export-secret answers keys/export-secret:notExportable and
  :neverExportable (typed KeyExportRefusal), reached only after the
  key-export, channel and scope checks.
- vault/release writes a durable vault.secret_release row (holder,
  entry, context, transport, kind; never the secret) before the sealed
  secret leaves, and refuses if it cannot.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic seals the mnemonic to the caller's did:key
  (new additive SealedPayloadV1::SeedMnemonic, Attested assertion)
  instead of returning plaintext; the guard is two-phase so a failed
  seal cannot lose the root seed.
- get_key_secret_internal records key.internal_use, not
  key.secret_export.
- P-256 (and imported X25519) public keys are stored multicodec-
  prefixed, matching custody; a boot migration re-encodes old records.

BREAKING CHANGE: POST /attestation/mnemonic takes a BootstrapRequest and
returns a sealed bundle; SealedPayloadV1 gains SeedMnemonic; internal
key loads are audited as key.internal_use.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: release the TEE mnemonic only sealed, over an end-to-end channel

- New Trust Task spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 (specced at
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649): super admin with key-export, the
  mnemonic sealed to the requester's did:key under an Attested assertion,
  dispatched over DIDComm and TSP. Over Trust Tasks on HTTPS it is refused
  with permissionDenied after entitlement and before the guard is touched,
  as the backup export is.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic is refused (403) and names the task: REST is
  hop-by-hop, and for a TEE TLS terminates outside the enclave.
- SeedMnemonicBundle zeroizes its mnemonic on drop.
- MnemonicExportGuard::export() and MnemonicExportResponse are removed:
  reserve/commit is the only way to read the words.
- The boot migration migrate_unprefixed_public_keys and its helper are
  removed; test deployments are recreated, not migrated.

BREAKING CHANGE: the mnemonic export moves from POST /attestation/mnemonic
to spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 over DIDComm or TSP; the
plaintext guard export is gone; unprefixed P-256 records are no longer
rewritten at boot.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): a signed first-boot mnemonic export over HTTPS

A freshly booted TEE VTA may have no DIDComm or TSP endpoint yet, and its
export window is short. The end-to-end-only rule left it with no way to take
the backup. spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 now defines a signed
first-boot path (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649).

- Both paths require the request to be the caller's own signed document:
  - the proof is made for authentication and verifies as issuer;
  - issuer is the session DID;
  - recipient is this VTA's DID (a VTA without one is refused);
  - issuedAt is inside the dispatch freshness bound.
- Over Trust Tasks on HTTPS the export is allowed only when clientDid is
  exactly the signing caller's DID, so the words are sealed to a key only the
  caller holds. A TLS terminator holding the bearer JWT cannot sign as the
  caller, so it can neither make its own request nor change the seal
  recipient in the caller's.
- A clientDid other than the signer is refused over hop-by-hop, and so is an
  unsigned request, on every path. All refusals happen before the guard is
  touched.
- The dispatch replay guard no longer keeps a response whose task discloses
  a secret. A replayed mnemonic export is absorbed with no body, never
  answered with the bundle.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic stays 403, and names both paths.
- The durable audit row before release and the one-shot guard are
  unchanged.
- test_support::sign_as_for signs for a chosen proofPurpose.
- deploy/nitro/README.md documents the first-boot path.

Tests:
- first boot over HTTPS, signed, clientDid == signer: released, and only the
  caller's key opens it;
- clientDid != signer over HTTPS: refused;
- unsigned: refused;
- signed by another DID: refused;
- proof made for assertionMethod: refused;
- non-super-admin: refused;
- a replayed document through the dispatch spine: not answered with the
  bundle.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: classify the mnemonic export for the MCP guard, and name its sealed request schema apart

vta/attestation/mnemonic-export is Sensitive, like keys/export-secret. The sealed-transfer BootstrapRequest schema is published as SealedBootstrapRequest so it no longer collides with the provision-integration BootstrapRequest in the OpenAPI document.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: the mnemonic export body carries ext, and the manifest counts its unpublished URI

MnemonicExportBody denies unknown fields, so it takes the SPEC §4.5.1 ext member like every other such wire type. vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 is bound ahead of the trust-tasks-rs this workspace takes (it is specified in 0.23), so the vta/ unpublished count is 7 until the workspace moves to 0.23.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): drop the mnemonic-export debt now that 0.23 publishes it

vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#649) is
published in trust-tasks-rs 0.23, taken by #1764:

- trust_task_manifest.rs's vta/ unpublished-URI count goes back to 6,
  and the entry drops out of vta-service's UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS.
- the mnemonic-export handler takes the generated
  trust_tasks_rs::specs::vta::attestation::mnemonic_export::v1_0
  payload type in place of the hand-written MnemonicExportBody, which
  is now unused and removed.
- the sealed_transfer::bundle.rs doc comment naming the retired
  POST /attestation/mnemonic REST route is corrected to name the
  Trust Task that replaced it.

Taking 0.23 also flips git-ns/bridge/job/0.4 and
git-ns/namespace/reseat/0.3 to published, so their manifest entries
come out too; the hand-written bridge::JOB_TYPE and
git_ns::reseat_v0_3 have not yet moved onto the generated types,
tracked by the TODOs on those two modules instead.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): tidy the mnemonic-export refusal string, add its conformance witness

- attestation.rs: collapse the accidental run of internal spaces in
  the hop-by-hop clientDid refusal message (line-continuation
  whitespace left in from the literal).
- conformance.rs: witness vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0 against
  the generated v1_0 types, tee-gated like its dispatch arm.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: security(vta-sdk)!: verify a proof's key against its proofPurpose (VTI-KEY-022)
body:
## What

A Data Integrity proof now verifies only when the signer's DID document lists its `verificationMethod` under the relationship named by its `proofPurpose` (VTI-KEY-022). This matches W3C Controlled Identifiers v1.0 §3.3, *Retrieve Verification Method*, steps 10 and 11. The check is strict and has no escape hatch.

## Why

Every verifier in the workspace looked the method up in `verificationMethod` and nowhere else. A key published only for `keyAgreement`, or authorised only to authenticate, could therefore make an `assertionMethod` proof over a credential.

## Changes

**vta-sdk** (`trust_task_proof::purpose`, new)
- `ProofPurpose` covers the four signing relationships. `parse` refuses `keyAgreement`, an empty value and unknown values.
- `PurposeVmResolver` resolves a method for one purpose.
- `PurposeBound` binds that resolver to one proof's purpose, as the upstream `VerificationMethodResolver` that `DataIntegrityProof::verify` takes.
- `authorised_method` requires three things:
  1. the resolved document's `id` is the DID;
  2. the method is listed under the purpose's relationship, by absolute DID URL, by `#fragment` or embedded. A reference resolves only against the top-level `verificationMethod` set, never to a method embedded under another relationship;
  3. the method's `controller` is the DID.
- **`TrustTaskVmResolver`** implements `PurposeVmResolver` and no longer implements the purpose-unaware trait.
  - For did:key, only `did:key:<id>#<id>` is accepted, and it is valid for every signing purpose. An X25519 did:key signs for nothing.
  - For did:peer, the document's own relationships apply: V keys are valid for `authentication` and `assertionMethod`, and E keys for nothing.
- `verify_trust_task_proof_with` and vetting's `verify_attached_proof` verify through `PurposeBound`.
- Refusals name the rule that failed. They contain no DID or key material.

**vtc-service**
- `DidVmResolver` delegates to `TrustTaskVmResolver` for a purpose. `resolve_ed25519`, `resolve_verifying_key` and `resolve_bbs_g2` each take the purpose.
- `check_issuer_binding` compares exact strings and requires a non-empty fragment.
- **Proof sets** (`proof_set`):
  - `accept_any` is replaced by `accept_all`: every proof present must verify, and there must be at least one.
  - A proof whose `cryptosuite` this build does not implement is skipped. A set with nothing verifiable left is refused.
  - `require_suites` lets policy require particular suites. No caller uses it yet.
  - `verify_one` checks that the proof declares the purpose the document is relied on for: `assertionMethod` for credentials and invitations, `authentication` for presentations and holder bindings.
- The credential, VP, VMC, VEC, VRC, recognition, personhood, invitation and audit paths all verify through the resolver above.
- `LocalSigner::verify_vc` checks each proof against the key that proof names.
- `assertion_method_id` returns `did:key:<id>#<id>` for a did:key issuer.

**vta-service**
- A did:key VTA signs as `did:key:<id>#<id>` instead of the store's `#key-0` (`vta_signing_vm`). This covers VC issuance, provision-integration and the rooms responses.
- `derive-and-sign-document` refuses a `proofPurpose` that no verifier accepts.
- Room invitations must declare `assertionMethod`.

**vti-rooms-dtg**: `VerificationKeys::public_key` takes the purpose. Room credentials must declare `assertionMethod`.

**vta-mcp**: the default holder fragment follows the DID method: the key id for did:key, `key-1` for did:peer, and `key-0` otherwise.

**Collapses #1757 onto this check.** #1757 added a separate relationship check for approver decisions: `ProofRelationship` and `TrustTaskVmResolver::requiring`. That check is gone, and so are the resolver's `relationship` field and `ProofRelationship::lists`/`require`. `verify_approval_proof_with` now refuses any `proofPurpose` other than `assertionMethod` (`WrongPurpose`). It then verifies through the general verifier, which binds the resolver with `PurposeBound` to `assertionMethod`, including on the retry after a DID-cache refresh (#1737's `resolve_for_vm` and `refresh_if_cached`). The public API is unchanged: `verify_approval_proof`, `verify_approval_proof_with` and `APPROVAL_PROOF_PURPOSE`. No caller outside vta-sdk used `ProofRelationship`. In `derive-and-sign-document`, #1733's `Sign` capability check runs first, then the purpose validation, both before any key is derived.

## Breaking changes

| Change | Who is affected | Migration |
|---|---|---|
| `TrustTaskVmResolver` no longer implements `VerificationMethodResolver` | callers of `DataIntegrityProof::verify` with it | `PurposeBound::for_proof(&resolver, &proof)?` |
| `VerificationKeys::public_key(vm, purpose)` | room hosts implementing it | pass the proof's purpose |
| A proof whose key is not listed under its purpose is refused | signers using a key under another relationship | sign with a key listed for the purpose |
| One failing proof refuses a proof set | documents carrying a stale or bad extra proof | drop it |
| A did:key method other than `#<id>` is refused | anything signing a did:key as `#key-0` | sign as `did:key:<id>#<id>` |

These are test deployments, so there is no migration path.

## Signer audit

**Now fails:**
- **openvtc personhood presentations.** `openvtc/src/state_handler/runtime_actions.rs:576` passes the persona's `keys.signing` key (`#key-1`) to `personhood::build_presentation`, which signs with `proofPurpose: authentication` (`openvtc-core/src/personhood.rs:316`). `create_initial_webvh_did` lists `#key-1` under `assertionMethod` only (`openvtc-core/src/config/did.rs`), so the VTC refuses the VP. Fix in openvtc: sign with `keys.authentication`.
- **did:key signers naming `#key-0`.** A did:key VTA or VTC did this; both are fixed here. So were the mock VTA in `vta-service/src/test_support.rs` and the test fixtures in `vtc-service/tests/{join_requests,invitations}.rs`.

**Pass today, will break when the VTC moves trust-task documents to `authentication`:**
- **VGI bridge.** `crates/vgi-bridge/src/wire.rs:257` refuses any inbound VTC document whose `proofPurpose` is not `assertionMethod`. No git-ns spec requires that. It must change in step with the VTC. The VTC keeps signing with `assertionMethod` for now, so nothing breaks today.

**Pass:**
- **VTC.** `LocalSigner` signs `assertionMethod` with `#key-0`, which is listed under both relationships. The hybrid ML-DSA `#key-2` is under `assertionMethod` only. That is fine for credentials, but `#key-2` could not sign an `authentication` proof.
- **VTA.** `#key-0` is listed under both relationships. The step-up, consent, credential and trust-task response signers all emit `assertionMethod`.
- **Bridge.** Its own signatures pass: the did:peer `#key-1` is listed under authentication and assertionMethod, and the did:key `#<id>` is valid for every purpose.
- **openvtc capability documents.** They are signed `assertionMethod` with `#key-1`. Under the key-roles rule they should move to the authentication key.
- **Trust Registry.** It has no DI signer.

**Verifiers outside this repo that still resolve without a purpose:** Trust Registry (trust-tasks-proof 0.21) and the bridge (0.22). Both need the next trust-tasks-proof release to get the strict check. Both compile unchanged. The in-flight bridge branches `bridge-vta` and `bridge-multi-org` implement `VerificationMethodResolver` for `Published` and pass it to `Verifier::with_resolver`, so they will need a `ProofPurposeResolver` instead.

**Not changed:** vta-vault and vta-mobile-core verify against did:key-derived or pinned keys. For those the did:key rule already holds.

## Companion changes

- Framework spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#24
- trust-tasks-proof: OpenVTC/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#637

This PR does not depend on either one; it carries its own resolver.

## Tests

- **vta-sdk**: purpose unit tests, and did:key / did:peer / wrong-purpose end-to-end tests through `verify_trust_task_proof_with`.
- **vtc-service `proof_set`**:
  - a failing proof refuses the set;
  - an unsupported suite is skipped, and a set with only unsupported suites is refused;
  - a proof with no suite is not skipped;
  - `require_suites`;
  - real did:key proofs for both purposes, a wrong purpose, and a foreign fragment.
- **Run locally**:
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`;
  - `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features bbs --all-targets -D warnings`;
  - `cargo test -p vtc-service --tests` (all integration binaries);
  - targeted `vtc-service`, `vta-service`, `vta-sdk`, `vti-rooms-dtg` and `vta-mcp` tests.

title: feat(git-ns): move repo/create to 0.3, name owners, close the self-grant hole
body:
## Summary

- Moves `openvtc-core`'s `git-ns/repo/create` client from `0.1` to `0.3`. In `0.3` a namespace admin whose `git.repo.create` is only implied by `git.ns.admin` can no longer make themselves owner (and forge admin) of a repository they create — they must name another member in the new optional `owners` field, or the VTC refuses with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`. Naming owners is itself a grant of `git.repo.own`, refused with `git-ns:escalation` without the authority to grant it.
- Adds an Owners field to the Repos panel's new-repository form (type to filter known members, Ctrl+A to add, Ctrl+D to paste a DID for someone not listed), and arms the change for confirmation once owners are named.
- `Refusal::explain()` shows the exact break-glass guidance for `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`.
- Updates existing `git-ns/repo/create` tests for the new `owners` field and adds tests for naming owners and for the `selfGrantNotAllowed` refusal, in both `openvtc-core` and the TUI (`repos_actions`, key mapping, rendering).

Pairs with [OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1745) and [trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#641](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/issues/641).

## Blocked on a vta-sdk / vta-service / vti-common release built on trust-tasks-rs 0.23

`trust-tasks-rs` 0.23 is now published (`git-ns/repo/create` 0.3 ships in it), and the temporary local patch this branch carried (`[patch.crates-io]` pinning `trust-tasks-rs` to the `feat/git-ns-break-glass` branch, plus the matching `deny.toml` `allow-git` entry) has been **reverted** — that commit is no longer needed for the spec, only for the release.

Taking the real 0.23 release is still blocked, though: this workspace holds to one node of `trust-tasks-rs` in the graph (see the comment above the `trust-tasks-rs` entry in the root `Cargo.toml`), and every VTI crate it pins is still on the 0.22 line as of this check:

- `vta-sdk` — pinned here at `0.51.0`; latest published is **0.52.0**, which still declares `trust-tasks-rs = "0.22.3"`.
- `vta-service` (dev-dependency, for `MockVta`) — pinned here at `0.41.0`; latest published is **0.42.0**, also on `trust-tasks-rs = "0.22.3"`.
- `vti-common` (transitive, via `vta-sdk`) — latest published is **0.25.0**, also on `trust-tasks-rs = "0.22.3"`.

`affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.28.0 and `affinidi-tdk` 0.18.0 — the releases built on trust-tasks 0.23 — are already published, so those are not what blocks this. The blocker is specifically **no `vta-sdk` (or `vta-service`/`vti-common`) release yet declaring `trust-tasks-rs 0.23`**.

This PR now merges `origin/main` and drops the temporary patch, but does **not** bump `trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` or `affinidi-tdk` — doing so alone would split the graph into two `trust-tasks-rs` nodes, which this workspace's pin discipline treats as a bug, not a bounded exception (unlike VGI's bridge, which tolerates a split for a `publish = false` crate). **CI fails to compile `openvtc-core`** (`specs::git_ns::repo::create` has no `v0_3` under 0.22.7) until a VTI release moves `vta-sdk` onto trust-tasks-rs 0.23; re-run this PR's bump once one is published. Left in draft.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p openvtc-core git_ns` — 28 passed (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo test -p openvtc` (repos-related + full suite) — all passed (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all passed (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` — clean (pre-revert, against the temporary patch)
- [ ] Re-run the full test plan once `trust-tasks-rs` 0.23 is taken for real

title: feat(vtc-service): re-project git roles, and use the bridge's reported role map
body:
## Summary

Two follow-ups to the configurable bridge role map (VGI #84). The spec comes first, in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#639. The bridge side is OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#91.

**Design: the bridge reports, and the VTC re-projects stale repositories itself**
- On start-up (the only time its configuration can change) and after a binding completes, the bridge sends `git-ns/bridge/event/0.3` `roleMapReported`. It carries the effective map as the forge applies it, the repositories whose own map differs, and the repositories it last projected under another map (`stale`).
- The VTC refuses an unordered map (`malformedRequest`) and any resource outside the namespace (`permissionDenied`). Otherwise it keeps the report on the namespace, and only while the same bridge DID serves it.
- **A report names its ladder.** The VTC refuses (`malformedRequest`) a `ladder` that lists `none` or is not strictly ascending, a map role that is neither `none` nor on it, and a ladder other than the one it knows for the namespace: GitHub organisation `read…admin`, GitHub personal account `write`, Codeberg's Forgejo `read`/`write`/`maintain`/`admin`. So `own: admin` on a personal account, or `triage` on Forgejo, is refused.
- **The newest report wins.** The VTC keeps the report's `issuedAt` and acknowledges, but applies no part of, one issued before the report it holds from the same bridge. A new bridge's report is never compared with the old one's.
- It drops from `stale` any repository it records neither active nor orphaned, since it re-projects no other.
- For each stale repository the VTC forgets the roles digest, so the projector re-sends its complete `desiredRoles`. The repository leaves `stale` when a `projectRoles` job queued after the report succeeds.
- This is secure without a human gate: re-projecting changes no right, and it only applies, now, a map the bridge would apply at its next projection anyway. The real control over the map is who can edit the bridge's config.

**The role map in use**
- The map is shown per person on the Repos page as the effective forge role, and a namespace admin shows as "no forge role".
- `drift/resolve` adopt derives the right as the **lowest** right whose role is the observed one. So where maintainers get `admin`, a forge `admin` is adopted as maintain, not own.
- A revert weighs as revoking own when the role is at or above own's role.
- **No map is assumed, the default included.** Until the bridge serving the namespace reports (after binding, after another bridge DID comes to serve it, or for good with a bridge before event 0.3), the map is **unknown**: `roleMapSource: "unknown"` with no `roleMap` on the namespace or repository rows, and a warning on the namespace card. Meanwhile drift adopt is refused with `git-ns:roleMapUnknown` (with `cnm` guidance), and every role revert (other than of `none`) weighs as revoking `git.repo.own`, the highest right the role could carry. The bridge reports whenever it starts serving a namespace and whenever it (re)establishes its link to the VTC (VGI #91).
- **Elevated by the map.** `Right::is_elevated_in(&ns, resource)`: a right is elevated if `Right::is_elevated` says so (unchanged), or if the map projects it to forge `admin` on the resource (any map in the report, on the namespace resource). While the map is unknown `git.repo.maintain` counts as elevated too. It is the helper the self-grant rules of `right/grant` 0.3 and `drift/resolve` 0.3 use; #1735 and #1745 wire it in.
- `ns.admin` gets no forge role under any map.

**`git-ns/roles/reproject/0.1`**
- For a namespace it is open to a community administrator, or to `git.ns.admin` by explicit record. For one repository, that repository's owner (`git.repo.own`, explicit or implied) may also run it. Entitlement is checked before the repository is looked up.
- It covers a namespace or a single repository.
- It is normal consent class, uses the policy action `roles.reproject`, and is audited as `gitNs.roles.reprojected`.
- It is refused with `manualMode`, or with `noForgeAccess` after the bridge reports `installationRemoved`.
- It is available as `cnm git reproject <resource> [--reason …]`, and as a "Re-project roles" button on the namespace card and the repository header.

## Behaviour change (flagged)

On a **personal account**, reverting collaborator `write` (or above) now weighs as revoking `own`, so it is elevated. Before, it weighed as revoking `maintain`. `write` is the role `own` projects to there, so this follows drift/resolve's "the role git.repo.own projects to" literally.

## Merge order

**This PR goes first.** Then #1735 (drift adopt names its subject), then #1745 (break-glass). Both are merged with this branch and switch their self-grant checks to `Right::is_elevated_in`.

## trust-tasks-rs 0.23

Built on main's trust-tasks-rs 0.23, which carries `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.3 and `git-ns/roles/reproject` 0.1. No `[patch.crates-io]`; Cargo.lock has one trust-tasks-rs.

Also in this PR: #1729 spelled out `git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.3 and `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 until a release generated them. 0.23 does, so `git_ns::reseat_v0_3` is gone. The handler, `ops::namespace_reseat` and vtc-client's `RESEAT_TYPE_URI` use `reseat::v0_3`, including its `SELF_GRANT_NOT_ALLOWED`. `bridge::JOB_TYPE` is `job::v0_4`'s `TYPE_URI`. The matching `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK` entries in `trust_task_manifest.rs` go back to zero.

## Merged with main (#1729, #1728)

- The console's drift adopt (`adoptStanding`, `driftAdoptTask`, `DriftResolveDialog`) now derives the right from the repository's reported role map, not the owner kind. It offers nothing while the map is unknown (`git-ns:roleMapUnknown`).
- `driftRevertTask(resource, item, reason, roleMap)` no longer takes the namespace.
- The personal-account adopt tests now take the personal map from the repository row.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns`: 131 pass, including new tests for the report, stale re-projection and clearing, refusals, map-derived adopt and noMatchingRight, and reproject authorization and refusals
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest --test openapi_snapshot --test openapi_response_census`, `cargo test -p cnm-cli --bins`, `cargo test -p vta-sdk --test generated_wire_types_census`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli -p vtc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`

title: security(vta-service)!: require assertionMethod on an approver's decision
body:
Stacked on #1740.

A task-consent decision and a step-up approve-response are the human approver's own attestation, not an operational message. The VTA already verified their signature and bound the signer, but it accepted any `proofPurpose`, and a key listed under any relationship. The other parties already hold decisions to `assertionMethod`, with the key listed under the signer's `assertionMethod` relationship:

- the did-hosting RP (affinidi-webvh-service #213, `verify_approval`);
- the browser wallet (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#279);
- the mobile engine (#1744).

This PR makes the VTA do the same.

## Changes

**vta-sdk**
- `TrustTaskVmResolver::requiring(ProofRelationship)` resolves a verification method only when its DID document lists it under that relationship.
  - This applies to `did:peer` and network DIDs.
  - A `did:key` lists its signing key under both relationships by definition, so it is not checked.
  - A resolution error is still a refusal, never an unknown that passes. So a deactivated `did:webvh` is refused once the resolver fails its resolution (upstream fix in progress).
- `verify_approval_proof_with` / `verify_approval_proof` check two things:
  - The proof must be made for `assertionMethod`. Anything else is refused with the new `DiProofError::WrongPurpose`.
  - The key must verify against an `assertionMethod`-only resolver.
- vti-common and vta-service re-export both.

**vta-service**
- `handle_decision` verifies decisions with `verify_approval_proof_with`, and logs the verifier's cause beside the refusal. The reply still does not carry it.
- `verify_did_signed_gate` uses `verify_approval_proof`, so every approve-response is held to the rule, approved or denied.
- A webauthn approve-response must also carry the approver's `assertionMethod` proof. The passkey assertion is still the gate.

## Tests

New:
- A decision signed for `authentication`, or unsigned, is refused before any pending is consulted. The same decision signed for `assertionMethod` gets past the proof check.
- An approve-response signed for `authentication` is refused.
- A `did:peer` key not listed under `assertionMethod` does not verify an approval.
- An assertion-only key does not count for `authentication`.

Local runs:
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features proof-verify,didcomm --lib trust_task_proof`: 9 passed.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib -- trust_tasks::task_consent trust_tasks::step_up`: 27 passed.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test step_up_approve_response`: 6 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vti-common -p vta-service -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Known failing test (not from this PR): `tests/delegated_consent_e2e.rs`

Five tests fail with `identityMismatch` on the base branch (35f1e0f2) as well as here:

- `a_did_update_is_approved_by_a_human_and_the_keys_they_saw_are_the_keys_installed`
- `an_approval_authorizes_exactly_one_execution`
- `the_requester_cannot_approve_its_own_task`
- `a_context_admin_approval_lets_a_cross_context_requester_execute`
- `a_reprovision_is_refused_pending_consent_and_executes_once_approved`

Root cause:
- #1739 (d3169ace) added a check in `dispatch_trust_task_core`: a document's in-band `issuer` must be the authenticated caller (SPEC §4.8.1).
- The tests still post documents on another party's bearer token:
  - the approver's `task-consent/decision` goes out on the requester's session;
  - `the_requester_cannot_approve_its_own_task` mints its DID with a document issued by a different requester than the token's.

The rule is correct and the tests are stale. Real clients send a decision as the approver, and a decision's authority is its proof plus approver-set membership, never the session.

`Test (workspace)` (`cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`) runs this file, so it fails on #1739, #1740 and here until the tests are fixed. A fix exists as a separate commit: each decision goes out on a `monitor` session of the approver, and `create_did` takes the identity it signs as. With it, all 9 tests in the file pass. It belongs with #1739, where the rule was introduced, and is not included in this PR.

## VTC: approvals verified as approvals (ca8c9188)

- `dispatch_trust_task_core` now verifies every `task-consent/decision/0.1` and `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4` with `verify_approval_proof_with` and `state.trust_task_vm_resolver()`. It refuses a proof made for any purpose other than `assertionMethod`, a key not listed under the signer's `assertionMethod`, and a signer DID that does not resolve. The verifier's cause is logged; only `Display` goes on the wire.
- An approve-response must carry a proof, even with webauthn evidence. The passkey stays the gate. The signer, or the admin its console key acts for, must be the step-up's `subject` (`subjectMismatch` otherwise). Both checks run before the pending mark is looked at, so no other party can spend an admin's challenge.
- The other verifier sites (login, relationships, rooms, reply waiters) verify operational documents and are unchanged.
- Senders needed no change. `sign_in_place_with` (used by the fixtures), the admin console's console-key signer and the mobile engine all sign for `assertionMethod`.
- Tests: `spine_proof_tests` covers authentication-purpose, capabilityDelegation-only did:peer and unresolvable did:web approvals (all refused at the proof), did:key and did:peer assertionMethod approvals (both pass), and an unsigned approve-response (`proofRequired`). `signed_step_up::an_approve_response_signed_by_another_admin_is_refused` checks that the challenge can still be answered afterwards.
- Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#637 (9e0b83c8) had moved the decision example to `authentication`. It is now back to `assertionMethod`, and `task-consent/decision/0.1` requires it normatively.

## Not in this PR

- `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4` still says a webauthn approve-response MAY omit its proof. The VTA and VTC now require one; aligning the spec would need approve-response 0.5.


- Once #1752 lands, this PR's `ProofRelationship` (`TrustTaskVmResolver::requiring`) should collapse onto #1752's general proofPurpose/relationship check (`PurposeBound` / `authorised_method`).
