title: security(vta-service)!: require assertionMethod on an approver's decision (#1757)
body:
security(vta-service)!: require assertionMethod on an approver's decision (#1757)

* fix(vta-service)!: require a document proof bound to the sender on every DIDComm and TSP trust task

A Trust Task that reaches the VTA or the VTC over an intrinsic-sender
transport (DIDComm, TSP) is now accepted only when the document carries a
Data Integrity proof that verifies as its `issuer`, and that issuer is the
transport-reported sender. The transport's sender alone no longer
authorizes anything (VTI-OPS-021/093).

VTA:
- `accept_from_proven_sender` binds every request (and every reply that no
  waiter claims) with `bind_document_to_sender` before ACL resolution:
  missing proof is `proofRequired`, a proof by someone other than the issuer
  is `proofInvalid`, an issuer other than the sender is `identityMismatch`.
- The spine refuses any document whose in-band `issuer` is not the
  authorized caller (`identityMismatch`), on every transport.
- The sender-authorized DIDComm protocol-message surface is removed:
  key/seed/context/ACL/audit/config management, restart, backup
  export/import, `did-management/1.0/*`, `protocol-management/*`, the
  task-typed `swap-acl`/`acl/swap-key` and `provision/integration` arms,
  step-up `approve-request`, and `credential-exchange/query`. Those
  operations remain available as Trust Tasks in the binding envelope.
- `acl/swap-key` also requires `issuer == currentSubject` (spec §6).

VTC:
- The spine requires, for DIDComm and TSP, a verified proof whose signer is
  the sender, so the vetter profile/resend, personhood challenge and git-ns
  view/link-status tasks no longer run on the sender alone.

vta-sdk:
- `InboundMessage.from` is replaced by `claimed_from` (untrusted) and
  `verified_signer`, set only from a verifying proof bound to the
  document's issuer (`InboundMessage::verify`, run by `AgentSession::run`).
- `provision_integration_didcomm` takes the relayer's `HolderKey` and sends
  a signed Trust Task in the binding envelope; the DIDComm provision runner
  lists webvh servers with the signed `vta/webvh/servers/list/1.0` task.

Also covers the direct-unpack guard's remaining cases: refresh routes, vault
unseal and anoncrypt-wrapped authcrypt, with each refusal pinned to its
specific `AuthcryptError`.

BREAKING CHANGE: DIDComm and TSP clients must sign every Trust Task
document with the sender's key and name it as `issuer`. The legacy DIDComm
protocol messages listed above are no longer served. `InboundMessage.from`
is removed; `provision_integration_didcomm` takes a new `relayer_key`
argument.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: release a reply waiter only to the peer that signed the reply

A reply to a Trust Task the VTA or the VTC sent now releases its waiter
only when its thread matches and its own Data Integrity proof verifies as
its `issuer`, which must be the peer the request went to. A document on
the thread that the peer did not sign falls through and leaves the waiter
for the genuine reply.

- VTA `PendingReplies::register(thread, peer)` / `complete(doc, signer)`,
  fed by `verified_issuer` on the DIDComm/TSP inbound path and the spine.
- VTC `hooks::PendingReplies` the same, with `complete_verified` on both
  the DIDComm envelope and TSP reply paths (registry writes and reads,
  git-ns bridge jobs, hook writes).
- vta-sdk `DIDCommSession::open_from_vta` refuses a sealed secret unless
  its authcrypt `skid` is bound to `apu`, is the key the unpack reports,
  and belongs to the session's VTA, which `from` must also name.
- `VtaClient::rpc` (the legacy protocol-message helper) no longer sends
  over DIDComm, which the VTA no longer serves: it fails with a typed
  `UnsupportedTransport` naming `--transport rest`.

BREAKING CHANGE: `PendingReplies::register` and `complete` take the peer
and the verified signer; a peer's unsigned replies no longer release a
waiter. Legacy protocol operations (`pnm`/`cnm services …` and the
deprecated inline backup and webvh update/rotate calls) are REST-only.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-cli-common): carry pnm and cnm services commands as Trust Tasks over messaging

Over DIDComm and TSP the VTA serves only signed Trust Tasks, so every
`services` command (list, rest/tsp/webauthn/didcomm enable/update/disable/
rollback, didcomm drain list/cancel) now dispatches the matching
`vta/services/*` Trust Task there. REST keeps its routes. `services
report` has no Trust Task and says so, naming `--transport rest`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test: align trust-task fixtures with the sender-bound proof rules

- The transport harness peer signs its replies, since a reply waiter is now
  released only to a reply its peer signed.
- Spine fixtures name the test admin as `issuer`, since the spine refuses a
  document whose issuer is not the caller.
- The authcrypt route tests expect the messaging library's own unpack refusal
  for a consistent attacker key naming the victim as `from`, and the VTC case
  runs each route on a fresh instance so its requests fit the per-IP burst.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: sign operational documents with the operational key

Every Trust Task document the VTA or the VTC composes as a party — a request
to a peer or a response — now carries a Data Integrity proof by its
operational key with `proofPurpose: authentication` (VTI-KEY-106), plus
`issuer`, `recipient`, whole-second `issuedAt` and a unique `id`
(VTI-KEY-107).

VTA:
- `push/provision` and `push/wake` to a push gateway are signed; a document
  that cannot be signed is not sent.
- Every DID-management request to a webvh host (`webvh_didcomm`
  `send_task`) is signed through `DIDCommBridge::sign_outbound_request`,
  which `build_app_state` arms with the resident operational key.
- Every trust-task response is signed, `trust-task-error` included, and
  including the refusals issued before dispatch (sender binding, ACL
  denial, a TSP frame that is not a binding envelope).

VTC:
- Registry writes, git-ns bridge jobs, trust-registry hook writes and
  member removal notices are signed with `LocalSigner::sign_operational_doc`.
- Every trust-task response is signed, errors and early refusals included.
- Credentials keep `assertionMethod`.

BREAKING CHANGE: responses and VTA/VTC-originated requests switch
`proofPurpose` from `assertionMethod` to `authentication`, so a verifier
must find the signing key under `authentication` in the signer's DID
document. Error responses now carry a proof. Deploy the VTA before the push
gateway and webvh fleet start requiring proofs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): sign trust-registry reads with the operational key

record/query and recognition are signed like writes (operational key,
proofPurpose authentication, recipient = registry DID, issuedAt, unique
id, issuer = this VTC's authority): the registry gates reads as it gates
writes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: sign consent and step-up approve-request pushes with the operational key

The consent approve-request, task-consent request and step-up
approve-request the VTA pushes to approvers are the VTA's own operational
messages: they are now signed with its operational key (the resident
signing key, falling back to #key-0) and proofPurpose authentication
(VTI-KEY-106). The approver's approve-response keeps assertionMethod per
its spec.

BREAKING CHANGE: approver devices must accept an authentication-purpose
proof on these requests, with the VTA key listed under authentication.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: seal the envelope of every document signed with the operational key

Before a VTA or VTC attaches an operational-key proof, the new
`vti_common::trust_task::envelope::seal_envelope` completes and checks the
document (VTI-KEY-107):

- a request must name this node as `issuer` and carry `id` and
  `recipient`, or it is not signed (and so not sent);
- a response, success or `trust-task-error`, is issued by this node
  whatever the request named, and gets an `id` when it has none;
- `issuedAt` is set when absent and truncated to whole seconds in `Z` form.

The VTC's unrestricted-admin `task-consent/request/0.1` pushes are signed
with the operational key under `authentication`, as the VTA's are.
`LocalSigner::sign_operational_response` signs the spine's responses.

BREAKING CHANGE: responses always name the responding node as `issuer`,
and a VTC- or VTA-originated request with no `recipient` or a foreign
`issuer` is refused before it is signed. Consent-request verifiers must
accept an `authentication` proof from the VTC.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vta-service)!: require assertionMethod on an approver's decision

A task-consent decision and a step-up approve-response are the human
approver's own attestation, not an operational message. The did-hosting RP
(affinidi-webvh-service #213, verify_approval), the browser wallet and the
mobile engine hold them to proofPurpose assertionMethod, with the key
listed under the signer's assertionMethod relationship. The VTA verified
the signature and bound the signer, but accepted any purpose, and a key
listed under any relationship.

vta-sdk:

- TrustTaskVmResolver::requiring(ProofRelationship) resolves a
  verification method only when its DID document lists it under that
  relationship (did:peer and network DIDs; did:key lists its signing key
  under both by definition).
- verify_approval_proof_with / verify_approval_proof refuse a proof not made
  for assertionMethod (new DiProofError::WrongPurpose) and verify it against
  an assertionMethod-only resolver. vti-common and vta-service re-export
  them.

vta-service:

- handle_decision verifies the decision with verify_approval_proof_with, and
  logs the verifier's cause beside the refusal.
- verify_did_signed_gate uses verify_approval_proof, so every
  approve-response, approved or denied, is held to the rule.
- A webauthn approve-response must also carry the approver's
  assertionMethod proof; the passkey assertion stays the gate.
- Tests: a decision signed for authentication, or unsigned, is refused
  before any pending is consulted; an approve-response signed for
  authentication is refused; a did:peer key not listed under
  assertionMethod does not verify an approval; an assertion-only key does
  not count for authentication. The decision fixture now names its purpose.

Not done: refusing a deactivated did:webvh approver. The DID cache drops
resolution metadata, so it would need the log itself; approvers today are
did:key.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): send each consent e2e document on its issuer's session

#1739 made the VTA act on a Trust Task only when its in-band issuer is the
authenticated caller (SPEC §4.8.1). Five tests in delegated_consent_e2e.rs
still posted documents on another party's bearer token and failed with
identityMismatch:

- the approver's task-consent/decision went out on the requester's session;
- the_requester_cannot_approve_its_own_task minted its DID with a document
  issued by a different requester than the token's.

The tests are stale, not the rule: a client sends a decision as the
approver, and a decision's authority is its proof and approver-set
membership, never the session. Decisions now go out on a monitor session
of the approver (post_as_approver), and create_did takes the identity it
signs as.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): send each consent e2e document on its issuer's session

#1739 made the VTA act on a Trust Task only when its in-band issuer is the
authenticated caller (SPEC §4.8.1). Five tests in delegated_consent_e2e.rs
still posted documents on another party's bearer token and failed with
identityMismatch:

- the approver's task-consent/decision went out on the requester's session;
- the_requester_cannot_approve_its_own_task minted its DID with a document
  issued by a different requester than the token's.

The tests are stale, not the rule: a client sends a decision as the
approver, and a decision's authority is its proof and approver-set
membership, never the session. Decisions now go out on a monitor session
of the approver (post_as_approver), and create_did takes the identity it
signs as.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test: expect the library's authcrypt sender refusal, and sign as the session's DID

With didcomm 0.15.9 the messaging library itself binds the authcrypt sender
to the key that encrypted the message, so a forged or split skid/apu envelope
is refused during unpack, before the VTC's own guard (which stays as defence
in depth). The sender-binding tests now expect that refusal.

The trust-task discovery and keys/import REST tests signed their documents as
the test admin but authenticated as a different DID, so the in-band issuer
check refused them first. Their sessions now belong to the signing DID.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* security(vtc-service)!: require assertionMethod on an approver's decision

A task-consent/decision and a step-up approve-response are the approver's
own attestation, not an operational message. The VTA, the did-hosting RP's
verify_approval, the mobile engine and the browser wallet hold them to
proofPurpose assertionMethod, with the key listed under the signer's
assertionMethod relationship. The VTC's dispatch spine verified them with the
generic verifier, which accepted any purpose and a key listed under any
relationship.

- The spine verifies a decision or approve-response with
  verify_approval_proof_with and the VTC's resolver. A proof made for another
  purpose, a key not listed under assertionMethod, or a signer DID that does
  not resolve is refused, with the cause in the operator's log only.
- An approve-response must carry a proof, even with webauthn evidence (the
  passkey assertion stays the gate). The signer, or the admin its console key
  acts for, must be the step-up's subject (subjectMismatch otherwise). Both
  checks run before the pending mark is consulted, so another party cannot
  spend an admin's challenge.
- Tests: an approval signed for authentication, by a did:peer key listed
  only under capabilityDelegation, or by an unresolvable did:web, is refused
  at the proof; did:key and did:peer assertionMethod approvals pass it; an
  unsigned approve-response is proofRequired; an approve-response signed by
  another admin is subjectMismatch and leaves the challenge answerable.

The senders already sign for assertionMethod: vta-sdk's sign_in_place_with
(used by the test fixtures), the admin console's console-key signer, and the
mobile engine. None changed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): expect the library's authcrypt sender refusal

With didcomm 0.15.9 the messaging library refuses a forged or split skid/apu envelope during unpack, before the VTA's own guard, which stays as defence in depth. A genuine authcrypt wrapped in anoncrypt still reaches the guard and is refused as not authcrypt.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): sign the fake trust registry's replies as the registry

The reply demux now releases a waiter only to a reply whose proof verifies
as its issuer, the peer the request went to. The test registry sent its
responses and rejections unsigned and unaddressed, so every round trip
timed out. TestJoinClient::sign_as_peer sets issuer, recipient and a fresh
issuedAt and signs with the peer's authentication key; serve_once signs
every reply, rejections included.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): expect the registry health probe to be signed

Every registry task, reads included, is now signed with the operational
key, so the probe carries a proof with proofPurpose authentication. A
registry that refuses it still answers, which is what health reports.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(e2e): the inline backup export is refused over DIDComm

The deprecated inline export is a legacy protocol message, which the VTA no longer serves over DIDComm, so the client refuses it before sending and names REST. Backups over DIDComm use the vta/backup/initiate-export Trust Task flow.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the relayed-request test signs its DID mint as the requester

create_did takes the identity it signs as since the issuer-bound spine; the test that arrived from main still used the old three-argument form.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the relayed-request test sends its decision as the approver

The in-band issuer must be the session's DID, so the approver's decision goes on the approver's own session, as every other decision in this file does.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials
body:
## Summary

Issued credentials are now verified before they are stored. A membership (VMC) or role (VEC) credential delivered as `credential-exchange/issue` used to be stored after checking only that its `issuer` matched the DIDComm sender; its Data Integrity proof was never checked.

### New modules

**`openvtc-core/src/proof_check.rs`** verifies a Data Integrity proof against the signer's DID document. The signature itself is checked by `affinidi-data-integrity` (`verify_with_public_key`); this module adds the binding to the signer's DID and to a relationship, and handles proof sets.
- **Resolution:** the signer's DID document is resolved, bounded to 10 s (R1.2).
- **Proof sets:** a single proof object or an array is accepted. At least one proof must be present, and **every** proof must verify; a bad, malformed or foreign proof next to a good one is a refusal.
- **Suites:** `eddsa-jcs-2022`, and `mldsa44-jcs-2024` for a VTC that also signs with its PQ key.
- **Relationship check (W3C Data Integrity):**
  - the DID part of `verificationMethod` must equal the signer exactly (a DID that merely shares the prefix is refused);
  - the method must be listed under the relationship its `proofPurpose` names;
  - the key is taken from that same document;
  - the method's `controller` must be the signer (a method embedded in, or referenced by, the signer's document but controlled by someone else is refused);
  - a revoked method, or a key that does not match the suite, is refused;
  - a proof `created` up to 5 minutes in the future is accepted, matching the `issuedAt` skew for operational documents, so a slightly fast clock at the VTC is not a refusal.

**`openvtc-core/src/issued_credential.rs`** holds the credential rules:
- the issuer must be the sender, and every proof must be `assertionMethod`;
- the validity window is enforced (`validFrom`/`validUntil`, or `issuanceDate`/`expirationDate`);
- **revocation fails closed**: a revoked or suspended credential is refused, and so is one whose status cannot be established. The refusal message tells the user to retry or ask for re-issue.

**`openvtc-core/src/status_list.rs`** reads Bitstring Status Lists. The list is verified with `proof_check`, so a list signed with a proof set verifies; the SDK's reader handles only a single proof object. It also checks:
- the list's `id` is the URL it was fetched from;
- its issuer is the credential's issuer;
- its validity window and `statusPurpose`;
- the bitstring is decoded only as far as the entry's index.

The vetter-grant revocation check uses the same reader. A fetched list is cached for at most 5 minutes, or less if its `validUntil` or `ttl` says so, and is re-verified on every use. The cache holds at most 64 lists.

### Local checks first, and a guarded status fetch

- **The cheap checks run before any network work.** `messaging::credential_issue_admissible` checks, locally, that the credential is issued by the sender, is for one of our personas, is of a known kind, and is for a live (Pending or Active) membership that persona holds with the sender. The dispatcher runs it **before** verifying, so a party we hold no membership with cannot make this client resolve a DID or fetch a status list. `handle_credential_issue` runs the same check again.
- **Status-list fetches stay on public hosts.** A status-list URL comes out of a credential someone else wrote. The production client (`vetting::status::status_client`) now uses `affinidi-net-guard`'s `public_internet` policy:
  - `status_list_url` refuses IP literals and special-use names for loopback, private, link-local and other non-public addresses;
  - a guarded DNS resolver refuses a name that resolves to one of those addresses;
  - every redirect hop is re-vetted, and no proxy is used.
- **A VRC's proof goes through `proof_check`.** `verify_vrc_proof` is no longer `tdk.verify_data`. It requires `proofPurpose: assertionMethod`, a method the issuer lists under `assertionMethod`, and the issuer as the method's controller.

### Wiring

- `messaging::handle_credential_issue` now takes a `VerifiedIssuedCredential`, which only the verifier produces, so the check cannot be skipped. `credential_in_issue` extracts the unverified credential.
- The dispatcher verifies the credential before storing it. On refusal it writes one activity-log line saying what failed, without the credential or any DID.
- **A join is admitted only by the verified membership credential.** An `approved` status response or an `allow` verdict is an unsigned reply. It now acknowledges the join and leaves it Pending, adopting the community's request id. The membership becomes Active, and our reciprocal VMC is sent, only when the credential arrives and verifies.
- **Activation only from our own pending join.** A credential lands only on a Pending or Active membership, and only a Pending join is activated. A membership that ended (Left, Withdrawn, Rejected, Removed, Expired) is not revived by a credential arriving, however well signed.
- **Account recovery** (`rebuild::plan`) proof-checks every membership it would restore; a failure is recorded as `RejectionReason::Unverified`.
- **Vault sync** (`credential_sync`) no longer pushes a locally held credential that does not verify. A new `SyncReport::unverified` count is shown in the activity log, which also flags credentials stored before this change.

### Breaking changes

This PR is written for test deployments only, with no backwards-compatibility path.
- **Behaviour:**
  - a credential that is not validly signed is not stored or activated;
  - an approval alone no longer activates a membership;
  - a credential whose status list is unreachable is refused.
- **Library:**
  - `handle_credential_issue(account, VerifiedIssuedCredential, from)`;
  - `sync_membership_credentials(config, client, resolver)`;
  - `GrantCheck::run(&DIDCacheClient)`;
  - new `RejectionReason::Unverified`;
  - new direct dependency `affinidi-status-list` (already in the graph via `vta-sdk`).

## Tests

- **Proof checks:**
  - accepted: a valid single proof; a valid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44 proof set;
  - refused: a tampered claim; a key of another DID (including a DID that only shares the prefix); a key listed only under `authentication`/`keyAgreement`; a set with one bad, outsider or malformed proof; a missing proof or empty set; the wrong purpose; a document for another DID;
  - refusal text contains no DIDs.
- **Status list:**
  - a list signed with a proof set is read, both ways;
  - an unsigned, tampered, foreign or wrong-URL list is not read;
  - an unreachable list is Unknown, never Active;
  - a signed credential whose list is unreachable is refused, with a retry message.
- **Join:** approval and allow leave the membership Pending.
- **Local checks first:** credentials from a stranger, for another subject, or of an unknown kind are not admissible.
- **Status fetch guard:** loopback, private, link-local, metadata and `.local` URLs are refused; the production client's resolver refuses `localhost`.
- **VRC:** a proof made for another purpose is refused.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (plus `--features dev-overrides`), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (plus `--no-default-features`) and `cargo deny check` all pass locally.

## Notes

- Revocation freshness is bounded by the 5-minute cache. Credential-issue verification still runs inline in inbound dispatch; it is bounded by the 10 s resolve timeout and the status-fetch timeout. Moving it off the loop is a follow-up.

- The relationship check is local to openvtc. It does not modify the shared VTI/trust-tasks resolvers.
- Other places that trusted the transport sender are handled in the stacked PRs #381 and the follow-up.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] Finite timeouts (R1.2): DID resolution 10 s; the status fetch reuses `vetting::status::status_client`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): verification happens before anything is stored
- [x] Retries bounded (R1.4): none added
- [x] Loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a refusal returns normally
- [x] Acks after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] Wire types (R3.*): no wire changes
- [x] Fail-closed (R5.*): an unresolvable issuer, an unverifiable proof or an unestablished status all refuse
- [x] Logs claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations flagged: none

title: fix(openvtc): require proofs for relationship DIDs, removal notices and community answers
body:
Stacked on #380 (base `fix/verify-issued-credential-proofs`). Review and merge that PR first.

## Summary

The sender a message arrives from is now treated as a **routing hint, not an identity**. Every decision that depends on *who said something* now requires a Data Integrity proof by that party, checked against their DID document with `proof_check` (added in #380).

### Relationships

**Proofs on request and accept.** Both now carry:
- `didProof`, made with an `authentication` key of the relationship DID;
- `personaProof`, made by the persona that names an R-DID.

Both sign `{role, did, persona, peer, thid}`, so a proof made for one handshake does not verify in another. `role` (`request` or `accept`) stops one side's proof standing as the other's within the same handshake. A request or accept whose proofs are missing or invalid is refused.

**Correlation by thread id only.** `Relationships::awaiting(thid, state, from)` matches accept, finalize and reject. It requires:
- our request's id, never empty;
- the right state: `RequestSent`, or `RequestAccepted` for finalize;
- the party the request went to.

The fallback that matched by sender alone is removed, so a reject can no longer end an established relationship.

**Other changes.**
- The request id is fixed before sending and written into the provisional record, so an accept that arrives early still matches.
- The unused `create_send_message_accepted`, which sent an accept with no proof, is removed.

### Operational documents (VTI-KEY-106 / VTI-KEY-107)

These are removal notices and a community's vetting answers (manifest, vetter list, profile, resend, withdrawal record). They are handled by the new `openvtc-core/src/operational.rs`, and acted on only if all of the following hold:
- `issuer` is the sending community;
- the document's signed `type` equals the type the handler handles. A community's signed answer therefore cannot be acted on as a removal notice, or as the answer to another question. The freshness window comes from that type (`OperationalKind::of`), so `verify_operational` takes the handled type rather than a kind;
- the proof has `proofPurpose: authentication`, by a key listed under `authentication`. An `assertionMethod` proof is **refused** for these;
- `recipient` is present and is one of our personas. For a removal notice it must also be the persona the payload removes;
- `issuedAt` is present and inside the kind's window: 30 days plus one for a removal notice (its delivery window), one day for an answer. Future-dated beyond a 5-minute skew, or an `expiresAt` in the past, is refused;
- the document `id` has not been acted on before.

**Replay store.** Ids go into `SeenDocuments`, which is persisted in the protected config and kept until each id's window passes, so a replay is refused across restarts too.
- `verify_operational` records nothing. It returns a `VerifiedOperational`, which the caller commits only once the document is **bound**: a removal notice from a community the named persona holds a membership with, or an answer that matched something of ours. A community's manifest is taken only from a community we asked, are applying to, or belong to. A party that can only sign with its own key never writes to the set.
- The set is keyed by `(issuer, id)`. Ids are capped at 256 characters.
- Quotas are 1024 ids per issuer and 256 issuers. At the bound they **refuse**; nothing is evicted before its window ends, so a flood cannot push out a genuine notice and replay it.
- The dispatcher reports a change whenever the set changes, so it is persisted even when a handler reports nothing else.

Membership and role credentials and vetter grants stay `assertionMethod`. A vetter grant is kept only when it verifies, including its revocation status, which fails closed.

### Sender sources

`dispatch_inbound`'s `from` selection, `authenticated_sender` and the dispatcher's `from_did` are now documented as routing hints, pointing to `proof_check`.

## Rollout

Deploy together with VTI PR 3 (the VTC signing operational documents, including refusals, with its `authentication` key, and including `recipient` and `issuedAt`). There is no compatibility window: these are test deployments, upgraded together. Until then, openvtc refuses the VTC's removal notices and vetting answers.

## Breaking changes

These are test deployments with no compatibility path.
- **Wire:**
  - relationship bodies gain `didProof`/`personaProof`, and both peers need this version;
  - a VTC must sign operational documents with an `authentication` key and include `recipient` and `issuedAt`.
- **Library:**
  - `verify_removal_notice(message, from, our_dids, resolver, seen, now)` and `handle_member_removal_notice(account, VerifiedRemovalNotice, from)`;
  - `vetting::inbound::handle(book, ctx, seen, message, sender)`, and `Context { did_resolver, .. }`;
  - new `ProtectedConfig::seen_documents`;
  - `create_send_message_accepted` removed.

## Tests

- **Relationship binding:**
  - a proven R-DID is accepted;
  - refused: missing DID proof, R-DID without a persona proof, a proof from another thread, a switch to a DID the sender does not control;
  - `awaiting` refuses: wrong sender, empty or unknown thread id, established relationship, wrong state.
- **Operational documents:**
  - a fresh, signed, addressed document is accepted once, and its replay is refused;
  - refused: an `assertionMethod` proof; an authentication-purpose proof by a key not under `authentication`; a missing or wrong recipient; a missing, old or future `issuedAt`; an expired document; a foreign issuer;
  - an unsigned copy does not burn the id;
  - a document is taken only as its own signed `type`: one without a type, or handled as another type, is refused.
- **Relationship binding role:** a request's proof does not verify as an accept's.
- **Removal notice:**
  - accepted once;
  - refused: `assertionMethod`, unsigned, bare, tampered, forged, wrong sender, unaddressed, misaddressed, stale.
- **Vetting:**
  - a community answer signed with the assertion key is refused, as is a replayed one or one addressed elsewhere;
  - a tampered grant is not kept, nor is a grant whose status list cannot be read.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings` (plus `--features dev-overrides`), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (includes the mediator end-to-end tests) and `--no-default-features` all pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] Finite timeouts (R1.2): proof-check resolution 10 s
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its effect (R2.1): proofs are verified before any mutation, and the seen id is recorded only after the proof verifies
- [x] Retries bounded (R1.4): none added
- [x] Loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks after handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] Wire types (R3.*): new camelCase fields; the breaks are flagged above
- [x] Fail-closed (R5.*): no proof or an unresolvable signer means no action
- [x] Logs claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations flagged: the wire breaks above

title: fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials (#380)
body:
fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials (#380)

* fix(openvtc-core): verify the proof on issued credentials

A credential a community delivers over credential-exchange/issue was
stored after checking only that its issuer matched the DIDComm sender.
Verify it before storing: resolve the issuer's DID document, require
every Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, mldsa44-jcs-2024) to verify
with a key of the issuer's own DID listed under assertionMethod, check
the validity window, and refuse a revoked credential via the existing
status-list check.

handle_credential_issue now takes a VerifiedIssuedCredential, which only
the verifier produces. Account recovery (rebuild::plan) applies the same
check to each membership it would restore, and the vault sync skips a
locally held credential that does not verify.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): admit a join only on a verified membership credential

An approved join status or an allow verdict is an unsigned reply; it no
longer activates the membership. It acknowledges the join, and the
membership becomes Active - and the reciprocal membership credential is
sent - only when the community's credential arrives and verifies.

Factor the proof check into proof_check (signer DID binding, relationship
per proof purpose, proof sets) so other signed messages can use it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): fail closed on credential status, and read proof-set status lists

A credential's revocation status must now be established: an unreachable
or unverifiable status list refuses the credential, with a message that
says to retry. The list is read by a new status_list module that
verifies it with proof_check, so a list signed with a proof set
(Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44) verifies. The vetter grant check uses the same
reader. StatusPolicy is removed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): activate only a pending join; bind verification methods to their controller

- a credential lands only on a Pending or Active membership, and only a
  Pending join is activated; an ended membership is not revived
- a proof's verification method must be controlled by the signer
- allow five minutes of skew on a proof's created, matching issuedAt
- cache fetched status lists for at most five minutes (or the list's
  validUntil/ttl), re-verifying on every use

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(openvtc-core): check a delivered credential locally before fetching; keep status fetches on public hosts

- a credential-issue is checked against local state (issuer is the sender,
  subject is our persona, known kind, a live membership with the sender)
  before its proof is verified or its status list fetched, so a party we
  hold no membership with cannot make this client resolve or fetch
- status-list fetches refuse loopback, private, link-local and other
  non-public hosts: IP literals and special-use names in the URL, names by
  what they resolve to, and every redirect hop (affinidi-net-guard); no proxy
- a VRC's proof goes through proof_check: assertionMethod purpose, a method
  the issuer lists and controls

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: feat(vta-service)!: sign operational documents with the operational key
body:
Stacked on #1739 (base `fix/didcomm-bound-proof`), because both change the trust-task spine's `accept_from_proven_sender` and response signing. Retarget to `main` once #1739 merges.

Every Trust Task document the VTA or the VTC composes as a party now carries a Data Integrity proof made with its operational key, with `proofPurpose: authentication` (VTI-KEY-106). That covers requests it sends to a peer and responses it returns. Each document also carries `issuer`, `recipient`, a whole-second `issuedAt` and a unique `id` (VTI-KEY-107).

## VTA

| Document | Change |
|---|---|
| `push/provision` and `push/wake` to a push gateway (`device.rs`, `step_up.rs`) | Signed. If a document cannot be signed, it is not sent. |
| DID-management requests to a webvh host (`webvh_didcomm.rs` `send_task`, DIDComm and TSP) | Signed through `DIDCommBridge::sign_outbound_request`. `build_app_state` arms that with the resident operational key. |
| Trust-task responses | Signed, success and `trust-task-error` alike. This includes refusals issued before dispatch: the sender-binding refusal, the ACL denial, and a TSP frame that is not a binding envelope. `sign_success_response` becomes `sign_response`. |
| Consent approve-request, task-consent request and step-up approve-request pushes | Signed with the operational key (the resident signing key, falling back to `#key-0`) and `authentication`. The approver's `approve-response` keeps `assertionMethod`, per its spec. |

## VTC

| Document | Change |
|---|---|
| Trust-registry writes (`registry/messaging.rs`) | Signed with the new `LocalSigner::sign_operational_doc`. |
| Trust-registry reads (`record/query`, `recognition`) | Now signed. The registry gates reads like writes. |
| git-ns bridge jobs, trust-registry hook writes, member removal notices | Signed with `sign_operational_doc`. |
| Trust-task responses | Signed, errors and early refusals included. `dispatch_trust_task_core` wraps the validated dispatch. |
| Credentials | Unchanged: they keep `assertionMethod`. |

## Issuer and recipient binding

- Every response names the responding node as its `issuer`, whoever the request came from.
- A request with no `recipient`, or whose `issuer` is not the node's own DID, is refused before anything is signed. A node never signs a document on behalf of someone else.
- Verifiers of the VTC's consent requests must accept an `authentication` proof. Only the approver's decision stays `assertionMethod`.

## Tests

- VTA: `push/wake` and `push/provision` are signed by the VTA with `authentication`, carry all envelope members and have unique ids, and a retargeted document fails verification.
- VTA: the webvh document is signed with the operational key (`eddsa-jcs-2022`, `authentication`, whole-second `Z` time), and a bridge with no signer signs nothing.
- VTA: error and success responses are signed with `authentication`.
- VTA: the step-up approve-request proof is `authentication` (unit and integration tests updated).
- VTC: a refusal is signed, both after dispatch and before it.
- VTC: a registry write request and a `record/query` are signed with `authentication`, addressed to the registry.

## Breaking changes and deploy order

- Responses and VTA- or VTC-originated requests switch `proofPurpose` from `assertionMethod` to `authentication`. A verifier must now find the signing key under `authentication` in the signer's DID document.
- Error responses now carry a proof.
- Approver devices (the iOS app, the browser extension) must accept an `authentication` proof on the consent, task-consent and step-up approve-requests.
- Requests without a `recipient`, or naming a foreign `issuer`, are refused before signing.
- `LocalSigner` gains `sign_operational_doc`.
- **Deploy order:** deploy the trust registry with affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs#142 (signed replies) before this VTC, since the VTC now accepts only a registry reply the registry signed (from #1739). Deploy the VTA and VTC with or before the push gateway (vti-push-gateway#32), the webvh fleet (affinidi-webvh-service#213) and the trust registry (registry#140) start requiring these proofs.

title: feat(vta-service)!: sign operational documents with the operational key (#1740)
body:
feat(vta-service)!: sign operational documents with the operational key (#1740)

* fix(vta-service)!: require a document proof bound to the sender on every DIDComm and TSP trust task

A Trust Task that reaches the VTA or the VTC over an intrinsic-sender
transport (DIDComm, TSP) is now accepted only when the document carries a
Data Integrity proof that verifies as its `issuer`, and that issuer is the
transport-reported sender. The transport's sender alone no longer
authorizes anything (VTI-OPS-021/093).

VTA:
- `accept_from_proven_sender` binds every request (and every reply that no
  waiter claims) with `bind_document_to_sender` before ACL resolution:
  missing proof is `proofRequired`, a proof by someone other than the issuer
  is `proofInvalid`, an issuer other than the sender is `identityMismatch`.
- The spine refuses any document whose in-band `issuer` is not the
  authorized caller (`identityMismatch`), on every transport.
- The sender-authorized DIDComm protocol-message surface is removed:
  key/seed/context/ACL/audit/config management, restart, backup
  export/import, `did-management/1.0/*`, `protocol-management/*`, the
  task-typed `swap-acl`/`acl/swap-key` and `provision/integration` arms,
  step-up `approve-request`, and `credential-exchange/query`. Those
  operations remain available as Trust Tasks in the binding envelope.
- `acl/swap-key` also requires `issuer == currentSubject` (spec §6).

VTC:
- The spine requires, for DIDComm and TSP, a verified proof whose signer is
  the sender, so the vetter profile/resend, personhood challenge and git-ns
  view/link-status tasks no longer run on the sender alone.

vta-sdk:
- `InboundMessage.from` is replaced by `claimed_from` (untrusted) and
  `verified_signer`, set only from a verifying proof bound to the
  document's issuer (`InboundMessage::verify`, run by `AgentSession::run`).
- `provision_integration_didcomm` takes the relayer's `HolderKey` and sends
  a signed Trust Task in the binding envelope; the DIDComm provision runner
  lists webvh servers with the signed `vta/webvh/servers/list/1.0` task.

Also covers the direct-unpack guard's remaining cases: refresh routes, vault
unseal and anoncrypt-wrapped authcrypt, with each refusal pinned to its
specific `AuthcryptError`.

BREAKING CHANGE: DIDComm and TSP clients must sign every Trust Task
document with the sender's key and name it as `issuer`. The legacy DIDComm
protocol messages listed above are no longer served. `InboundMessage.from`
is removed; `provision_integration_didcomm` takes a new `relayer_key`
argument.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: release a reply waiter only to the peer that signed the reply

A reply to a Trust Task the VTA or the VTC sent now releases its waiter
only when its thread matches and its own Data Integrity proof verifies as
its `issuer`, which must be the peer the request went to. A document on
the thread that the peer did not sign falls through and leaves the waiter
for the genuine reply.

- VTA `PendingReplies::register(thread, peer)` / `complete(doc, signer)`,
  fed by `verified_issuer` on the DIDComm/TSP inbound path and the spine.
- VTC `hooks::PendingReplies` the same, with `complete_verified` on both
  the DIDComm envelope and TSP reply paths (registry writes and reads,
  git-ns bridge jobs, hook writes).
- vta-sdk `DIDCommSession::open_from_vta` refuses a sealed secret unless
  its authcrypt `skid` is bound to `apu`, is the key the unpack reports,
  and belongs to the session's VTA, which `from` must also name.
- `VtaClient::rpc` (the legacy protocol-message helper) no longer sends
  over DIDComm, which the VTA no longer serves: it fails with a typed
  `UnsupportedTransport` naming `--transport rest`.

BREAKING CHANGE: `PendingReplies::register` and `complete` take the peer
and the verified signer; a peer's unsigned replies no longer release a
waiter. Legacy protocol operations (`pnm`/`cnm services …` and the
deprecated inline backup and webvh update/rotate calls) are REST-only.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-cli-common): carry pnm and cnm services commands as Trust Tasks over messaging

Over DIDComm and TSP the VTA serves only signed Trust Tasks, so every
`services` command (list, rest/tsp/webauthn/didcomm enable/update/disable/
rollback, didcomm drain list/cancel) now dispatches the matching
`vta/services/*` Trust Task there. REST keeps its routes. `services
report` has no Trust Task and says so, naming `--transport rest`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test: align trust-task fixtures with the sender-bound proof rules

- The transport harness peer signs its replies, since a reply waiter is now
  released only to a reply its peer signed.
- Spine fixtures name the test admin as `issuer`, since the spine refuses a
  document whose issuer is not the caller.
- The authcrypt route tests expect the messaging library's own unpack refusal
  for a consistent attacker key naming the victim as `from`, and the VTC case
  runs each route on a fresh instance so its requests fit the per-IP burst.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: sign operational documents with the operational key

Every Trust Task document the VTA or the VTC composes as a party — a request
to a peer or a response — now carries a Data Integrity proof by its
operational key with `proofPurpose: authentication` (VTI-KEY-106), plus
`issuer`, `recipient`, whole-second `issuedAt` and a unique `id`
(VTI-KEY-107).

VTA:
- `push/provision` and `push/wake` to a push gateway are signed; a document
  that cannot be signed is not sent.
- Every DID-management request to a webvh host (`webvh_didcomm`
  `send_task`) is signed through `DIDCommBridge::sign_outbound_request`,
  which `build_app_state` arms with the resident operational key.
- Every trust-task response is signed, `trust-task-error` included, and
  including the refusals issued before dispatch (sender binding, ACL
  denial, a TSP frame that is not a binding envelope).

VTC:
- Registry writes, git-ns bridge jobs, trust-registry hook writes and
  member removal notices are signed with `LocalSigner::sign_operational_doc`.
- Every trust-task response is signed, errors and early refusals included.
- Credentials keep `assertionMethod`.

BREAKING CHANGE: responses and VTA/VTC-originated requests switch
`proofPurpose` from `assertionMethod` to `authentication`, so a verifier
must find the signing key under `authentication` in the signer's DID
document. Error responses now carry a proof. Deploy the VTA before the push
gateway and webvh fleet start requiring proofs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): sign trust-registry reads with the operational key

record/query and recognition are signed like writes (operational key,
proofPurpose authentication, recipient = registry DID, issuedAt, unique
id, issuer = this VTC's authority): the registry gates reads as it gates
writes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: sign consent and step-up approve-request pushes with the operational key

The consent approve-request, task-consent request and step-up
approve-request the VTA pushes to approvers are the VTA's own operational
messages: they are now signed with its operational key (the resident
signing key, falling back to #key-0) and proofPurpose authentication
(VTI-KEY-106). The approver's approve-response keeps assertionMethod per
its spec.

BREAKING CHANGE: approver devices must accept an authentication-purpose
proof on these requests, with the VTA key listed under authentication.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: seal the envelope of every document signed with the operational key

Before a VTA or VTC attaches an operational-key proof, the new
`vti_common::trust_task::envelope::seal_envelope` completes and checks the
document (VTI-KEY-107):

- a request must name this node as `issuer` and carry `id` and
  `recipient`, or it is not signed (and so not sent);
- a response, success or `trust-task-error`, is issued by this node
  whatever the request named, and gets an `id` when it has none;
- `issuedAt` is set when absent and truncated to whole seconds in `Z` form.

The VTC's unrestricted-admin `task-consent/request/0.1` pushes are signed
with the operational key under `authentication`, as the VTA's are.
`LocalSigner::sign_operational_response` signs the spine's responses.

BREAKING CHANGE: responses always name the responding node as `issuer`,
and a VTC- or VTA-originated request with no `recipient` or a foreign
`issuer` is refused before it is signed. Consent-request verifiers must
accept an `authentication` proof from the VTC.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): send each consent e2e document on its issuer's session

#1739 made the VTA act on a Trust Task only when its in-band issuer is the
authenticated caller (SPEC §4.8.1). Five tests in delegated_consent_e2e.rs
still posted documents on another party's bearer token and failed with
identityMismatch:

- the approver's task-consent/decision went out on the requester's session;
- the_requester_cannot_approve_its_own_task minted its DID with a document
  issued by a different requester than the token's.

The tests are stale, not the rule: a client sends a decision as the
approver, and a decision's authority is its proof and approver-set
membership, never the session. Decisions now go out on a monitor session
of the approver (post_as_approver), and create_did takes the identity it
signs as.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): send each consent e2e document on its issuer's session

#1739 made the VTA act on a Trust Task only when its in-band issuer is the
authenticated caller (SPEC §4.8.1). Five tests in delegated_consent_e2e.rs
still posted documents on another party's bearer token and failed with
identityMismatch:

- the approver's task-consent/decision went out on the requester's session;
- the_requester_cannot_approve_its_own_task minted its DID with a document
  issued by a different requester than the token's.

The tests are stale, not the rule: a client sends a decision as the
approver, and a decision's authority is its proof and approver-set
membership, never the session. Decisions now go out on a monitor session
of the approver (post_as_approver), and create_did takes the identity it
signs as.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test: expect the library's authcrypt sender refusal, and sign as the session's DID

With didcomm 0.15.9 the messaging library itself binds the authcrypt sender
to the key that encrypted the message, so a forged or split skid/apu envelope
is refused during unpack, before the VTC's own guard (which stays as defence
in depth). The sender-binding tests now expect that refusal.

The trust-task discovery and keys/import REST tests signed their documents as
the test admin but authenticated as a different DID, so the in-band issuer
check refused them first. Their sessions now belong to the signing DID.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): expect the library's authcrypt sender refusal

With didcomm 0.15.9 the messaging library refuses a forged or split skid/apu envelope during unpack, before the VTA's own guard, which stays as defence in depth. A genuine authcrypt wrapped in anoncrypt still reaches the guard and is refused as not authcrypt.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): sign the fake trust registry's replies as the registry

The reply demux now releases a waiter only to a reply whose proof verifies
as its issuer, the peer the request went to. The test registry sent its
responses and rejections unsigned and unaddressed, so every round trip
timed out. TestJoinClient::sign_as_peer sets issuer, recipient and a fresh
issuedAt and signs with the peer's authentication key; serve_once signs
every reply, rejections included.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): expect the registry health probe to be signed

Every registry task, reads included, is now signed with the operational
key, so the probe carries a proof with proofPurpose authentication. A
registry that refuses it still answers, which is what health reports.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(e2e): the inline backup export is refused over DIDComm

The deprecated inline export is a legacy protocol message, which the VTA no longer serves over DIDComm, so the client refuses it before sending and names REST. Backups over DIDComm use the vta/backup/initiate-export Trust Task flow.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the relayed-request test signs its DID mint as the requester

create_did takes the identity it signs as since the issuer-bound spine; the test that arrived from main still used the old three-argument form.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the relayed-request test sends its decision as the approver

The in-band issuer must be the session's DID, so the approver's decision goes on the approver's own session, as every other decision in this file does.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): sign a request under the registry's real record/put URI

The unit test named trust-registry/record/put/0.1, which the registry does not publish; the VTC writes registry/record/put/0.1.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: chore(deps)!: take trust-tasks 0.23
body:
## Summary

Bumps every trust-tasks crate to **0.23** (`trust-tasks-rs`, `-capability-client`, `-https`, `-didcomm`, `-tsp`, `-proof`) and fixes what the release breaks. It adopts no new spec versions and changes no behaviour beyond what 0.23 itself requires.

## Versions

affinidi-tdk-rs#898 has published, so the workspace now takes the affinidi crates built on trust-tasks 0.23:

- `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.28, `affinidi-tdk` 0.18
- `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` 0.11 (vtc-service, vta-service, room-host, tests/e2e)
- `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin` 0.3, `affinidi-messaging-mediator-tui` 0.3 (pnm-cli)

`Cargo.lock` resolves **one** `trust-tasks-rs` and **one** `trust-tasks-proof`, both 0.23.0. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` is clean, and the earlier `MediatorAcl` / `ATMProfile` mismatches are gone.

## Breaking changes adapted to

| 0.23 change | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **proof: check a proof's verificationMethod against its proofPurpose** (#637). `CachedDidResolver` no longer implements `VerificationMethodResolver` | `vta-mobile-core/src/proof.rs` | Verify through `PurposeBound::new(&resolver, ProofPurpose::AssertionMethod)`. The function already rejects any purpose other than `assertionMethod`, so this is the same check, now enforced against the DID document relationship as well. |
| **device: register the `keyExport` capability** (#643) | `vta-service/src/operations/device.rs` (tests only) | `key-export` is now in the closed `capabilities` enum rather than carried under `ext`. Two tests asserted the old registry and now assert the new one. No code change. |
| **didcomm: a consumer may require a proof** (#642). `vtc/vetting/vetters/profile/0.1`, `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1` and `vtc/members/personhood/challenge/0.1` now declare `proof` REQUIRED | `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs` (tests only) | The proof census moves 41 -> 44. The personhood-challenge dispatch tests now send signed documents from a real `did:key` member, using the existing `signed_document` helper. |

**Downstream-visible:** the spine now refuses a proofless request for those three tasks with `proofRequired`. That comes from the spec. The REST routes (bearer token + `Trust-Task` header: `vtc-client::resend_vetter_grant`, admin-ui) don't use the proof spine and are unaffected. I found no in-repo DIDComm sender of those tasks.

The regenerated types and new spec versions in 0.23 (git-ns reseat 0.3, drift/resolve 0.3, bridge job 0.4, event 0.3, repo/create 0.3, grant 0.3, break-glass, approve-response 0.5, mnemonic-export, backup channel, message/status) needed no changes: they're additive to the modules this workspace uses. Adopting them is for separate PRs.

## Files in the other session's areas

**None touched.** `vti-common/src/trust_task_push.rs`, `vtc-service/src/member_push.rs`, `vta-sdk/src/task_consent.rs`, `vta-cli-common/src/consent_approve.rs`, `pnm-cli/src/commands/consent.rs`, `cnm-cli/src/consent.rs` and `vtc-service/src/acl/admin_consent.rs` all compile unchanged against 0.23.

## Tests

These results come from a **local diagnostic build only**, not from this branch as pushed. For that build I patched the trust-tasks crates to the v0.23.0 release checkout and temporarily bridged the `MediatorAcl` mismatch with a serde round-trip. The bridge is not committed.

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: every suite passed except five vtc-service lib tests (the census test and four personhood tests), all caused by #642. They pass after the fixes above: `trust_tasks::` has 128 passed, and `operations::device` has 31 passed after the `keyExport` update. The census tests (`error_code_census`, `trust_task_manifest`, `openapi_*`) pass.

On the committed branch the workspace builds; the full `cargo test --workspace` and clippy run is in progress.

Bump trust-tasks-rs, -capability-client, -https, -didcomm, -tsp and
-proof to 0.23 and adapt to what the release breaks. No new spec
versions are adopted here.

  updated to the new registry.

  signed documents from a real did:key member.

with proofRequired on the Trust-Task spine.

0.17 are built on trust-tasks-rs 0.22, and MediatorAcl crosses the SDK
API in vta-sdk/src/acl_setup.rs. It needs the affinidi-tdk-rs release
that takes trust-tasks 0.23.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): a namespace admin gets no forge role; bridge jobs are git-ns/bridge/job 0.4
body:
## What

This implements the decision from 2026-09-25 (design doc §4.2 and §11): a namespace admin (`git.ns.admin`) gets no role on the forge. They are not made organisation owner and get no repository role. The wire rules are `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#635, draft). The bridge side is OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#84 (merged) and OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#92 (draft).

**This PR breaks compatibility on purpose.** All deployments are test instances and will be recreated. The VTC now sends job 0.4 only, and a bridge before 0.4 gets nothing.

### Role projection (`git_ns/bridge.rs`)

- **Rights counted:** `highest_repo_rights` counts only rights recorded in the person's own name: `own`, `maintain` or `commit.sign` on the repository, or `commit.sign` on the namespace. It never counts what `ns.admin` implies.
- **Admin with no right of their own:** sent as `git.ns.admin`, which the bridge maps to no role. It is sent rather than left out so that the bridge takes off a stale role it manages.
- **Admin who is also an explicit owner:** still sent as `git.repo.own`.
- **One entry per linked forge account.** Should two subjects ever share an account, it is listed at the lower role and a warning is logged. Uniqueness at link time is being fixed separately.
- **No namespace-level `projectRoles` job.** It is never queued (`enqueue` refuses one), and one already queued is cancelled rather than delivered. A reseat no longer asks for it.

### Job version (`git_ns/bridge.rs`)

- **Every job is 0.4.** `JOB_TYPE` is the 0.4 URI, spelled out by hand until a trust-tasks-rs release carries `job::v0_4`. The acknowledgement is read with `job::v0_3`.
- **Discovery first.** Before sending, the VTC asks the bridge with `trust-task-discovery/0.2` and caches the answer for an hour. The answer is used only if it is a discovery response issued by the bridge's own DID. Old answers (keys `bridgever:<did>`) are not migrated; test instances are recreated anyway.
- **No downgrade.** A bridge that refuses discovery, or does not list 0.4, is sent nothing:
  - In-line jobs (bind, account link, a `roleAdded` revert) fail with "…does not take git-ns/bridge/job 0.4 … upgrade the bridge".
  - Queued jobs stay pending with that message as `last_error`, and go through once the bridge is upgraded.
  - A bridge that listed 0.4 but then refuses it is asked again.
- **New `BridgeClient` methods:** the trait now has `send_job(type_uri, …)` and `discover_jobs`.

### Drift (`git_ns/drift.rs`)

- **Revert of a `roleAdded` item** held by an admin with no right of their own: the admin stays in `desiredRoles` at `git.ns.admin` and is also named in `removeAccounts`, which 0.4 allows. A revert for an account the projection gives a real role is still refused `notRevertible`.
- **Adopt of a `roleChanged` item** still compares against the member's highest *effective* right, as `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.2 step 4 requires. So a namespace admin's forge `admin` role on a repository where they hold `maintain` is not adoptable. Adopting a `roleAdded` item works.

### Reseat (`git_ns/reseat_v0_3.rs`, `git_ns/ops.rs`)

- **0.3 only.** The VTC serves `git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.3 and no longer serves 0.1. There is no compatibility path. 0.3 is wire-identical to 0.2, so its payloads are 0.2's generated types under a hand-written 0.3 type URI until the trust-tasks release (TODO in `reseat_v0_3.rs`; `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK` gains one entry for it, next to job 0.4's).
- **Separation of duties.** Reseating a headless namespace to yourself is a self-grant of `git.ns.admin`, so step 4 refuses it with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`. The check runs before the members-only floor, and the message names `git-ns/right/break-glass`. The subject is compared with the DID the signer resolved to, so a delegated key cannot reseat to its principal. This matches #1745, which adds the same rule for every elevated self-grant. Whichever lands second takes the other's constant.
- **Clients.** `vtc-client`, `cnm git reseat` and the admin console send 0.3. The console will not build a reseat to the signed-in viewer, and `cnm` explains a `selfGrantNotAllowed` refusal.

### UI, CLI, docs

- **Admin console:** the grant and reseat previews no longer say `ns.admin` is projected onto the forge. The repository page says `git.ns.admin` gives no forge role, and that a namespace-level `git.commit.sign` is projected like a repository one.
- **cnm:** the `notRevertible` guidance names job 0.4.
- **Docs:** `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` and the git-ns notes in CLAUDE.md are updated.

## How to test

- `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib git_ns` (139 pass locally after the rebase). The new tests are:
  - **Reseat:**
    - a reseat to the sender is refused `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`, names break-glass, and records nothing
    - reseat 0.3 is served and 0.1 is not
  - **Projection:**
    - an admin with nothing of their own is sent as `ns.admin`
    - an admin who is also an explicit owner is sent as owner
    - namespace `commit.sign` is sent as `commit.sign`
    - an admin whose `own` is revoked, or has lapsed, falls back to `ns.admin`
    - a departed admin is not sent
    - a lapsed admin is not sent
    - one account is listed once, at the lower role
  - **Jobs:**
    - no namespace-level job is sent; a queued one is cancelled; `enqueue` refuses one
    - a bridge before 0.4 is sent nothing, and a revert says "upgrade the bridge"
    - a queued job waits for the upgrade
  - **Drift:**
    - an admin's forge role is reverted, with the admin in both lists
    - a revert is refused for an admin who is also an explicit owner
    - an admin adopts their own `roleAdded` admin role
    - someone else adopts it (an owner is refused, since it is elevated; the community administrator succeeds)
    - an adopt of `roleChanged` is refused, per drift/resolve 0.2
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. The `cnm-cli` guidance test passes. The `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` help is now generic, naming own, repo.create and ns.admin and pointing to `cnm git break-glass`. Its text is identical to #1735's and #1745's. A new check in the reseat test covers a console key acting for an administrator, which cannot reseat to that administrator.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest` and `cargo test -p cnm-cli git::` pass.
- Admin UI: `npx vitest run src/plugins/repos.test.tsx src/plugins/repos/actions.test.ts` (111, including a new test that a reseat to the viewer is not built) and `npm run lint` pass.

## Open questions

- **trust-tasks release.** A release carrying #635 is needed before the hand-written job 0.4 and reseat 0.3 URIs can be swapped for generated types and the two manifest exceptions dropped. Both are marked `TODO(trust-tasks release carrying trust-tasks #635)`.
- **`git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.3.** Should `roleChanged` adoption be measured against the projected right instead of the effective one? That would be a new version.
- **Grant rules unchanged.** Whether a namespace admin may grant themselves `own` is with the user, so no grant rule was changed here.

title: fix(openvtc): sign personhood and capability documents with the authentication key
body:
## What

Sign personhood presentations and capability documents with the persona's authentication key (#key-2) instead of the assertionMethod signing key (#key-1), and carry `proofPurpose: authentication` through consistently.

`openvtc-core/src/personhood.rs`'s `build_presentation` already set `proofPurpose: authentication` on the presentation, but the caller signed it with `keys.signing` (#key-1), which is listed only under `assertionMethod` in the DID document, not `authentication`. Under a strict proof-purpose rule — one that refuses a proof by a key not listed under the relationship it claims — that combination is refused.

Similarly, `openvtc-core/src/capabilities.rs::sign_document` (used for `governance/capability/enable|disable`) signed with `keys.signing` under the Data-Integrity default `proofPurpose: assertionMethod`. Enabling or disabling a capability is acting on the community, not making a claim the issuer stands behind later, so it belongs on the authentication key with `proofPurpose: authentication` too.

Also covers trust-tasks 0.23 (spec #642), which makes `proof` REQUIRED on three more VTC tasks: `vtc/members/personhood/challenge/0.1`, `vtc/vetting/vetters/profile/0.1` and `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1`. Once VTI #1764 is deployed the VTC refuses an unsigned one. All three are the member or vetter acting on their own standing with the community, not a claim to be held to later, so each is signed with the same authentication key and purpose.

### Changes

- `openvtc/src/state_handler/runtime_actions.rs`: the personhood-assert job now signs with `keys.authentication` instead of `keys.signing`; the personhood-challenge job now does too.
- `openvtc/src/state_handler/capability_actions.rs`: the capability-toggle job now signs with `keys.authentication` and calls the new `sign_document_as(..., "authentication")`.
- `openvtc-core/src/capabilities.rs`: added `sign_document_as`, taking an explicit `proofPurpose`; `sign_document` keeps the `assertionMethod` default for every other caller.
- `openvtc-core/src/trust_task_doc.rs`: added `build_signed_value_as`, the same idea for the enclosing Trust Task document; `build_signed_value` keeps its default for join, self-remove, member VMC, git-ns and vetting, which are unchanged.
- `openvtc-core/src/personhood.rs`: `assert_personhood`'s envelope is now built with `build_signed_value_as(..., "authentication")`, matching the key and purpose the presentation inside it already uses; `request_challenge` now signs its document the same way (the now-unused plain `build_document` helper is removed).
- `openvtc-core/src/vetting/wire.rs`: added `sign_as`, the same idea for the vetting wire.
- `openvtc/src/state_handler/vetting_actions.rs`: added `sign_and_send_operational`, which signs with `keys.authentication` instead of `keys.signing`; `publish_profile` (vetter profile) and `ask_resend` (vetter resend) now use it.
- `openvtc/src/state_handler/community_actions.rs`: `Verb::RequestPersonhoodChallenge` now carries a `signing_secret`.

Pairs with OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1752 (VTI-KEY-022) and OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1764.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --lib personhood::`, `trust_task_doc::`, `capabilities::`, `vetting::` pass, including new tests pinning the proof purpose each helper produces.
- `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc capability_actions::`, `runtime_actions::`, `community_actions::` and `vetting_actions::` pass.
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc-core -p openvtc --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
