title: feat(vgi-bridge): work off the VTC's VTA (VTA mode)
body:
Design §5.7, "The bridge works off the VTC's VTA (decided 2026-09-25)".

## What changes

A new **VTA mode** (`[vta]` in the config). The bridge's identity, secrets and state live in its own trust context of the VTC's VTA. The bridge host holds only a context-scoped `did:key` credential, which can be revoked and re-issued.

| What | Where in VTA mode |
|---|---|
| The bridge's `did:webvh` and its keys | In the context. Fetched into memory (one `contexts/secrets` call). Never written to disk or logs. Which keys are held is decided by the DID's current document (see *Key rotation*). |
| GitHub App credentials, webhook secrets, Forgejo tokens | In the context's `vta/app-state` (namespace `vgi-bridge`), **sealed** with AES-256-GCM, each bound to its name. The sealing key is derived by HKDF from a dedicated context key (`vgi-bridge/app-state-seal`), and only an admin of the context can export that key. The seal exists because app-state is documented as "not for secrets". On the host these values are held in memory only, never in the redb file. |
| Namespaces (binding, installation, capabilities, managed set, pin), repository records, the Dependabot provenance ledger, bookkeeping | Mirrored to app-state, one record each, with conditional (versioned) writes. The local redb store becomes a cache, so a new host with a new credential rebuilds fully. |
| Job ledger, outbox, pending flows, webhook delivery ids, device-flow codes | Local only. The VTC repeats unfinished jobs, and jobs are convergent. |

The bridge keeps signing as itself: its own key signs its proofs, job results and Dependabot re-signs. Nothing it signs claims the VTC's authority.

**Transport.** The bridge reaches the VTA over **DIDComm only**, through `vta.mediator_did` (default: the bridge's own `mediator_did`). This is required because the VTA releases private keys only over an end-to-end channel (VTI #1733).

**Durability and failure handling**
- Results and events go to the VTC only once the state they report is written to the VTA. Until then they are held in the outbox and sent again later.
- A rotated Forgejo token retires its predecessor only after the new token is persisted.
- The App registration page says so if the App's credentials could not be persisted yet.
- An unreachable VTA is retried with capped backoff, at start-up (`start_timeout_secs`) and for writes. A refusal is not retried.
- **A second writer fails closed.** If a conditional write finds a version this host did not write, the mirror stops writing, results are held, the reason is logged, and `/healthz` answers 503.

**Key rotation**
- The bridge's **current DID document** decides which keys it holds: every `assertionMethod` and `keyAgreement` key the document lists, with a matching public key, and nothing else.
- Private halves come from the VTA. A key the VTA no longer releases but the document still lists stays in memory.
- **Which key signs:**
  - The bridge records when it first sees each signing key listed in its document. The record is mirrored to the VTA, so a restart or a new host keeps it.
  - It keeps signing with the **oldest** listed key it may use until a newer one has been listed for `vta.signing_switch_after_secs` (default 86400, the proposed 24 h verifier cache cap; must be ≥ `did_cache_ttl_secs`), then switches to the newest. The refresh re-evaluates this when the switch comes due, even if nothing else changed.
  - If the older key stops being listed first, its successor signs at once.
  - Only a key the VTA still releases signs.
  - TODO (VTI #638): switch at `activatesAt` once the VTA exposes key-role states.
- Through a rotation the bridge holds old and new keys for the whole overlap, so a job encrypted to either opens. It drops a key only when the document stops listing it; there is no grace timer.
- Every `key_refresh_secs` (default 60) the bridge compares the VTA's key list with the freshly resolved document (public halves only). It re-exports only on a change; `SIGHUP` forces a check. DIDComm reconnects whenever the held keys change.
- A key whose id the document lists with another public key is not used. A context that names a different DID is refused.

**DID caches**
- `did_cache_ttl_secs` (default 60, range 10–3600) bounds how long the bridge caches the VTC's document, the registry's document and endpoint, and commit signers' documents.
- A job proof that fails against a cached document is checked once more after evicting that DID. The same applies to a commit reported as `UnknownKey` or `UnresolvedSigner`. If the second check fails, it is refused (fail closed).
- verify-trust gains `build_resolver_with_cache_ttl`, an additive function.

**CLI**
- `vgi-bridge vta setup` checks the context, its DID, the keys the document lists and that they export, the sealing key (created if missing), app-state write/read/delete, and that the credential sees no other context. It prints the DID.
- `secret set` / `secret list` work against app-state.
- `identity import`, `export` and `mint` are refused in VTA mode.
- `identity show` prints the context's DID without exporting keys.

The self-contained modes (sealed store, `did:peer`, imported bundle) are unchanged.

## Breaking changes
- A config with `[vta]` **and** `master_key_file` / `master_key_env` is refused.
- VTA mode refuses a `data_dir` holding a self-contained store, or the cache of another context or DID. It starts from an empty data directory; there is no migration from self-contained mode (test deployments are recreated).
- VTA mode never uses REST to the VTA.
- Both modes now use a 60 s DID-document cache instead of the resolver's implicit 300 s.
- `vgi_bridge::run` takes `Keys`, `Bridge::identity` is a method, and `Store` gains a VTA-mirror mode.

## Dependencies on VTI
- **Credential scope.** Exporting a key needs `key-export`, which only `admin` derives, so the credential is an **admin scoped to the bridge's context**.
  - Every key, sign and app-state operation checks the target's own context. The credential therefore cannot read, sign with or list the VTC's keys, any other context's keys, or unscoped keys.
  - `update_acl` currently has no self-check, so a narrowed context admin could widen its own entry. **A separate VTI change fixes this; the least-privilege claim for this credential depends on it.**
- **VTI #1733** (draft) refuses key export over REST/HTTPS. This PR already uses DIDComm only.
- **VTC-side DID caching** (read-only finding): vtc-service uses two resolver caches, both at 300 s with no eviction on failure.
  - After the bridge's document changes, the VTC may keep encrypting to the old X25519 key for up to about 5 minutes. The bridge still holds that key while the document lists it, so those jobs open.
  - The VTC may refuse results signed with the new key for up to about 5 minutes after the switch. The outbox resends them.
  - No VTI change was made here.

## Tests
- `appstate`:
  - round trip, and a new host rebuilding from the VTA;
  - secrets never reach the redb file and leave the host sealed;
  - an unreachable VTA keeps changes pending;
  - a second writer stops the mirror.
- `vta`, against a scripted VTA behind vta-sdk's `test-loopback` transport:
  - credentials and the URL rule;
  - identity from the context and its document;
  - a missing `key-export` gets an actionable error;
  - app-state versions and conflicts;
  - a new host rebuilds;
  - `vta setup`, including the other-context warning;
  - cache binding;
  - **rotation, step by step:**
    - successor keys not yet listed are not held;
    - during the overlap all four keys are held, and the old key keeps signing until the new one has been listed for the horizon (checked one second short and at the horizon), then the new one signs;
    - old keys the VTA stopped releasing stay held while listed;
    - old keys are dropped once unlisted;
    - jobs flow throughout;
    - a mismatched public key, and a switch to another DID, are refused.
- `wire`: re-resolve once, then fail closed.
- `tests/vta_mode.rs`:
  - state and secrets land in app-state, and the job ledger and identity do not;
  - a new host on an empty store serves the namespace with its App back;
  - results are held while the VTA is down.
- `config`: `[vta]` validation and the DIDComm default.


## Security review follow-ups (3b70950)
- **The VTA is the authority on restart (medium).** Each host records the version it mirrored each record at, in a local-only `mirror` table.
  - On pull, the change feed is read with tombstones.
  - A record this host mirrored that the VTA no longer holds (tombstoned, or already reaped) is **dropped locally**, never written back. A stale host therefore cannot resurrect what a recovery host deleted.
  - Only records never mirrored are pushed, and a tombstoned key's never-mirrored local copy is dropped.
  - A remote version older than the one mirrored (rolled back or replayed) **fails closed**.
- **Secrets are sealed to their record version.** The AAD is the name plus the version the write is predicted to take, and the prediction is checked on the write. A replayed older ciphertext no longer opens, and the start is refused.
- **No fallback signing key.** Only a listed signing key the VTA still releases signs; otherwise the bridge refuses.
- **Re-resolve limit.** Evict-and-re-resolve after a failed proof, or a commit with an unknown key, runs at most once per DID per 30 s.
- **One sealing key.** More than one active key under the sealing label is refused.
- **Tests:**
  - `a_removed_record_is_not_resurrected_by_a_stale_host`, with the tombstone retained and after it is reaped;
  - `a_rolled_back_remote_is_refused`;
  - `a_replayed_secret_does_not_open`;
  - `a_signing_key_the_vta_withdrew_is_never_used`;
  - `a_second_sealing_key_is_refused`;
  - the once-per-DID limit in `wire`.


## Follow-up (5fb5a20): the signing key switches at the verifier cache horizon
The bridge keeps signing with the oldest listed key until a newer one has been listed for `vta.signing_switch_after_secs` (default 24 h), or until the older one is unlisted. The first-listed times are kept in the mirrored state. Tests:
- `the_signing_key_moves_on_at_the_horizon_or_when_the_old_one_is_unlisted`;
- the rotation walk: still signing with the old key one second short of the horizon, and the new key after it;
- config validation (the horizon must be ≥ the DID cache lifetime).

## Re-review follow-ups (e6047c5)
- **Rollback to a snapshot from before a record existed (medium).** Pull now fails closed (conflict, 503, nothing written) when the VTA's namespace counter is behind the highest version this host mirrored, or when a mirrored key is missing above it. A record that is missing because of a rollback is no longer taken for deleted. Test: ns_1@v1 and ns_2@v2 mirrored, the remote restored to ns_1 at watermark 1 → refused, and ns_2 is kept.
- **One writer at a time (low).** Deletions pass their tombstone's version on, so the next sealed write predicts its version correctly.
  - Every writer of the bridge's app-state takes a short lease record (`lease/writer`, 2 min, renewed while held) before writing: the mirror for each pass, `secret set`, and `vta setup`'s probe.
  - With the lease, a secret is sealed once to the version it lands at and is never left live and unopenable.
  - A stray write that ignores the lease is sealed over again before `put_sealed` returns.
  - The mirror takes the lease before it takes its batch, so a pass abandoned while waiting loses nothing.
- **Tests:**
  - the rollback probe;
  - a secret written after a deletion is sealed once;
  - writers take turns under the lease and every secret opens;
  - a stray write is resealed;
  - an abandoned lease expires.


## Hardening follow-ups (5f1c9c8)
- **The lease is bounded by the VTA's clock, not the holder's.** A lease's expiry is the holder's `until` capped at the VTA's own `updatedAt` for that write plus the TTL (a record without it is taken as expired). A writer with a wrong clock, or one that writes a far-off `until` on purpose, holds the lease for at most one TTL after its last write. The holder times its own lease on the monotonic clock from before the write was sent, never renews one that has run out, and renews before each sealed-secret attempt.
- **A rollback the counter has moved past is refused.** A `Listing` now says whether it is the change feed from the start (every deletion present as a tombstone) or a snapshot (the VTA answered `watermarkTooOld`). From the feed, a record this host mirrored that has no record at all, not even a tombstone, was lost, not deleted. The start is refused even when the counter has since moved past the restore point. Only a snapshot takes such a record for deleted.
- **Requests end well inside the lease.** Every app-state request is abandoned after 20 s. A compile-time check keeps that at most a third of half the TTL, so no write is still being waited on once its lease could have run out.
- **A refused state fails the start at once.** Rollback, replay and a secret that does not open raise a typed `StateRefused` error, which start-up's retry loop does not retry.
- **`/healthz` reports a stall.** It answers 503 once changes have waited 5 minutes (more than two leases) with every pass failing, whether the VTA is away or another writer is keeping the lease. The body says how many changes are waiting. Until now it answered `ok` while nothing reached the VTA.
- **Tests:**
  - `a_lease_lasts_one_ttl_past_the_vtas_time_whatever_its_holder_claims`;
  - `a_rollback_the_counter_has_moved_past_is_refused_from_the_feed` (refused from the feed with the cached record kept; taken for deleted from a snapshot);
  - `a_refused_state_is_not_retried_at_start`;
  - `changes_that_stop_reaching_the_vta_fail_health`;
  - `a_request_fits_well_inside_half_a_lease`.
- BRIDGE.md §2a/§7 and the RUNBOOK troubleshooting table are updated to match.

title: trust-tasks-proof-v0.23.0
body:
### Security

- **proof**: Check a proof's verificationMethod against its proofPurpose ([#637](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/637))

* security(proof)!: check a proof's verificationMethod against its proofPurpose

  The stock Verifier accepted a proof signed by any key listed under the
  issuer's authentication or assertionMethod, whatever proofPurpose the proof
  declared. It did not check that the verification method's controller was the
  issuer. W3C Data Integrity requires both, through Controlled Identifiers
  v1.0 §3.3.

  - New ProofPurpose type (assertionMethod, authentication,
    capabilityInvocation, capabilityDelegation). Parsing refuses keyAgreement
    and unknown values.
  - New ProofPurposeResolver trait resolves a verificationMethod for one
    purpose. CachedDidResolver implements it. It requires the resolved
    document's id and the method's controller to be the DID that names the
    method. It requires the method to be listed under the relationship the
    purpose names, by absolute DID URL, by a fragment relative to the
    document id, or embedded. DidKeyResolver implements it with did:key's
    implicit relationships: the key named `did:key:<id>#<id>` signs for all
    four purposes, and an X25519 did:key signs for none.
  - Verifier resolves through a ProofPurposeResolver, so every proof is
    checked against its own purpose.
  - New PurposeBound wraps a ProofPurposeResolver as an upstream
    VerificationMethodResolver bound to one proof's purpose. It is for
    callers of DataIntegrityProof::verify.
  - sign_trust_task and ProofExt::sign default to proofPurpose authentication.
    They refuse a purpose that names no signing relationship.
  - Resolver errors name the rule that failed. They carry no DID, document or
    key material.

### Fixed

- **didcomm**: Require affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.9, which binds the authcrypt sender to its key ([#644](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/644))

affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.15.9 resolves an authcrypt sender only from
  the `skid` the envelope names and refuses a JWE whose `apu` disagrees
  with it, or whose `skid` names no key. Requiring it means the sender this
  binding hands to §4.8.1 is always the key that opened the ECDH-1PU wrap.

  - `affinidi-messaging-didcomm` 0.15 -> 0.15.9 (floor).
  - `DidcommError::into_reject_reason`: the library's sender/signer key
    binding refusals (`SenderKeyBinding`, `SignerKeyBinding`) map to
    `ProofRequired`, like this binding's own sender checks.
  - tests/fail_closed.rs: a fragment-less `skid` is now refused by the
    library first; either refusal is accepted.
  - tests/interop.rs: the Go-produced JWE decrypts through `decrypt_bound`
    with the fixture's sender key id (the key-only `decrypt` is deprecated
    and refuses authcrypt when given a key).
  - pack.rs: the comment on the ignored `UnpackResult` fields no longer
    describes the removed pre-0.14 KEK fallback.
  - dev-dependencies move to the 0.27 SDK line the crate is built against
    (affinidi-tdk 0.17, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.2,
    affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.10.2).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.23.0
body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: Separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass ([#641](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/641))

* feat(git-ns): separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass

  An elevated git right (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create, git.repo.own) is now
  always granted by someone other than its recipient, and the one way to give
  oneself one is an explicit, justified, highly visible break-glass that another
  administrator ratifies or revokes.

  - git-ns/right/grant 0.3: fixed rule 7, separation of duties, refused with
    git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. It binds every task that records a right on the
    actor's own authority (drift/resolve adopt, repo/adopt, namespace/reseat);
    bind and repo/create are not self-grants. Rules 3 and 4 count only records
    with no expiry that are not unratified break-glass.
  - git-ns/right/break-glass 0.1 (new): self-grant of an elevated right the
    actor may already grant, or git.ns.admin on a headless namespace for a
    community administrator. Mandatory justification, destructive, immediate,
    no expiry, highest-severity audit, notice to every administrator, visible
    until ratified or revoked. Policy may disable, delay or tighten it, never
    quieten it.
  - git-ns/right/ratify 0.1 (new): another administrator clears the flag,
    bound to the breakGlass.at they read.
  - git-ns/right/break-glass-notice 0.1 (new): the VTC's signed push to every
    community administrator and namespace admin, for break-glass, ratified and
    revoked.
  - git-ns/right/revoke 0.3: any community administrator may revoke an
    unratified break-glass record; policy cannot refuse that.
  - git-ns/view 0.4: unratified break-glass records go to every administrator
    they concern, whatever else the caller may see.
  - git-ns/_shared 0.4: BreakGlass, RightRecord.breakGlass, ElevatedRight.

  Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

- **git-ns**: Drift/resolve 0.3 binds an adoption to the member it names ([#640](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/640))

* feat(git-ns): drift/resolve 0.3 binds an adoption to the member it names

  A drift/resolve 0.2 adoption did not name who receives the right. The VTC
  resolved the item's forge account to whoever had linked it when the task
  ran, so an account unlinked and linked again, to someone else, between the
  resolver reading the item and signing granted a right, published to the
  Trust Registry, to a member the resolver never saw. The signed document
  said nothing otherwise: observed bounded which role an adoption records,
  nothing bounded to whom.

  drift/resolve 0.3 adds `subject`, the DID of the member the resolver read
  as linked to the account. It is required for adopt and absent for revert,
  refused as malformedRequest otherwise (as a missing `observed` is, and
  likewise stated in prose rather than a schema conditional). The VTC adopts
  only while the account is still linked to exactly that member, re-checked
  under the same exclusion as the write that records the right, and refuses
  otherwise with the new git-ns/drift/resolve:subjectChanged.

  Versioning. A 0.2 document is a 0.3 document with no `subject`: still a
  valid revert, now a malformed adopt. Required-for-one-action is not
  backwards-compatible, so this is a MINOR increment under the draft
  allowance of SPEC 5.2. A VTC serving older versions SHOULD NOT accept a
  0.1 or 0.2 adopt, since it cannot know whom that resolver meant, and SHOULD
  refuse one naming 0.3.

  git-ns/view still returns a member only their own account links, so a
  client that has only git-ns/view cannot adopt another member's role; the
  spec says so. Invalid examples cover a DID URL, shell metacharacters and a
  list as `subject`.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

- **git-ns**: Re-project roles on demand, and the bridge reports its role map ([#639](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/639))

* feat(git-ns): re-project roles on demand, and the bridge reports its role map

  A bridge's role map (which forge role own, maintain and commit.sign get)
  is the community's to configure per bridge, forge, namespace and
  repository, but nothing told the VTC what map was in force, and a
  change reached a repository only at its next unrelated projection.

  - git-ns/bridge/event 0.3: a new event type, roleMapReported. The bridge
    reports, per namespace, its role map as the forge applies it (rounded
    onto the forge's ladder: `none` < `read` < `triage` < `write` <
    `maintain` < `admin`), each repository whose map differs (`repos`), and
    each repository whose roles it last projected under a different map
    (`stale`). Sent at start-up, on a map change and after bindCompleted.
    The map has no member for git.ns.admin: a namespace admin projects to
    no forge role whatever the configuration. The VTC refuses an unordered
    map, confines `repos` and `stale` to the namespace, uses the map
    wherever it shows or derives a forge role, and SHOULD re-project each
    stale repository. Everything else is restated unchanged from 0.2; the
    schema pins _shared/0.3, wire-identical for every event shape.

  - git-ns/roles/reproject 0.1 (new): a community administrator, or a
    namespace admin by explicit record, has the VTC send the complete
    desiredRoles of one repository, or of every active or orphaned
    repository in a namespace, again. No right changes and nothing is
    published; the audit record says who asked and why. Refused in manual
    mode (manualMode) and while the bridge has no access (noForgeAccess).

  - git-ns/drift/resolve 0.2 (draft, in place): the projected right of a
    role is the lowest right whose role in the bridge's reported map is
    that role; the default map without a report.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

- **vta/webvh/dids/keys**: Named key roles and per-role rotation for a VTA's DIDs ([#638](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/638))

* feat(vta/webvh/dids/keys): named key roles and per-role rotation for a VTA's DIDs

  Adds the Trust Tasks every client uses to manage the key roles of the
  did:webvh identities a VTA holds keys for (its own, and those of the
  VTCs and VTNs provisioned on it), aligned with the VTI key-roles draft
  (dtgwg-vti-spec#42): attestation, operational, messaging and update.

- **git-ns/account/unlink**: A member unlinks their own forge account ([#636](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/636))

* feat(git-ns/account/unlink): a member unlinks their own forge account

  git-ns/account/link said a binding lasts "until the member unlinks or
  leaves", but no task unlinked: the only way to drop an account was to
  link another on the same forge, or to leave the community.

- **git-ns**: Bridge/job 0.4 and namespace/reseat 0.3, a namespace admin gets no forge role ([#635](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/635))

* feat(git-ns): bridge/job 0.4 and namespace/reseat 0.3 — a namespace admin gets no forge role

  A namespace admin exercises git.ns.admin through the VTC and its bridge,
  never through a forge role: the bridge does not make them an owner of the
  organisation and gives them no role on any repository for it.

  git-ns/bridge/job 0.4:
  - desiredRoles carries, per person, the highest right recorded in their
    own name on the repository (own, maintain or commit.sign there, or
    commit.sign on the namespace), never one held only because git.ns.admin
    implies it. A namespace admin with none is listed at git.ns.admin, which
    every adapter maps to no role, so the bridge takes off a role it manages
    that they still hold. An admin who is also a recorded owner is listed as
    the owner.
  - Each forge account appears in desiredRoles at most once.
  - repo is required for projectRoles: the namespace-level job, which only
    ever projected git.ns.admin as organisation owners, no longer exists.
  - removeAccounts may name an account listed at git.ns.admin.
  - A VTC must not send 0.4 to a bridge that has not shown it takes 0.4, and
    should read an unsupportedType or unsupportedVersion refusal as the
    bridge taking only earlier versions.

  git-ns/namespace/reseat 0.3: step 8 no longer queues a namespace-level
  forge projection. Wire-identical to 0.2.

  Earlier versions are unchanged. Both are draft, so the breaking changes
  ship as MINOR increments under the draft allowance of SPEC 5.2.



### Security

- **didcomm**: A consumer may require a proof over DIDComm ([#642](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/642))

The DIDComm binding lets a producer omit `proof` because the envelope
  authenticates the sender. A consumer that authorizes on the sender's identity
  now MAY decline that allowance and require an in-band proof on every document
  it accepts over the binding, rejecting a document without one as
  `proofRequired` and one whose proof does not identify the transport sender as
  `identityMismatch`. A producer SHOULD include a proof on every document it
  sends over DIDComm so it is accepted either way.

  The tasks whose consumer authorizes or answers on the caller's identity alone
  now declare `proof` REQUIRED, so the identity rests on the document on every
  transport:

  - vtc/vetting/vetters/profile/0.1
  - vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1
  - vtc/members/personhood/challenge/0.1
  - git-ns/view/0.1, 0.2 and 0.3
  - git-ns/account/link-status/0.1

  All are drafts, edited in place. Bindings regenerated for Rust, TS, Go and
  Dart.

- **proof**: Check a proof's verificationMethod against its proofPurpose ([#637](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/637))

* security(proof)!: check a proof's verificationMethod against its proofPurpose

  The stock Verifier accepted a proof signed by any key listed under the
  issuer's authentication or assertionMethod, whatever proofPurpose the proof
  declared. It did not check that the verification method's controller was the
  issuer. W3C Data Integrity requires both, through Controlled Identifiers
  v1.0 §3.3.

  - New ProofPurpose type (assertionMethod, authentication,
    capabilityInvocation, capabilityDelegation). Parsing refuses keyAgreement
    and unknown values.
  - New ProofPurposeResolver trait resolves a verificationMethod for one
    purpose. CachedDidResolver implements it. It requires the resolved
    document's id and the method's controller to be the DID that names the
    method. It requires the method to be listed under the relationship the
    purpose names, by absolute DID URL, by a fragment relative to the
    document id, or embedded. DidKeyResolver implements it with did:key's
    implicit relationships: the key named `did:key:<id>#<id>` signs for all
    four purposes, and an X25519 did:key signs for none.
  - Verifier resolves through a ProofPurposeResolver, so every proof is
    checked against its own purpose.
  - New PurposeBound wraps a ProofPurposeResolver as an upstream
    VerificationMethodResolver bound to one proof's purpose. It is for
    callers of DataIntegrityProof::verify.
  - sign_trust_task and ProofExt::sign default to proofPurpose authentication.
    They refuse a purpose that names no signing relationship.
  - Resolver errors name the rule that failed. They carry no DID, document or
    key material.



### Specifications

- **device**: Register the keyExport capability ([#643](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/643))

keys/export-secret/0.1 authorizes against "standing over the key's
  scope" and leaves the grant's shape to the implementation. Where it is a
  device capability there should be a registered value, as there is for
  roomPresent and roomOpen, so implementations do not each carry a private
  one. The VTA already gates export on it.

  keyExport (key-export in the 0.1 casing) is deliberately separate from
  sign: a producer that may ask the custodian to use a key loses that the
  moment its entitlement changes, while a producer that took the key keeps
  it after its authority is withdrawn. export-secret now names the value
  and says a sign grant is not a keyExport grant. The value is additive,
  so a consumer that does not recognise it ignores it.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); no version bumps.

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.3.0`) | `0.2.8` → `0.3.0` | breaking |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.8` → `0.3.0` | breaking |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(messaging/message/status): let a sender confirm on evidence that its message was collected
body:
A sender's only signal that a message arrived is seeing it in its send
queue (`messaging/message/list`) and later seeing it gone. That signal is
wrong in both directions.

- A recipient connected live collects within milliseconds, before any poll
  has seen the message queued, so a collected message leaves no evidence
  at all.
- A message leaves the send queue the same way whether the recipient took
  it, the mediator expired it, or its account was removed.

A sender that retries on missing evidence re-sends collected messages. One
that treats absence as delivery records lost messages as delivered.

`messaging/message/status/0.1` answers, per message the requester sent:
`queued`, `delivered` (handed over, not yet acknowledged), `collected`,
`withdrawn`, `discarded` or `unknown`. A conforming mediator records, when
a message whose sender it knows leaves the queue, a short-lived receipt
keyed under that sender, and the reason comes from who removed the
message. The mediator answers only for the requester's own sending and
says `unknown` for everything else, so the task cannot be used to probe
for other accounts' messages.

Driven by affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#896, where the delivery layer re-sends
messages its recipients already collected.

`npm run build` validates, and all four bindings are regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: spec(auth/step-up): approve-response 0.5, every response carries the approver's assertionMethod proof
body:
Adds `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.5`. Every approve-response now carries the approver's `assertionMethod` proof. Passkey (webauthn) evidence is checked in addition to that proof, never instead of it.

Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1757. That PR already enforces this rule in the VTA and the VTC against 0.4. This version makes the spec say the same thing.

## Why

In 0.4 a `webauthn` response MAY omit the framework `proof`. But the document is the approver's statement of a decision. A WebAuthn assertion signs the challenge, not the document around it. So anyone holding a captured assertion could wrap it in a document of their own and pick its `decision`, `grantedAcr` and `subject`.

## What changes from 0.4

- **`proofRequirement: REQUIRED`.** Every response carries a proof with these properties, whatever evidence it attaches:
  - it is made for `assertionMethod`;
  - its key is listed under the signer's `assertionMethod` relationship;
  - the signer's DID is the `issuer`.
- **The signer is the approver.** That is the subject in self step-up, and the delegated approver in delegated step-up. When the approver signs through a console key that the relying party's own state records as acting for an administrator, the approver is that administrator. In self step-up the approver must be `payload.subject` (`subjectMismatch` otherwise).
- **Passkey evidence is in addition.** A `webauthn` assertion is still checked in full (WebAuthn L2 §7.2). The approver its credential resolves to must be the same approver the proof established.
- **Order.** The consumer checks the proof and ties the signer to the approver before it looks up the pending step-up. A refused document does not use up the step-up, so no other party can spend an approver's challenge.
- **Error codes.** A missing proof is `proofRequired` and an invalid one is `proofInvalid` (SPEC §8.3). `noGate` now covers only an evidence kind the relying party does not recognise or did not offer.
- **Examples.** Every example is signed for `assertionMethod`, including the two webauthn examples.

Nothing else changes: the payload schema is the same as 0.4 apart from the version in its URIs.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: 522 specs valid.
- Bindings regenerated for Rust (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen`, `cargo fmt --all`), TypeScript, Go and Dart.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree; 1087 error codes match.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --lib approve_response::v0_5`: 3 passed.

title: spec(vta/attestation): mnemonic-export/1.0, sealed, end-to-end or signed at first boot
body:
Adds `spec/vta/attestation/mnemonic-export/1.0`. A TEE agent releases its seed mnemonic once, inside the first-boot export window. The mnemonic is sealed to a key only the requester holds, under an attestation-bound producer assertion.

- **Channel.** A normative section defines the only two paths the task may use. Any other path is refused with `permissionDenied`. The refusal comes after the entitlement check and before the entropy is read, so a refused request does not spend the release.
  - **End-to-end path.** DIDComm authcrypt or TSP. `clientDid` is an ephemeral key made for this one export.
  - **Signed first-boot path.** A freshly booted agent may have no DIDComm or TSP endpoint yet, and the export window is short. So the task is also allowed over a hop-by-hop channel, HTTPS included, when **all** of these hold:
    - the producer is entitled;
    - the proof verifies as `issuer`, for `authentication`, and `issuer` is the DID the session authenticated;
    - `clientDid` is **exactly** `issuer`;
    - `recipient` names the agent;
    - `issuedAt` is fresh, and the `id` is new and recorded before the agent acts. A duplicate is never answered with the bundle.
  - **Threat model.** The first-boot path is designed against a TLS terminator that holds the bearer token. That terminator cannot sign as the producer, cannot change `clientDid`, and cannot redirect or replay the request. It can still see and keep the sealed answer. So on this path the producer signs with a `did:key` kept for this purpose, and retires that key once the words are written down.
  - Over a hop-by-hop channel, a `clientDid` that differs from the signer is refused, and so is an unsigned request.
- **Proof on both paths.** The request carries an `authentication` proof bound to `issuer`, as the front matter's `proofRequirement: REQUIRED` already said.
- **Authorization.** The caller needs custody of the agent, and must also be entitled to export key material.
- **Processing order.** Seal, then record durably, then wipe. A failure before the wipe leaves the release available inside the window. The duplicate-execution record keeps the document's `id` and digest, never the response.
- **Bindings** regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

Implemented in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1743. Until this is released in trust-tasks-rs, the VTA lists the URI in its unspecced-dispatch debt.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: 522 specs valid.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --lib mnemonic_export`: 4 passed, covering both request examples, the response example and the invalid examples.

body:
spec(vta/attestation): mnemonic-export/1.0, sealed, end-to-end or signed at first boot (#649)

* spec(vta/attestation): mnemonic-export/1.0, sealed and end-to-end only

A TEE agent's one-time first-boot release of its BIP-39 seed mnemonic, for
an offline paper backup. The answer is sealed to the requester's ephemeral
did:key under an attestation-bound producer assertion, and the task MUST
travel over an end-to-end confidential channel (DIDComm authcrypt or TSP):
over HTTPS it is refused with permissionDenied, after entitlement and before
the entropy is read, so a refused request does not spend the release. The
processing order keeps a failed seal or audit write from losing the root.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vta/attestation): a signed first-boot path for mnemonic-export over HTTPS

A freshly booted TEE agent may have no DIDComm or TSP endpoint yet, and the
export window is short, so an end-to-end-only export could lose the only
chance to take the backup. The Channel section now defines two paths.

- End-to-end path: DIDComm authcrypt or TSP, clientDid an ephemeral key, as
  before.
- Signed first-boot path: allowed over a hop-by-hop channel, HTTPS included,
  only when all of these hold:
  - the producer is entitled;
  - the request's proof verifies as issuer, for authentication, and issuer is
    the DID the session authenticated;
  - clientDid is exactly issuer;
  - recipient names the agent;
  - issuedAt is fresh, and the id is new and recorded before the agent acts.
    A duplicate is never answered with the bundle.
- A TLS terminator holding the bearer token cannot sign as the producer,
  change clientDid, redirect the request or replay it. It can see and keep
  the sealed answer, so on this path the producer signs with a did:key kept
  for the purpose and retires it once the words are written down.
- Anything else over a hop-by-hop channel is refused with permissionDenied,
  including a clientDid that differs from the signer.
- Both paths require the request's authentication proof, bound to issuer.
- The agent's duplicate-execution record keeps the id and digest, never the
  response.
- Request examples are signed, with a new first-boot example.

title: fix(vta-service)!: apply the key-export and sign capability checks on every transport
body:
## Summary

This change applies the `key-export` capability check on every transport. It also applies the `sign` capability check to the generic signing oracle. Both checks move into the operation layer, so a transport added later cannot skip them.

Before this change:

- `keys/export-secret` checked `KeyExport` in its Trust-Task handler only. `GET /keys/{id}/secret` and DIDComm `get-key-secret` call the same `operations::keys::get_key_secret`, but checked only the admin role. An admin whose ACL entry had been narrowed without `key-export` could still export a private key over those two transports.
- `Capability::Sign` was not checked anywhere. `keys/sign`, `POST /keys/{id}/sign`, DIDComm `sign-request` and `keys/derive-and-sign(-document)` checked only the role, so a narrowing that removed `sign` had no effect.

## Changes

### Export (VTI-VTA-003, `keys/export-secret/0.1`)

- `get_key_secret` now does all of the following, in the order the spec sets (entitlement, then the refusals, then the response):
  - `ensure_may_export` (the `KeyExport` capability, read from the caller's ACL entry) runs before the key is looked up. A store error refuses the request.
  - A hop-by-hop channel is refused. The caller now states an `ExportChannel`: `EndToEnd`, `Sealed`, `Local` or `HopByHop`. `keys/export-secret/0.1` requires the exchange to be "carried over a channel confidential to the two parties". Over REST or HTTPS the plaintext key would exist wherever TLS terminates. This is the same reasoning `keys/import` already uses for its cleartext carrier.
  - Scope, internal-key and non-exportable refusals are unchanged.
  - The `key.secret_export` audit row is written with `audit::record` **before** the material is returned. If the write fails, the export is refused. The row names the actor, the key id, the context and the transport, and never the material.
- The Trust-Task binding is now recorded at the three entry points: HTTPS, DIDComm and TSP. The export's audit `channel` reads `trust-task/https`, `trust-task/didcomm` or `trust-task/tsp`.
- `vta/contexts/secrets` uses the same gate (`ensure_may_export` moved from `export.rs` into `keys.rs`) and the same channel rule.
- Provisioning (`provision-integration`) delivers keys derived from the seed to the holder. That is an export, so it now requires `key-export` in its preconditions, before anything is minted. This covers the `did:key` branch as well as the webvh read-back, which now goes through `get_key_secret` with `ExportChannel::Sealed`.
- The trust-task handler no longer carries its own capability check. The check is in the operation now.
- `POST /attestation/mnemonic` (TEE) now requires `key-export`. It also writes a durable `seed.mnemonic_export` row before the entropy is released, and refuses if the write fails. Sealed delivery, and zeroing the entropy only after the bundle and its row exist, are in #1743.

### Backup export (VTI-VTA-003)

A backup carries the seed, so it is an export of every key the VTA holds.

- `export_backup` requires `key-export`, read from the caller's ACL entry, in addition to super-admin. Every backup path calls it: REST, DIDComm, and both `initiate-export` versions.
- The `backup.export` and `backup.initiate-export` rows are written durably **before** the envelope or descriptor is returned. If the write fails, the export is refused and the staged bundle is aborted.
- **Never hop-by-hop.** The bundle is sealed with the password the request carries. Over REST or HTTPS, that password exists in plaintext wherever TLS terminates, next to the bundle it opens. So `POST /backup/export` always answers 403, and `vta/backup/initiate-export` is refused over the HTTPS binding. DIDComm (`backup-export`) and `initiate-export` over DIDComm or TSP still work. Fetching the ciphertext afterwards (`GET /backup/blob/{id}` or `get-chunk`) is unaffected.
- **Import the same way.** `POST /backup/import` always answers 403. `initiate-import` and `finalize-import` (1.0 and 1.1) are refused over the HTTPS binding, after the super-admin check and before a slot is minted or the password is used. `finalize-import` carries the password. `initiate-import` returns a bearer credential for writing into the agent. DIDComm `backup-import` and the import tasks over DIDComm or TSP still work.
- **Spec:** trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646 adds this Channel requirement to `initiate-export`, `initiate-import` and `finalize-import`, 1.0 and 1.1.

### Scope before existence

`keys/export-secret` and `keys/sign` check the caller's scope before they say whether a key exists (`load_record_in_caller_scope`). An out-of-scope caller gets the same refusal for a key in another context and for a key that does not exist. The refusal names neither the key's context nor whether the key exists. Only a super-admin is told that a key is absent.

### Revoked keys

`get_key_secret` and `get_key_secret_internal` refuse a revoked record. A retired key, or a rotation's staging record, is kept for history and is not released or loaded.

### Signing (VTI-VTA-003 "the capability to use the key", VTI-VTA-007)

- `sign_payload` requires `Capability::Sign` for `SigningDomain::Opaque` (caller-supplied bytes), before any lookup.
- `ProtocolDefined` input is built inside the VTA by an operation that has already applied its own constrained capability, for example `credential-write` for a room's credentials. It does not require `sign`, because VTI-VTA-007 says a constrained grant must not need or confer the general one.
- `derive_and_sign` and `derive_and_sign_document` require `sign`.

### Policy gate on the legacy surfaces

`POST /keys/{id}/sign`, `POST /keys/derive-and-sign(-document)` and DIDComm `get-key-secret` / `sign-request` now call the PDP gate (`rest_gate`) with the Trust-Task URI and a payload of the same shape. Before this, a policy rule written for `keys/export-secret/0.1` or `keys/sign/0.1` (a step-up, a consent or a deny) bound the Trust Task only.

## Breaking changes

- **A private key is no longer released over REST or HTTPS.** `GET /keys/{id}/secret` always answers 403. Over the HTTPS Trust-Task binding, `keys/export-secret` and `vta/contexts/secrets` are refused with `permissionDenied`, and the message names the fix: use DIDComm or TSP, or the on-host CLI.
  - SDK clients that reach the VTA over DIDComm or TSP are unaffected. This includes `IntegrationOnboarding` / `startup()`, which use a DIDComm session.
  - A REST-only client that exported keys must move to DIDComm or TSP, or run the export on the VTA host (`vta keys bundle`, `vta did-webvh --export-secrets`).
- An ACL entry narrowed without `key-export` can no longer export over any transport, and can no longer run `provision-integration`.
- An ACL entry narrowed without `sign` can no longer use the generic signing oracle. Un-narrowed entries are unaffected, because every role that can reach the oracle derives `sign`.
- `operations::keys::get_key_secret` gains `acl_ks` and takes `ExportChannel` instead of `&str`. `derive_and_sign(_document)` gain `acl_ks`. `get_context_secrets` and `build_did_secrets_bundle` take `ExportChannel`.
- An export, a backup export or a TEE mnemonic export whose audit row cannot be written now fails instead of succeeding without a row.
- **`POST /backup/export` and `POST /backup/import` always answer 403**, and `initiate-export`, `initiate-import` and `finalize-import` are refused over HTTPS. `pnm backup export` and `pnm backup import` must reach the VTA over DIDComm or TSP. This follows trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646.
- A super-admin narrowed without `key-export` can no longer export a backup or the TEE mnemonic.
- `keys/export-secret` and `keys/sign` answer an out-of-scope or absent key with one `Forbidden` refusal. A super-admin still gets `NotFound`.
- A revoked key is no longer exported, or loaded by the VTA for its own use.

## Authorization after this change

| Path | Role floor | Scope | allowed_keys | Capability | Exportability / internal | Channel | Policy gate | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keys/export-secret` (HTTPS / DIDComm / TSP) | none (capability) | key's context | n/a | key-export | refused | E2E only | spine | durable, before release |
| `GET /keys/{id}/secret` | admin | key's context | n/a | key-export | refused | always refused | n/a | n/a |
| DIDComm `get-key-secret` | admin | key's context | n/a | key-export | refused | E2E | rest_gate | durable, before release |
| `vta/contexts/secrets` | none (capability) | context | n/a | key-export | refused per key | E2E only | spine | durable per key |
| `provision-integration` | admin + context | context | n/a | key-export | refused | sealed | spine / n/a | durable per key |
| `keys/sign` / REST / DIDComm | application+ | key's context | enforced | sign (opaque) | n/a | any | spine / rest_gate | `keys.sign` |
| `keys/derive-and-sign(-document)` | super-admin, `m/26'/9'` | n/a | n/a | sign | n/a | any | spine / rest_gate | digest row |
| room / VC signing (`ProtocolDefined`) | per task | key's context | enforced | the task's own | n/a | any | spine | `keys.sign` |

## Tests

- REST secret export without `key-export` is refused, and so is every other channel (`vti_vta_003_export_without_key_export_is_refused_on_every_channel`).
- An export over hop-by-hop is refused even for an entitled caller. Over HTTPS the refusal names the transports that work.
- A non-exportable key and an internal key are refused on every channel.
- A successful export writes exactly one durable row with actor, key, context and channel, and no material. An export whose row cannot be written is refused.
- Opaque signing without `sign` is refused before the lookup. Protocol-defined signing does not need `sign`. `derive-and-sign(-document)` without `sign` is refused.
- `out_of_scope_and_absent_keys_are_indistinguishable`
- `revoked_keys_are_neither_exported_nor_loaded`
- `a_backup_export_over_https_is_refused`, `a_backup_export_over_an_end_to_end_channel_mints_a_bundle`, `backup_export_is_refused_over_rest`, `backup_export_over_https_is_refused` (mock VTA), `backup_import_tasks_over_https_are_refused`, `a_backup_import_over_an_end_to_end_channel_mints_a_slot`, `backup_import_is_refused_over_rest`
- The existing `get_context_secrets`, trust-task export and backup tests pass. The REST import preview and wrong-password tests are replaced by the refusal test. Wrong-password handling stays covered in `vta-backup`.


## Follow-ups

These are in #1743 (stacked on this PR): spec error codes `notExportable` / `neverExportable`, a `vault/release` audit row, sealed TEE mnemonic delivery, `key.internal_use` for the VTA's own key loads, and multicodec-prefixed P-256 public keys.

title: fix(vta-service)!: apply the key-export and sign capability checks on every transport (#1733)
body:
fix(vta-service)!: apply the key-export and sign capability checks on every transport (#1733)

* fix(vta-service): apply the key-export and sign capability checks on every transport

The KeyExport capability was checked only by the keys/export-secret
Trust-Task handler, so GET /keys/{id}/secret and DIDComm get-key-secret
released private keys to an admin whose entry was narrowed without
key-export. Capability::Sign was checked nowhere.

Both checks now live in the operation layer (VTI-VTA-003, VTI-VTA-007):

- get_key_secret requires key-export before any lookup, refuses a
  hop-by-hop channel (keys/export-secret/0.1 requires a channel
  confidential to the two parties), keeps the internal-key and
  non-exportable refusals, and writes the key.secret_export audit row
  durably before releasing the material, refusing if it cannot.
- The Trust-Task binding (https, didcomm, tsp) is recorded at the three
  entry points and named in the export's audit channel.
- vta/contexts/secrets and provision-integration use the same gate.
- sign_payload requires sign for opaque caller bytes; derive-and-sign
  and derive-and-sign-document require sign.
- The legacy REST and DIDComm key routes now consult the policy gate
  with the matching Trust-Task URI.
- The TEE mnemonic export writes a durable audit row before release.

BREAKING CHANGE: private keys are no longer released over REST or the
HTTPS Trust-Task binding; use DIDComm, TSP or the on-host CLI. Entries
narrowed without key-export or sign lose export, provisioning and
generic signing respectively.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: gate backup export on key-export and a confidential channel

A backup carries the seed, so it is an export of every key the VTA holds
(VTI-VTA-003).

- export_backup requires the key-export capability, read from the caller's
  ACL entry, on every path (REST, DIDComm, both initiate-export versions).
- The backup.export and backup.initiate-export audit rows are written
  durably before the envelope or descriptor is returned; a failed write
  refuses the export and aborts the bundle.
- POST /backup/export is refused, and initiate-export is refused over a
  hop-by-hop transport: the sealing password would exist in plaintext
  wherever TLS terminates, next to the bundle. DIDComm and TSP work.
- POST /attestation/mnemonic requires key-export.
- keys/export-secret and keys/sign check the caller's scope before they
  say whether a key exists, so an out-of-scope caller gets one refusal for
  both and learns neither the key's context nor its existence.
- Revoked keys are neither exported nor loaded with InternalAuthority.
- The non-exportable refusal message no longer carries a run of spaces.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the admin key-export gate test expects the scoped refusal

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service)!: refuse backup import over REST and HTTPS Trust Tasks

The import carries the backup and the password that opens it, which
together are every key the backup holds. Over a hop-by-hop channel both
exist in plaintext wherever TLS terminates.

- POST /backup/import always answers 403.
- initiate-import and finalize-import (1.0 and 1.1) are refused over the
  HTTPS binding, after the super-admin check and before a slot is minted
  or the password is used. DIDComm and TSP still work, as does DIDComm
  backup-import.
- This implements the vta/backup Channel requirement proposed in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#646, which also covers initiate-export.
- The pnm --use-rest-legacy help and the backup docs say DIDComm or TSP.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(e2e): drive the chunk tasks over DIDComm

Backup export tasks are refused over a hop-by-hop transport, so the dispatch-spine chunk test now runs over DIDComm like a real producer, on 8 MiB worker stacks as the round-trip test does.

title: spec(backup): require an end-to-end confidential channel for backup export and import
body:
## Summary

Three VTA backup tasks now **MUST** be carried over a channel confidential end-to-end between the producer and the recipient, in both 1.0 and 1.1:

- `vta/backup/initiate-export`
- `vta/backup/initiate-import`
- `vta/backup/finalize-import`

DIDComm with authenticated encryption and TSP qualify. A channel confidential only hop by hop does not, the HTTPS binding included.

The same requirement covers the community's backup and the node-neutral family, all 0.1:

- `vtc/backup/export` and `vtc/backup/import`
- `backup/initiate-export`, `backup/initiate-import` and `backup/finalize-import`

## Export record before release

`vtc/backup/export` and every `initiate-export` version (`vta/backup` 1.0 and 1.1, `backup` 0.1) **MUST** now record the export durably **before** the envelope or descriptor is returned. They **MUST** refuse the export when they cannot record it. Previously this was a **SHOULD**. A copy released unrecorded cannot be recalled.

## Why

- **`initiate-export`** carries `password`. Its response carries the descriptor that retrieves the bundle the password unlocks.
- **`finalize-import`** carries `password` for a bundle whose ciphertext may have travelled over HTTPS.
- **`initiate-import`** carries no secret. Its `stream` response, though, carries a bearer credential for writing into the agent. Requiring one channel for the whole import keeps the slot, the password and the commit readable by the recipient alone.

Over HTTPS, TLS terminates wherever the operator terminates it. Whoever holds that point would hold the password next to the bundle, which is every key the agent has.

## What a recipient does

- It refuses any other channel with `permissionDenied`.
- It refuses after it has established entitlement, and before it serializes state, mints a slot or derives a key.
- The refusal **SHOULD** name the bindings it accepts.

The bundle bytes themselves are ciphertext. They may still move over HTTPS (`transportUrl`) or chunk by chunk.

## Change type

This is a prose-only normative change to draft specs. No schema, error code or generated binding changes. `npm run validate` passes.

A sibling of #643. The VTI implementations are OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1733 (VTA) and OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1755 (VTC).

title: feat(auth/passkey): step-up-only passkeys a member enrols through an admin's invite
body:
## Why

`git-ns/right/break-glass` (#641) always needs a passkey gesture bound to the one request. A namespace admin who is not a console user acts only through signed documents and has no passkey the VTC knows. The signing key alone cannot be allowed to enrol one: whoever stole the key would enrol their own passkey, and the step-up would add nothing. So the first binding is anchored in an administrator's signed, single-use invite, redeemed with a claim code delivered over a different channel.

## What

- **`auth/passkey/enroll/invite` 0.2**
  - Adds `purpose` (`session` | `stepUp`, default `session`).
  - Adds `claimCode`, returned once, required at redemption, and never in the URL.
  - Rules that bind every issuer of a `stepUp` credential:
    - it is never offered or accepted by login or session step-up;
    - it is accepted only as operation-bound, self-mode user verification of its own subject: a `boundTo` approve-response, or the UV assertion of redeem/finish or revoke/finish 0.2;
    - it confers no role or scope;
    - its redemption and revocation are audited.
  - A further step-up credential needs a UV assertion from one the subject already holds.
- **`auth/passkey/enroll/redeem/start` 0.1** and **`redeem/finish` 0.1** (new): the redemption wire that 0.1 never specified.
  - One `inviteInvalid` refusal for a wrong token or code, with the same timing, so redemption is not an oracle.
  - A per-invite attempt limit (`tooManyAttempts`).
  - A ceremony handle.
  - The invite is consumed in the same step as the binding.
- **`auth/passkey/revoke/start` 0.2** and **`revoke/finish` 0.2**
  - An administrator may revoke a credential for its subject (`subject`). Their authority comes from the consumer's own state, and they verify with their own passkey.
  - An owner's step-up credential may verify its own revocation.
  - The last-credential refusal covers session credentials only.
  - `remaining` may be 0 for a step-up credential.
  - A revoked step-up credential can no longer answer step-ups that are still pending.

`auth/step-up/approve-response` 0.4 is unchanged. Its webauthn path already resolves the credential to the approver; the new restriction is carried by invite 0.2's rules on `stepUp` credentials.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass.

Draft. Not for release yet. Implementation: a stacked VTI draft on OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745.

spec(device): register the keyExport capability (#643)

keys/export-secret/0.1 authorizes against "standing over the key's
scope" and leaves the grant's shape to the implementation. Where it is a
device capability there should be a registered value, as there is for
roomPresent and roomOpen, so implementations do not each carry a private
one. The VTA already gates export on it.

keyExport (key-export in the 0.1 casing) is deliberately separate from
sign: a producer that may ask the custodian to use a key loses that the
moment its entitlement changes, while a producer that took the key keeps
it after its authority is withdrawn. export-secret now names the value
and says a sign grant is not a keyExport grant. The value is additive,

title: spec(device): register the keyExport capability
body:
## Summary

Registers `keyExport` (`key-export` in the `0.1` casing) in the shared device `Capability` enum, and names it in `keys/export-secret/0.1`'s Authorization section.

`keys/export-secret` authorizes against "standing over the key's scope" and leaves the shape of that grant to the implementation. Where the grant is a device capability, there should be a registered value rather than one private value per implementation, as #351 did for `roomPresent` and `roomOpen`. The VTA already gates export on this capability (VTI-VTA-003: export "MUST be gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key").

## Changes

- `specs/device/_shared/{0.1,0.2}/device-binding.schema.json` adds the value to `Capability`. The enum is additive, so a consumer that does not recognise it ignores it.
- `specs/keys/export-secret/0.1/spec.md` names the value and states that a custodian **MUST NOT** treat a `sign` grant as a `keyExport` grant, and that `keyExport` confers no other capability. The reason is the one VTI-VTA-002/003 give: a producer that may *use* a key loses that ability the moment its entitlement changes, while a producer that *took* the key keeps it.
- Bindings are regenerated for Rust, TS, Go and Dart. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass.

There are no version bumps and no CHANGELOG entry; release-plz assigns those.

title: feat(git-ns): separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass
body:
## What

Separation of duties for git-ns rights, with an explicit break-glass (decision of 2026-09-25).

**Normal rule.** An *elevated* right (`git.ns.admin`, `git.repo.create`, `git.repo.own`) must be granted by someone other than its recipient. Self-grants of `git.repo.maintain` and `git.commit.sign` stay allowed.

**Escape hatch.** A member who already has the authority to grant an elevated right, but cannot give it to themselves, uses `git-ns/right/break-glass`. It takes effect at once, never expires, carries a mandatory justification, and stays flagged, and in front of every other administrator, until one of them ratifies or revokes it.

## Specs

| Spec | Change |
|---|---|
| `git-ns/right/grant` **0.3** | New fixed rule 7, separation of duties: `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`, with a message that names break-glass. The rule is compared after delegation, so a console key cannot grant its principal. A table lists the tasks it also binds: drift/resolve `adopt`, repo/adopt (naming yourself an owner), namespace/reseat (to yourself). `bind` and `repo/create` are explicitly not self-grants. Rules 3 and 4 now count only *counting* records: no `expiresAt`, and not an unratified break-glass. This folds in reseat 0.2's expiring-record reading. |
| `git-ns/right/break-glass` **0.1** (new) | Payload `{right: ElevatedRight, resource, justification}`, with no `subject` and no `expiresAt`. There are two entitlements: grant authority over the right (the usual case is a ns admin taking an explicit `own`), or community admin plus a headless namespace for `git.ns.admin` (reseat to self). `sideEffects: destructive`. The response is not sent until the record and the highest-severity audit event are durable. That event records the justification, the entitlement and the step-up evidence. Every administrator of the namespace gets a signed notice. Policy may disable (`:disabled`), defer (`effectiveAt`) or require more. It can never suppress the audit, the notices or the surfaces. Break-glass is enabled by default. |
| `git-ns/right/ratify` **0.1** (new) | Another administrator clears the flag: a community admin, or a holder of grant authority whose own right is not an unratified break-glass. Never the grantee (`:selfRatification`). The request is bound to the `breakGlass.at` the ratifier read (`:recordChanged`). |
| `git-ns/right/break-glass-notice` **0.1** (new) | The VTC's signed push to every community admin and ns admin of the namespace, for the events `breakGlass`, `ratified` and `revoked`. Policy cannot narrow who receives it. |
| `git-ns/right/revoke` **0.3** | Any community admin may revoke an unratified break-glass record. It never counts toward last-owner/last-admin, and policy cannot refuse the revocation. Revoking one is audited and announced. |
| `git-ns/view` **0.4** | Records carry `breakGlass`. Every unratified break-glass record, with its justification, goes to every community admin, every ns admin of its namespace and every owner of its resource, whatever else the caller may see. |
| `git-ns/_shared` **0.4** | Adds `BreakGlass {by, at, justification, effectiveAt?, ratifiedBy?, ratifiedAt?}`, `RightRecord.breakGlass` and `ElevatedRight`. The registry projection is unchanged, and `breakGlass` is never published. |

## Choices worth reviewing

- **Step-up is not in the spec.** SPEC §7.3 item 13 forbids a spec from declaring a step-up requirement. break-glass therefore requires the audit row to record the evidence of any step-up the VTC applied, and recommends that such a step-up be bound to the request. The VTC (VTI) requires a passkey (aal2, user verification) bound to the request, unconditionally.
- **Ratify is a separate task, not a field on grant.** Its entitlement, its refusals and its instance binding differ from a grant's. A grant of a right the subject already holds through break-glass returns the record unchanged; it never ratifies it as a side effect.
- **Ratified records keep `breakGlass`**, with `ratifiedBy`/`ratifiedAt` set, as history. "Unratified" means `ratifiedBy` is absent.
- **Unratified break-glass does not count toward the invariants.** Otherwise a community admin who reseated a headless namespace to themselves could never be revoked, because they would be the last admin.
- **The rule for drift/resolve, repo/adopt and reseat is stated in grant 0.3**, the way reseat 0.2 stated its last-admin reading for the other tasks, instead of in new versions of each. The next versions should declare `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` in their `errorCodes`. In particular, **#640** (drift/resolve 0.3) and **#635** (reseat 0.3) should add it along with an adopt/reseat step. This PR does not touch them, to avoid conflicts.

## Coordination

- #640 (drift/resolve 0.3 recipient binding): complementary. Once `subject` is bound, the self-grant check compares `subject` with the resolver.
- #635 (reseat 0.3, bridge/job 0.4): reseat to oneself becomes break-glass.
- #639 edits drift/resolve 0.2 in place. There is no overlap in files.

## Implementations

- VTI (vtc-service, admin console, `cnm`): OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1745. It builds against this branch through a local `[patch]` and needs a `trust-tasks-rs` release carrying these modules before its CI can pass.
- openvtc TUI (Repos panel banner): OpenVTC/openvtc#384.

## Checks

- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm run check-bindings`: 527 specs agree across TS/Rust/Go/Dart, and 1110 declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` on the new modules passes, including `rejects_invalid_examples`.

No version or CHANGELOG edits. A trust-tasks release is needed before the consumers can leave draft.

title: feat(git-ns): separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass (#641)
body:
feat(git-ns): separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass (#641)

* feat(git-ns): separation of duties for elevated rights, with an audited break-glass

An elevated git right (git.ns.admin, git.repo.create, git.repo.own) is now
always granted by someone other than its recipient, and the one way to give
oneself one is an explicit, justified, highly visible break-glass that another
administrator ratifies or revokes.

- git-ns/right/grant 0.3: fixed rule 7, separation of duties, refused with
  git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. It binds every task that records a right on the
  actor's own authority (drift/resolve adopt, repo/adopt, namespace/reseat);
  bind and repo/create are not self-grants. Rules 3 and 4 count only records
  with no expiry that are not unratified break-glass.
- git-ns/right/break-glass 0.1 (new): self-grant of an elevated right the
  actor may already grant, or git.ns.admin on a headless namespace for a
  community administrator. Mandatory justification, destructive, immediate,
  no expiry, highest-severity audit, notice to every administrator, visible
  until ratified or revoked. Policy may disable, delay or tighten it, never
  quieten it.
- git-ns/right/ratify 0.1 (new): another administrator clears the flag,
  bound to the breakGlass.at they read.
- git-ns/right/break-glass-notice 0.1 (new): the VTC's signed push to every
  community administrator and namespace admin, for break-glass, ratified and
  revoked.
- git-ns/right/revoke 0.3: any community administrator may revoke an
  unratified break-glass record; policy cannot refuse that.
- git-ns/view 0.4: unratified break-glass records go to every administrator
  they concern, whatever else the caller may see.
- git-ns/_shared 0.4: BreakGlass, RightRecord.breakGlass, ElevatedRight.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(git-ns/view): return breakGlass in full, justification included

_shared/0.4 makes the justification a required member of BreakGlass, so
omitting it under the reason rule produced a record the schema refuses.
Everyone view shows such a record to is an administrator, an owner or the
member who broke the glass.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(git-ns): no creator ownership from an implied git.repo.create; elevated rights for members only

Review follow-ups to separation of duties.

- git-ns/repo/create 0.3 (new): a creator owns the repository only when
  they hold git.repo.create by explicit record, granted by someone else or
  recorded through break-glass. A git.repo.create implied by git.ns.admin
  carries no creator ownership: such a requester names another member in
  the new optional owners, or is refused git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, naming
  break-glass. Naming others is a grant of own (git-ns:escalation,
  git-ns:membersOnly). Without this, every namespace admin could give
  themselves own, and a forge admin role, one repository at a time. A
  single-admin community breaks the glass once for git.repo.create.
- git-ns/right/grant 0.3, fixed rule 5: an elevated right (ns.admin,
  repo.create, own) goes only to a current member holding standing in the
  VTC's access-control records, and is granted only by a member, on every
  task that records one; policy cannot waive it. This closes handing an
  elevated right to a throwaway DID the actor controls. The security
  section states that two member DIDs held by one person are out of scope
  for the DID comparison.
- grant 0.3: the tasks rule 7 binds name drift/resolve 0.3 and
  namespace/reseat 0.3, which declare git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed, and
  repo/create 0.3; the text claiming a creator's git.repo.create was
  always granted by someone else is corrected, and "a later version will
  declare the code" is gone.
- git-ns/right/break-glass 0.1: the members-only refusal covers every
  elevated right.

Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: feat(git-ns): bridge/job 0.4 and namespace/reseat 0.3, a namespace admin gets no forge role
body:
## What

A namespace admin gets no role on the forge. `git.ns.admin` is exercised through the VTC and the community's bridge (bind, adopt, reseat, grants). The bridge does not make its holder an organisation owner and gives them no repository role for it. Making someone an organisation owner stays a decision the community makes outside the VTC.

Earlier versions are **unchanged**. The new rules ship in new versions, because they change behaviour that is normative there. Both specs are draft, so these breaking changes ship as MINOR increments under the draft allowance of SPEC §5.2.

### `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4

- **`desiredRoles` right:** each person's highest right recorded in their own name. That is `own`, `maintain` or `commit.sign` on the repository, or `commit.sign` on the namespace. It never counts a right that exists only because `git.ns.admin` implies it (0.3 said "highest effective right", which does count it).
  - A namespace admin with no right of their own on the repository is listed at `git.ns.admin`, which every adapter maps to no role. Being listed, rather than left out, means the bridge takes off a role it manages that they still hold.
  - An admin who is also a recorded owner is listed as the owner.
- **Only `own` may map to admin:** a bridge MUST refuse, at config load and on any change, a role map that gives `maintain` or `commit.sign` the forge's administrator or owner role. `git.ns.admin` itself never projects a forge role; an admin's own non-elevated rights (`maintain`, `commit.sign`) project to non-admin roles and are allowed self-grants. On a personal account `own` and `maintain` both map to `write`, so separation of duties is enforced at the VTC, not the forge.
  - Creator ownership from a `repo.create` implied only by `ns.admin` does not arise (specified in `git-ns/right/grant` 0.3, #641).
- **One entry per account:** each forge account appears at most once in `desiredRoles`.
- **`repo` is required for `projectRoles`:** the namespace-level job (organisation owners) no longer exists.
- **`removeAccounts`:** may name an account listed at `git.ns.admin`.
- **Negotiation:** a VTC MUST NOT send 0.4 to a bridge that has not listed the 0.4 Type URI in answer to `trust-task-discovery` from that VTC. A 0.3 bridge, including one that reads later minor versions forward-compatibly (SPEC §5.2), would take `git.ns.admin` as ownership. A bridge that takes 0.4 MUST answer discovery. A VTC MUST NOT fall back to an earlier version: it sends such a bridge nothing and tells its operator to upgrade the bridge.

### `git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.3

- **No namespace-level projection:** step 8 no longer queues a namespace-level forge projection; it MUST NOT.
- **Separation of duties:** a community administrator MUST NOT reseat a namespace to themselves. That is a self-grant of `git.ns.admin`, an elevated right, and is refused with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` (step 4, checked before the members-only floor). The refusal names `git-ns/right/break-glass`, the explicit, audited way to do it that another administrator ratifies or revokes. This follows the separation-of-duties rule that #641 adds to `git-ns/right/grant` 0.3. 0.2 said the subject "may be the administrator themselves".

The schema is wire-identical to 0.2; only the `subject` description changed.

`right/grant` is unchanged. The forge-projection rule is normative in `bridge/job`, and the rights model's implication rules have not changed.

## Implementations

- VGI bridge: OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#84 (merged; ns.admin maps to no role) and OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#92 (draft; takes 0.4 only and answers discovery).
- VTC: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1729 sends 0.4 only, and only after discovery. A bridge that does not list 0.4 gets nothing, and the operator is told to upgrade it. It serves `git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.3 only (0.1 is no longer served) and refuses a reseat to the sender with `git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed`.

A trust-tasks release is needed before the VTC and VGI can use the generated `job::v0_4` and `reseat::v0_3` types. Until then they carry the 0.4 and 0.3 type URIs by hand.

## Checks

The Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings were regenerated. `npm run check-bindings` and `npm run build` pass.

title: feat(backup): a node-neutral backup and restore family
body:
`vta/backup/*` is the agent's descriptor-based backup and restore: a slot,
digests pre-committed before any byte moves, the bundle carried either as an
HTTPS stream or chunk by chunk over the agent's own Trust Task transport, and a
finalize step that previews before it replaces. Nothing in that transfer is
specific to an agent, and a community node needs exactly the same thing for the
same reason: a backup of any real node is too large for one document, and a
node that bounds a document's size before checking its proof — as it must on a
binding that authenticates no sender — cannot accept one that way.
`vtc/backup/import/0.1`, which carries the whole envelope inline, is the case
in point.

This adds `backup/{initiate-export, get-chunk, complete-export,
initiate-import, put-chunk, finalize-import, abort}/0.1`, derived from the
latest `vta/backup/*` versions and made node-neutral:

- The parties, prose and error-code slugs name a node rather than an agent.
- What a backup contains is the node's to define. `finalize-import`'s
  response replaces the agent-specific `keyCount` / `aclCount` /
  `contextCount` / `auditCount` / `importedSecretCount` with one `counts` map
  keyed by the node's own record kinds — an agent's `keys`, `acl`, `contexts`,
  `audit`, `importedSecrets`; a community's backed-up keyspaces — still
  counts, never contents.
- The transfer shapes (descriptor, chunk manifest, chunk data, bundle id) are
  referenced from `vta/_shared/0.1/backup-transfer` rather than copied. A copy
  with the node-neutral wording would have been a second definition that the
  TypeScript generator disambiguates by renaming the published `ChunkData`,
  `ChunkSize`, `ChunkManifest`, `ChunkedDescriptor` and `BundleDescriptor`
  exports — a break for every TS consumer, for no difference on the wire.
- The "Changes from 1.0" history sections are dropped; a new 0.1 has no
  predecessor, and the abstract says where the family came from.

`vta/backup/*` stays served while agents adopt this family, and
`vtc/backup/{export,import}` remain for a node small enough to fit one
document. Retiring the agent-specific versions is a later change.

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart; the only change to
existing generated code is the new `backup` feature and index entries.

## Verified locally (rebased onto #631)

- `npm run validate`: 521 specs, 80 shared schemas
- `npm run check-bindings`: 521 specs agree across TypeScript, Rust, Go and Dart; declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`: 1194 passed, 0 failed
- Regenerating after the rebase produced no diff.
