title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): adopt drift through git-ns/drift/resolve
body:
## What

A follow-up to #1725. **Adopt** on a drift item used to build a plain `git-ns/right/grant`. It now sends `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1 with `action: "adopt"`, carrying the same selector as Revert: `type`, the account (`forge` + `id`, `login` for display) and the `observed` value read. The VTC then:
- adopts nothing if the forge has changed since it was read (`driftNotFound`);
- records the right as the resolver's own grant (`right_grant_via`, `via: drift.adopt`);
- takes the item off the outstanding drift itself, which a plain grant never did.

An optional reason becomes the right's `reason`.

**Review fix.** The right is now the one the server projects. Adopt used `rightForForgeRole`, which mapped `write`/`push` to `git.commit.sign`, so on a personal-account namespace `write` said "No git right corresponds" when the VTC would project maintainer. It now uses `projectedRight`, which mirrors `git_ns::drift::projected_right`. `rightForForgeRole` had no other caller and is removed.

### Server rules, mirrored
`adoptStanding` (`repos/model.ts`) follows `git_ns::drift::adopt`, in order:
1. the repository is active or orphaned;
2. the signer holds `git.repo.own` there, explicit or implied by `git.ns.admin`, which is the same visibility as Revert;
3. the item is `roleAdded` or `roleChanged` (`notAdoptable` otherwise);
4. a member linked the account (`accountNotLinked`);
5. a right projects to the observed role (`noMatchingRight`);
6. for `roleChanged`, the projected right is a raise over what the member already holds on the repository, explicit or implied and unexpired (`heldRepoRank`). A lowering is `notAdoptable`, and the fix is to revoke the right;
7. the consent class: `right_grant_via` gates it as `right.grant`, so adopting owner is elevated and needs a community administrator (`elevated_requires_admin`, assumed on as for every elevated task).

When a viewer can't adopt but someone else could, they see why and the `cnm git drift resolve <resource> adopt --type=… --account-id=… --account-login=… --observed=… [--reason=…]` command, quoted fish-safe (#1723). When no one could adopt the item as it stands, it says why and offers no command. Revert is unchanged and stays on offer beside it.

`RevertDriftDialog` is now `DriftResolveDialog`, serving both actions. For adopt it names the member who receives the right, and the sign dialog lists them as "Receives the right".

## Behaviour changes (deliberate)

This PR follows the standing rule for this work: stronger security and better usability win over keeping existing behaviour.

- **Organisation `write` / `push` roles are no longer adoptable as committer.** The old button granted `git.commit.sign` for them with a plain grant. The VTC's own projection maps `write` to nothing on an organisation, because a committer is not necessarily given `write`, so drift/resolve refuses it with `noMatchingRight`. Adopting it would record a right the projection does not produce. The page now says so and points at the two safe paths: Revert, or grant the right with Add person and then revert the role.
- **Adopt no longer tolerates a stale read.** A plain grant went through whatever the forge showed by then. Now the VTC refuses it (`driftNotFound`) when the forge changed after the page was read.
- **Adopt checks more before sending.** A lowering (`roleChanged` no higher than what the member holds), an unlinked account, and an owner-level adopt from a non-community-administrator are no longer offered. Each shows why, and where someone else could do it, the command to hand over. Previously these were offered and then refused, or in the lowering case granted.
- **The hand-over command changed** from `cnm git grant …` to `cnm git drift resolve <resource> adopt …`. It needs a `cnm` with `git drift` (#1703) and a VTC that serves drift/resolve. The console ships inside `vtc-service`, so the console and the VTC always match.
- **The fixed reason is gone.** The grant used to carry "Adopted from a role added on the forge". The reason is now whatever the operator types, or none. The VTC tags the grant `via: drift.adopt` for policy and audit anyway.
- **`roleChanged` raises are now adoptable.** Previously only `roleAdded` was.

## Review follow-up (second commit)

- **Adopt waits for the rights listing.** While the listing is still loading, the list shows "Reading who holds what here before offering to adopt…" and no button. Before, it ranked against an empty list, so a `roleChanged` lowering could be offered as a raise.
- **`heldRepoRank` now matches the server's `effective_on`.** The namespace's admins (`ns.admins`) count as owners of every repository, with or without a row. `roleDerived` rows are ignored, because they are v0.1 hook-relay grants merged from the registry and never held in the git-ns store.
- **Tests:** a loading-window test (it fails without the gate), plus ranking tests for an admin with no row and for a `roleDerived` row.

## Tests

- actions:
  - adopt payload, command and party
  - normal class for maintainer, elevated for owner
  - shell safety for the resource, account, observed and reason
- model: `adoptStanding` covers
  - an owner adopting maintain
  - personal-account `write` → maintainer, while on an organisation `write` projects nothing
  - personal-account `admin` projects nothing
  - a lowering refused, and a raise from committer accepted
  - `roleRemoved` refused, and an unlinked account refused
  - hand-over to non-holders, elevated adopt only for a community administrator, a namespace admin allowed
  - `heldRepoRank`: explicit, implied and expired rights
- RepoDetail:
  - an owner adopts through the form, and the sign dialog shows the exact command and drift/resolve document without sending anything
  - personal-account `write` offers "Adopt into VTC as maintainer"
  - organisation `write` offers nothing, with the reason
  - a `roleChanged` lowering offers no adopt but keeps Revert
  - a non-holder, and a viewer with no whoami, get the command instead of the button
  - an owner-level adopt is hidden from an owner who is not a community administrator and shown as Elevated to one who is

`npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npm run wire:check` and `npx vitest run` (416 tests) pass. No Rust changed: drift/resolve is already in the `trust_task_manifest` census (#1725).

## How to test (ROLE-13, adopt side)

1. Bridge-mode namespace. On the forge, give a collaborator role to an account a member has linked. Wait for the drift report.
2. Admin console → Repos → the repository. As an owner or namespace admin, **Adopt into VTC as …** → optional reason → **Build the adopt** → sign.
3. The member now holds the projected right, the drift item is gone without a separate revert, and `gitNs.drift.resolved` appears in the activity.
4. On a personal-account namespace, a `write` collaborator adopts as maintainer.
5. When the forge shows a role no higher than the member already holds (`roleChanged`), the page says to revoke instead and offers only Revert.

title: Create the DTG predicate vocabulary as a repo-driven registry
body:
## Summary

#47 introduces the verifiable statement credential (VSC), whose meaning is carried by a predicate from a governed vocabulary, and says that predicates beyond the two core profiles will be defined in a planned "DTG Predicate Vocabulary" specification. Review has already produced the first candidates (#50 identity vetting; presentation/custody in the #47 thread), and the question of where they go is blocking. This issue proposes the answer: **a repo-driven registry, on the model of the ToIP glossary, not a specification** — and lays out what the repository needs to contain so that it can be created and populated without further design work.

The proposal was discussed against the alternative of growing the credential spec, or a dedicated vocabulary spec, and rejected both on cadence: a ToIP specification moves WD → Implementers Draft → Approved Deliverable, and a vocabulary needs to add an entry the week a community needs it. A generated registry governed by pull request is the only shape that matches how the content changes.

Assumption for this issue: ToIP is amenable to hosting the namespace and the published artifacts, at least for now. The IRIs below are placeholders until #48 is decided.

## Three things that were being called "the vocabulary"

| | What it is | Nature | Home |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. The rules** | what a predicate definition must contain, how it is published, immutability, NFC, labels, admission criteria | normative, changes rarely | the credential spec's *Predicate Profiles* section for now (it already states the nine required members); split out into a small "DTG Vocabularies" spec if and when the definition format needs its own normative home |
| **B. WG-curated predicates** | `endorses`, `witnessed`, and whatever the WG agrees to define under the DTG namespace | content, grows one entry at a time | **this repository** |
| **C. Community predicates** | terms a VTC or VTN defines under a namespace it controls | content, not ours to hold | the community's own namespace, referenced from its governance framework; published in the same format as B so tooling works for both |

The credential spec's *Community-Defined Predicates* section keeps one illustrative example and no more; every real predicate goes to B or C.

## The repository

Proposed name: `trustoverip/dtgwg-predicate-vocab`. Same tooling philosophy as `ctwg-main-glossary`: one source file per entry, a generator, a published output, PR governance.

```
dtgwg-predicate-vocab/
├── README.md                     what this is, how to propose a predicate
├── GOVERNANCE.md                 admission criteria, review, statuses, versioning
├── predicates/                   one file per predicate — the source of truth
│   ├── endorses.jsonld
│   ├── witnessed.jsonld
│   ├── identity-vetting.jsonld   from #50
│   └── presented.jsonld          from the #47 review thread
├── schemas/                      JSON Schema for each predicate's `value` payload
│   └── identity-vetting.schema.json
├── meta/
│   ├── predicate.schema.json     the definition format (mirrors the nine points in the credential spec)
│   └── meta-context.jsonld       JSON-LD context for the definition files themselves
├── tools/                        generator: validates predicates/ against meta/, builds dist/
└── dist/                         generated, published at the namespace; never hand-edited
    ├── vocab.jsonld              all active and deprecated terms, additive
    ├── index.html                human-readable vocabulary document
    ├── accept-list.json          machine-readable list verifiers can import
    └── context/
        └── v1.jsonld             frozen context for the additional members of core profiles
```

## The definition format

One JSON-LD document per predicate. The members are the nine points a profile MUST state under *Predicate Profiles* in #47, plus registry metadata. `witnessed`, as it would appear:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://trustoverip.org/dtg/vocab/meta-context.jsonld",
  "id": "https://trustoverip.org/dtg/vocab#witnessed",
  "type": "Predicate",
  "status": "active",
  "since": "2026-10-01",
  "label": {
    "en": "witnessed",
    "de": "bezeugt",
    "nl": "getuige geweest van"
  },
  "definition": {
    "en": "The issuer observed the subject issue the credential the object names, under the conditions of a specific trust task exchange."
  },
  "classification": "evidence",
  "weighedBy": "The community whose witnessing policy the attestation is issued under.",
  "objectKind": ["digestMultibase"],
  "subjectObjectRelationship": "credentialSubject.id MUST be the issuer of the credential object.digestMultibase names; a verifier holding that credential MUST check it.",
  "additionalMembers": {
    "witnessContext": {
      "required": false,
      "schema": "https://trustoverip.org/dtg/vocab/schemas/witness-context.schema.json"
    }
  },
  "taskContextRequired": true,
  "minimumIssuerScope": "directed",
  "issuer": "A member, or a VTA acting according to VTC policy.",
  "establishes": "That the issuer attests that, in the exchange identified by taskContext, it observed the subject issue the credential whose claims digest to object.digestMultibase.",
  "doesNotEstablish": [
    "that the referenced credential is currently valid or unrevoked",
    "that the referenced credential's claims are true",
    "that the exchange reached its terminal state (Outcome Interpretability applies)",
    "that the witness is a member of any community",
    "that any consequential action is authorized"
  ],
  "definedIn": "https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-cred-spec/#the-dtgwitnessed-profile-vwc",
  "governedBy": null
}
```

The presentation/custody predicate from the #47 thread, showing the case where the observed party is the referenced credential's *subject*:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://trustoverip.org/dtg/vocab/meta-context.jsonld",
  "id": "https://trustoverip.org/dtg/vocab#presented",
  "type": "Predicate",
  "status": "proposed",
  "label": { "en": "presented" },
  "definition": {
    "en": "The issuer observed the subject present the credential the object names. The subject is the holder; the credential's issuer need not have been present."
  },
  "classification": "evidence",
  "objectKind": ["digestMultibase"],
  "subjectObjectRelationship": "credentialSubject.id MUST be the credentialSubject.id of the credential object.digestMultibase names.",
  "taskContextRequired": true,
  "minimumIssuerScope": "directed",
  "issuer": "A member, or a VTA acting according to VTC policy.",
  "establishes": "That the issuer attests that, in the exchange identified by taskContext, the subject presented the credential whose claims digest to object.digestMultibase.",
  "doesNotEstablish": [
    "that the presented credential is valid, unrevoked, or was issued to the subject",
    "that the presented credential's claims are true",
    "that the subject controls the presented credential's subject identifier",
    "that any consequential action is authorized"
  ]
}
```

A community predicate uses the same format under its own namespace, with `governedBy` pointing at the governance framework that defines who may issue it and how it is weighed. That is what makes one generator, one validator and one accept-list format serve both tiers.

## Generated outputs

| Artifact | Consumer | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `vocab.jsonld` | tooling, RDF consumers, `rdfs:label` lookups | additive; a term is never removed or altered once active, only deprecated |
| `index.html` | people | the human-readable vocabulary, one section per predicate, labels in every language supplied |
| `accept-list.json` | verifiers | the active IRIs with their machine-checkable constraints (object kinds, `taskContextRequired`, minimum scope, schema URLs), for import into verifier configuration at configuration time |
| `context/v1.jsonld` | credentials under core profiles | the JSON-LD terms for additional members such as `witnessContext`; frozen per version, as VC contexts must be |

An `accept-list.json` entry, so the shape is concrete:

```json
{
  "https://trustoverip.org/dtg/vocab#witnessed": {
    "status": "active",
    "objectKind": ["digestMultibase"],
    "taskContextRequired": true,
    "minimumIssuerScope": "directed",
    "additionalMembers": { "witnessContext": { "required": false } }
  }
}
```

## Versioning and immutability — two different rules

This is the part that needs to be got right before anything is published, and it feeds #48.

- **Predicate IRIs are unversioned and term-immutable.** `…/vocab#witnessed` never changes meaning and is never deleted; adding `#presented` does not touch it. Versioning the namespace (`…/vocab/v1#witnessed` → `…/vocab/v2#witnessed`) would change every predicate's IRI whenever any predicate is added, and break byte-exact matching for every issued credential. So the namespace IRI decided in #48 **must carry no version segment**. The current placeholder in #47 (`https://firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1#witnessed`) has one and should not be the final form.
- **Contexts are versioned and frozen.** A JSON-LD context that credentials list must not change after publication, so `context/v1.jsonld` is frozen and additions go in `v2`. This is fine because credentials do not need the vocabulary context to carry a predicate — predicates are absolute IRIs — only to carry a core profile's additional members.

Releases are git tags. `dist/` at a tag is the published state; the namespace serves the latest tag's `vocab.jsonld` and `index.html`, and every `context/vN.jsonld` ever released.

## Governance

`GOVERNANCE.md`, drawing on the credential spec's rules:

- **Not a gate.** The registry curates a shared, trusted default set; it does not decide who may define or use a predicate. Because a predicate is an absolute IRI that a verifier accepts by configuration, resolved at configuration time and never at verification time (Predicate Handling in #47), a community that publishes a predicate under a namespace it controls can issue under it, and verifiers can accept it, without waiting on or ever seeking admission here. #50's identity vetting predicate already works this way. Admission is what a community seeks when it wants convergence — one identifier shared across communities — not what it needs in order to use the standard. The admission criteria below therefore bound what enters the DTG namespace, not what the mechanism permits. This is a stated design guarantee, mirrored in the credential spec's editor's note on where profiles live (#47), not an emergent property.
- **Admission to the DTG namespace.** A proposed predicate is accepted when it (1) is complete against `meta/predicate.schema.json`, including the establishes / does-not-establish block; (2) is on the *attests* side of the statement/establishment test — it is not a predicate whose PASS a verifier would act on as representation, authority, membership, admission, governed status or task completion; (3) is unilateral; (4) is not meaningful only inside one exchange; (5) has no existing term with the same meaning — one identifier per concept; (6) has an NFC IRI and at least an English label; and (7) is either needed by a DTG specification or in use, or credibly about to be, by more than one community.
- **Statuses.** `proposed` (merged, not yet in a release), `active`, `deprecated` (kept forever, marked, with a pointer to any replacement). Nothing is ever deleted.
- **Review.** Two WG approvals for a new `active` term; one for editorial changes to labels or definitions that do not alter meaning; meaning changes are not permitted — deprecate and add.
- **Equivalence.** The registry MAY record that a community term has the same meaning as a DTG term, as information for people configuring verifiers. Verifiers never follow it (Predicate Handling in #47).

## Relationship to the credential spec

- The credential spec keeps the statement mechanism, Predicate Handling, What Verification Establishes, Predicate Profiles (which is where the definition format's requirements live for now), and — for WD03 — the `endorses` and `witnessed` profiles, because they replace WD02 normative text and need a published home. Once this repository has a release, those two move here and the credential spec references them; nothing on the wire changes.
- The `dtg:` notation in the credential spec resolves to this repository's namespace once #48 is decided.
- *Related Specifications* in the credential spec should describe this as a registry, not a specification.
- #50 should target this repository rather than the credential spec's example section, as the first entry.
- #47's reviewer request for a core presentation/custody profile is answered by `presented.jsonld` above rather than by a third profile in the credential spec.

## Sequencing

1. Create the repository with `README.md`, `GOVERNANCE.md`, `meta/`, and an empty `predicates/`; decide #48 so the placeholder IRIs can be replaced.
2. Add the generator (validation against `meta/predicate.schema.json`, build of `dist/`), and CI that fails a PR whose definition is incomplete.
3. First entries: `identity-vetting` (#50), `presented`. Mirror `endorses` and `witnessed` as `proposed` so the format is exercised against the two real profiles.
4. First release once the credential spec reaches WD03; then move `endorses` and `witnessed` here for WD04 and update the credential spec's references.

## Open questions

- Which ToIP deliverable type a repo-driven registry is, and whether the glossary's process and tooling can be borrowed wholesale. (A question for ToIP staff.)
- Whether this repository should also carry the other community-defined vocabularies the DTG already depends on — VDC `scope` terms, VAC `actions`, the VEC endorsement vocabulary — since they are the same kind of thing with the same publication gap. If so, "DTG Vocabularies" is the better name. Flagged, not proposed here.
- Namespace and hosting: #48.

Refs #45, #47, #48, #50, #51.

title: Publish the DTG credential context at /dtg/context/v1 once cred-spec #46 settles
body:
## Summary

Decision 1 in PLAN.md moves the credential `@context` from the First Person placeholder to `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1`, served frozen from `contexts/v1.jsonld` in this repository. The predicate examples in `predicates/` already list that IRI. Nothing publishes it yet: the spec's Base Structure requires a context that has never been published anywhere, and this repository has no `contexts/` folder.

Writing the context is spec work rather than registry work, which is why it was taken out of the predicates PR. A `v1` context has to define terms for all seven DTG credential types and their members, not only the VSC, and once released it is frozen (GOVERNANCE.md §3, the immutability check). Freezing it before the open naming questions are settled would bake a known gap into a permanent IRI.

## Blocked on

- [trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#48](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/48): the specification's editors recording the credential `@context` IRI as `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1`, in exactly those bytes (`https`, no `www.`, no trailing slash), and the term namespace `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/credentials#` beside it. Publishing `contexts/v1.jsonld` here has to apply a decision the specification has made, not make one for it. This is the only dependency. The draft is open as #7 so the editors can review the content while deciding the IRI.

## Not blocked on

- [trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#46](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/46). The correlation-scope declaration is one term, and a concrete proposal (`issuerScope`) is in that issue so it can be decided alongside #48. If it is decided before #7 merges, the term goes into `v1`; if not, `v1` is published with what specification 0.5.0 defines and the term goes in `v2`, under the freeze rule in GOVERNANCE.md §3.1. Nothing issued under the First Person IRI is long-lived (see #48), so a `v2` following `v1` costs each implementation one bundle update, and the move away from the First Person IRI already requires that update.
- The seven-type term list being final. `v1` is the context for specification 0.5.0; a later specification version that adds or renames a term mints `v2`. That is the freeze rule working as intended, not a reason to wait.

## What the PR needs to contain

- `contexts/v1.jsonld`: a JSON-LD 1.1 context with `@protected` terms for `DTGCredential`, the seven concrete subtypes, `taskContext`, `taskDigestMultibase`, and the type-specific members of each credential type as specification 0.5.0 defines them. For the VSC: `predicate` as `@id`, `object.id` as a node identifier, `object.value` as `@json`, and `witnessContext`, per the editor's note in the spec's *Statements in the Graph*. `digestMultibase` comes from the W3C VC 2.0 context and is not redefined. The correlation-scope term from #46 is not in `v1`; it arrives in `v2`. Drafted in #7.
- Review by the credential spec editors, since the context is the wire-level shape of every DTG credential, not only the statement ones.
- A check in `scripts/lib/registry.mjs` that every example credential lists the registry's context IRI in `@context`, which can only be turned on once the context exists.
- A matching editorial change in the credential spec: Base Structure's required context IRI, the `dtg:` notation, and the examples.

## Until then

The IRI `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` does not resolve; #7 publishes it once merged. Implementations that need a context today carry a bundled copy of the First Person placeholder, as cred-spec #48 records, and the resolution is not load-bearing for any of them.

Refs PLAN.md decision 1 and §1.8 step 3.

title: Retry each verification check while a deployment propagates
body:
## Summary

The preview job for #7 failed twice in a row, on a different set of files each time: first `/dtg/vsc` with `Accept: application/ld+json`, then the home page, the endorses definition by its direct path, and `release.json`. Every failing URL answered 200 when fetched moments later, and the failing responses were Pages' own `text/html` 404s without the worker's CORS header, so the asset store was still filling in when the checks ran. The wait for `release.json` added in 6dfed92 does not cover this: the second run saw `release.json` pass the probe and then fail its check seconds later.

## Change

`infra/verify.mjs` now runs each check through a `check()` helper that retries with a short backoff (1 s, 2 s, ... capped at 5 s) until the check passes or its own deadline runs out, 60 s by default and settable with `--retry <seconds>`. A check that passes on a later attempt reports the attempt count. A check that never passes reports the last attempt's problems and the attempt count, so a real defect (wrong content type, missing header, wrong body) still fails and is still diagnosable. The initial wait for `release.json` stays, since it also covers DNS and TLS not being ready and gives a clear message when a deployment never appears.

The check list and the expectations are unchanged. `expect()` is split into `problemsWith()`, which computes the mismatches, and `check()`, which loops.

## Verification

- `docker compose run --rm shell -c 'node infra/verify.mjs https://36570ae3.dtgwg-vsc-registry.pages.dev'` against the second failed preview: all 17 checks pass.
- With `--wait 3 --retry 2` against a base that has no `release.json`, the wait loop still fails with its message and exit code 1.
- `docker compose run --rm test`: 22 tests pass.

The retry path itself was not exercised against a live propagating deployment, since that needs a fresh deploy; the first PR preview job after this merges is the real test.

moments later. Waiting for release.json before the checks, as 6dfed92

fails every attempt and is still reported, with the last attempt's

title: feat(didcomm)!: authenticate provision and wake by the document's proof
body:
## What changes

`push/provision` and `push/wake` received over **DIDComm** are now authenticated by an `eddsa-jcs-2022` Data Integrity proof on the Trust Task document, the same kind of evidence the HTTPS adapter already requires (a signature over the body). These are the caller's own operational messages, not attestations, so per **VTI-KEY-106** they are signed with the caller's **operational** key under `proofPurpose: authentication`; an `assertionMethod` proof (reserved for attestation artefacts) is refused, with no dual acceptance. The caller is the document's `issuer`, and only once the proof binds it (`src/proof.rs`):

1. proof is `eddsa-jcs-2022`, `proofPurpose: authentication`;
2. DID of `proof.verificationMethod` == `issuer` (exact match);
3. the issuer's DID document lists that method, its `controller` == `issuer`, and it is referenced or embedded under `authentication`;
4. the signature verifies over the raw document with `proof` removed.

**An `authentication` proof carries no challenge, so the document binds it to one delivery (VTI-KEY-107):**
- `recipient` is **required** on a signed document and must be this gateway;
- `issuedAt` is required and must fall inside the acceptance window: at most 5 min old and at most 60 s in the future (**VTI-OPS-024**, `FreshnessPolicy::consequential`; otherwise `expired` / `malformedRequest`);
- `expiresAt`, when present, must not have passed (`validate_basic`).
- The document `id` is claimed in a replay record (`src/replay.rs`, **VTI-OPS-026**), keyed by **(issuer, id)** and partitioned per issuer. The claim happens **only after** the per-DID rate limit and the controller/allowlist check, through an `AdmitOnce` hook in the dispatch core, so a refused caller leaves no entry. The record is kept until the last instant the window accepts the document (`issuedAt + max_age + skew`, or `expiresAt` if sooner) plus 1 s.
  - A second delivery of an accepted document gets the first response back and is not executed again, so no second push is sent.
  - A different document under the same issuer's accepted id gets `idConflict`.
  - A transient push failure releases the claim, so a retry is attempted.
  - At its bounds (8192 per issuer, 65536 total) the record refuses new documents rather than evicting entries. An unavailable record also refuses.
- The verification method is refused if `revoked` is set or `expires` has passed or does not parse. A resolved DID document over 64 KiB is refused.

The dispatch core is unchanged: `push/provision` still requires the proven issuer to be the handle's `controllerVtaDid`, and `push/wake` requires it to be on the allowlist.

**The envelope sender no longer authorises anything by itself:**
- no proof → the document is anonymous: `push/register` works as before, provision/wake get `proofRequired`;
- envelope `from` present but a different DID from the proven issuer → `identityMismatch`;
- `recipient` present and not this gateway's DID → `wrongRecipient`;
- proof present but fails any check → `proofInvalid` (fixed message; the detail goes to a `debug!` log).

Proof DIDs resolve through a separate `DIDCacheClient` built from the same `ResolverTuning` (and so the same public-only host policy) as the listener's.

**Only listed controller VTAs are served (`GATEWAY_ALLOWED_CONTROLLERS`).** The operator lists the VTA DIDs the gateway serves (comma/space separated, exact match, no patterns).
- A `push/register` naming any other controller is refused with `permissionDenied`, and nothing is stored.
- A provision by a controller no longer on the list is refused and spends no replay record.
- Unset or empty means nothing is served, and startup logs an error saying so.
- `*` alone is an explicit open mode. It logs a startup warning, and every limit below still applies.
- A malformed list stops startup.

**Who can spend the replay record.** `push/register` is anonymous and names its controller freely, so anyone can become the controller of a handle naming a DID they hold. A controller proof at registration would not stop this, because the attacker *is* that controller. So the allowlist above is the root fix. Within the served controllers (or in open mode), the record's budgets still apply:
- A provision that re-applies the stored allowlist spends no record.
- Records are charged per handle (512 per window, shared by the controller and every trigger on that handle) as well as per issuer (8192).
- At the overall soft bound (65536), only issuers above their fair share (soft bound ÷ issuers holding records) are refused. A hard bound of twice the soft bound caps memory.
- One controller DID may hold at most 4096 live handles (`GATEWAY_MAX_HANDLES_PER_CONTROLLER`).
- Unprovisioned handles are swept after 1 h (previously 24 h).
- Registration stays anonymous. It is rate-limited globally, and per peer IP over HTTPS. The DIDComm path has no trustworthy anonymous source to key a per-source limit on.

## Breaking change

A VTA that sends `push/provision` / `push/wake` over DIDComm **without a document proof is refused** (`proofRequired`), and so is one signed under `assertionMethod`. Today `vta-service` sends both unsigned:
- `provision_gateway` in `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/device.rs`
- `trigger_gateway_wake` in `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/step_up.rs`

Both need to sign with the VTA's **operational** key under `proofPurpose: authentication` (the VM listed under `authentication`). They must also carry `recipient` (the gateway DID), a current `issuedAt`, and a unique `id`; the two senders already set all three. This has to land before this PR is deployed. **Also breaking:** a gateway must now be given `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_CONTROLLERS`; without it every registration is refused. The `test-wake` helpers register under a throwaway controller, so they need a local gateway in open mode. Until then, wakes over DIDComm fail and devices fall back to mediator queue + voluntary pickup. **Release ordering: ship the VTA change first, then this.** The HTTPS path is unchanged.

## Tests

- `tests/didcomm_auth.rs` (new, 23 tests; the latest additions: three self-registered controllers flooding fresh provisions cannot lock out a legitimate wake (the reviewer's probe); re-applying the stored allowlist spends no record; one handle cannot exceed its budget) drives `didcomm::handle_envelope` with offline `did:key` parties: signed provision + wake succeed; a valid proof with no envelope sender succeeds; envelope sender alone → `proofRequired`, and the allowlist is not changed; proof by another key claiming the controller → `proofInvalid`; document edited after signing → `proofInvalid`; valid proof by a non-controller → `permissionDenied`; envelope sender differs from issuer → `identityMismatch`; other recipient → `wrongRecipient`; `assertionMethod` proof → `proofInvalid`; signed document without `recipient` → `malformedRequest`; `issuedAt` 10 min old → `expired`, 10 min in the future or missing → `malformedRequest`; replayed signed wake → first response returned and no second send; reused id on a different document → `idConflict`. Regression tests from review:
  - an already-expired document is refused on every delivery, with nothing sent or recorded;
  - an unauthorised issuer squatting a victim's id leaves no record, and the victim's document is accepted;
  - an unauthorised self-signed flood cannot evict a legitimate record;
  - one authorised issuer at its bound is refused and cannot evict another's records;
  - the same id from two issuers is two documents;
  - a transient failure is retried, not cached;
  - a refused provision leaves no record.
- Allowlist tests (`tests/didcomm_auth.rs`): default refuses every registration; an unlisted controller is refused at register and a listed one is accepted (provision + wake work); a delisted controller cannot provision and spends no record; open mode admits any controller while the per-controller cap and per-handle budget still apply. `src/controllers.rs` unit tests cover parsing: empty, exact match, `*` only when alone, no patterns, non-DID entries refused.
- Unit tests: `src/replay.rs` (keying, refuse-not-evict, release); `src/didcomm.rs` (retention outlives acceptance by the margin; expired document fails the window); `src/proof.rs` (revoked/expired/garbled `expires`; oversized document).
- `src/proof.rs` unit tests: VM controller, `authentication` membership (a key listed only under `assertionMethod` is refused) (absolute and relative references), document id, unlisted VM.
- `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo deny check`: all pass locally and in CI.

## Scope notes

- The 64 KiB cap applies after resolution. The resolver SDK has no response-size limit of its own, so the download is bounded only by its network timeout.
- The replay record is in memory and per process. Per VTI-OPS-027 it would have to be shared across replicas; the gateway runs as a single process today.
- The HTTPS path is unchanged. It authenticates with a did:key signature over the raw body in headers, not a document proof, and keeps its documented stance that a replayed wake is harmless (`auth.rs`). A document captured from DIDComm cannot be replayed over HTTPS without the issuer's key. The record lives in `AppState`, so the HTTPS path could use it if that stance changes.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — the proof resolver uses the listener's tuned network timeout
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a failed resolve refuses the one document
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [ ] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — the error codes are the registry's; vta-service still has to sign (see above)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no opt-out; resolver build failure stops the listener
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no new mutation
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — R3.7: reply shapes coordinated with the VTA via the break above
```

title: fix(inbound): believe a task-consent outcome only from the executor it answers
body:
> **Blocked on a release:** needs `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` **0.12.0** (OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#27) published to npm. `packages/core/package.json` asks for `^0.12.0`, but `package-lock.json` still resolves 0.11.0, so `npm ci` and CI fail until then. After publishing, run `npm install -w @openvtc/pnm-core @openvtc/vti-didcomm-js@^0.12.0` and commit the lockfile here.

## What changes

When the executor answers a `task-consent/decision`, a refusal raises "The VTA refused your approval" and drops the pending decision (`awaitingDecisions`). Until now that reply was believed whenever the message's `from` named *any* enrolled executor, and `from` is plaintext the sender writes. The wallet now keys on the sender the **transport authenticated**:

- **Transport → handler.** vti-didcomm-js 0.12 passes a `VerifiedSender` (the authcrypt `skid`'s DID) to `onInbound`, and `connectMediatorSession` passes it through. `MediatorConnection.waitFor` accepts the library's `from` filter. On the TSP path the sender is the one `unpackInboundTsp` proved.
- **Handler → pipeline.** `onInboundMessage` → `handleInbound` → `dispatchInbound` carry `senderDid`, and `PendingInbound` persists it. A message re-driven after an MV3 teardown is therefore attributed the same way it was on arrival.
- **`parseTaskConsentOutcome(message, { senderDid, expectedExecutorDid })`** (now async):
  - the authenticated sender must be **the executor the decision was sent to**. That executor is recorded as `AwaitingDecision.executorDid` at send time; when the thread is no longer remembered, the session's own VTA is used. Another enrolled executor is **not** accepted;
  - an in-band `issuer` naming anyone else → dropped;
  - if the reply carries a Data Integrity proof, it must verify (`assertionMethod`) as that executor, with `issuer` equal to it. The VTA signs its success responses but not its error documents (their proof is RECOMMENDED), so a missing proof is not a refusal in itself; the authenticated sender is the evidence then;
  - `message.from` is not consulted.
- **`parseTaskConsentGranted(message, vtaDid, senderDid)`** requires the authenticated sender to be the session's VTA. A missing sender is no longer tolerated.
- **Replies to this wallet's own requests** are accepted only from the peer each request went to. `DidcommMessageBridge.sendAndAwaitReply` now takes a **required** `from`, and `MediatorSessionBridge` hands it to the session's `waitFor` filter, so a frame on the thread from any other sender is never returned as the answer. Call sites:
  - `DidcommVtaTransport` → the VTA, plus the forwarding mediator when one is configured (its refusal of the hop is an answer the caller already maps);
  - `MediatorClient` → the mediator;
  - `loginViaDidcomm` → the RP.

  `InMemoryDidcommBridge` enforces the same rule.
- `taskConsentOutcomeThread()` lets the caller look up the awaiting decision (and its executor) before the reply is trusted.
- **Adapts to 0.12's exact-`skid` key selection.** `connectMediatorSession` seeds the VTA key with its `kid`, and `resolveSender(did, skid)` resolves that exact keyAgreement key (`resolveX25519KeyAgreementKey`).
- CLAUDE.md gains a section on this invariant and on the new `^0.12.0` floor.

## Breaking changes

- `parseTaskConsentOutcome` changed shape (async; `{ senderDid, expectedExecutorDid }` replaces `{ enrolledExecutorDids }`).
- `parseTaskConsentGranted` takes a third argument.
- `PendingInbound` has a required `senderDid`. Per this repo's no-compat-folds rule there is no migration for stored records: a record written by an older build re-drives with `senderDid` undefined, so its outcome or granted notice is dropped rather than believed. Request prompts are unaffected, because they are proof-verified.
- `MediatorConnection.onInbound`'s handler gets a third `sender` argument.
- `DidcommMessageBridge.sendAndAwaitReply`'s options, including `from`, are required. Any other bridge implementation must honour `from`.

## Tests

- `inbound.task-consent-outcome.mjs`:
  - refusal with `from` = VTA but a different authenticated sender (the forged notice) → `null`;
  - reply from another enrolled executor → `null`;
  - no authenticated sender → `null`;
  - a missing `from` doesn't matter when the sender is proven;
  - contradicting `issuer` → `null`;
  - signed response from the executor → believed;
  - proof by another key → `null`;
  - signed reply edited after signing → `null`;
  - thread lookup.
- `inbound.task-consent.mjs`: granted notice keyed on the authenticated sender, not `from`; no sender → dropped.
- `inbound.pending.mjs`: `senderDid` persists.
- `vta.bridge-peer.mjs` (new): `MediatorSessionBridge` passes `from` to `waitFor`; a VTA request names the VTA as its only peer; a mediator request names the mediator; the in-memory bridge refuses a reply from an unnamed peer. `rp-login.didcomm.mjs`: the login names the RP.
- `inbound.consent-schema.mjs`: updated to the new options.
- Run locally against a packed 0.12.0 tarball of vti-didcomm-js#27: `npm run lint` and `npm run build` are clean, and `npm test` passes (core 705/705, plus the other workspaces). `inbound.ack-ordering.mjs` still passes, so R1.6 ordering is unchanged.

## Release ordering

1. Merge vti-didcomm-js#27 and publish 0.12.0.
2. Refresh this PR's lockfile; CI goes green.
3. Merge this.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — proof verification resolves did:webvh via the existing resolver
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — persist still precedes resolve; senderDid is written in the same put
- [ ] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire change; depends on vti-didcomm-js 0.12
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no sender → dropped
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — inbound log shows the authenticated sender
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — senderDid is persisted with the message
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: fix(tui): stop adopting drift the panel cannot name a recipient for
body:
## Why

An adoption grants a right to whichever member linked the drift item's forge account. This panel sends `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1, and a 0.1 adopt does not name that member: the VTC picks the recipient from the account link as it stands when the task runs. If the account is relinked between the member reading the item and confirming, the right goes to someone the member never saw, and is published to the Trust Registry.

`git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.3 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#640) fixes this by naming the recipient (`subject`). VTI (companion draft PR, linked from #640's thread) serves 0.3 and refuses a 0.1 adopt with `unsupportedVersion`.

This panel cannot send a 0.3 adopt, because `git-ns/view` tells a member only their *own* account links. It cannot show who the recipient would be, so it cannot name them.

## What changed

- **`o` no longer arms an adoption.** It says the adoption would grant the projected right to the member who linked the account, that the panel can't see who that is, and where adopting works: the admin console, or `cnm git drift resolve … adopt --subject <DID>`.
  - When no right projects to the role, the existing "No git right corresponds…" message still comes first.
  - **Revert (`v`) is unchanged.**
- **Hints updated.** The key hint and the drift footer no longer offer `o adopt drift`. The footer says where to adopt instead.
- **openvtc-core** refuses to build a 0.1 adopt payload at all, so no future caller can send one by mistake.
- **Refusal message.** A VTC's refusal of a 0.1 adopt (`unsupportedVersion` naming drift/resolve 0.3) is now explained as exactly that. It no longer reads as "this community does not serve git namespaces".

## Behaviour change (deliberate, per the standing security/usability rule)

**This removes adopt from the TUI**, which #379 shipped. The choice was between keeping an adopt that could grant to someone the member never saw, and removing it with a pointer to the two places that can name the recipient. I removed it.

Bringing adopt back needs the member-to-account join visible to repository owners in `git-ns/view`. `git-ns/view` deliberately withholds that join today, so it's a separate privacy decision, raised on #640.

No dependency or version changes: this PR doesn't need the 0.3 types.

## Tests

- core: a 0.1 adopt is never built; the new refusal reads correctly; other `unsupportedVersion` refusals read as before.
- state: `o` arms nothing, names the right, and says where to adopt; `write` on an organisation still says "No git right".
- render: the hints offer revert only and point at the admin console or cnm for adopting.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally.

## How to test

On a repository you own with a `roleAdded` drift item: highlight it and press `o`. Nothing is armed, and the status says where to adopt. `v` then `y` still reverts.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing is sent for adopt
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): adopt fails closed
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: ci(vtc-admin-ui): run the admin console's unit tests
body:
## Summary

CI never ran the admin console's tests. `cargo build -p vtc-service` runs `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`), which only proves the console compiles. The vitest suite (400 tests in 35 files) and the `openapi.json` -> `src/lib/wire.ts` drift check only ever ran on a developer's machine.

### New job: `Test (VTC admin UI)`
- `actions/setup-node` (pinned SHA), node version from `vtc-service/admin-ui/.nvmrc`, `cache: npm` keyed on the lockfile
- `npm ci` (exact lockfile, and it fails if the lockfile disagrees with `package.json`)
- `npm run wire:check` (lint: generated wire types match `openapi.json`)
- `tsc -b --noEmit` (typecheck)
- zsh and fish installed (bounded, best-effort apt) so that the `shellQuote` round-trip tests in `src/plugins/repos/actions.test.ts` actually run. Without them the runner has only sh and bash, and those 6 tests were skipped without anyone noticing.
- `vitest run`
- No Rust, no system packages, no secrets. `timeout-minutes: 10`. Gated on the VTC closure (`affects.vtc_tests`), the same as `Test (VTC)`.

I checked the rest of the repo: this is the only JS/TS package with tests. `examples/vta-auth-demo` and `vtc-service/website-default` are static files with no package.json, and `vti-rooms-wasm` is a Rust crate that `Mobile build` already builds.

### `Test (VTC)` robustness (the #1725 timeout)
Across the 34 runs before this change, the job took 11-16 min: disk freeing 0.6-2.5 min, `cargo test` 8-12 min, and the no-op guard about 2 min. The run that timed out on #1725 was on a slow runner where every step took 2-3x as long (disk freeing 7.4 min, tests 21.1 min), and the 30-minute ceiling ran out during the no-op guard.
- **Disk freeing only runs when needed.** The job links two crates, and the image has about 100 GB free even after the removal, so about 80 GB before it. The `rm -rf` of Android, .NET and GHC now only runs when less than 30 GB is free.
- **The no-op guard (#1243) is fast now.** It re-runs the test step's own build with `--no-run` (one settle build, then the check) so it reuses that step's artifacts. Before, it ran `cargo build -p vtc-service`, which compiled vtc-service and its bin again in a different profile before it could check anything.
- **The job has its own cache key.** It used to share `cargo-test-` with `Test (workspace)`. It now also caches `~/.npm` for the `npm install` in build.rs.
- **Timeout raised from 30 to 40 min.** That leaves headroom for a slow runner, and a real hang still ends the job.

No crate versions changed.

## Test plan
- [x] Locally on origin/main: `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` all pass (400/400)
- [x] `scripts/check-workflow-action-pins.sh` passes
- [x] CI: `Test (VTC admin UI)` green. 400/400 pass, 0 skipped. The job takes about 1 min (`npm ci` 6 s, typecheck 8 s, zsh/fish 14 s, vitest 19 s).
- [x] CI: `Test (VTC)` green, including the no-op guard.

### Test (VTC) timings, before and after
| | disk freeing | `cargo test` | no-op guard | job total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (34 runs) | 0.6-2.5 min | 8-12 min | 1.3-2.3 min | 11.6-16.2 min |
| before (#1725 timeout) | 7.4 min | 21.1 min | cancelled | 30.3 min (limit) |
| after, run 1 | 0 s (86 GB free) | 11.5 min | 3 s | 11.9 min |
| after, run 2 | 0 s | 8.0 min | 2 s | 8.4 min |

title: feat(unpack)!: bind an authcrypt message's `from` to its sender key
body:
## What changes

**`unpack` binds an authcrypt message's `from` to the key that authenticated it.** It already required `apu == skid`, which pins the sender *key*. Nothing tied that key to the plaintext `from`, and consumers read `from`. DIDComm v2 requires `from` on an authcrypt message and requires `skid` to be a key of it; both are now enforced. A message whose `from` is missing, is a DID URL, or names any DID other than `DID(skid)` throws `SenderMismatchError` (`code: "E_SENDER_MISMATCH"`, R3.7).

**The authenticated sender is passed to consumers directly**, so none of them has to read `from`:

| API | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `unpack()` | `{ message, senderKid, authenticated, legacyKekUsed }`; anoncrypt `senderKid: undefined` | adds `senderDid`; anoncrypt `senderKid` and `senderDid` are both `null` |
| `onMessage` / `onMediatorMessage` | `(message, thid)` | `(message, thid, sender)`, where `sender` is a frozen `VerifiedSender { did, kid }` |
| `waitFor(thid, ms)` | resolves `message` | `waitFor(thid, ms, { from })` resolves `{ message, sender }`. Given `from` (a DID or a list of DIDs), only a reply authenticated as one of them claims the waiter; anyone else's frame on that thread goes to other waiters or the listener |
| `VtaMediatorClient.sendAndWait` | any reply on the thread | only a reply authenticated as its VTA; still returns the message |
| `unpackInbound` | — | also returns `senderDid` |

**Sender key selected by the exact `skid`.** `unpackInbound` now matches a `senderKeys` entry only when its `kid` equals the `skid`, so the reported `senderKid` is the key the envelope was actually authenticated with. A relative `#fragment` is resolved against the DID, and an entry without a `kid` matches nothing. `resolveSender` is called as `(did, skid)` and held to the same rule. `connectVtaViaMediator` uses the new `resolveX25519KeyAgreementKey(did, kid)`, which requires the key to be listed under `keyAgreement`.

**Refused frames are acked and dropped.** A frame that decrypts and is then refused for good (`E_SENDER_MISMATCH`, or anoncrypt carrying a `skid`, which returns the new `E_UNAUTHENTICATED_FRAME`) is logged via `onError` and acked, so it isn't redelivered forever. Other unpack failures, which may be transient, are still left queued.

JSDoc, the generated `types/`, and the README now call `message.from` sender-asserted plaintext, and say to authorise on `senderDid` / `sender.did`.

## Breaking changes (0.11.0 → 0.12.0)

- `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }` instead of the bare message.
- Anoncrypt `senderKid` is `null` (was `undefined`).
- Authcrypt with no `from`, or with a `from` that doesn't match, no longer unpacks. Through `MediatorSession` such a frame goes to `onError` and is not acked, like any other frame that fails to unpack.
- `senderKeys` entries need `kid`; `resolveSender` receives `(did, skid)` and must return that key.
- Consumer: **pnm-browser-plugin** (`connectMediatorSession` wraps `waitFor` and `onMessage`). Its adaptation is a separate draft PR, which needs this published first. CHANGELOG has migration notes.

## Tests

- `test/sender-binding.test.js` (13 tests, now timer-free: every wait is on the event asserted), including exact-skid selection (wrong kid, no kid, relative kid, resolver asked for the skid) and ack-and-drop of a forged-`from` frame and of an anoncrypt-with-skid frame. Original cases:
  - unpack: genuine authcrypt returns `senderDid`/`senderKid`; a forged `from` with a mismatched `skid` is refused with `E_SENDER_MISMATCH` (the attacker's key, the victim's DID); a missing `from` is refused; a DID-URL `from` is refused; anoncrypt gives a `null` sender whatever `from` says.
  - session: a genuine frame reaches `onMessage` with its verified sender and is acked; a forged-`from` frame is never delivered and never acked; `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }`; a waiter bound with `from` ignores an attacker's frame on its thread, which falls through to the listener, and still gets the genuine reply; a malformed `from` throws `TypeError`.
- Existing fixtures updated to the new shapes. Authcrypt fixtures that had no `from` now carry one.
- `npm test`: 304 tests, 297 pass, 7 skipped, 0 fail (the Rust round-trip suite skips locally and runs in CI). `npm run build:types` is clean.

## Release

Publish **0.12.0** after merge, because the plugin resolves from npm. `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and the CHANGELOG are bumped in this PR.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a refused frame is reported via onError; the loop continues
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — unchanged; a refused frame is never acked
- [ ] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire change; the JS consumer (pnm-browser-plugin) is updated in its own PR
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no opt-out
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: fix(vti-common)!: bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key used, before trusting a DIDComm sender
body:
Bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key used, before trusting a DIDComm sender.

An authcrypt (ECDH-1PU) JWE names its sender key twice in the protected header: `skid`, and `apu` (the PartyUInfo the key derivation is bound to). A conforming packer writes the same key id into both. The direct-unpack callers now require that they agree, and that the key the unpack metadata reports is that same key, before a sender is trusted.

## Changes

- **`vti_common::auth::verify_authcrypt_header(raw_jwe)`** (new). Reads the outer JWE (JSON or compact serialization), decodes the protected header, and for an ECDH-1PU layer requires: `skid` is a string DID URL with a `#fragment`, `apu` is present, and `BASE64URL-decode(apu)` is exactly the `skid` bytes (canonical encoding only). Returns the `skid`. Any other `alg` is refused, so authcrypt nested inside anoncrypt is not accepted on these paths.
- **`vti_common::auth::bind_authcrypt_sender(raw_jwe, message, metadata)`** now takes the raw envelope as well. It requires: the header check passes; the unpack wrapping is `authcrypt(plaintext)` or `authcrypt(sign(plaintext))` (never `anoncrypt(authcrypt(plaintext))`); `metadata.encrypted_from_kid == Some(skid)`; and `DID(from) == DID(skid)`.
- `AuthcryptError` gains variants for these cases and becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- Every caller is updated: VTA `POST /auth/` and `/auth/refresh`, VTC `POST /v1/auth/`, `/wallet/auth/` and their refresh routes, and VTA vault unseal (`vault/upsert` with a `didcomm-authcrypt` sealed secret).
- New `vti-common` feature `test-support` (`auth::authcrypt_test_support`) that builds authcrypt envelopes with a caller-chosen protected header. The `test-support` features of `vta-service` and `vtc-service` turn it on. Never enabled in a production build.

## Breaking changes

- **API:** `bind_authcrypt_sender` takes a new first argument, `raw_jwe: &str`. `AuthcryptError` has new variants and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **Wire:** the direct-unpack routes above now refuse:
  - a bare-DID `skid` (no `#fragment`);
  - an authcrypt header missing `skid` or `apu`, or whose `apu` does not encode `skid`;
  - authcrypt wrapped in anoncrypt (`anoncrypt(authcrypt(plaintext))`) posted directly to these routes.

  The messaging SDK's packer writes `skid = apu = <DID URL of the key-agreement key>` in every in-repo client, so the SDK login and refresh used by pnm, cnm, vta-sdk and vtc-client are unchanged. Third-party packers that emit any of the refused shapes will now get a 401.

## Tests

- `vti-common` unit tests cover: a `skid`/`apu` split; `skid` or `apu` missing; a non-string `skid`; a bare-DID `skid`; a near-miss or non-canonical `apu`; the compact serialization; an anoncrypt outer layer and nested authcrypt; a metadata key other than `skid`; and a `from` mismatch. One case runs a real envelope through the messaging library's decryptor, to show it decrypts before the header check refuses it.
- `vta-service/tests/auth_authcrypt_sender_binding.rs` and `vtc-service/tests/auth_authcrypt_sender_binding.rs` drive the real routes: `/auth/` on the VTA, and `/v1/auth/` and `/wallet/auth/` on the VTC. They use an offline ATM that decrypts real envelopes. Each test gets a challenge for an enrolled admin DID and answers it with a JWE whose `skid` names another party's key while `apu` and `from` name the admin. That is refused with 401, no token is issued, and the session stays unauthenticated. The same tests cover a missing `skid`, a missing `apu`, a bare-DID `skid`, and a consistent key whose `from` names a different DID. A genuine envelope packed by the library still logs in and gets tokens.

The check is local to VTI and does not depend on what the messaging library verifies, so it stays in place as defence in depth.

title: fix(vti-common)!: bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key used, before trusting a DIDComm sender (#1732)
body:
fix(vti-common)!: bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key used, before trusting a DIDComm sender (#1732)

An authcrypt (ECDH-1PU) JWE names its sender key twice in the protected
header: `skid` and `apu` (the PartyUInfo the key derivation is bound to). A
conforming packer writes the same key id into both. The direct-unpack callers
now require that the two agree, and that the key the unpack metadata reports is
that same key, before a sender is trusted.

- New `vti_common::auth::verify_authcrypt_header(raw_jwe)`: for an ECDH-1PU
  outer layer (JSON or compact serialization) requires `skid` to be a DID URL
  with a key fragment, `apu` to be present, and `BASE64URL-decode(apu)` to be
  exactly the `skid` bytes. Any other `alg` is refused, so authcrypt nested
  inside anoncrypt is not accepted on these paths.
- `bind_authcrypt_sender(raw_jwe, message, metadata)` now takes the raw
  envelope and requires: the header check; an `authcrypt(plaintext)` or
  `authcrypt(sign(plaintext))` wrapping; `encrypted_from_kid == Some(skid)`;
  and `DID(from) == DID(skid)`.
- Callers updated: VTA `/auth/`, `/auth/refresh`, vault unseal; VTC
  `/v1/auth/`, `/v1/wallet/auth/` and refresh.
- New `vti-common` `test-support` feature with builders for authcrypt
  envelopes with a caller-chosen protected header; route tests on both
  services.

BREAKING CHANGE: `bind_authcrypt_sender` takes a new first argument
`raw_jwe: &str`; `AuthcryptError` gains variants and is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
The direct-unpack routes refuse a bare-DID `skid`, a missing `skid` or `apu`,
an `apu` that does not encode `skid`, and `anoncrypt(authcrypt(plaintext))`.

title: refactor(vti-common): move the task-consent core out of vta-policy so the VTC can share it (VTI-APV-014)
body:
First of four PRs for **VTI-APV-014** at the VTC. The requirement: creating an entry with unrestricted act scope, or widening an entry to it, needs consent from a party other than the requester. The design is in `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-operation-bound-step-up.md` §4.

The VTC is to use the same `task-consent/*` ceremony the VTA runs (VTI-VTC-020: one model, not a parallel one). The ceremony's data layer lives in `vta-policy`, which the VTC cannot depend on. This PR moves it to `vti-common` so the VTC can reuse it instead of copying it. It is a move only, with no behaviour change.

## What moves

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `vta-policy/src/consent.rs` | `vti_common::task_consent` |
| `vta-policy/src/effects.rs` | `vti_common::task_consent::effects` |

- Both files are moved with `git mv`, so their history follows.
- `vta_policy::{consent, effects}` re-export the new modules, so every existing path still resolves.
- `vta-policy` no longer needs `multibase` or `serde_json_canonicalizer`, and `vti-common` gains `serde_json_canonicalizer`.

## One copy of the digest

The VTC's operation-bound step-up (`vtc-service/src/acl/bound_step_up.rs`) carried a byte-for-byte copy of the digest function, differing only in its domain tag (`vtc/step-up/v1\0`). The construction is now public as `domain_digest(domain, type_uri, payload, salt)`, and the step-up calls it.

## Evidence that no digest changed

- `digest_matches_its_pinned_vectors` pins the task-consent digest and the step-up digest, salted and unsalted, against vectors computed independently in Python.
- That matters because the digest keys stored pendings, grants and step-up marks, and it is what approvers sign. A pending or mark in flight across an upgrade still resolves.
- The `vta/task-consent/v1\0` tag is kept for the same reason. It separates this digest from other digests, not one node from another, because a pending never leaves the node that minted it.

## Checks

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4913 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 2158 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Next in the series

2. The VTC consent gate and ceremony on `acl/grant` and `acl/change-role`, with the per-community threshold.
3. Attrition checks, plus two paths that confer unrestricted admin today without any check: `vtc/admin/invites/create`, and an `acl/grant` rewrite that narrows an unrestricted admin.
4. A co-admin at install, and audit rows for the offline ACL writers.

title: fix(vta): a DIDComm reply is accepted only from the peer it was asked of
body:
fix(vta): a DIDComm reply is accepted only from the peer it was asked of

`DidcommMessageBridge.sendAndAwaitReply` correlated a reply by thread
id alone. A thread id is the id of a message this wallet sent through
the mediator, not a secret, so any authenticated sender that learned
it could have its frame returned as the answer.

`sendAndAwaitReply` now takes a required `from` — the DID(s) the reply
must be authenticated as — and `MediatorSessionBridge` hands it to the
session's `waitFor` filter (vti-didcomm-js 0.12), which leaves anyone
else's frame on the thread unclaimed. Each call site names its
addressee:

- `DidcommVtaTransport`: the VTA, plus the forwarding mediator when one
  is configured (its refusal of the hop is an answer the caller maps);
- `MediatorClient`: the mediator;
- `loginViaDidcomm`: the RP.

`InMemoryDidcommBridge` enforces the same rule, failing fast on a reply
from an unnamed peer.

title: fix(inbound): believe a task-consent outcome only from the executor it answers
body:
fix(inbound): believe a task-consent outcome only from the executor it answers

The executor's answer to a `task-consent/decision` is read by
`parseTaskConsentOutcome`, and a refusal both raises "The VTA refused
your approval" and drops the decision the wallet is waiting on. It was
believed when the message's `from` named any enrolled executor, and
`from` is plaintext the sender writes.

It now keys on the sender the transport authenticated:

- `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` 0.12 delivers a `VerifiedSender` (the
  authcrypt `skid`'s DID) to `onInbound` handlers; `connectMediatorSession`
  passes it through, and its `waitFor` takes the library's `from` filter.
  The TSP path uses the sender `unpackInboundTsp` proved.
- `onInboundMessage` → `handleInbound` → `dispatchInbound` carry that
  `senderDid`, and `PendingInbound` persists it, so a message re-driven
  after an MV3 teardown is attributed exactly as it was on arrival.
- `parseTaskConsentOutcome(message, { senderDid, expectedExecutorDid })`
  requires the authenticated sender to be the executor the decision was
  sent to (`AwaitingDecision.executorDid`, recorded at send time; the
  session's VTA when the thread is no longer remembered). Another
  enrolled executor is not accepted. An in-band `issuer` that names
  someone else is dropped, and a reply that carries a Data Integrity
  proof must verify as that executor. Error documents are unsigned by
  the executor, so a missing proof is not itself a refusal. It is now
  async; `taskConsentOutcomeThread` exposes the thread lookup.
- `parseTaskConsentGranted` takes the authenticated sender and no
  longer tolerates a missing one.

`@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` is raised to `^0.12.0`. That release is not
yet published, so the lockfile still resolves 0.11.0 and must be
refreshed once it is.

title: feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm; REST is optional
body:
## What

verify-trust no longer needs the Trust Registry's REST interface. It queries over the binding the registry's DID document advertises, preferring **TSP, then DIDComm, then HTTPS**. There is **no fallback**: if the chosen binding fails, the run fails. A blocked mediator never downgrades the check to HTTPS.

### Choosing the binding
- **CLI:** `--transport <auto|tsp|didcomm|https>`.
  - `auto` is the default and uses the strict preference order above.
  - Naming a binding the registry doesn't advertise, or one this build can't speak, fails closed and names what each side offers.
  - `https` uses the `#rest` endpoint from the DID document.
  - `--registry-url` stays the explicit HTTPS override and implies `https`. Combining it with `tsp` or `didcomm` is an error.
- **Action:** a `transport` input, validated, and passed to the CLI only when it is not `auto`.
- **Workflows the bridge writes, and `vgi repo init`:** `[verify_trust] transport` and `--verify-trust-transport`. The input is written into the workflow only when it isn't `auto`, so existing workflows don't drift.

### CI runs (GitHub required and in-repo workflows, Forgejo workflow, local CLI)
- **Per-run identity:** each run generates a fresh `did:peer:2` in memory. It is never written to disk or logs, and its keys are removed from the resolver when the run ends. Its service entry names the registry's mediator, so replies route back.
- **Accepting a DIDComm reply:** the envelope is read packed and checked before it is unpacked. The sender key id must be bound to the key the key agreement actually used:
  - the envelope is authcrypt (`ECDH-1PU`);
  - `skid` and `apu` are both present, and `apu` decodes to exactly `skid`;
  - the key belongs to the registry's DID;
  - neither member appears outside the protected header.

  After unpacking, the message's sender must be that key and `from` must name the registry. A signature by anyone else refuses the reply. The registry does not sign its replies today, so authcrypt is the proof of origin.
- **Accepting a TSP reply:** the sender VID whose signature was verified must be the registry DID. The run forms a relationship with the registry (Rev 3 §7.2.2) before the first query.
- **Query ids:** every query goes out under a fresh random UUID v4, and the reply's thread must match it.
- **Failing closed:** each of these makes that signer's commits `registryUnavailable`:
  - the mediator refuses the run's DID;
  - the registry or its mediator sends a problem report whose sender passes the same check;
  - no proven answer arrives within 30 seconds.

  A problem report from an unproven sender is ignored and does not end the run.

### Bridge-posted checks
These use the registry's `#rest` endpoint (HTTPS) **until the messaging SDK's authcrypt fix is released**. The bridge's mediator session delivers replies already unpacked, so it can't run the envelope check above. The bridge's DIDComm registry channel from the first revision of this PR is removed for now. A follow-up PR will re-enable bridge-DID DIDComm registry queries on the fixed SDK and keep this PR's header check as defence in depth. Until then, the registry must publish `#rest` for bridge-posted checks.

The bridge's job path is unaffected: a job is accepted only on a Data Integrity proof by a key of the VTC DID, which must also be the document's issuer.

### Also
- `UNKNOWN-KEY` now names the usual cause: the signer rotated their key, so the commit needs re-signing with the current key. It includes the re-sign recipe.
- The RUNBOOK now says to re-sign the commits in your open pull requests after rotating your signing key.

## Breaking changes / release note
- **CI binding change:** a registry that advertises `#tsp` or `#didcomm` is now queried over it, not over `#rest`. For that to work, the registry's mediator must admit unknown DIDs:
  - `mediator_acl_mode = explicit_deny`;
  - a `global_acl_default` with an open inbox; the narrowest that works is `DENY_ALL,LOCAL,SEND_MESSAGES,RECEIVE_MESSAGES,SEND_FORWARDED,RECEIVE_FORWARDED,MODE_EXPLICIT_DENY`.

  The mediator's shipped default gives a new DID a closed inbox, so runs fail `registryUnavailable` until this is changed. To keep today's HTTPS behaviour, set `transport: https`. The release note text is in the RUNBOOK.
- **Library API:**
  - new: `Registry`, `TransportSelector`, `verify_prepared_with`, and `authcrypt_sender_kid`;
  - `VerifyTrustArgs` gains `transport`;
  - `discover_registry_route` takes a selector.
- **Bridge config:** `[verify_trust] transport` is new. A `[checks] transport` key is rejected.

## Dependencies
- `didcomm` and `tsp` are default features of verify-trust. `--no-default-features` builds an HTTPS-only verifier.
- TSP adds `affinidi-tsp` and its crypto dependencies.
- `trust-tasks-trql` is an alias for the trust-tasks-rs 0.21 node that trql-client already resolves, so no new version enters the tree.
- Dev-only: `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` 0.9.17 and `sha2`.

## Tests
- **Unit tests:**
  - binding selection, including named transports, bindings the registry doesn't advertise, bindings this build can't speak, and `--registry-url` with a conflicting transport;
  - the reply rule;
  - the authcrypt binding: a `skid`/`apu` mismatch in either direction, a missing `skid` or `apu`, anoncrypt, and sender members outside the protected header;
  - query ids are random UUID v4s;
  - the run identity;
  - failing closed.
- **Against an in-process mediator:**
  - DIDComm and TSP round trips;
  - a correlated reply from another DID is ignored;
  - a reply sealed with another DID's key whose party info names the registry's key is never believed. Disabling the binding check makes this test fail with `authorized: true`.
  - an `ExplicitAllow` mediator and a mediator on the shipped ACL default both fail closed.
- **Workflow templates and bridge config:** the transport input and the config option.
- **Local runs:** fmt, clippy with warnings as errors (workspace, plus the verify-trust feature subsets), `cargo test --workspace`, and the 1.95 MSRV check all pass.
