title: feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm; REST is optional (#88)
body:
feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm; REST is optional (#88)

* feat(verify-trust): query the Trust Registry over TSP or DIDComm

The registry's REST interface is now optional. Discovery takes the
highest-preference binding the registry's DID document advertises and
this build speaks — TSP, then DIDComm, then HTTPS — instead of bailing
on a registry that advertises no #rest service.

Over the mediator bindings each run queries as a fresh did:peer:2,
minted in memory on the first query (never written to disk, logs or the
environment) with a DIDComm service naming the registry's mediator so
the reply routes back. The verdict rests on the registry's key: a reply
is believed only when the binding authenticated it as the registry DID
(authcrypt sender key and `from`, or the TSP-verified sender VID) and it
answers the query asked. verify-trust implements these transports itself
because trql-client's route replies by threadId alone.

A mediator that refuses the run's DID, a problem report, or no proven
answer within 30s fails the signer's commits as registryUnavailable and
the session stops asking for the rest of the run. A range with nothing
to ask about never opens a session.

--registry-url stays as the explicit HTTPS override and behaves exactly
as before. `didcomm` and `tsp` are default features; HTTPS-only builds
use --no-default-features. The library gains `Registry` (HTTPS, an
ephemeral sender, or a caller-owned `RegistryChannel`) and
`verify_prepared_with`; `verify_prepared` and `resolve_registry_endpoint`
keep their HTTPS meaning.

Tests cover selection for TSP-only and DIDComm-only documents, the reply
rule, the run identity, fail-closed on an unreachable mediator, and —
against an in-process mediator — DIDComm and TSP round trips, a
correlated reply from another DID being ignored, and ExplicitAllow and
shipped-default-ACL mediators failing closed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): query the registry as the bridge's DID over DIDComm

The bridge-posted check now reaches a registry that advertises DIDComm
over the bridge's existing mediator session, as the bridge's own stable
DID, preferring it to HTTPS. It does not open a second session: the
mediator permits one websocket per DID, and a second would take the job
link's slot.

Replies arrive on the same inbound stream as jobs. Bridge::handle_inbound
offers each document to RegistryReplies::route first, which takes it only
when authcrypt proved it came from the registry's DID and it answers a
query in flight; everything else goes to the job path unchanged. A link
that is down, a refusal, or no proven answer in 30s is
registryUnavailable. The start-up git.commit.sign grant probe uses the
same binding.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: the registry's REST interface is optional for the commit check

verify-trust README, RUNBOOK, BRIDGE.md, the top-level README and the
action's registry-url input now describe binding selection, the per-run
did:peer, what the registry's mediator must allow for it (explicit_deny,
an open-inbox global_acl_default, and the forwarded bits for DIDComm),
fail-closed behaviour, the absence of an automatic HTTPS fallback, and
the bridge querying as its own DID.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat: explicit registry transport selector; no fallback

verify-trust gains --transport <auto|tsp|didcomm|https>. auto keeps the strict
TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS preference with no fallback; a named binding the
registry does not advertise, or this build cannot speak, fails closed naming
both sides. https uses the DID document's #rest endpoint; --registry-url
implies https and refuses tsp/didcomm.

The action takes a matching transport input (validated, passed only when not
auto). The workflows the bridge and vgi repo init write carry it from
[verify_trust] transport / --verify-trust-transport, written only when not
auto so existing workflows do not drift. The bridge-posted check takes
[checks] transport (auto = DIDComm > HTTPS; tsp is refused).

UNKNOWN-KEY now names the usual cause, a key rotated since signing, and how to
re-sign; the runbook says to re-sign open pull requests after rotating a key
and carries the release note for the behaviour change.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(verify-trust): bind the authcrypt sender key id to the key actually used

A DIDComm reply was believed on the unpacked sender the messaging SDK
reports. That sender comes from the envelope's party info (`apu`), while
the key the SDK looks up comes from `skid`, and nothing tied the two
together. The DIDComm transport now reads each envelope packed and checks
its protected header before unpacking: it must be authcrypt (ECDH-1PU),
with both `skid` and `apu` present, `apu` decoding to exactly `skid`, the
key belonging to the registry DID, and neither member repeated outside
the protected header. The unpacked sender must then be that key, `from`
must name the registry, and a signature by anyone else refuses the reply.
The registry does not sign replies today, so authcrypt remains the proof
of origin.

Every mediated query now goes out under a fresh UUID v4 from the OS
CSPRNG, whatever id the client chose (trql-client falls back to a clock
and counter id in the build verify-trust uses), and the reply must carry
that id as its thread.

A problem report ends a query only if its sender passes the same check
and is the registry or its mediator. Unauthenticated DIDComm frames on a
TSP session are ignored. Neither can latch the session any more.

The bridge-posted check goes back to HTTPS only. The bridge's mediator
session hands it replies already unpacked, so it cannot check the
binding above and cannot prove a reply came from the registry. The
bridge's DIDComm registry channel, and the inbound hook that fed it, are
removed. The bridge's job path is unaffected: it accepts a document only
if a Data Integrity proof verifies against a key of the VTC DID, which
must also be the document's issuer. The authcrypt sender is an extra
refusal condition on that path, never a reason to accept.

Tests: the binding is exercised on crafted headers (a mismatch in either
direction, missing skid or apu, anoncrypt, sender members outside the
protected header), and query ids are checked to be random. A regression
test against the in-process mediator sends a reply sealed with another
DID's key whose party info names the registry's key: the query times out
and is never answered.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(unpack)!: bind an authcrypt message's `from` to its sender key
body:
feat(unpack)!: bind an authcrypt message's `from` to its sender key

`unpack` already required `apu == skid`, which pins the key an authcrypt
envelope was made with. Nothing tied that key to the `from` the plaintext
carries, and consumers read `from`. Both halves of DIDComm v2's rule are
now enforced: an authcrypt message whose `from` is missing, is a DID URL,
or names another DID than the `skid`'s is refused with
`SenderMismatchError` (`code: "E_SENDER_MISMATCH"`).

The authenticated sender is also handed to consumers directly, so none
has to read `from`:

- `unpack` returns `senderDid` beside `senderKid`; both are `null` for
  anoncrypt (previously `senderKid` was `undefined`).
- `MediatorSession` passes a frozen `VerifiedSender` `{ did, kid }` as a
  third argument to `onMessage` / `onMediatorMessage`.
- `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }` and takes `{ from }`, a DID or
  list of DIDs a reply must be authenticated as; a message on the thread
  from anyone else is left for other waiters and the listener.
- `VtaMediatorClient.sendAndWait` only accepts a reply from its VTA.

`from` is documented as sender-asserted plaintext throughout (JSDoc,
generated types, README).

BREAKING CHANGE: `waitFor` resolves `{ message, sender }` instead of the
message; anoncrypt `senderKid` is `null`; authcrypt without a matching
`from` no longer unpacks. Release 0.12.0 (+ CHANGELOG, with migration
notes).

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): revert drift on a repository through git-ns/drift/resolve
body:
## What

The repository Drift card listed what the bridge reported but the only way to revert was "remove the role on the forge by hand". The VTC already serves `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1 (`vtc-service/src/git_ns/drift.rs`, #1703) and `cnm git drift resolve` already signs it. This PR adds the console action. No server change.

- **Revert action** (`repos/RepoDetail.tsx`): every drift item gets a **Revert to the VTC's state** button. It opens `RevertDriftDialog` (`repos/dialogs.tsx`), which shows the item, says what the bridge will do, and takes an optional reason. That builds `driftRevertTask` (`repos/actions.ts`):
  - payload `{ resource, action: "revert", drift: { type, account?, observed? }, reason? }`. The item is selected as the spec selects it: by `type`, by account (`forge` + `id`, with `login` for display) for the role types, and by the `observed` value read here. If the forge has changed since, the VTC refuses with `driftNotFound` instead of reverting a state nobody looked at.
  - command `cnm git drift resolve <resource> revert --type=… [--account-id=… --account-login=…] [--observed=…] [--reason=…]`, with every value quoted by the fish-safe `shellQuote` from #1723.
  - what the bridge does, per type: `roleAdded` removes the role (bridge job 0.2 `removeAccounts`), `roleRemoved`/`roleChanged` re-project roles, `requiredCheckMissing`/`protectionWeakened` re-apply the ruleset and required check, and `bootstrapMissing` re-runs the bootstrap plan.
- **Shown only to roles the VTC accepts** (`revertStanding` in `repos/model.ts`). It mirrors `drift_resolve` + `revert`:
  - the namespace is in bridge mode (manual mode answers `notRevertible`)
  - the repository is active or orphaned
  - the session's DID holds `git.repo.own` on the repository, explicitly (an owner) or implied (a namespace admin). A console key acts as that DID (`acting_as`).
  - a revert that weighs as revoking `own` (taking an `admin` role off an org repository) also needs a community administrator, as `consent_gate` requires under `elevated_requires_admin`. The console already assumes that setting is on for every elevated task.

  Anyone else sees why they can't revert, plus the `cnm` command to hand to an owner.
- **Consent mirror**: the server gates a revert as `consent_gate("right.revoke", impact)`, so `consentClass("drift.resolve", impact)` classes it the same way: elevated for `own`, normal otherwise. `projectedRight` and `driftRevertImpact` mirror `projected_right`, including personal accounts, where `write` is maintain and `admin` projects nothing.
- `useViewerDid()` (`lib/viewer.ts`) reads the session subject from the shell's whoami cache. It is the same observe-only query as `useIsSuperAdmin`.
- The `git-ns/drift/resolve/0.1` URI is added to `trust_task_manifest`'s `SIGNED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, and the activity feed now names `gitNs.drift.resolved`.

Adopt is unchanged: it still builds a `right/grant`.

## Tests

- actions:
  - payload and command for a role item and for a ruleset item (no account)
  - elevated class for an `admin` role, normal for re-projection and on a personal account
  - shell safety for the resource, account id, login, observed and reason
- model:
  - `projectedRight` for org and personal accounts
  - `revertStanding` for owner, namespace admin, non-holder, unknown viewer, the elevated case, manual mode, and archived vs orphaned repositories
  - consent mirror
- RepoDetail:
  - an owner reverts through the form, and the sign dialog shows the exact command and document without sending anything
  - a non-holder, and a viewer with no whoami, get no button but do get the command
  - an `admin`-role revert is hidden from an owner who is not a community administrator, and shown to one who is, as elevated

`npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npm run wire:check` and `npx vitest run` (400 tests) pass, as do `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest` and `cargo fmt --check`.

## How to test (test guide ROLE-13)

1. Bridge-mode namespace, active repository. On the forge, weaken the ruleset or remove the required check, or add a collaborator role. Wait for the bridge to report drift.
2. Admin console → Repos → the repository. The Drift card lists the item.
3. Signed in as an owner or namespace admin: **Revert to the VTC's state** → optional reason → **Build the revert**. Sign in the browser (console key), or run the `cnm git drift resolve …` command shown.
4. The item leaves the outstanding drift (sync `pending`), the bridge re-applies the state, and the follow-up inspect returns it to `in sync`. `gitNs.drift.resolved` appears in the activity.
5. Signed in as an admin who holds no git right on the repository: no button. You see the reason and the command.

title: feat(tui): resolve drift from the Repos panel (revert or adopt)
body:
## What

On a repository screen the TUI listed drift but said "a namespace admin adopts or reverts drift from the admin console". An owner of the repository, or a namespace admin, can now resolve it in the panel (test guide **TUI-10**) with `git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1, which the VTC already serves (VTI `vtc-service/src/git_ns/drift.rs`, #1703):

- **`v` revert**: the bridge re-applies what the community's rights call for, and no right changes. Per item type:
  - `roleAdded`: takes the unprojected forge role off
  - `roleRemoved` / `roleChanged`: re-projects roles
  - `requiredCheckMissing` / `protectionWeakened`: re-applies the ruleset and required check
  - `bootstrapMissing`: re-runs the bootstrap plan
- **`o` adopt (accept)**: records a role added or raised on the forge as the right it projects. On an organisation `admin` becomes owner and `maintain` becomes maintainer; on a personal account `write` becomes maintainer. The VTC records it as the resolver's own grant. Whether the account is linked to a member is the VTC's call (`accountNotLinked`).

### Selection and consent
- Drift rows now render after the people and take the highlight: ↓ past the last person reaches them, marked `▸`. An item is selected as the spec selects it: `type`, the account (`forge` + `id`, `login` for display) for role items, and the `observed` value read. If the forge has changed since, the VTC refuses with `driftNotFound` instead of acting on a state nobody looked at.
- Both keys arm a confirmation and send only on `y`. The consent class follows what the VTC gates each action as:
  - a revert is gated as the revocation it amounts to, which is elevated when it takes an owner-level (`admin`) role off
  - an adopt is gated as the grant it records

  When only a community administrator may do it (`elevated_requires_admin`), the confirmation says so.
- The actions are offered only to an owner or namespace admin (`governs`), and a revert only where the namespace has a bridge (manual mode would answer `notRevertible`). Each declared refusal code (`driftNotFound`, `notAdoptable`, `accountNotLinked`, `noMatchingRight`, `notRevertible`) gets an explanation with the key to try next.

### Code
- `openvtc-core::git_ns` gains `Request::DriftResolve`, `Reply::DriftResolved`, `DriftRef`, `DriftAction` and `DriftAccount`. It also gains `projected_right`, `adoptable_right`, `revert_weighs_as` and `has_bridge`, which mirror the VTC's `git_ns::drift::{projected_right, revert}`. The payload goes through the generated `drift::resolve::v0_1::Payload`, so the schema is checked before sending. An adopt without `observed` is refused locally.
- **Dependency**: `trust-tasks-rs` and `trust-tasks-capability-client` (and so `-didcomm`, `-https`, `-proof` and `-tsp`) move from 0.22.3 to 0.22.7. This is a patch on the same line, and the one the VTI workspace is on; 0.22.4 is the first to generate `git-ns/drift/*`. The `Cargo.toml` note is updated. `cargo tree -d -e normal,build,dev` still shows one `trust-tasks-rs`.

**No VTI crate release is needed**: nothing here depends on a new VTI crate. The community's VTC must be running a build with #1703 (`git-ns/drift/resolve`). An older one answers `unsupportedType`, and the panel already explains that.

## Tests

- core:
  - a drift item read as its selector
  - payload for a role revert (with a trimmed reason) and for a ruleset revert (no account, blank reason dropped)
  - an adopt without `observed` is refused before sending
  - projected, adoptable and weighted rights for organisation and personal accounts, plus the consent class
  - typed `DriftResolved` reply
  - every `drift/resolve` declared code is explained
- state:
  - the highlight runs from the people into the drift
  - a non-owner is refused
  - an owner arms a normal revert of a ruleset item, and adopt is refused for it
  - taking an `admin` role off is armed as elevated and names the community administrator
  - a `maintain` role adopts as maintainer, and `write` on an organisation adopts nothing
  - a manual namespace has no bridge to revert with
  - the reply reports success and triggers a fresh read
- keys: `v` / `o` are mapped on a repository and not on the list
- render: drift rows show the highlight and the `v revert drift   o adopt drift` hints, and no longer point at the admin console

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` pass locally.

## How to test (TUI-10)

1. Use a bridge-mode namespace with a repository you own (or a namespace you admin). On the forge, add a collaborator role or weaken the ruleset, and wait for the drift report.
2. Communities → the community → `r` → the repository. The *Drift from the forge* section lists the item.
3. Press ↓ past the people to highlight it, then `v`. The confirmation says what the bridge will do. Press `y`. The status reads "Reverted: …"; press `r` to see the item gone and, after the bridge's inspect, the repository back in sync.
4. For a role added on the forge whose account a member has linked, press `o` then `y`. The member now holds the projected right.
5. As a member who only commits there, `v` and `o` explain that it is an owner's decision.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the send reuses the existing DIDComm path and its 30 s reply window
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing is patched locally; the view is read again after the reply
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retry, and a timeout says to refresh before trying again
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): generated types from trust-tasks-rs 0.22.7
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): "Reverted" is said only on the VTC's response, and it says the bridge is re-applying, not that it is done
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): the VTC is the record; a lost reply times out and asks for a refresh
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(vgi-forge): review follow-ups for #84
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #84 (merged before these landed).

## Changes
- **EffectiveRights serde round trip (published crate).** Before this, serialisation wrote every held right, including the ones implication adds, and deserialisation ran `from_granted` over that list. So `[git.ns.admin]` came back as a value that projects `own`, i.e. repo `admin`.
  - It now serialises the canonical grants (`EffectiveRights::granted()`): `ns.admin`, or else `repo.create`, plus the highest repository right granted in its own name.
  - A round trip is now the identity. Equality holds exactly when the canonical grants are equal: `[ns.admin]` and `[ns.admin, own]` are different values.
  - **Wire change:** implied rights are no longer listed. For example, `[maintain]` now serialises as `["git.repo.maintain"]`.
- **Quoted `runs-on:`** in the Forgejo workflow, so labels such as `-`, `null`, `true`, `1` and `1.5` stay YAML strings.
- **Docs** (the `desired_roles` comment and BRIDGE.md §6c):
  - An account listed with no role loses *any* direct collaborator role, including one given by hand on the forge.
  - The namespace-admin guarantee only holds end to end once the VTC sends `git.ns.admin` for namespace admins. Today it sends them as `git.repo.own`; a VTI fix is in progress.

## Tests
- Serde round trips for `[]`, `[NsAdmin]`, `[NsAdmin, RepoOwn]`, `[NsAdmin, RepoMaintain]` and more.
- The runner label parses as a YAML string for tricky labels.
- A namespace admin's hand-given repo admin role is DELETEd by a projection.
- The Forgejo merge allow-list:
  - `maintain = "admin"`: admin, and on the list
  - `maintain = "write"`: write, and the list is not touched
  - default: write, and on the list

The Forgejo test bridge moved into `tests/common` so both test files can use it.

`cargo test --workspace`, clippy (`-D warnings`, all features) and fmt pass locally.

title: fix(vgi-bridge): guard identity mint --replace (review follow-ups for #85)
body:
Review follow-ups for #85. That PR merged before these fixes landed.

## Changes

1. **`identity mint --replace` is guarded.** Replacing the identity isn't a key rotation: the new DID is a different bridge. The guards apply to `mint --replace` and to an `identity import` of a *different* DID.
   - **Backup required.** `--backup <file>` must be given. The current identity's bundle is written there (0600, `O_EXCL`) before it is replaced, and the old DID is printed.
   - **Explicit confirmation.** The command refuses, and lists the namespaces (id, resource, state), while the store holds namespaces bound or being bound to the current DID. It also refuses when the current DID wasn't minted by the bridge (a VTA-provisioned `did:webvh`). `--abandon-current-did` overrides both.
   - **Consequences printed.** Every replace, and every refusal, says what a new DID breaks:
     - the VTC's `[git_ns] bridges` must change;
     - the VTC accepts a namespace's results and events only from the DID it bound;
     - the registry's `git.commit.sign` service grant is held by the old DID, so Dependabot commits the new one re-signs fail the check;
     - with no re-attach yet, re-binding needs an unbind, which revokes every right in the namespace.
   - **Mismatch error reordered.** Setting `mediator_did` back to the DID's mediator is now the first fix offered. It is the only one that keeps bound namespaces working.
2. **`identity export` writes the stored bundle verbatim.** An imported bundle's keys are all exported, including a P-256 key, which used to fail the export with a misleading error. A `did:key` seed is still exported as its two keys.
3. **No partial file after a failed export.** If writing or syncing the export fails, the partial file is removed, so a retry isn't refused over it.

Docs: BRIDGE.md §2 gets a paragraph on replacing the identity. The `mint --replace` references in BRIDGE.md, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md and RUNBOOK.md now include `--backup <file>`.

## Behaviour change (from #85, noted here)

`identity import`, and `run`, now refuse a `did:peer` whose document doesn't name the configured `mediator_did` as its `DIDCommMessaging` endpoint. A hand-made `did:peer` imported with an `https` endpoint, or with several services where the DIDComm one names another mediator, is refused. Before #85 it would have been accepted. `did:webvh` identities are not checked this way; their host publishes the document.

## Tests

- `run_refuses_a_did_peer_that_names_another_mediator`
- `export_refuses_to_write_through_a_symlink` (nothing is written to the link target)
- `a_did_peer_advertises_didcomm_through_its_mediator` now also checks that the resolved `keyAgreement` is the X25519 secret's id (`#key-2`) and that `assertionMethod` is `#key-1`, and that the mismatch error offers `mediator_did` first
- `mint_replace_refuses_while_namespaces_are_bound_to_the_did`: the refusal names the namespace, writes no backup and keeps the identity. With `--abandon-current-did` it replaces, and the backup holds the old DID.
- `a_vta_provisioned_did_exports_verbatim_and_is_not_replaced_unasked`: a did:webvh bundle with Ed25519, X25519 and P-256 keys exports byte-for-byte as imported, and replacing it needs the flag
- The existing CLI flow checks that `--backup` is required, that the consequences are printed, and that the backup restores the old DID through `import`.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): mint a did:peer the VTC can reach, and export the identity
body:
## Problem

A bridge on a `did:key` cannot receive jobs. The VTC resolves the bridge's DID and picks a transport from the services its DID document advertises (`vtc-service` `git_ns::bridge::MessagingBridgeClient::select`, TSP > DIDComm by service type). A `did:key` document has no services, so every job fails with `noMatchingProtocol`. BRIDGE.md listed this as a limit.

## Change

- **`did:peer:2` identity.** `vgi-bridge init`, and the new `vgi-bridge identity mint [--replace]`, mint a `did:peer:2`. Its identifier carries the Ed25519 signing/authentication key, the X25519 key-agreement key and a single `DIDCommMessaging` service naming the configured `mediator_did`. The VTC's current selection then picks DIDComm through that mediator, with no change to the VTC or the protocol. The VTC's `TrustTaskVmResolver` and verify-trust both resolve `did:peer` locally, so Trust Task proofs and re-signed Dependabot commits verify. room-host already does the same thing for the same reason.
  - The service is DIDComm only. The bridge speaks no TSP, and advertising TSP would make the VTC prefer it.
  - A `did:peer` names its mediator for good. So `run` and `identity import` refuse a `did:peer` whose mediator doesn't match the config. Without that, jobs would be delivered to a mediator the bridge isn't listening on.
  - Mint refuses a DID longer than 1000 bytes, the limit DID resolvers enforce. Past it, both ends fail with a timeout and nothing names the cause.
  - `run` warns about a `did:key` left by an earlier release.
- **`identity export <file>`** writes the identity's secrets bundle in the format `identity import` reads. The file is created 0600 and never overwrites an existing one. This lets you back up the bridge's DID separately from the store. The DID matters because the VTC records it per namespace and accepts results only from it, the registry service grant names it, and re-signed commits carry it.
- **Docs.** BRIDGE.md §2/§5, RUNBOOK.md §8i and the error table, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md §2.2 and the crate README no longer carry the `did:key` limit, and they now cover the identity backup. The lost-store re-attach limit is **still documented**: fixing it needs a VTC-side protocol and rights decision, which is tracked separately.

## Tests

- `identity::tests::the_vtc_selects_didcomm_for_a_did_peer_and_nothing_for_a_did_key` follows the VTC's own path: `DIDCacheClient` resolve, `ServiceCapabilities::from_did_document`, `select_protocol`. It gets DIDComm through the mediator for the `did:peer` and nothing for a `did:key`. It also checks that verify-trust's `ed25519_keys_from_doc` finds the git signing key.
- Further unit tests cover:
  - a proof from the production `proof_checker` verifying;
  - the DID syntax, which survives the trailer's `#?/` split;
  - the mediator-mismatch refusal;
  - the length limit;
  - export/import round trips for both `did:peer` and `did:key`.
- `tests/cli.rs` runs the binary through `init`, a repeat `init`, `export` (0600, no overwrite), losing the store, `import` giving back the same DID, and `mint` with and without `--replace`. It also refuses a `did:peer` minted for another mediator.
- Not exercised end to end against a live mediator and VTC.

the 1000 bytes DID resolvers accept, and `run` warns about a did:key left
by an earlier release.

`identity export <file>` writes the identity's secrets bundle (0600, never
over an existing file) in the format `identity import` reads, so the
bridge's DID - which the VTC records per namespace, the registry's service
grant names and re-signed Dependabot commits carry - can be backed up apart
from the store and restored into a fresh one.

BRIDGE.md, RUNBOOK.md and SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md drop the did:key limit and
document the identity backup. Re-attaching a namespace after losing the
store is still unsolved and stays documented as a limit.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): configurable Forgejo runner label and role map; never project git.ns.admin
body:
## What

Two forge config gaps from the VTC-managed git namespaces design (§5.8 community hooks, §5.9 Forgejo):

1. **Forgejo runner label**: `[[forgejo]] runs_on` sets the `runs-on:` label of the workflow the bootstrap writes. The default is still `docker`. It is checked at start-up.
2. **Role map**: `[role_map]` (bridge), `[github|forgejo.role_map]` (forge entry), `[<forge>.namespaces.<owner>.role_map]` and `[<forge>.namespaces.<owner>.repos.<name>.role_map]` override `own` / `maintain` / `commit` field by field, with the most specific level winning. With nothing set, behaviour is unchanged (`admin` / `maintain` / `none`; Forgejo `maintain` = `write` + merge allow-list). The start fails unless every resolved map is ordered (`own >= maintain >= commit`) with `commit <= write`.

## Namespace admins (decision 2026-09-25)

A namespace admin gets no forge role. Before this change, a `desiredRoles` entry carrying `git.ns.admin` was projected as repo `admin`, because `ns.admin => own` implication fed into `RoleMap::requested`. Now `EffectiveRights` keeps the rights implication grants separate from the rights that may become a forge role (`forge_tier`), so `ns.admin` alone maps to `none` under any map. `RoleMap` has no `ns.admin` entry, and an `ns_admin` / `nsAdmin` / `admin` key is refused. Namespace-level role jobs (org owners) were already refused `notCapable`.

## Docs

BRIDGE.md §4 (runner label) and the new §6c (role map), RUNBOOK §8b / §4a, `bridge.example.toml`, and the vgi-forge README.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- New tests: `vgi-forge` rights (ns.admin never projects; map ordering and serde), `vgi-forge-forgejo` config (`with_runs_on`), `vgi-bridge` config (layering, refusals), and `vgi-bridge/tests/role_map.rs`, which checks against a mocked GitHub that default and overridden maps PUT the expected permissions and that a `git.ns.admin` entry PUTs nothing.

title: feat(vtc): the backup/* chunked transfer on the signed door (#1641)
body:
This puts the node-neutral `backup/*` family (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#633, trust-tasks-rs 0.22.7) on the VTC's signed-document door, over REST, DIDComm and TSP. It uses the shared transfer core that #1721 moved into `vti_common::backup_transfer`. It closes the last #1641 verb the signed door couldn't carry: `vtc/backup/import`'s inline envelope never fits in one document.

## What it does
| task | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `initiate-export` | encrypts the community the same way `vtc/backup/export` does (`export_inner`, which also audits `BackupExported`), stages the bytes and returns the chunk manifest |
| `get-chunk` / `complete-export` | serves one chunk by index / releases the bundle and deletes its bytes |
| `initiate-import` / `put-chunk` | commits to the manifest before any bytes move / checks each chunk against its committed digest before writing it |
| `finalize-import` | checks the upload is complete and the assembled bytes match what was committed, then previews or applies the backup the same way `vtc/backup/import` does (`import_inner`, split out of the bearer route in this PR). Answers with a `counts` map |
| `abort` | cancels an open bundle |

- **Algorithm:** only `chunkedTrustTask`. The VTC doesn't publish a blob endpoint, so a `stream` request (named, or implied by omitting the algorithm) gets `transportUnavailable`, as the spec requires.
- **Chunk size:** at most **32 KiB**, the largest whose `put-chunk` document still fits in the 64 KiB the door accepts before it checks a proof. A test pins this. An import that asks for larger chunks gets `chunkSizeUnacceptable`, and an export never uses them.
- **Authority:** only an unrestricted admin, read from the signer's ACL row. A bundle belongs to whoever opened it, so another admin's `bundleId` gets `notFound`.
- **Error codes:** the shared export and import functions raise `vtc/backup/*` error codes. Where this family names the same condition differently, the code is renamed (`weakPassword`, `decryptionFailed`). Any other code goes out as its underlying error rather than under another task's code.
- **Storage:** a new `backup_bundles` keyspace, excluded from backup. Staged bytes live owner-only under `<data_dir>/backups`, and the retention sweeper runs the shared bundle sweeper over them.

## Known limit: REST throughput
`/v1/trust-tasks` sits behind the per-IP limiter for unauthenticated requests: a burst of 10, then one request every 5 s. That caps a chunked transfer over REST at about 12 chunks a minute. DIDComm and TSP aren't behind that limiter, and there chunk requests are bounded per admin instead (50/s). The operator guide (`docs/03-vtc/backup-restore.md`) says so. Lifting it for authenticated chunk traffic would need its own decision.

## Tests
`trust_tasks::backup_tasks`:
- **Round trip:** export in chunks, upload again at a different chunk size, preview writes nothing, and commit restores a row removed in between.
- **Algorithm refusals:** `stream`, and an unknown algorithm.
- **Chunk size:** an oversized chunk size is refused, and a full-size `put-chunk` document fits the door.
- **Authority:** a scoped admin is refused, and another admin's bundle gives `notFound`.
- **Import errors:** an incomplete upload names the missing indices, and the wrong password gives `decryptionFailed`.

Local runs:
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: green apart from the proof-count census, which moves from 33 to 40 because the seven new tasks all declare proofs REQUIRED. I updated that count and re-ran the affected tests after the rebase; the full suite wasn't re-run.
- clippy (`-D warnings`): clean.
- fmt: clean.

body:
feat(vtc): the backup/* chunked transfer on the signed door (#1641) (#1724)

`vtc/backup/import/0.1` carries the whole encrypted envelope in one document,
which no real community's backup fits inside the 64 KiB the signed door accepts
before it has checked a proof. So it was the one admin verb #1641 could not move
off its bearer route. The node-neutral `backup/*` family
(trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#633, trust-tasks-rs 0.22.7) moves a backup as a
bundle of small signed documents instead, and #1721 put the transfer the agent
already ran into `vti_common::backup_transfer` so this node runs the same code.

This dispatches all seven tasks on the signed door, over REST, DIDComm and TSP:

- `initiate-export` encrypts the community exactly as `vtc/backup/export` does
  (`routes::backup::export_inner`, which audits `BackupExported`), stages the
  bytes and returns the chunk manifest; `get-chunk` serves one chunk by index;
  `complete-export` releases the bundle and deletes its bytes.
- `initiate-import` commits to a manifest before any byte moves; `put-chunk`
  checks each chunk against its committed digest before writing it;
  `finalize-import` checks every chunk is present and the assembled bytes are
  the committed ones, then previews or applies exactly as `vtc/backup/import`
  does (`routes::backup::import_inner`, split out of the bearer route and
  auditing `BackupImported` on a commit), answering the per-keyspace `counts`.
- `abort` cancels either.

Only `chunkedTrustTask`: this node publishes no blob endpoint, so `stream`, named
or meant by absence, is refused `transportUnavailable`, as the specification
requires of a recipient that recognises the algorithm but cannot serve it.
Chunks are at most 32 KiB, the largest whose `put-chunk` document fits the door.
A larger import manifest is `chunkSizeUnacceptable`, and an export never uses
larger chunks. A test pins that a full-size chunk's document fits.

Authority is an unrestricted administrator's, from the signer's ACL row, as
`vtc/backup/{export,import}` require, and a bundle belongs to whoever opened it:
another administrator's handle is `notFound`. The shared export and import raise
`vtc/backup/*` declared codes; the two this family names differently are renamed
(`weakPassword`, `decryptionFailed`), and any other goes out as its underlying
error rather than under another task's code.

Bundles live in a new `backup_bundles` keyspace, excluded from backup, with
bytes staged owner-only under `<data_dir>/backups`; the retention sweeper runs
the shared bundle sweeper.

Over REST, `/v1/trust-tasks` is behind the per-IP unauthenticated limiter,
which bounds a chunked transfer there to about 12 chunks a minute. DIDComm and
TSP are not behind it. The operator guide says so.

Tests (`trust_tasks::backup_tasks`): a community backup round-trips chunk by
chunk — export, upload at a different chunk size, preview writes nothing, commit
restores a removed row; `stream` and an unknown algorithm; an oversized chunk
size; a full-size `put-chunk` document fits the door; a scoped administrator is
refused; another administrator's bundle is `notFound`; an incomplete upload
names what is missing; a wrong password is `decryptionFailed`.

title: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages from GitHub Actions
body:
## Summary

Lands [PLAN.md Part 2](PLAN.md): deployment to Cloudflare Pages, on the account and project set up per decisions 2 and 3. The `preview` job on this PR is the first CI deploy; the first production deploy happens when this merges.

**`deploy.yml`.** On every push to `main`: build, upload the artifact, deploy it with `wrangler pages deploy` (project name from `wrangler.toml`), verify the deployment URL against the commit it was built from, and verify the production host with `continue-on-error` until the CNAME exists. Serialized by a concurrency group; tied to a `production` environment so a reviewer gate can be added later without touching the workflow.

**`release.yml`.** On a `v*` tag: build, check `release.json` recorded the tag as its revision, package `dist.tar.gz` with a sha256 sidecar, copy the accept-list and its digest, attest build provenance with Sigstore, and create the GitHub Release with generated notes (every term and its status, and the `gh attestation verify` command). Tags are created by an editor by hand.

**`validate.yml`.** A `preview` job deploys every same-repo PR to a Pages preview URL, verifies it, and posts or updates one comment with the link, so a reviewer sees a proposed predicate's rendered page before merging. Fork PRs are validated only.

**`infra/verify.mjs`.** Checks a live host against the negotiation table in PLAN.md §1.7 (HTML, JSON-LD and JSON at each URL, 406 at a bare name, 404 for an unknown term, the trailing-slash redirect) plus, with `--expect-commit`, that the deployment is the build of that commit. Paths come from `registry.config.json`, so the same script checks a preview, `pages.dev` and the production host. Also `npm run verify`.

**`wrangler.toml`.** Project name, output directory, compatibility date. The second of the two instance files.

## Two fixes from running the worker under the real Pages runtime

`wrangler pages dev` in Docker surfaced two things the unit tests could not:

- The build now emits `404.html`. Without it, Pages answers an unknown path with `index.html` and a 200, so a mistyped predicate IRI would have resolved to a page.
- The worker now redirects an explicit `.html` request to the clean URL itself. Pages does that redirect on its own, and the worker's refusal to follow asset-store redirects (which protects the canonical IRI form) turned it into a 500.

## Verification

- `docker compose run --rm check`: 22/22 tests, build clean.
- `verify.mjs` against `wrangler pages dev` in Docker: 17/17 live checks.
- The placeholder upload on `dtgwg-vsc-registry.pages.dev` already negotiates JSON-LD and redirects the trailing-slash form.

## After merge

1. `deploy.yml` publishes `main` to `dtgwg-vsc-registry.pages.dev`.
2. Add `registry.trustoverip.org` as a custom domain on the Pages project and send ToIP the CNAME (`registry` → `dtgwg-vsc-registry.pages.dev`), per PLAN.md §2.2.
3. When it resolves, drop `continue-on-error` from the production verify step (§2.7 step 3).

Refs #1, #3.

title: fix(vtc-admin-ui): fish-safe shell quoting, and reseat follow-ups
body:
Follow-ups to #1722.

## Shell quoting that fish cannot break out of (security)

`shellQuote` (`vtc-service/admin-ui/src/plugins/repos/actions.ts`) and `shell_word` (`cnm-cli/src/git.rs`) used POSIX `'…'` + `'\''`. fish reads `\'` and `\\` as escapes even inside single quotes, so the value `x\' ; echo INJECTED ; echo \`, pasted into fish, ran `echo INJECTED`.

Both now emit runs of characters other than `'` and `\` in single quotes, `'` as `"'"` and `\` as `"\\"`. These mean the same thing in POSIX double quotes and in fish double quotes. `$`, backticks, newlines and unicode stay literal inside the single-quoted runs.

Running the words through each shell turned up two more bare-word cases, and both are now quoted:
- zsh expands a leading `=` (`=ls` becomes `/bin/ls`).
- fish expands a leading `%` (`%self` becomes the shell's PID).

`cnm`'s `shell_word` also now quotes a leading `-`.

A repo-wide search found only these two helpers. Other `'{…}'` format strings are error prose, not shell.

**Tests:** `actions.test.ts` runs every generated word through `sh -c`, `bash -c`, `zsh -c` and `fish -c` using `env printf '%s\0'`. It checks that each hostile value comes back byte-exact: quotes, backslashes, `\'`, `$(…)`, backticks, newlines, emoji, a leading `-`/`=`/`%`, `~`, globs and braces. The values are checked all together, one at a time, and bound to a flag, and a whole reseat command is checked too. zsh and fish are skipped where they are not installed; sh and bash are required. Exact-output unit tests are included. `cnm-cli` has the equivalent Rust round-trip test. Against the old implementation, the zsh and fish round-trips fail.

## Reseat is offered only to a community administrator

`NamespaceCard` shows Reseat only when the viewer is a community (super) admin: the `admin` role with no scopes. This is read from the shell's `whoami` cache through the new `src/lib/viewer.ts` (`isSuperAdmin` / `useIsSuperAdmin`). `App.tsx` now uses the same predicate. Unbind is **not** gated, because the server also admits a namespace `git.ns.admin` (`rules::unbind_admitted`). Tests cover a community admin, a context-limited admin and no session.

## Accurate headless wording

The server (`ops.rs` `namespace_reseat` step 3) refuses a reseat only for a live `git.ns.admin` held by a current member. The finding, the task effect and the dialog now say "refused while a current member holds a live git.ns.admin there". `lifecycle::headless` is unchanged.

## `didError` rejects a `#fragment`

This now matches `vta_sdk::identifier::validate_did_core`, including its 1024-byte bound. All callers are party fields: grant subject, create owner, add owner and reseat subject. None needs a DID URL, so no separate check was needed.

## Checks

- `vtc-service/admin-ui`: `npm ci && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build` all pass (382 tests).
- `cnm-cli`: tests, `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` pass.

title: feat(vgi-cli): add vgi repo init for manual and personal-account namespaces
body:
## What

A `vgi` binary with `vgi repo init` — the command the VTC's `git-ns/repo/create` manual steps, the GitHub and Forgejo adapters' hints, and design §7.3 / §8 all tell people to run, which did not exist.

```sh
vgi repo init --vtc <vtc-did> --resource <host>/<owner>/<repo> [--dry-run]
              [--registry <did>] [--owner <did>]... [--code-owner <login>]...
              [--forge auto|github|forgejo] [--platform-keyring <file>]
              [--verify-trust-action <ref>] [--verify-trust-version <tag>]
              [--verify-trust-sha256 <hex>] [--required-check <name>]
              [--forgejo-url <url>] [--runs-on <label>]
```

`--vtc` and `--resource` are exactly the VTC's step 2 (`vgi repo init --vtc {vtc_did} --resource {resource}`), so the VTC's text works as written. `--resource` defaults to the clone's `origin` (the step says "in a clone of it"); `--registry` defaults to the VTC DID document's `TrustRegistry` referral.

## How

- **New crate `crates/vgi-cli`** (lib + `vgi` bin). Not a bin in an existing crate: `did-git-sign` is consumed as a library by OpenVTC, and `verify-trust` is the CI binary; neither should carry both forge adapters and reqwest. `vgi` is taken on crates.io by an unrelated project, hence `vgi-cli`; the binary is still `vgi`.
- **The adapters' own plans and request shapes, not copies.** GitHub: `github_plan` + `render_workflow` / `render_codeowners`, and the ruleset body and "already satisfied" test the adapter uses — `ruleset_body` and a new `ruleset_satisfies` are now public (`protection()` became a free `protection_of`, behaviour unchanged). Forgejo: `forgejo_plan`, and the merge-settings / branch-protection bodies and their "already satisfied" tests, pulled out of `configure_repo` / `protect` into free functions and exported (`settings_body`, `settings_satisfied`, `protection_body`, `protection_satisfies`, `managed_protection_rule`, `plan::default_status_context`). The adapter code paths call the same functions; adapter tests unchanged and green.
- **GitHub acts through the person's `gh` login.** One `gh api --hostname <h> --include --method <M> -H … [--input -] <path>` process per request: argument vector, never a shell string; bodies on stdin; each path segment percent-encoded (including `{`/`}`, which `gh api` would otherwise fill in). Guard as the adapter chooses it outside a required workflow: the personal repository's account holder plus each `--code-owner` (by numeric id) → `CheckGuard::for_owners` — one owner is **solo** (the check only), two or more is **owner review** (managed `CODEOWNERS` block + code-owner review in the ruleset). DIDs are literals in the workflow and stale `TRUST_REGISTRY_DID` / `VTC_DID` variables are removed, as the adapter does now. Ruleset: PR required, check required and pinned to the GitHub Actions app, no force-push, no deletion, no bypass.
- **Forgejo acts with `FORGEJO_TOKEN`.** Fast-forward-only merges (refused with the adapter's message on an instance without them), the workflow with DIDs inline, branch protection with `protected_file_patterns` over every workflow directory, the status-check context, applying to admins. One deliberate difference from the bridge: the person running it is seeded onto the merge allow-list (the bridge seeds admin collaborators only; a personal repository's owner is never a collaborator, and would lock themselves out).
- **Check-then-apply everywhere**; a re-run sends only GETs. `--dry-run` reads and prints every change with the file or JSON body, and sends nothing.
- **Adopt is printed, not performed.** `git-ns/repo/adopt` is a VTA-signed Trust Task and the CLI holds no VTA session (help text says so). It prints `cnm git adopt <resource> --owner <did>…`, every `--owner` DID-core-validated and each argument shell-quoted. This matches the VTC's manual steps (step 3 is the separate `cnm git adopt`); design §7.3's "then calls `git-ns/repo/adopt`" is superseded by that.

## Hints and docs

- Adapter hints now give the full form: `vgi repo init --vtc <vtc-did> --resource <repo>` (`FORGEJO_TOKEN=… ` on Forgejo), then `cnm git adopt`.
- README crate row; RUNBOOK §4 gains a short manual-mode paragraph pointing at `vgi repo init` (the by-hand setup stays below it), and the `notCapable` row mentions it; BRIDGE.md §6 notes the personal-account-without-App case; SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md §9.1 / §9.3 use it (bridge mode still skips step 2 — the adopt's bootstrap does it with the bridge-posted guard) and the "does not exist" bullet is gone.

## Publishing

`vgi-cli` is publishable and appended to `publish.yml`'s list (after the adapters it depends on). **Its first version must be published by hand** and then given a Trusted Publisher config on crates.io, like every crate on the list; until then the publish job fails at `vgi-cli`, after the other crates have uploaded. Not published here.

## Tests

- GitHub (`tests/github.rs`, unix): a fake `gh` on `PATH` records every argv and stdin body and answers from canned replies. Files written equal `github_plan` / `render_workflow` byte for byte; the ruleset body equals `ruleset_body`; argv shape (`--input -`, path last, no placeholders); re-run against the state the first run produced sends no change; `--dry-run` sends no change and prints the contents; drifted ruleset rewritten and a stale variable removed; two owners → managed `CODEOWNERS` + code-owner review; missing repository → the `gh repo create` hint; bad DIDs refused before any call.
- Forgejo (`tests/forgejo.rs`): wiremock. The plan lands (merge settings, workflow equal to `forgejo_plan`'s, protection equal to `protection_body`), token on every request; re-run against the converged instance sends no change; dry-run sends nothing; no token → no requests; no fast-forward-only → refused before any write.
- Unit: DID-core syntax, shell quoting round-tripped through `sh`, remote-URL → resource, TrustRegistry referral parsing, `gh --include` parsing.

## Review follow-ups

- **Organisation repositories need two owners or `--solo`.** Owners are now the person running `vgi` (the account holder, on a personal repository) plus each `--code-owner`, deduped by id. On an organisation repository with fewer than two owners `vgi repo init` refuses unless `--solo` is given: otherwise any other member with write access could edit the workflow in the pull request it judges. The solo guard text no longer claims no one else can review. Tests: org refused without `--solo` (also with `--code-owner <self>`), accepted with it (check only, no `CODEOWNERS`), and runner + one code owner giving owner review.
- **`FORGEJO_TOKEN` goes only to a confirmed Forgejo.** `GET /api/v1/version` is asked without the token; the token is attached only if the reply is JSON with a `version` string. `--forge auto` off github.com is treated as Forgejo only after that probe, and otherwise the error suggests `--forge`. `--forgejo-url` must be on the resource's host. Tests (wiremock): the probe is the first request and has no `Authorization` header; a non-Forgejo host sees exactly one unauthenticated request; a mismatched host gets no requests.
- **Forgejo admin check** now requires `permissions.admin == true` (a missing field is refused), as on GitHub.
- **Protected-workflow error** in manual mode explains lifting the branch protection and re-running, instead of pointing at the bridge. RUNBOOK §4 documents upgrading `--verify-trust-version`: a pull request on GitHub; on Forgejo, lift protection, re-run, and it puts the protection back.
- **Action tag resolution** goes through `git/ref/tags/{tag}` and dereferences annotated tags (`git/tags/{sha}`), so a branch with the same name can't be picked up. The inputs client is `https_only`. The report labels the pinned action as trust on first use and says when the registry came from the VTC's `TrustRegistry` referral.
- **Docs** (crate README, README, RUNBOOK §4, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC §9.3): manual mode sets per-repository guards, not the organisation required workflow, which only the bridge sets. `--solo` is documented. `RepoFacts.owner` doc fixed.

title: Add the endorses and witnessed predicates as draft
body:
## Summary

Lands [PLAN.md §1.8 step 2](PLAN.md): the two core profiles of the DTG Credentials Core Specification (Working Draft 0.5.0) as the first entries in the registry, `endorses/1` and `witnessed/1`, both `draft`. This is the first real content through the validator.

**`endorses/1`** (VEC). `objectKind: ["value"]` with the shape delegated to the governing community's endorsement vocabulary, `taskContext` optional, no issuer-scope constraint, and the VEC establishes / does-not-establish block. One example, the spec's skill endorsement.

**`witnessed/1`** (VWC). `objectKind: ["digestMultibase"]`, `taskContext` required, `directed` minimum scope, the unconditional subject-is-issuer rule, the five does-not-establish items, and a published `witness-context.schema.json` for the optional `witnessContext` member. One example, the spec's witnessed-VRC credential. Labels in `en`, `de`, `nl` as drafted in cred-spec #52.

Each `profile.md` paraphrases the spec's informative prose (one statement per direction and why the direction rule is unconditional, what the digest binds, that presenting or holding is a different predicate) and links the normative section under *Defined in*. Both flag that the spec still prints the `dtg:` shorthand for a placeholder namespace, to be aligned in the editorial pass cred-spec #48 calls for.

The examples carry the proof in the `DataIntegrityProof` / `eddsa-jcs-2022` shape the spec's Base Structure requires, with illustrative values.

## What is deliberately not here

The credential context (`contexts/v1.jsonld`). Writing it is spec work: a `v1` must define terms for all seven credential types, and cred-spec #46 (the correlation-scope property) is still open, so a context frozen now would carry a known gap into a permanent IRI. Tracked in #4. The examples list `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` as decided; it does not resolve until #4 lands, exactly as the spec's own examples reference an unpublished context today.

## Verification

`docker compose run --rm check`: 2 predicate versions valid, immutability clean (both new, both draft), instance values clean, 21/21 tests, build produces 2 accept-list entries and the pages for both terms. The `validate` workflow runs the same here.

Review needs two approvals from the `predicates/` owners (GOVERNANCE.md §6).

Refs #4, PLAN.md decision 1.

title: fix(vgi-forge): pass the namespace as the check's fallback resource
body:
## Problem

git-ns `right/grant` 0.1 (projection rule, trust-tasks #623): the VTC publishes the implied `git.commit.sign` of every `git.ns.admin`, and any namespace-wide grant, on the **namespace** resource, and "a bridge that sets up a repository's check MUST configure the namespace as the check's fallback resource". Only the bridge-posted check did that. The workflows the adapters bootstrap passed no fallback:

- the GitHub org required workflow in `<org>/.vgi`
- the GitHub in-repo workflow (owner review, solo)
- the Forgejo workflow

So in the recommended setup (org + required workflow), namespace admins' commits, namespace-wide grants and the bridge's own service grant failed `unauthorized`. The service grant is what every Dependabot commit the bridge re-signs relies on.

## Fix

**The mechanism.** Each rendered workflow now passes this, next to `resource-format: qualified`:

```yaml
          # The namespace: where the VTC publishes namespace-wide commit rights.
          fallback-resource: <forge-host>/${{ github.repository_owner }}
```

- The **host** is fixed at render time from the repository's resource. It is already validated and lowercased (`github.com`, a GHES host, `codeberg.org`, a Forgejo host). `github.server_url` carries a scheme, so it cannot be used as is.
- The **owner** is read at run time. The one `.vgi` workflow therefore serves every repository of the organisation, and its content is identical for all of them, so the pin is unchanged. A copied workflow can never name another owner. Forgejo Actions fills the same `github` context.
- The value goes through the action's existing `fallback-resource` input. The action passes it through `env` and a quoted variable, never into the script. No new verify-trust flag was needed, so the fix works with already-released binaries and action SHAs.

**Defence in depth in verify-trust** (`resource.rs`, `select_resources`):
- Under `qualified`, a fallback that does not **contain** the resource is refused before any query. That covers another owner, a byte-prefix owner (`acme` vs `acme-labs`), another forge, a sibling repository, and a deeper path. The error names the namespace to use.
- Under `legacy`, a forge-qualified fallback is refused, because one run uses one form. A bare owner still passes through untouched, as before.

**Pin/convergence.**
- **GitHub, required workflow.** The existing pin logic moves the pin only to content it wrote or read back byte for byte. `.vgi` is protected, so until the new workflow is merged there, the bootstrap step fails with "lands through a pull request" and the old pin stays in force, with no gap. Once it is merged, the next bootstrap pins the new head. There is a new test for both halves.
- **GitHub, in-repo.** The ruleset has no bypass, so an owner lands the change by pull request. After that, the bootstrap reports the step unchanged.
- **Forgejo.** The bootstrap's `workflow`/`keyring` `WriteFile` steps now go through the audited `refresh_managed_files` whenever the repository has a default branch. On a protected repository with an outdated workflow, the rule is opened for the bot alone, the file is written, and the rule is restored and read back. A current file is left alone. An unprotected repository is written directly, and an empty repository still uses the plain write. Before this change, a re-bootstrap after the rendering changed would have failed on the protected path.

`docs/BRIDGE.md` has a new §6b that covers what is passed and how to upgrade each guard. RUNBOOK §8a, §8e and the failure table, and SETUP-GITHUB-VTC, lose the "namespace-wide rights don't count" limit that #80 added. Manual mode is told to pass the namespace fallback.

## Tests

- Rendered-workflow assertions (GitHub in-repo and required, Forgejo) check the exact lines: the fallback appears once, only next to `qualified`, the GHES host is used for GHES, and the output is identical across repositories of the namespace.
- verify-trust: `select_resources` refuses a fallback on another owner, a prefix owner, another forge, a sibling or a deeper path, and refuses a qualified fallback under legacy. The e2e tests show that a namespace-only grant passes through the workflow's fallback and fails without it, and that grants on owner B, `acme-labs` or another forge never authorize owner A.
- Bridge (`tests/resign.rs`): the Dependabot commits the bridge re-signs are checked with the real verifier and a stub registry, against the resources the **required workflow the bridge renders** hands verify-trust (the owner substituted as the runner would, then selected as the binary does). They pass, and they fail `unauthorized` without the fallback.
- GitHub `check_guard`: an outdated `.vgi` pin does not move while the head is old, and moves to the merged commit once the head holds exactly the rendering.
- Forgejo: a re-bootstrap refreshes a stale protected workflow (open for the bot, write, restore).

fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, the full workspace tests and MSRV 1.95.0 `check` all pass locally.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The bridge does not report an outdated managed workflow as drift, so after an upgrade nothing re-sends the bootstrap on its own. BRIDGE.md §6b tells operators to have the VTC re-send it.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): reseat a headless git namespace
body:
## What

- **Headless finding text** (`repos/model.ts`): no longer says reseat will work "once this VTC serves it". It now describes reseat as the VTC serves it (`git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.1, `cnm git reseat`): only a community administrator can do it, only while the namespace has no live `git.ns.admin`, the new admin must be a current member, and a statement is required and kept in the audit record.
- **Reseat action**: a headless namespace card shows a destructive-class **Reseat** button with "Needs a community administrator." It opens `ReseatDialog`, which has a members-only picker (DID-core validated) and a required statement (1–1024 characters, per the spec). That builds `reseatTask`:
  - payload `{ namespace, subject, statement }`
  - command `cnm git reseat <ns> --subject=… --statement=…`, with every value shell-quoted
  
  `SignTaskDialog` then shows the namespace and the subject (name and full DID). If the browser has a console key, a checkbox confirm comes before sign-and-send. If not, it hands over the command and document. A new optional `consentNote` on `SignedTask` explains that a reseat is authorized by the community-administrator capability, not by a git right.
- **Consent mirror**: `consentClass` (TS) and `git_ns::ops::consent_class` (Rust) both class `namespace.reseat` as destructive, matching the spec's `sideEffects: destructive`. The reseat handler does not call `consent_gate` (it already requires community admin), so this changes no runtime behaviour.
- **trust_task_manifest**: the reseat URI is added to `SIGNED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`. It is checked against `git_ns::tasks::served_uris`.

## Tests

- model: new finding text, and the consent mirror
- actions: payload shape, trimmed statement, cnm command, statement validation, shell-safety of all three reseat arguments
- overview:
  - Reseat is hidden on a non-headless card and shown on a headless one
  - a no-console-key flow sends nothing and shows the command and document
  - the destructive confirm gates sign-and-send, which posts the exact payload

`npm ci && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build` pass (348 tests).

title: refactor(vti-common): move the node-neutral backup transfer core out of vta-backup (#1641)
body:
This is the prerequisite for the VTC's chunked `backup/*` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#633, released in trust-tasks-rs 0.22.7). It moves the node-neutral half of backup transfer out of `vta-backup` into `vti_common::backup_transfer`, so the VTC can use the same implementation. The VTC can't depend on `vta-backup` itself, because that pulls in `vta-config`, `vta-keys`, `vta-support` and `vta-webvh`. Tracks #1641.

**This is a refactor only. Behaviour doesn't change, and no public path in `vta-backup` disappears.**

## What moved (via `git mv`, so history follows)
| was | now |
|---|---|
| `vta_backup::backup_bundle_store` | `vti_common::backup_transfer::bundle_store` |
| `vta_backup::backup_bundle_sweeper` | `vti_common::backup_transfer::sweeper` |
| `vta_backup::ops::chunked` (all but `initiate_export`) | `vti_common::backup_transfer::chunked` |
| the ownership, kind, TTL and cap helpers, plus `abort`, from `ops::descriptors` | `vti_common::backup_transfer` |

`vta-backup` re-exports each moved module under its old path. It keeps `initiate_export`, which serializes the agent's state and hands the bytes to the shared `stage_export`. `abort_bundle` now goes through the shared `abort`.

The core also gains two functions the VTC will use:
- `chunked::check_initiate`: super-admin plus the open-bundle cap.
- `chunked::complete_export`: node-neutral release of a chunked export.

## Dependency changes
- `vti-common` gains `subtle`, for the constant-time token compare.
- `vti-common` now declares the tokio `fs` and `io-util` features. `vta-backup` had been using `tokio::fs` without declaring `fs`, and built only through feature unification.

## Tests
- The 32 moved tests now run in `vti-common` and pass.
- `vta-backup`'s own suite passes: 54 tests.
- The `vta-service` backup tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

## Next
The VTC's `backup/*` handlers on the signed-document door, built on this core. They let the VTC import a backup that is too large for one document.

title: refactor(vti-common): move the node-neutral backup transfer core out of vta-backup (#1641) (#1721)
body:
refactor(vti-common): move the node-neutral backup transfer core out of vta-backup (#1641) (#1721)

The community node needs the backup transfer the agent already has. A VTC
backup, like any real node's, is too large for one Trust Task document, and the
node-neutral `backup/*` family (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#633, released
in trust-tasks-rs 0.22.7) is how it moves: a bundle, a manifest committed before
any byte moves, chunks pulled and pushed by index, a finalize that checks the
assembled bytes before trusting them.

`vta-backup` implements all of that for `vta/backup/*`, but the VTC cannot
depend on it — it pulls `vta-config`, `vta-keys`, `vta-support` and `vta-webvh`.
Only a thin layer of it is the agent's: serializing the agent's state into an
envelope, and applying one. The rest never asked what a bundle contains.

So that rest moves to `vti_common::backup_transfer`, which both nodes already
depend on for storage and auth:

- `bundle_store` — the `BundleRecord` state machine, token minting and the
  constant-time token check (was `vta_backup::backup_bundle_store`);
- `sweeper` — TTL expiry and retention (was `vta_backup::backup_bundle_sweeper`);
- `chunked` — staging, the chunk plan, `get_chunk`, `initiate_import`,
  `put_chunk`, `finalize_precheck` and the per-DID rate limiter (was
  `vta_backup::ops::chunked`), plus `check_initiate` and a node-neutral chunked
  `complete_export`;
- the ownership, kind, TTL and open-bundle-cap rules, and `abort`, from
  `vta_backup::ops::descriptors`.

Files moved with `git mv`, so their history follows them. `vta-backup`
re-exports every moved module under its old path, keeps `initiate_export`
(which serializes the agent's state and hands the bytes to `stage_export`), and
routes `abort_bundle` through the shared `abort`. No behaviour changes, and no
public path in `vta-backup` disappears.

`vti-common` gains `subtle`, and now declares the tokio `fs` and `io-util`
features the moved code uses. `vta-backup` had used `tokio::fs` without
declaring `fs`, building only by feature unification.

The 32 moved tests run in `vti-common`, and `vta-backup`'s own suite (54) is
unchanged. The VTC's `backup/*` handlers follow in the next change.

title: security(vta)!: step-up approval, audit verify, policy reads and device management are scoped
body:
These are the last four findings from the scope sweep that followed FTL-29904 (#1715, #1717). In each one the gate checked the caller's role and never what the caller acted on. I confirmed all four by reading the code before fixing them.

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `step-up/approve-request` (DIDComm) | Any authcrypt sender got an approval signed with the VTA's `#key-0`, behind a stub that always approves | The holder must be a principal of this VTA, meaning a live ACL entry (VTI-SES-006's rule). Refusals and issued approvals are both audited (VTI-VTA-006) |
| `audit/verify` | Admin role only, although it reads the whole log | Super-admin, the same as `audit/list` without a `contextId`. Both a verification and a refusal are audited (VTI-AUD-006) |
| `policy/list`, `policy/get` | Any admin or initiator saw every context's policy | A scoped caller sees global rows and the rows for its own contexts. A row outside its reach answers `get` with NotFound (VTI-CTX-002) |
| `device/list`, `/disable`, `/wipe` | Visibility only, so an initiator could see, disable or wipe an admin's device in its context | `acl/delete`'s rule: visibility plus `validate_role_assignment` |

The step-up gate lives in the operation, as the testable `operations::step_up_approval::authorize_holder`. The always-approve stub stays as the placeholder for user verification. It is now documented as not being the authorization control.

## Tests

- `only_a_principal_of_this_vta_is_authorized_for_approval`
- `audit_verify_is_super_admin_only`, a Trust Task dispatch test
- `a_scoped_caller_reads_only_the_policy_that_governs_it`
- `an_initiator_cannot_manage_an_admins_device`

Local runs of what CI runs:
- workspace and VTC tests: 7,056 passed, 0 failed;
- clippy `-D warnings`, full and the three reduced-feature `vta-service` builds: clean;
- fmt: clean.

## Breaking (behaviour)

- A sender that isn't a principal of this VTA no longer gets step-up approvals.
- Context-scoped admins lose `audit/verify` and other contexts' policy rows.
- Initiators lose sight and control of more-privileged principals' devices.

This closes out the sweep's list.

body:

The last four findings of the scope sweep that followed FTL-29904 (#1715,
#1717). Each checked the caller's role and never what the caller acted on.

- step-up/approve-request signed an approval with the VTA's own #key-0 for any
  authcrypt sender. An RP reads it as "this VTA approved a step-up for sub",
  so any DID anywhere could get that statement signed. The holder must now be
  a principal of this VTA (a live ACL entry; the rule VTI-SES-006 applies to
  issuing an auth challenge), through the testable
  `operations::step_up_approval::authorize_holder`. Refusals and issued
  approvals are both audited (VTI-VTA-006). The always-approve stub stays as
  the placeholder for user verification and is documented as not being the
  authorization control.
- audit/verify needed only the admin role, although it reads the whole log,
  which audit/list reserves for a super-admin. It is now super-admin, and a
  verification and a refusal each leave an audit row (VTI-AUD-006).
- policy/list and policy/get showed any admin or initiator every context's
  policy. A scoped caller now reads the rows that govern it (global rows and
  those naming a context it may act in); a row outside its reach answers
  NotFound on get, so it cannot be probed (VTI-CTX-002).
- device/list, device/disable and device/wipe checked context visibility but
  not privilege, so an initiator could see, disable or wipe the device of an
  admin in its context. They now apply `acl/delete`'s rule (visibility and
  validate_role_assignment).

Breaking in behaviour: non-principals lose step-up approvals; context-scoped
admins lose audit/verify and other contexts' policy rows; initiators lose
sight and control of more-privileged principals' devices.

title: feat(vtc): acl/change-role on the signed door, with a promotion's gesture bound to it (#1641)
body:
Step 3 of `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-operation-bound-step-up.md`, now complete. `acl/change-role` joins `acl/grant` (#1718) on the signed-document door. On that door, promoting someone to admin needs a passkey gesture tied to that one operation, not to a session. Tracks #1641.

## How
- The role-change pipeline now takes a `StepUpSource`. It is either `Session` (the bearer route, unchanged) or `BoundTo { type_uri, payload }` (the signed door). Either way the pipeline resolves the fact itself, never from a boolean the caller passes in (#1645).
- On the bound source the pipeline decides as if the gesture were present. It acts on that verdict only after spending the mark, and both happen under `PROMOTE_LOCK`. So a promotion refused by the policy or by an invariant is refused for that reason, and nobody is asked for a passkey. `decide` is pure.
- The body of `update_acl` is now `routes::acl::change_role_inner`, shared by both doors.
- `handle_acl_grant` now calls `require_manage()` explicitly, matching the bearer route's `ManageAuth` extractor. `plan_grant` already refused those roles, so this states the gate; it doesn't close a gap.
- On the signed door, `AdminPromoted.authorising_session_id` is empty. The gesture is recorded in the `OperationStepUpRecorded` row under the same actor.

## Tests
`tests/signed_step_up.rs` now has 15 tests. The new ones cover:
- the promotion loop end to end;
- a gesture recorded for a grant does not authorize a promotion;
- a stale `fromRole` is refused as a conflict;
- a demotion needs no gesture;
- a non-admin signer, including one promoting themselves, is refused without being asked for a gesture.

Local runs:
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: green.
- Clippy `-p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`: flagged one large enum variant. I boxed it, and it's clean now.
- `signed_step_up` and `passkey_step_up`: re-run after the boxing, both green.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Left
Still to do, from the design note's order of work:
- VTI-APV-014 second-party consent (§4)
- console-key enrolment, once `auth/signing-key/*` is published
- retiring the bearer routes

body:
feat(vtc): acl/change-role on the signed door, with a promotion's gesture bound to it (#1641) (#1719)

The second of the three verbs gated on a passkey gesture moves onto the
signed-document door, behind the operation-bound step-up #1718 built for
`acl/grant` (`vtc-operation-bound-step-up.md`, VTI-APV-015).

A promotion is the role-change ceremony, whose host invariant `StepUpForAdmin`
reads a `step_up` fact the pipeline resolves itself — #1645 took that boolean
away from callers. The pipeline now takes a `StepUpSource`: the bearer route's
live session, as before, or a gesture bound to the operation. On the bound
source it decides as if the gesture were present and acts on that verdict only
after spending the mark, under `PROMOTE_LOCK`, so:

- a promotion the policy or another invariant refuses is refused for that
  reason and never asks for a passkey it could not use;
- a promotion nothing else refuses, with no gesture recorded, is refused
  `permissionDenied` with the ceremony inline (`details.stepUpRequest`), and the
  identical document, re-sent after `approve-response/0.4` records the gesture,
  completes;
- a gesture recorded for a grant does not promote — the digest covers the
  task's type.

`update_acl`'s body is now `routes::acl::change_role_inner`, shared by both
doors: the `fromRole` compare-and-swap, the scope checks, the ceremony, the
admin sister record, session revocation on a privilege reduction and the audit
rows. On the signed door `AdminPromoted.authorising_session_id` is empty; the
gesture is the `OperationStepUpRecorded` row under the same actor.

The signed `acl/grant` handler also checks `require_manage()` explicitly, the
bearer route's `ManageAuth`. `plan_grant`'s role checks already refused every
role it refuses, so this states the gate rather than closing a gap.

Tests (`tests/signed_step_up.rs`, 15 now): the promotion loop end to end, a
grant's gesture not authorizing a promotion, a stale `fromRole` as the
conflict, a demotion needing no gesture, and a member refused — including
promoting themselves — without being asked for one.

Left in the design note's order of work: VTI-APV-014's second-party consent,

title: Add build tooling: definition format, validator, generator, worker
body:
## Summary

Lands [PLAN.md §1.8 step 2](PLAN.md): the tooling, with zero predicates, so the validator is exercised by CI alone before any real content goes through it. The two predicates follow in the next PR, deployment in the one after.

**Definition format** (`meta/`). `predicate.schema.json` is the JSON Schema every `predicate.jsonld` validates against: the nine members of the spec's *Predicate Profiles* plus lifecycle metadata, with conditionals for `since`, `deprecatedOn`, `objectSchema`/`objectSchemaDelegated` and `weighedBy`. `predicate-context.jsonld` maps the members to `rdfs:label`, `skos:definition`, `dcterms:replaces` and a registry vocabulary. `accept-list.schema.json` is what verifiers can validate an imported accept-list against. Instance URLs in these files are `{{tokens}}` filled from `registry.config.json` at build time.

**Validator and generator** (`scripts/`). `build-registry.mjs` (`npm run validate` / `npm run build`) checks every predicate version against the schema and the governance rules: byte-exact IRI equal to namespace + folder path, NFC, local schema `$id`s, version `n` requiring `n-1` and superseding it with the predecessor deprecated in the same change, the convergence-record rule for a term that supersedes a community term, `supersededBy` implying `deprecated`, every example credential against its profile (type, predicate bytes, object kind, `taskContext`, additional members against their schemas), and one English label per live concept. It then generates `dist/`: byte-copies of every frozen file, one static HTML page per URL, `vocab.jsonld`, `accept-list.json` with its sha256, and `release.json` digesting everything. `check-immutability.mjs` diffs non-draft versions against the base branch and allows only `status`, `since`, `deprecatedOn`, `supersededBy` and `profile.md` to change, and checks status transitions. `check-instance-values.mjs` enforces the two-file guarantee from the README. `new-predicate.mjs` scaffolds a version folder.

**Worker** (`site/_worker.js`). The Pages advanced-mode worker from the plan: canonical-form redirect, an RFC 9110 `Accept` parser, the negotiation table from §1.7, 406 for machine requests at a bare name, immutable caching on versioned artifacts, CORS, and a `Link: rel=alternate` header on predicate pages. It refuses to follow a redirect from the asset store, which is how the `<path>.html` layout rule is enforced.

**Tests**. 21 tests under `node --test`: 11 drive the validator and generator against a fixture registry in an example namespace, mutating it to trigger each rule; 10 cover the worker's routing against a stub asset store.

**Toolchain**. `package.json` with a lockfile generated inside a container, a Dockerfile on `node:24-slim` with git, `compose.yaml` with `validate`, `build`, `test`, `check`, `serve` and `shell` services running as the invoking user, and `validate.yml` running the same steps on every PR and push to `main`.

## Decisions worth a look

- **HTML pages are `<path>.html`, not `<path>/index.html`.** Cloudflare serves the first at the extensionless URL without a redirect but answers a directory index with a redirect to the trailing-slash form, which would contradict the canonical IRI. PLAN.md §1.7 is updated.
- **The instance-value check scans tooling paths only.** Its first run caught the namespace in the PR templates and the site name in the CODEOWNERS header; the templates are now namespace-neutral and the scan covers `scripts`, `site`, `meta`, `infra`, `.github/workflows` and the build files.
- **Ajv runs in strict mode with `strictRequired` off**, because the meta-schema's conditional `required` blocks name properties defined at the top level.
- British spellings in `README.md` and `GOVERNANCE.md` from #2 are corrected to American here rather than in a separate PR.

## Verification

`docker compose run --rm check` passes: validate (0 predicates), immutability, instance values, 21/21 tests, build. `validate.yml` runs the same on this PR.

Refs #1, #2.
