title: fix(vgi-bridge): re-sign lease race; report access removeAccounts cannot remove
body:
Two changes to the bridge.

## 1. The flaky re-sign test was a real bridge race

`a_dependabot_rebase_after_a_missed_own_push_is_re_signed` sometimes failed in CI (the first run on #77) with `git push: ! [rejected] … (stale info)`.

**Root cause.** `resign::run` read the pull request's head from GitHub's API *before* it took the per-branch guard, and nothing checked that head again once the guard was held. Two runs for one branch (here, one started by the push webhook and one called directly; in production, `push` plus `pull_request.synchronize`) could interleave like this:

1. Run B reads the PR, which names head `H`.
2. Run A holds the guard. It re-signs `H` to `H'`, pushes, and releases the guard.
3. Run B takes the guard and re-signs `H` again. It pushes with `--force-with-lease=…:H`, and git rejects it as stale because the branch is at `H'`.

The lease did its job and nothing was overwritten, but the run ended as a failed re-sign when it should have skipped. GitHub's API can go on naming `H` for a while after a push, so re-reading the pull request would not close the gap. In the test, the mock API always names `H`.

**Fix (in the bridge, not the test).** Once it holds the guard, a run reads the branch's actual head from the forge (`git ls-remote`, using the same hardened git and read token). It re-signs only if that head is still the one the PR names:

- If the branch is at the head the bridge's own recorded push made from `H`, the run skips with "already re-signed by the bridge".
- If anything else moved the branch, the run skips and leaves the re-sign to the push that moved it.

The lease stays in place for a push by someone else between the read and the push.

**Tests.**
- New: `a_run_behind_the_api_after_a_re_sign_does_nothing` reproduces the race deterministically. Without the fix it fails with the same `stale info` error seen in CI.
- The moved-head test (renamed `nothing_is_pushed_when_the_head_moved`) now expects the skip, and still checks the branch was not overwritten.
- `for i in $(seq 30); do cargo test -q -p vgi-bridge --test resign || break; done` passed 30 of 30 twice, once during development and once on the final tree. On unchanged `main`, the same loop failed on run 3 of 30.

## 2. `removeAccounts`: report team and org-owner access (job 0.2)

The spec says `removeAccounts` removes only a direct role. Access the account keeps through a team or as an organisation owner "is not a role on the repository, and the bridge reports it as a failed `roles` step rather than change the team or the organisation." This implements that:

- New `Forge::indirect_access(repo, account) -> Option<IndirectAccess>`, with `IndirectAccess { role, via: Vec<AccessSource> }`. The default returns `None`, so the change is additive for other adapters.
- **GitHub** reads the effective permission from `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission`. It then works out where the access comes from:
  - ownership, via `/orgs/{o}/memberships/{u}` with role `admin`
  - teams, via `/repos/{o}/{r}/teams` plus `/orgs/{o}/teams/{slug}/memberships/{u}`
  - otherwise, the organisation's base permission

  The token asks for Members (read), which the App manifest already requests.
- **Forgejo** uses the same permission endpoint (checked against the swagger: `none|read|write|admin|owner`). For sources it reads `/users/{u}/orgs/{o}/permissions` (`is_owner`), `/repos/{o}/{r}/teams` and `/teams/{id}/members/{u}`. Forgejo has no base permission.
- `read` on a repository everyone can read is not reported.
- The bridge checks every named account whose removal did not itself fail. The step detail names the account, its effective role and each source found, for example: ``eve-dev (5550123): no direct role any more, but still `maintain` access through team `Core`; the bridge does not change teams or the organisation``.
- Only GET requests are sent; the tests assert that the collaborator DELETE is the only write.

**Tests** (wiremock, in `vgi-bridge/tests/remove_accounts.rs`):
- GitHub: access through a team (only the team the account is in is named), org owner, base permission on a private repo, and `read` on a public repo (still succeeds).
- Forgejo: access through a team, org owner, and `read` on a public repo.
- The live Forgejo test now reads back the org owner's access, and its swagger table covers `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/teams`.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` (MSRV) all pass locally. The live Forgejo job needs Docker, so it runs in CI only.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in

  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

title: fix(vgi-bridge): re-sign only a branch still at the head it read
body:
fix(vgi-bridge): re-sign only a branch still at the head it read

A re-sign read the pull request's head from GitHub's API before it held
the per-branch guard, and nothing under the guard checked the branch was
still there. A run that read the pull request while another run was
re-signing the branch (a webhook-started one, say) took the guard once
the first finished, re-signed the head that had just been replaced, and
pushed on a lease that could no longer hold: `[rejected] (stale info)`,
reported as a failed re-sign. GitHub's API can go on naming the old head
for a while after a push, so re-reading the pull request would not close
it.

Holding the guard, a run now reads where the branch points on the forge
itself (`git ls-remote`, over the same hardened git and read token) and
re-signs only if that is still the pull request's head. If the branch is
at the head the bridge's own recorded push made from it, the run skips as
"already re-signed by the bridge"; if anything else moved it, it skips
and leaves the re-sign to the push that moved it. The lease stays, for a
push by someone else between the read and the push.

This was the intermittent failure of
`a_dependabot_rebase_after_a_missed_own_push_is_re_signed` in CI.
`a_run_behind_the_api_after_a_re_sign_does_nothing` reproduces the race
deterministically; the moved-head test now expects the skip.

title: feat(git-ns/bridge/event): detach on transfer and name reuse, confine events to their namespace
body:
Follow-up to #625, which merged before this change was pushed to it. This PR adds `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2.

The wire format is unchanged. What the VTC does with three kinds of event changes.

**Rights never follow a repository out of its namespace.**
- A namespace is one owner on one forge, so every `repoTransferred` leaves the namespace the event arrives on.
- The VTC now detaches the repository and withdraws its rights wherever `to` is: another owner, another forge, or another namespace, even one the same VTC governs.
- 0.1 treated a transfer into a bound namespace "as for a rename" and moved the rights. That let a forge-side act, which never passes the VTC's rules, give the receiving namespace owners and committers its admins never chose.
- The receiving namespace sees the repository as `repoCreatedUnmanaged`, and its admins adopt it and grant afresh.
- Renames within the namespace are unchanged.

**Name reuse detaches the old repository.**
- A `repoCreatedUnmanaged` at a governed name whose forge id differs from the recorded one means the name was reused.
- The VTC detaches the old repository and withdraws its rights before recording the new one as `unmanaged`, so the newcomer inherits nothing.
- This does not apply to a `pendingCreate` repository, which has no forge id yet. Its `createRepo` job reports the name as taken.

**Events are confined to their namespace.**
- Every `resource`, `from`, rename `to` and drift-item `resource` must lie inside the event's namespace. Otherwise the event is refused with `permissionDenied` and no part of it is applied.
- A transfer's `to` is exempt by definition: it records where the repository went, and nothing is done there.
- A repository transferred *into* a namespace is reported as `repoCreatedUnmanaged`, never as `repoTransferred`.

Changing what a member means is a breaking change, released as a MINOR increment under the SPEC §5.2 draft allowance. The spec has a *Changes from 0.1* section and restates everything else. `drift/resolve` 0.1 and `bridge/job` 0.2 now link to event 0.2. Bindings are regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run build` / `validate` and `check-bindings` pass: 502 specs, 992 error codes agree.
- New examples validate against the schema.
- Rust passes: `cargo fmt --check`, tests (1007 default + 1152 with `--features validate`), `cargo doc -D warnings`, and clippy (default and all-features) with `-D warnings`.
- TypeScript passes: `tsc`, 79 tests, and smoke.
- Go passes: build, vet, gofmt and `test -race`.
- Dart passes: `analyze --fatal-infos` and 74 tests.
- After rebasing onto current `main`, regenerating the bindings produces no diff, and the `--features validate` tests pass again.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): bridge job 0.2 removeAccounts
body:
## What

Adds support for `git-ns/bridge/job` **0.2**. In 0.2, a `projectRoles` job on a repository can carry `removeAccounts`: forge accounts whose direct role on that repository the bridge removes, whatever the role is. This is the job a VTC sends to revert a forge-side `roleAdded` drift (`git-ns/drift/resolve`). Job 0.1 had no way to undo such a role.

### Jobs
- The bridge accepts **both 0.1 and 0.2** job documents and picks the version from the type URI. A 0.1 payload is parsed against the 0.1 type, so a 0.1 job that carries `removeAccounts` is refused. The bridge then runs the job as a 0.2 job; the two are wire-identical for every member 0.1 has. The response comes back in the version of the request (`…/job/0.1#response` or `…/job/0.2#response`).
- The bridge refuses these shapes with `malformedRequest` and does not record the job:
  - `removeAccounts` without `repo` (a namespace-level `projectRoles`)
  - `removeAccounts` on any other kind
  - an empty `removeAccounts`, or one that names the same account twice
  - an account that is also in `desiredRoles` (matched by `forge` and `id`)
  - an account on a different forge from the namespace's
- **Accounts are matched by forge id.** Both adapters take the login from the forge's current collaborator listing, never the display login in the job, so an account that was renamed is still the one removed. Removing an account that holds no role changes nothing and the job succeeds.
- **The bridge never removes the namespace's owner or its own App or bot.** The new `Forge::is_protected_account` trait method is checked before the adapter is called. By default it protects the owner; the Forgejo adapter also protects its bot, by id. As a second guard, the GitHub adapter refuses to delete `<app-slug>[bot]` and the Forgejo adapter refuses to delete its bot. Either refusal is reported as a failed `roles` step.
- `vgi-forge`: the new trait method has a default, so this is a semver-minor change. The `Unlisted` docs now describe how a single named account is removed: it is listed in `desired` with `ForgeRole::None`.

### Dependencies
- `trust-tasks-rs` / `trust-tasks-proof` go from **0.22.3 to 0.22.4** (with the `git-ns` feature); 0.22.4 is the release that has job 0.2.
- `cargo tree -d` still shows the same two `trust-tasks-rs` nodes as before. vta-sdk 0.51 resolves 0.22.4, and the 0.21.21 node comes only through `trql-client` 0.18 (and the `affinidi-tdk` 0.16 it pulls in). `Cargo.toml` notes this.

### Events (`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#627)
trust-tasks-rs 0.22.4 has no event 0.2 types, so events are still sent as **0.1**. This PR makes only the 0.2 changes that are also valid under 0.1:
- A repository transferred into the namespace from an owner outside every bound namespace is now reported as `repoCreatedUnmanaged` in that namespace. Before, it went out as a `repoTransferred` whose `from` lay outside the namespace.
- A managed repository transferred out of every bound namespace is now also removed from the namespace's managed set.
- A rename whose `from` lies outside the namespace is not reported.

A transfer between two bound namespaces is still handled the 0.1 way: the record moves with the repository. Under 0.2 the repository would instead be detached, with `repoCreatedUnmanaged` reported in the receiving namespace. That change waits until #627 is released in trust-tasks-rs and the bridge can send event 0.2.

**Not done:** the spec says that if a removed account still has access through a team or as an organisation owner, the bridge should report it as a failed `roles` step. The bridge does not check for that yet. Removal covers direct roles only, and nothing touches teams or the organisation.

## Tests
- `tests/remove_accounts.rs`:
  - a 0.2 revert removes the account by id, with a fresh login, on mock GitHub and on mock Forgejo
  - removing an account with no role changes nothing and succeeds
  - each refused shape is `malformedRequest` and is not recorded: overlap, namespace-level, other forge, other kind, empty, duplicate, and `removeAccounts` in a 0.1 job
  - a 0.1 `projectRoles` job is still accepted and answered as 0.1
  - a personal account's owner, the GitHub App's bot and the Forgejo bot are never removed
- `tests/forge_flows.rs`: a transfer in is reported as `repoCreatedUnmanaged`, and a transfer out clears the record and the managed set.
- Local runs: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` all pass.

title: Name a baseline cryptosuite every consumer can verify
body:
The framework left the proof cryptosuite open and named no floor. Two conforming implementations were therefore not guaranteed to verify each other's documents, which undercuts the two-interoperable-implementations bar for candidate (§5.3). NAOMS raised this as Q4 in their review of WD 0.6.0.

## The rules (new §4.7 "Cryptosuites")

- **Baseline:** every conforming consumer **MUST** verify `eddsa-jcs-2022`, which is Ed25519 over JCS. This is a floor on *verification*, not a constraint on signing. JCS is used because a Trust Task document is JSON whether or not it carries `@context`, so verifying one must not require a JSON-LD processor.
- **Choosing a suite:** the producer picks the suite from its key, and the consumer picks the verifier from `cryptosuite` plus the key type of `verificationMethod`. There is no negotiation member.
  - If the producer doesn't know what the consumer verifies, it SHOULD sign with the baseline.
  - It MAY use another suite where the spec, the trust framework, or the recipient's published keys indicate the consumer verifies it. For example, a party that publishes an ML-DSA key verifies ML-DSA.
- **P-256:** consumers **SHOULD** also verify `ecdsa-jcs-2019` with P-256, because secure enclaves, WebAuthn authenticators and many HSMs sign only with P-256.
- **Unsupported suite:** the consumer rejects the document with `proofInvalid`. It is never treated as unsigned.
- **Specs may require a suite:** added to Specification Requirements item 8, e.g. a quantum-resistant suite for long-lived evidence.
- **Quantum-resistant suites (draft):** `mldsa44-jcs-2024` (ML-DSA-44, multicodec `0x1210`) and `slhdsa128-jcs-2024` (SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s, `0x1220`), both using base64url multibase, are pinned to the W3C [Quantum-Resistant Cryptosuites v1.0](https://w3c.github.io/vc-di-quantum-resistant/) experimental draft.
  - They are agreed suites, not baseline.
  - If the draft changes, the change is adopted as a new entry and never reinterprets a pinned one.
  - We expect to move one into the baseline once there is a W3C Recommendation.

## Versioning

This adds a consumer obligation, so it is a **MINOR** change: it belongs in 0.7.0 with #20, not in the 0.6.1 patch (#21). The changelog entry sits under **Unreleased**. Whichever of #20 and this merges second combines the two Unreleased entries.

## SDK status against this (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf main)

| SDK | `eddsa-jcs-2022` (MUST) | `ecdsa-jcs-2019` (SHOULD) |
|---|---|---|
| TypeScript proof | yes | yes |
| Dart proof | yes | yes |
| Go proof | yes | yes |
| Rust `trust-tasks-proof` | yes | **no** (follow-up) |

None of the SDKs implement the pinned PQC suites yet. TDK's `affinidi-data-integrity` implements both under its `post-quantum` feature.

title: Name a baseline cryptosuite every consumer can verify (#22)
body:
Name a baseline cryptosuite every consumer can verify (#22)

The framework left the proof suite open with no floor, so two conforming
implementations were not guaranteed to verify each other's documents
(raised by NAOMS against WD 0.6.0, Q4).

- Every conforming consumer MUST verify eddsa-jcs-2022. A floor on
  verification, not a constraint on signing.
- Producers choose the suite from their key; with an unknown consumer
  they SHOULD sign with the baseline, and MAY use another where the
  specification, a trust framework, or the recipient's published keys
  indicate the consumer verifies it. No negotiation member is added.
- Consumers SHOULD also verify ecdsa-jcs-2019 with P-256, for
  hardware-backed signers.
- An unimplemented suite is rejected with proofInvalid, never treated
  as an absent proof.
- A Trust Task specification MAY require a suite (item 8).
- Quantum-resistant suites mldsa44-jcs-2024 and slhdsa128-jcs-2024 are
  pinned, with their Multikey encodings, to the W3C Quantum-Resistant
  Cryptosuites draft; they are agreed suites, not baseline. A draft
  change is adopted as a new entry, never a reinterpretation.
- References and an Appendix B entry under Unreleased.

title: feat(git-ns): drift resolution, namespace reseat, linked accounts in view
body:
Three follow-ups to the git-ns family (#621). The `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.2 change was pushed after this merged and is in #627. No released spec is edited: every change is a new version folder or a new task.

## What's added

| Spec | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `git-ns/view/0.2` | new version | The response adds `accounts: [{account: ForgeAccount, linkedAt}]`: only the caller's own linked accounts, narrowed to the resource's forge when `resource` is given. The member is required and empty when there are none. The rest is restated from 0.1 with a *Changes from 0.1* section. |
| `git-ns/drift/resolve/0.1` | new task | An owner of the repo, explicit or implied (so `ns.admin` too), resolves one drift item: `adopt` or `revert`. |
| `git-ns/namespace/reseat/0.1` | new task | A community administrator grants `git.ns.admin` on a **headless** namespace to a current member. Destructive; needs an audit statement. |
| `git-ns/bridge/job/0.2` | new version | `projectRoles` gains `removeAccounts`, which revert needs. |
| `git-ns/_shared/0.2` | new component version | Adds `DriftType`. Wire-identical to 0.1. |

## Design choices worth reviewing

**Drift items have no stable id, and none is added.** Every `bridge/event` recomputes drift and replaces it wholesale, so an id would only last until the next comparison. The selector is `{type, account?, observed?}` on the request's `resource`:
- `account` is required for the three role types and forbidden for the others. An account's role on a repo is missing, changed or unprojected, so a repo has at most one role item per account.
- The non-role types have no account. Their selector covers every item of that type, which is fine because they are reverted by re-applying the whole protection or bootstrap plan.
- `observed` is an optimistic-concurrency guard. It is required for `adopt`, because the adopted right comes from the observed role and must not change between reading the drift and resolving it.

**Adopt** records the right the observed role projects to (the inverse of the adapter's mapping). It is evaluated exactly as `right/grant` 0.1 request steps 3 to 7: fixed rules, policy, idempotent return, and `grantedBy` set to the resolver. No `right` member is accepted, so the projection comes to match the forge exactly. Refusals:
- `accountNotLinked`: the forge account is linked to no member.
- `noMatchingRight`: no right projects to the observed role, e.g. `triage`, or `write` where committers get no forge role.
- `notAdoptable`: `roleRemoved`, a protection or bootstrap item, or a lowering `roleChanged`, which is a revoke.

**Revert and `bridge/job`:** 0.1's `projectRoles` removes only roles the bridge *manages*. It says outright that other roles are "reported as drift, not removed", and a collaborator added on the forge is exactly such a role, so 0.1 cannot revert `roleAdded`. `bridge/job/0.2` adds `removeAccounts` to `projectRoles` (repo-level only, must not overlap `desiredRoles`). It keeps the existing kind and its desired-state meaning. The other drift types reuse 0.1 jobs: `projectRoles` for `roleChanged`/`roleRemoved`, and `bootstrap` for the protection and bootstrap items. If the bridge only speaks 0.1, the result is `notRevertible`.

**Consent class:** SPEC §7.3 item 13 forbids a spec from declaring consent or step-up requirements. So the "elevated for revert of an owner-level role" requirement is written descriptively instead:
- a `consequences` entry;
- prose that grades each resolution's impact against the equivalent grant or revoke, so a VTC consent policy can classify it.

`sideEffects` stays `mutating`. Reseat is `destructive`.

**Headless and the last-admin invariant:** *headless* means no live `git.ns.admin` record, where live means not revoked, unexpired, and held by a current member. Reseat also states that **records with `expiresAt` do not count toward the last-admin invariant**, so revoking the last non-expiring admin is refused with `git-ns:lastAdmin`. This is not a new `right/grant` version, because it isn't strictly needed: 0.1 says nothing about expiring records, no valid document changes meaning, and the refusal uses a code both specs already declare. The next grant/revoke versions should fold it in, and the spec says so. Reseated records never expire.

**`_shared/0.2`:** `DriftType` has to be shared (it is used by `DriftItem` and by the selector). `DriftItem` keeps its inline enum so it stays textually identical to 0.1. Pointing it at `DriftType` makes the TS generator rename the hoisted `SharedComponents.DriftItem`/`Sync`/`RepoSummary` to `_GitNsV0_1`/`_GitNsV0_2` variants, which is a TS API break. As shipped, the TS diff is additive.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run build` / `validate`, `check-bindings` (501 specs, 991 error codes agree), `check-dart-packages`, `test:infra`
- The example payloads in all four new/versioned specs validate against their schemas, and every invalid-example fixture is rejected (checked with ajv).
- Rust: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`, `cargo doc --all-features` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, clippy (default + all-features) `-D warnings`, all under `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings`. 2148 tests passed.
- TS: `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (79 pass), `npm run smoke`
- Go: build, vet, gofmt, `go test -race ./...`, plus the nested modules
- Dart: `dart analyze --fatal-infos`, `dart test` (74 pass)
- Regenerating all four bindings after the final edit produces no drift.

title: fix(vtc): OpenAPI schema names are unique, so each endpoint documents its own shape (#1697)
body:
utoipa keys `components.schemas` by bare type name, and
`OpenApiRouter::routes` merges each route's schemas with a plain map
`extend`, so two `ToSchema` types with one name fail nothing: the last
registered wins and every `$ref` to the name describes that one. The VTC
document had 18 such names across vtc-service and vta-sdk, and six were
wrong in the published document — `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` was described
as the console-key list, `/v1/auth/challenge` as the personhood challenge,
and five revoke endpoints as the endorsement revoke response.

- vtc-service: the service-side types get distinct names with
  `#[schema(as = …)]`. Rust type names are unchanged, so no handler moves
  and `openapi_response_census` still compares like with like.
- vta-service: `RollbackResponse` and `EnrollPasskeyChallengeBody` were
  field-for-field copies of vta-sdk's types registered under the same
  names. The shapes matched, so the document happened to be right; the
  copies are deleted in favour of the vta-sdk types.
- `openapi_schema_names.rs` in both services: a source-scan census that
  fails when two `ToSchema` definitions in the crate or its path
  dependencies share a schema name, and when the scan finds too few names
  to prove anything.
- admin-ui: `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated; `PasskeyListResponse`
  restored as a generated alias and used by `myPasskeys.tsx` in place of
  the local interface that let the drift go unnoticed.

Closes #1697.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 1969 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4848 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus the three reduced-feature vta-service clippy runs CI does: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, admin-ui `tsc -b` and `npm run lint` (`wire:check`): clean
- Negative check: removing the two `ListResponse` annotations makes the census fail and name both definitions

title: utoipa schema names collide across route modules, so the published document describes the wrong shape
body:
## The gap

utoipa keys `components.schemas` by the **bare Rust type name**, so two route modules declaring types with the same name collide silently — last one registered wins, and the published document then describes one endpoint with another's shape.

`vtc-service/src/routes/admin/console_keys.rs` (#1692) declares `ListResponse` and `RevokeResponse`. Both names are already in use — `ListResponse` by `routes/admin/passkeys.rs`, and `RevokeResponse` by that and other routes. The console-key shapes won, so in the published document **`GET /v1/admin/passkeys` now `$ref`s a schema describing `{consoleKeys: [...]}`**.

## Why it matters

The document is wrong, not merely untidy. It is generated into `admin-ui/openapi.json` and from there into `admin-ui/src/lib/wire.ts`, which is the console's source of truth for wire types, and it is what an external integrator reads.

It was found because `wire.ts`'s `PasskeyListResponse` alias pointed at the console-key shape. Nothing caught it: `myPasskeys.tsx` carries a local interface rather than using the generated alias, so the console compiled and ran correctly against a document that described the wrong thing. #1695 removed the stale alias and left a note, and deliberately does not read the revoke response body.

The `RevokeResponse` collision predates #1692; the `ListResponse` one arrived with it.

## Suggested fix

1. Give the colliding types explicit schema names — `#[schema(as = ConsoleKeyListResponse)]` and so on — for the console-key types and any other collision.
2. Sweep for the rest: any duplicate bare type name across `#[derive(ToSchema)]` types is the same defect waiting. A census test asserting that every registered schema name is unique would make this class impossible rather than caught by eye — that is the shape of guard this repo already prefers (the URI census, the error-code census, the keyspace partition census).
3. Restore `PasskeyListResponse` in `wire.ts` once the passkey endpoint describes its own shape again, and consider having `myPasskeys.tsx` use the generated alias, since a local interface is what let the two drift unnoticed.

## Found by

#1695 (console signing, client side), while consuming the generated wire types.

body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: Drift resolution, namespace reseat, linked accounts in view ([#625](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/625))

Three follow-ups to the git-ns family. Released versions are untouched;
  every change is a new version folder or a new task.

  - git-ns/view 0.2: the response also carries `accounts`, the forge
    accounts linked to the caller's own DID (ForgeAccount + linkedAt),
    never another member's; narrowed to the resource's forge when
    `resource` is given. Required, empty when none. Everything else is
    restated unchanged from 0.1.

  - git-ns/drift/resolve 0.1 (new): an owner of a repository, explicit or
    implied (so namespace admins too), resolves one reported drift item.
    Drift items have no stable id -- they are recomputed and replaced
    wholesale by every bridge event -- so the item is selected by type,
    plus the account for the three role types (at most one role item per
    account per repository), plus an `observed` guard, required for adopt.
    `adopt` records the right the observed role projects to, evaluated
    exactly as git-ns/right/grant (fixed rules, policy, idempotence);
    refused with accountNotLinked when the account has no member, and
    notAdoptable / noMatchingRight where no right fits. `revert` sends the
    bridge the job that restores the projection.

  - git-ns/bridge/job 0.2: projectRoles gains `removeAccounts`. 0.1 only
    converges roles the bridge manages and reports other roles as drift
    without removing them, so it cannot revert a collaborator added on
    the forge. The rest of the revert table reuses 0.1 jobs.

  - git-ns/namespace/reseat 0.1 (new): a community administrator grants
    git.ns.admin on a headless namespace (no live, unexpired, member-held
    git.ns.admin record) to a current member, with a required audit
    statement. Destructive class; refused with notHeadless otherwise. It
    also states that expiring git.ns.admin records do not count toward
    the last-admin invariant. That rule lives here and is not a new
    right/grant version: 0.1 says nothing about expiring records, so no
    valid document changes meaning.

  - git-ns/_shared 0.2: adds DriftType, the value set a drift selector
    shares with DriftItem.type. DriftItem keeps its inline list so it is
    textually identical to 0.1. That keeps the TypeScript component
    hoisting additive: renaming SharedComponents.DriftItem would have
    been a break.

  The spec forbids declaring consent classes (SPEC 7.3 item 13), so the
  "elevated" impact of reverting an owner-level role is written as a
  consequence and as descriptive impact prose in drift/resolve.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

title: Let a private Type URI be any absolute URI
body:
## Why

§6.1 required every Type URI to use `https`. The reason given protects consumers that *dereference* the URI, but a consumer matches `type` by exact string and never has to dereference it. The rule tied every specification's name to DNS and a CA for no benefit to those consumers, and it shut out implementers with no DNS presence (raised by NAOMS against WD 0.6.0).

## What changes

- **Public registry: unchanged.** `https://trusttasks.org/spec/<slug>/<MAJOR.MINOR>`, and registry specs MUST use it.
- **Private specs: any absolute URI.** This includes https, a DID URL, a URN, or another scheme.
  - Path form (everything except URNs): `<prefix>/spec/<slug>/<MAJOR.MINOR>`
  - URN form: `urn:<NID>:<prefix>:spec:<slug-segments>:<MAJOR.MINOR>`, with the slug's `/` written as `:`
  - Slug and version extraction is defined for both forms.
- **`http` stays non-conformant** in every form.
- **A Type URI is a name.** This is now stated: consumers match it by exact string equality and need not dereference it. Content negotiation applies to `https` only. Other schemes rely on out-of-band distribution, with the schema's source authenticated per Schema-Validation DoS.
- Producer requirement 3 and spec requirement 7.5 no longer assume content negotiation.
- Fixes the private example that omitted the `/spec/` segment the slug rule depends on.
- Changelog entry under **Unreleased** in Appendix B.

## Compatibility

Additive: every document conforming to 0.6.0 still conforms. The SDK Type URI parsers need follow-ups in `dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf` before they can accept non-https private forms. For example, `trust-tasks-rs/src/type_uri.rs` rejects any scheme other than `https`.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no errors, and every in-page anchor resolves.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.22.3` → `0.22.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.20.4` → `0.20.5` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.2.5`) | `0.2.4` → `0.2.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.4` → `0.2.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

  `adopt` records the right the observed role projects to, evaluated
  exactly as git-ns/right/grant (fixed rules, policy, idempotence);
  refused with accountNotLinked when the account has no member, and
  notAdoptable / noMatchingRight where no right fits. `revert` sends the
  bridge the job that restores the projection.

- git-ns/bridge/job 0.2: projectRoles gains `removeAccounts`. 0.1 only
  converges roles the bridge manages and reports other roles as drift
  without removing them, so it cannot revert a collaborator added on
  the forge. The rest of the revert table reuses 0.1 jobs.

- git-ns/namespace/reseat 0.1 (new): a community administrator grants
  git.ns.admin on a headless namespace (no live, unexpired, member-held
  git.ns.admin record) to a current member, with a required audit
  statement. Destructive class; refused with notHeadless otherwise. It
  also states that expiring git.ns.admin records do not count toward
  the last-admin invariant. That rule lives here and is not a new
  right/grant version: 0.1 says nothing about expiring records, so no
  valid document changes meaning.

- git-ns/_shared 0.2: adds DriftType, the value set a drift selector
  shares with DriftItem.type. DriftItem keeps its inline list so it is
  textually identical to 0.1. That keeps the TypeScript component
  hoisting additive: renaming SharedComponents.DriftItem would have
  been a break.

The spec forbids declaring consent classes (SPEC 7.3 item 13), so the
"elevated" impact of reverting an owner-level role is written as a
consequence and as descriptive impact prose in drift/resolve.

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

title: chore: release 3 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.20.3` → `0.20.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.2.4`) | `0.2.3` → `0.2.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.2.3` → `0.2.4` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(git-ns/right/grant): publish the implied commit right of a namespace admin
body:
Follow-up to #621, which merged moments before this landed on its branch.

A namespace admin implies `git.repo.own` on every repository in the namespace, and so `git.commit.sign` on each. But the projection rule in `git-ns/right/grant` named only recorded `own` and `maintain` rights, so an admin's commits would fail every verify-trust check.

The rule now also publishes an admin's `git.commit.sign` on the namespace resource. A bridge that sets up a repository's check must configure the namespace as the check's fallback resource, so that record counts.

This changes spec prose only: no schema, example or generated-binding changes. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass.

title: feat(pnm): show the VTA's DID as a QR code with `pnm vta qr`
body:
`pnm vta qr` prints the active VTA's DID as a terminal QR code, for a phone (Keyring) to scan instead of retyping it. It's the pnm counterpart of the VTC landing-page QR code (#1698).

## Usage

```console
$ pnm vta qr                          # the default VTA's DID
$ pnm --vta work vta qr               # another configured VTA
$ pnm vta qr --did did:webvh:…        # any DID
$ pnm vta qr --out vta-did.svg        # also write the code as an SVG
```

It runs offline and reads the DID from this machine's config, so there's no connection or authentication. A VTA with no stored DID gets an error naming `pnm setup continue <slug>` and `--did`. A `--did` value that doesn't start with `did:` is refused.

## Choices

- **Bare DID.** The code carries the DID and nothing else, so it's safe on a shared screen. A DID is already a URI with scheme `did`, so there's no `did://` or app-specific wrapper, the same choice as #1698.
- **Dark on white, always.** Each line paints its own colours, black modules on bright white, because on a dark theme the terminal's defaults draw the code inverted and many phone cameras refuse an inverted code. The four-module quiet zone is part of the output.
- **Shared renderer.** `vta_cli_common::qr::{terminal_lines, svg}` holds the rendering, so `cnm` can adopt it without copying code. `qrcode` 0.14 is added with the `svg` feature only.
- **No PNG.** PNG output would need the `image` crate. SVG covers files.

## Testing

- `vta-cli-common` has three unit tests. One unpacks the half blocks back into a module grid and checks every module, quiet zone included, against the encoder's.
- `pnm-cli` has five unit tests: the CLI parse, the default VTA, a `--did` override with no config, a non-DID, and an unknown `--vta`.
- I ran `pnm vta qr --out …` against a real config. It drew the default VTA's DID and wrote the SVG. I didn't scan it with a phone.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` was still running when this PR opened. I'll add the result as a comment.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): report forge status to the VTC in ext
body:
## What

The VTC's admin console (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1694) shows bridge-known status that the `git-ns/*` payloads don't carry. The VTC reads it from `payload.ext["org.openvtc.git-ns"]` of `git-ns/bridge/result` and `git-ns/bridge/event`, shaped `{"namespace": {...}, "repo": {...}}`. This PR makes the bridge send it.

Every result and event now carries the report whenever the bridge has something to say:

| `namespace` member | Source |
|---|---|
| `installationId` (string) | the binding's GitHub App installation id |
| `appName` | `[[github]].app_name` |
| `appSlug` | the registered App's slug |
| `appRegistration` | `registered` / `pending` (an open manifest link) / `unregistered` |
| `missingPermissions` (array, omitted when empty) | what the installation lacks (`name:level`, `event:<name>`) |
| `permissionUpgradePending` (bool) | something is missing, or the bridge-posted check is wanted but the installation isn't ready; omitted until probed |
| `orgRulesets` (bool) | org rulesets on the owner's plan, as probed; omitted until probed |
| `requiredWorkflow` (bool) | the adapter's capability in force |
| `bridgePostedCheck` (bool) | the adapter's capability in force (configured, installation ready, no required workflow) |

| `repo` member | Source |
|---|---|
| `guard` | the guard in force from the last inspection: `requiredWorkflow`, `codeOwnerReview`, `bridgePostedCheck`, `protectedFiles` (Forgejo), or `none` (a solo repository, or a guard whose source protection has drifted) |
| `lastCheck` | `{sha, conclusion, at}` for the last check the bridge posted |

## When it goes

- Every result gets the namespace report and, when the job reached a repository, the repo report. That covers bind, inspect, create, bootstrap, archive and projectRoles.
- Every event gets the namespace report, plus the repo report when it names a `forgeId` (for example `protectionChanged` or `repoRenamed`).
- Create and bootstrap read the repository back once they finish, so their result carries the guard they set up.
- After a check it posts on a managed repository, the bridge records it, inspects the repository, and sends a `protectionChanged` with the full drift and `lastCheck`. This is throttled to one per repository per minute, and a report that is waiting picks up the newest check.
- When an installation accepts new permissions, the bridge probes it again and now also refreshes its missing-permission list (`GitHubForge::detect_installation`).

## Framework rules

`ext` is the payload-level member from SPEC §4.5.1, which both generated payload types declare. It has reverse-DNS keys and at least one property, and it is signed with the rest of the payload. The payload with `ext` is checked against the generated type before it is sent. If it doesn't fit, it is dropped, but the document still goes. If there is nothing to report, `ext` is left out entirely, and a member the bridge doesn't know is never sent as `null`.

## Tests

The fake-VTC protocol tests check the report on each document type:
- inspect: exact `ext` on both the `protectionChanged` and the result, and a tampered `ext` fails the proof
- unprobed namespace: `permissionUpgradePending`, `orgRulesets` and `repo` are left out, with no nulls
- bind: `bindCompleted` and the result carry the installation, the missing events, org rulesets and the pending upgrade
- create: the result's `repo.guard`
- bridge-posted check: `protectionChanged` carries `lastCheck` and `guard`
- installation re-probe: the missing list is refreshed
- unit test: the guard mapping

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` all pass locally.

title: feat(ui): every DID can be shown as a QR code for a phone to scan
body:
Every DID drawn by the shared `Did` component now has a small QR button after it. The button opens a popover with "Scan with Keyring", the QR code, the full DID and **Copy DID**, so a phone can take a DID by scanning instead of retyping it.

This is the wallet counterpart of the VTC landing-page QR code (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1698) and `pnm vta qr` (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1700). All three encode the bare DID, so one scanner reads them all.

## Where it appears

- **Through `Did`, `DidNamed` and `MailDid`**, about 32 places: the console panes, the Mediator Lens, setup/network, and disclosure consent.
- **The popup:** beside the VTA DID, the holder DID, and each configured VTA.
- **Not yet:** about 25 places draw a DID without `Did`, including `confirm.tsx`'s `DidField`, the persona screens, onboarding and the popup's warning banners. Moving them onto `Did` also changes how they look, and the consent window is a security prompt, so that's a follow-up rather than part of this.

## Decisions

- **A button beside the DID, not a click on it.** In the DIDs table and the lens, clicking a DID already opens its log or its mail, and the QR code mustn't take that over.
- **The bare DID, UTF-8 bytes, level M, four-module quiet zone.** A DID is already a URI with scheme `did`, so there's no `did://` or app wrapper.
- **Black on white in every theme.** This is the one colour literal outside `theme.ts`, and it's commented as such. A token would invert the code in dark mode, and many phone cameras refuse an inverted code.
- **The popover is portalled to `document.body`, and clicks stop at the component.** React bubbles a portal's events through the component tree, so without the stop, dismissing the popover also clicked the row behind it. A test pins this.
- **`qr={false}`** is for a DID inside another control, where a nested button is invalid: the DIDs table's open button and the did-create checkbox label. The DIDs table puts its QR button beside the open button instead.
- **`qrcode-generator` ^2.0.4** (MIT, no dependencies) builds the module grid. `did-qr.ts` turns it into one run-length SVG path. The QR code adds about 20 KB to the popup/options chunk and to `manager.js`.

## Testing

- `tests/did-qr.test.mts`:
  - A did:webvh is a version-5 code.
  - The path, repainted module by module, is exactly the library's grid inside the quiet zone, with no module drawn twice.
  - The finder patterns are in place.
  - Non-ASCII input is encoded as UTF-8.
- `tests/did-qr.render.test.mts`, in happy-dom:
  - The button opens the popover with the code and full DID, and Escape closes it.
  - Opening, and dismissing with an outside click, never reaches the enclosing row.
  - `qr={false}` inside a button renders no nested button.
- `npm test` across all workspaces passes (1,654 tests), and `tsc -b` is clean.
- `npm run build -w packages/extension` succeeds, and CI's bundle-confinement assertions pass locally:
  - The worker is a single bundle.
  - Admin, persona and mediator task URIs stay confined.
  - `manager.js` is a single bundle.
- **Not done:** I haven't loaded the unpacked extension in Chrome or scanned a code with a phone.

title: feat(persona): read one attribute by name, and call an arrangement a world
body:
Takes **vta-sdk 0.51**, which needed `did-git-sign` 0.4.13 first (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#71): `vta-sdk` is 0.x, so a consumer on 0.51 beside a `did-git-sign` asking for `^0.50` held two copies, and `TrustTask<Value>` crosses between `openvtc` and `openvtc-core` — a build failure, not an untidy graph.

The workspace now holds **one** each of `vta-sdk`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` and `affinidi-tdk`.

### `pool::reveal` reads one attribute

It was a `typePrefix` listing filtered here by id, because the family had no by-id read. To show one email address the agent decrypted **every** email address the holder has and sent them all, and its audit trail recorded a listing of the pool rather than a decision about one value.

`persona/attribute/get` is that read (spec dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#616). The claim type is gone from the signature — it existed only to build the prefix.

### A facet is a world

`persona/world/*`, `worldId`, and the Rust types to match. The screen has said "world" since the Worlds tab existed; `face` and `facet` share a stem while naming different things, and code saying one word while the UI says another is the collision the rename exists to end.

The retired `persona/facet/*` spellings still answer for a release, so this could have waited — but the alias window is for moving, not for staying.

### A face made in a context claims no provenance

saying one word while the UI said another is the collision the rename

title: feat(vtc): show the community DID as a QR code on the landing page
body: A wallet (Keyring first) can now add a community by scanning its DID off the default landing page instead of retyping it. This is the "VTC landing page" row of the Keyring QR proposal: public, carries nothing secret. ## What changes - **`GET /v1/community/did-qr.svg`**: new public, unauthenticated route (classified in `PUBLIC_UNGOVERNED` beside `public-profile`). It renders the profile's `communityDid` as a black-on-white SVG QR code (ECC level M, 4-module quiet zone) and returns 404 until the profile is initialised. The response carries `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` and `nosniff`. - **Landing page (`website-default/`)**: a pass card in the hero shows the QR code, "Scan with Keyring", and the DID with Copy. The Community DID row moves out of the Daemon card into it. - The code stays hidden until it loads, so there is no broken image before setup. - It stays dark on white in the dark theme, because inverted codes fail on many scanners. - On a touch device the caption says to copy the DID instead, since a phone can't scan its own screen. - The DID text now comes from `public-profile`, the same source as the QR, so the two can't disagree. `/health` covers only the window before the profile exists. - **Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` covers the endpoint, including how an operator site under `website.root_dir` can show the same code with one `` tag. - **Dependency**: `qrcode` 0.14, `svg` feature only (MIT/Apache, no extra dependencies). - `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated for the new documented route. ## What the QR carries The bare DID, exactly what Copy copies. A DID is already a URI with scheme `did`, so there is no `did://` or app-specific wrapper. A phone's camera hands the scan to whichever app registers the `did` scheme. Signalling intent to a wallet ("join this community") is still the open "format to agree" item in the Keyring proposal, and a bare DID can't conflict with whatever format that becomes. ## Testing - `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: no failures, including `openapi_snapshot`, `openapi_response_census` and the unauthenticated-route classification test. Two new unit tests cover the renderer. - `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `npm run wire:check`: clean. - Previewed the new page files in Chrome against a running VTC's `/health` and `public-profile`, with the QR rendered by the same `qrcode` code. The stacked phone layout was not checked in a browser, and the code was not scanned with a phone.

title: feat(vtc): the admin console signs its Trust Task documents
body:
Client side of #1684, against the design note merged in #1685 (Option A) and
the server half merged in #1692. The admin console had **no signing primitive
at all** — no `eddsa-jcs-2022`, no Ed25519, no `crypto.subtle.sign` — and that
is the single reason every bearer route #1641 would retire is still mounted
(#1681 §"the bearer routes stay"). It has one now.

## The key, and the flag

```ts
const kp = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: "Ed25519" }, false, ["sign", "verify"]);
```

**The `false` is load-bearing and is not a typo to tidy up.** It governs the
*private* key only; WebCrypto sets `publicKey.[[extractable]]` unconditionally
for a generated pair, so `exportKey("raw", publicKey)` still returns the 32
bytes needed to derive `did:key:z6Mk…`, while `true` would hand the private
half to any script in the origin. That is exactly the defect found in
`did-hosting-ui/lib/session-key.ts` — the file this design says to lift — and
fixed in affinidi-webvh-service#210. So the reason is stated in the code, and
`console-key.test.ts` asserts `privateKey.extractable === false` *and* that
`exportKey("pkcs8"|"jwk", privateKey)` throws, so it cannot quietly flip back.

The `CryptoKey` objects go into IndexedDB as objects, never as bytes; the
structured-clone round trip preserves non-extractability. Where IndexedDB is
unavailable (a private window, an embedded webview, jsdom) the fallback is an
in-memory record that loses the key on reload — the honest degradation, since
nothing writes key material anywhere weaker.

## What is signed, and where

One seam, `src/lib/api.ts::postSignedTrustTask`, as #1692 asked and as
`pnm-browser-plugin` does it (signing belongs to the channel, not to 116 call
sites). It builds `{id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, payload}`, attaches
the proof, and POSTs to `/v1/trust-tasks`.

```
hashData   = SHA-256(JCS(proofConfig)) || SHA-256(JCS(document minus "proof"))
signature  = Ed25519(hashData)                    // via crypto.subtle.sign
proofValue = "z" + base58btc(signature)
```

`issuer` is the **console key's own `did:key`**, not the operator's admin DID:
SPEC §4.7 binds the proof to the in-band issuer, and the delegation is resolved
server-side from the signer. `created` is back-dated 60 s, matching the plugin.

**Lifted**: the JCS canonicaliser and base58btc, near-verbatim from
`pnm-browser-plugin`'s `packages/core/src/trust-tasks/canonical.ts` and
`did-hosting-ui/lib/session-key.ts` (the same code in both). **Written**:
everything around them — the custody, the enrolment, the seam, the fallback,
and the timestamp rule below. Zero new dependencies; the CSP stays
`script-src 'self'`.

### The bug the Rust fixture caught

**Timestamps go out at whole-second precision, and that is not cosmetic.** The
VTC does not verify the proof over the bytes it received: it parses them into a
`trust_tasks_rs::TrustTask`, strips `proof`, and re-serialises *that*.
`issuedAt` is a `chrono::DateTime<Utc>`, whose serde writes `SecondsFormat::
AutoSi` — **no** fractional digits when the sub-second part is zero.
`Date.prototype.toISOString()` always writes three.

So a document stamped on a whole second went out as `…:00.000Z`, came back from
the parser as `…:00Z`, canonicalised to different bytes, and the proof failed —
while every other document that second verified. One request in a thousand,
never reproducible, and indistinguishable at the client from a revoked
delegation. The first run of `vtc-service/tests/console_signed_document.rs`
failed on exactly this. Nothing on the TypeScript side could have found it,
which is the argument for the fixture.

## Does a signed document verify against the real service?

**Yes.** `vtc-service/tests/console_signed_document.rs` verifies a document
produced by `admin-ui/src/lib/console-key.ts` through
`vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::verify_trust_task_proof` — the `did:key`-only
verifier `POST /v1/trust-tasks` reaches via
`trust_tasks/helpers.rs::verify_trust_task_proof`. Three tests: it verifies,
the proven signer is the document's `issuer` (SPEC §4.7), and tampering with
either the payload or the `recipient` breaks it. Regenerate the fixture with
`cd vtc-service/admin-ui && npx vite-node scripts/write-rust-fixture.ts`.

## Which calls now sign

| call | task | door |
|---|---|---|
| member credentials | `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` | **signed**, bearer fallback |
| admin-remove | `vtc/members/admin-remove/0.1` | **signed**, bearer fallback |
| purge | `vtc/members/purge/0.1` | **signed**, bearer fallback |

That is three of the four #1681 tasks. The fourth, `vtc/members/update/0.1`, is
**not reachable from any console screen** — the Members panel promotes through
`acl/change-role` and has no metadata editor — so there is nothing to move.

### The 64 KiB verdict for `members/update`

Checked rather than assumed, as #1684 asks. `UNAUTH_BODY_SIZE = 64 * 1024`
(65536 bytes, `DefaultBodyLimit` on the governed chain, a 413 refusal not a
truncation); `MEMBER_EXTENSIONS_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024` (16384 bytes, measured
on `serde_json::to_vec(&extensions)`). `extensions` is embedded as JSON in the
payload rather than as a string, so nothing is re-escaped and the bag costs its
own size. A document carrying a maximal bag, a 256-character label and every
other optional member comes to **under 18 KiB** — roughly 47 KiB of headroom.
Pinned by a test in `console-key.test.ts` so a later field addition has to
re-do the sum rather than discover it.

## Everything else still uses a bearer route, and why

No bearer route is retired in this PR. Beyond the three above, every console
call still uses one, for three distinct reasons:

1. **No signed door exists yet.** The rest of #1641's 49 are still on the
   bearer surface; each needs its own `DISPATCHED_URIS` binding in a #1641
   batch. This PR unblocks them but does not do them.
2. **A signed document cannot spend a step-up.** `admin_signer` builds claims
   with `session_id: ""`, so `require_fresh_step_up` always fails on that door.
   Anything gated on a live passkey gesture — `acl/grant`, `acl/change-role`,
   console-key enrolment itself — must stay on the session-bearing path until
   that interaction is designed. Worth stating as a design fact, not an
   oversight: the design note (§6f) wants the step-up to stay exactly where
   #1658 put it.
3. **Three routes have no published task at all** — `/v1/admin/console-keys`
   itself, which is why it uses the `*Exempt` helpers.

**Before the bearer routes can be retired**, in order: (a) this ships and
operators enrol; (b) `vtc-client` gets the same path for the three of the four
it reaches (it has `vta_sdk::trust_task_sign` already, so it is small); (c) the
step-up-over-signed-documents question above is answered for the verbs that
need one; (d) then the routes, their OpenAPI entries and the transitional
descriptions come out and `openapi.json` + `wire.ts` regenerate.

## Fallback behaviour

`signedOrBearer(typeUri, payload, bearer)` catches `SigningUnavailableError`
and **nothing else**. Two causes produce it: no WebCrypto Ed25519 (below Chrome
137 / Firefox 130 / Safari 17, detected by an actual `generateKey` since
nothing advertises the curve synchronously), or no key enrolled in this
browser. Both fall through to the existing call, unchanged.

A signed call that is *refused* propagates. Retrying it over a bearer token
would use the session as the authority the signed door exists to stop relying
on, and would hide a revocation from the operator who just performed it.

## The Signing keys screen

Beside **My passkeys**, because it is the same kind of thing. Lists the
caller's keys with the server's own `active` (not re-derived — the two
disagreeing is how a page shows a key as working after it stopped), marks the
row this browser holds, labels a new one, and revokes. Revoking this browser's
own key also forgets the local copy, so it cannot sit there signing documents
the daemon refuses. It handles: already enrolled, a browser with no key yet, a
browser whose key was revoked (a fresh one is generated — a revoked console DID
is tombstoned and can never be re-enrolled), a refused passkey, and a browser
that cannot sign at all.

## One finding, deliberately not fixed here

#1692 introduced an OpenAPI **schema-name collision**. utoipa keys
`components.schemas` by the bare Rust type name, and `routes/admin/
console_keys.rs` declares `ListResponse` and `RevokeResponse` — names already
used by `routes/admin/passkeys.rs` and by four other routes. The console-key
shapes won, so the published document now has `GET /v1/admin/passkeys` pointing
at a schema describing `{consoleKeys}`. Nothing noticed because
`myPasskeys.tsx` carries a local interface.

The fix is `#[schema(as = ConsoleKeyListResponse)]` / `…RevokeResponse` plus a
regenerate, and it is server-side, so it is not smuggled into a console PR.
`wire-types.ts` records it where the stale `PasskeyListResponse` alias was, and
`console-keys-api.ts` deliberately does not read the revoke response body. The
`RevokeResponse` collision predates #1692.

## Tests

`npm run lint` (wire:check + tsc) passes — `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are
untouched, which is the check that this PR only consumes the API.
`npx vitest run`: **222 passed, 27 files**, of which 50 across five new files are new. They assert on
the document that would go on the wire, not on "we called fetch": the envelope
member by member, the proof's six members, and an independent recomputation of
`hashData` from the serialised document verified against the public key.

Covered: the private key does not export while the public key does; the derived
`did:key` *is* the public key; a page reload restores the same key still
non-extractable; the JCS rules the signature rests on (key order, presence
sensitivity, non-ASCII); whole-second timestamps; the signature verifies; the
fallback on both causes; the non-fallback on refusal; enrolment order (gesture
before write) and that a refused passkey writes nothing; revocation with and
without the local key; and the screen's states, including that a successful
enrolment updates it without a reload (checked to fail without the fix, so it
is not a vacuous assertion).

`cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`, run without
`VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` so the admin UI builds as part of it and
`openapi_snapshot` would catch an unintended API change.

That run found one thing, in a second commit. `trust_task_manifest.rs::
every_admin_ui_task_is_enforced_by_a_route` scans **every** file under
`admin-ui/src` — tests included — and treats each spec URI as a `Trust-Task`
header the console sends. `signed-door.test.ts` mocks the daemon's *error*
document, whose type is `trust-task-error/0.5`: a framework type no route
binds and no client ever sends. The guard called it a dead page. The scan now
skips `*.test.ts(x)`, which is the rule `collect_prefixed_in_file` already
records for the other side of the same comparison — a URI in a fixture is not
wiring — and it still fails on an orphan added to a non-test file, checked
rather than assumed.
`cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
are clean; the only Rust in this PR is the new test and its fixture.

Refs #1684, #1641.

title: chore(deps)!: messaging-sdk 0.27.1 + trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3; answer a mutual TSP cancel the SDK could not (Keyring VTI-38)
body:
## What

Moves VTI onto **affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.1** and **trust-tasks-rs 0.22.3**, with exactly one copy of each in the graph. Also adapts the TSP control path to the SDK's new meaning of `reply_expected`, which is what closes **Keyring VTI-38** (mutual TSP cancellation left unanswered) on the VTI side.

#1690 already moved main to trust-tasks 0.22.1 / SDK 0.27.0 / tdk 0.17 / test-mediator 0.10 / mediator-admin 0.2. This PR raises the floors and makes the SDK pin structural:

| Crate | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `affinidi-messaging-sdk` | `0.27.0` (five per-crate literals) | `0.27.1` (**workspace table**, floor) |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | 0.22.1 | **0.22.3** (floor: first release with the `git-ns` family, `trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns`) |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | 0.22 | 0.22.3 (floor) |
| `trust-tasks-{https,tsp,capability-client,didcomm}` | 0.22.x | resolve to 0.22.3 |

No `version =` field of a workspace crate is touched; release-plz owns those.

### Why the others have to move with it

`trust_tasks_rs` types cross the public API of six upstream crates: `affinidi-messaging-sdk` (`MediatorAcl` among them), `affinidi-messaging-mediator` (via test-mediator), `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin`, and `trust-tasks-{proof,https,tsp,capability-client}`. If any one of them stays on its 0.21-line release, the graph holds two `trust-tasks-rs` and fails with `expected X, found a different X`. `mediator-admin`/`-tui` 0.1 and `test-mediator` 0.9 were the non-obvious ones: 0.1 still pinned SDK 0.26 and 0.9 pulled mediator 0.26.

### The SDK pin moves into the workspace table

`affinidi-messaging-sdk` was a hand-written literal in `vta-sdk`, `vta-service`, `vti-common`, `room-host` and `tests/e2e`. A literal that falls behind the others still resolves, so nothing catches it until `affinidi-tdk` moves a minor and the graph splits. It is now one workspace entry, `{ version = "0.27.1", default-features = false }`. Members inherit it and add their own features. `tests/e2e` asks for `default` explicitly, so its feature set is the same as before.

## Breaking changes adapted to

1. **affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.27.1: `reply_expected` has a new meaning** (tdk #887, Keyring VTI-38). `TspOps::record_incoming_control` now sends the §7.3 answer to a mutual cancellation itself. `reply_expected` (and `InboundKind::RelationshipControl::reply_expected`) now means *the answer is still owed*: it is `true` only when the SDK's own send failed. For a cancellation, `thread_digest` is now the relationship digest the peer named.
   - Before this PR, when `decide_control` returned `ControlDecision::Cancel`, the VTA's and VTC's `handle_tsp_control` called `cancel_relationship`. By then the relationship is already `None`, so that call refuses `SendCancel` out of `None`. That refusal is the VTI-38 failure itself, and it was still reachable on the retry path.
   - Both now call **`TspOps::answer_cancellation(profile, sender_vid, thread_digest)`**, which sends without running the state machine. `vta-service/src/messaging/{service.rs,tsp_inbound.rs}` and `vtc-service/src/messaging.rs` are updated, including the `ControlDecision::Cancel` docs and the §7.3 comments.
   - `decide_control` is unchanged. Its unit tests (VTA + VTC) are renamed and re-documented for the new semantics: `false` now also covers "already answered", and answering then would send twice. The retry path needs a failed mediator send partway through a control frame, which the embedded test mediator cannot inject, so no e2e test was added for it.
2. **trust-tasks-rs 0.22.0: `persona/facet/*` → `persona/world/*`.** #1690 (merged) already migrated to it. Nothing further needed here.
3. trust-tasks-rs 0.22.1–0.22.3 (`persona/attribute/get`, vetting/PCS tasks, `git-ns`) are **additive**. `all-specs`, the workspace's existing pattern for spec families, already enables `git-ns`. `schema_index::error_codes_for` / `spec_policy_for` did not change shape, so `error_code_census` and the proof/recipient/issuedAt enforcement in `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs` needed no change and their tests pass.
4. SDK 0.26.19–0.27.0, tdk 0.17, test-mediator 0.10 and mediator-admin 0.2: no source change needed. 0.26.26 and 0.26.27 (Keyring VTI-39/VTI-41) are pure SDK fixes that VTI now picks up.

## Single-copy evidence

```
$ cargo tree --workspace --all-features -d -e normal,dev,build --depth 0 | grep -E '^(trust-tasks|affinidi|dtg)'
(no output; the same holds without --all-features)

$ cargo tree --workspace --all-features -e normal,dev,build -i <crate> --depth 0
trust-tasks-rs v0.22.3
trust-tasks-proof v0.22.3
affinidi-messaging-sdk v0.27.1
dtg-credentials v0.11.0
affinidi-tdk v0.17.0
```

`Cargo.lock` has one entry each for `trust-tasks-*`, `affinidi-messaging-{sdk,mediator,mediator-common,didcomm,core,delivery}`, `affinidi-tdk`, `affinidi-tdk-common`, `affinidi-tsp`, `affinidi-data-integrity`, `affinidi-secrets-resolver`, `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` and `dtg-credentials`.

## Unblocks

The **hidden-vetting branch (`zkp-pcs`)**, which needs the `vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-*`, `vetting/attestation` and `vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge` schemas from 0.22.2, and the git-ns work, which needs `trust_tasks_rs::specs::git_ns` from 0.22.3. `vtc-service/src/vetting/schemas/` and `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK` are deliberately **not** touched here; the hidden-vetting branch owns that cleanup.

## Semver report

This may go red. Public dependencies (`trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-messaging-sdk`, `affinidi-tdk`) moved a minor under 0.x, which is a breaking change for any crate that re-exports their types, and cargo-semver-checks cannot see a break that arrives through a dependency. A red report here is the report doing its job, not a defect. release-plz picks the bumps.

## Tests run

- Before the rebase: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, and `cargo check --workspace --locked`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets [--all-features] -- -D warnings`
- The CI reduced feature sets: the `vta-service` `tee,rest,didcomm` / `rest,didcomm` checks and the `rest` / `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis` / `setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis` clippies; `vti-rooms --features mls` clippy; the `vta-sdk` `attest-verify` and `client,sealed-transfer,provision-integration` checks; `vta-enclave rest,didcomm,vsock-store`
- wasm32: `cargo check -p vti-rooms --lib --no-default-features --features mls --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo build -p vti-rooms-wasm --profile wasm-release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vta-service` on trust-tasks 0.22.3, **before the rebase onto #1688/#1690–#1692**: 164 test binaries, **5089 passed, 0 failed**, TSP e2e suites included.
- `cargo test -p vta-service`, also before the rebase: the lib suite plus the first 11 integration binaries, **1561 passed, 0 failed**. The run was stopped partway through the integration tests (the machine is shared with other sessions). **The rest of the vta-service integration tests, and the full suite on the rebased tree, are left to CI.**
- After the rebase: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, fmt, and the `cargo tree` single-copy check above were all re-run and are clean.
- TSP e2e suites (tt 0.22.2, then again inside the 0.22.3 run above): `tsp_vta_trust_task` (12), `tsp_vtaclient_relate` (11), `tsp_dual_client_reply` (10), `tsp_self_repair_on_drop` (10), `tsp_round_trip` (13), `tsp_binding_pair` (10), `tsp_dual_leg` (13), `tsp_ping_correlation` (11). All pass.
