title: feat!: add taskDigestMultibase, so a VWC binds to the witness/session it cites
body:
Adds `taskDigestMultibase`. The only VWC-issuing flow the specifications define requires it, and this crate had no way to produce it.

**Specification dependency:** trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#56 defines the member in DTG Core Credentials. It is approved but not merged. This PR can merge once #56 is accepted.

## What the specifications require

- **`witness/session/submit/0.1`** (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf), Conformance item 1: the VWC in the witness's response MUST carry two members. `taskContext` MUST equal the `id` of the `witness/session` document that opened *this* session. `taskDigestMultibase` MUST be that document's *task digest*. The same spec says the member's schema "belongs to DTG Core Credentials". `witness/session/0.1`'s `outcomeEvidence` declares the binding at `/payload/vwc/taskContext` and `/payload/vwc/taskDigestMultibase`. Both are top-level members of the VWC.
- **Trust Tasks §4.9.3** (Binding a Citation to the Document It Names) defines the digest as `multibase(multihash(H(JCS(document ∖ proof))))`:
  - only the **top-level** `proof` is removed; a `proof` inside `payload` is content and stays;
  - `H` is any multihash algorithm, with SHA-256 RECOMMENDED;
  - the encoding is any `DigestMultibase` form (`z` or `u`);
  - a verifier compares **decoded multihash bytes**;
  - a verifier treats an unimplemented algorithm as *unverified*, with no fallback to comparing `id`s.
- **dtgwg-cred-spec#56** makes it a top-level property: "REQUIRED wherever `taskContext` is REQUIRED, OPTIONAL otherwise". It adds the property as the sixth member under §Digest Encoding, so an issuer emits sha2-256 and base58btc. That is a valid narrowing of §4.9.3, and it makes the task digest exactly `digest_multibase_json` computed over a Trust Task document.

## API

| | |
|---|---|
| `DTGCommon::task_digest_multibase` + accessors | A modelled member, so a non-string value is refused at parse time. A VWC without it still deserializes. |
| `task_digest_multibase_json(&doc)` | The task digest. It has its own name because Trust Tasks also defines a *step digest* that includes the `proof`, and the two must not stand in for each other. VTI #1630 fixed exactly that confusion. |
| `DTGCredential::new_vwc_for_session(issuer, subject, from, until, &session, digest, ctx) -> Result` | Reads `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` from the session document, so the pair cannot disagree. The edge digest is REQUIRED. Refuses anything except the opening `witness/session` (`NotAWitnessSession`): a `submit` document, a `#response`, or a document whose `threadId` is not its own `id`, which `witness/session` Conformance item 1 requires. |
| `with_task_citation` / `set_task_citation` | Sets both members from one document, on any credential type (for example a `vetting/session` statement). |
| `cites_task(&doc) -> Result<bool>` | Checks the `id` and recomputes the digest, comparing decoded bytes. A credential with no `taskDigestMultibase` returns `Ok(false)`, never an `id`-only match. An unimplemented algorithm is an error. |
| `new_vwc` | Deprecated, because it cannot set the digest. |

### Why this breaks the API

`DTGCommon` is not `#[non_exhaustive]`. Its fields are public, and every constructor builds it with `..Default::default()`. Adding a field therefore breaks exhaustive struct literals only, which is the same break 0.3.0 made for `credentialStatus`. I chose that over the fully additive alternative, which would keep the member in `DTGCommon::extra`, for two reasons:

- The specification makes the member REQUIRED on every VWC, beside `taskContext`, which is already a modelled field.
- `extra` is documented as holding members this library does *not* model, and it would accept a non-string value without complaint.

Marking `DTGCommon` `#[non_exhaustive]` now would be worse: it forbids `..Default::default()` outside the crate. `new_vwc` keeps its signature and is deprecated rather than given a new required parameter, following the pattern 0.10.0 used for `new_member_vmc` → `_for`.

The wire is unchanged for a credential that lacks the member. An older release carries the member through a round trip in `extra`, so this release has no upgrade-ordering constraint. I have not bumped the version. The CHANGELOG entry is under `[Unreleased]`, and `#[deprecated(since = "0.11.0")]` assumes the next release is 0.11.0.

## Tests (`tests/task_citation.rs`, 22)

- **Vector from a second implementation.** `vetting/session/0.1` prints a session document and the `taskDigestMultibase` of it (`zQmWAWEtpUqE3xd3LUpZ8GryGrZMCqH1A5D7bZcayvEfJTK`). `task_digest_multibase_json` reproduces it. The four steps are also recomputed by hand. The Vetting Statement printed there parses, and `cites_task` accepts it against that session.
- **Proof handling.** The digest ignores a top-level `proof` (signed, unsigned and re-signed copies give one value) and keeps a `proof` nested in `payload`.
- **Round trip.** A session VWC serializes with `taskDigestMultibase` at the top level. It parses back into the modelled field (not `extra`), still cites its session, and `digest_multibase()` agrees with the digest of the wire form.
- **Decoded-bytes comparison.**
  - A base64url (`u…`) spelling of the same multihash is accepted.
  - A sha2-512 multihash returns `UnsupportedDigestAlgorithm`, not `false`.
  - A counterfeit that reuses the session `id` with different content is refused.
  - A VWC with no digest cites nothing.
- **Constructor refusals.** The `submit` document, the `#response`, a mismatched or missing `threadId`, a missing `id`, and an inverted validity window.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: pass
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: pass. Also passes with `--no-default-features`.
- `cargo test --all-features`: 186 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --no-default-features`: 170 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`: no warnings

## Not addressed here

- **The VWC's type on cred-spec `main`.** It is no longer `WitnessCredential`. The spec now expresses it as a `StatementCredential` under the `dtg:witnessed` predicate profile (dtgwg-cred-spec#45). This crate, `new_vwc_for_session` included, still builds the WD02 `WitnessCredential` shape. That migration is separate work. `taskDigestMultibase` is a top-level member either way, so this change carries over.
- **`vwcDigestMultibase`.** In `witness/session/submit#response` it is taken over the credential **including** its `proof`, unlike every digest this crate computes. `digest_multibase` is the wrong function for it.

Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1068.

title: Witness credentials are reasoned about but never built or verified
body:
## Summary

The ceremony engine treats `WitnessCredential` as a policy fact — with
trusted-issuer, validity and holder-binding predicates — but no VWC is ever
constructed or verified anywhere in the stack. `DTGCredential::new_vwc` and
`digest_multibase` are never called.

## Detail

`WitnessCredential` occurs in `ceremony/verify.rs`, `ceremony/facts.rs`,
`ceremony/evaluate.rs`, `routes/ceremonies.rs` and `policy/default.rs` — in
every case as a `credential_type` string in a fact the policy reasons over, not
as a credential the code builds or checks.

The exacting part is therefore entirely untested here. Per DTG Credentials the
VWC's `credentialSubject.digest` MUST be:

- the SHA-256 hash of the witnessed VRC,
- canonicalised with JCS (RFC 8785),
- encoded as a Multibase-encoded Multihash,
- `sha2-256` (header `0x12`, length `0x20`), base58btc (`z` prefix).

And Security Considerations 4 requires a verifier relying on that binding to
have the referenced VRC in hand, recompute the hash, and compare **decoded
digest bytes rather than encoded strings**.

`dtg-credentials` implements all of this correctly (`DTGCredential::digest`,
`digest_multibase`), including the recent multibase change. Nothing calls it.

## Why it matters

A ceremony can currently reach a decision on the *assertion* that a witness
credential was present, without any code path that could have established it
was valid or that it witnessed the edge in question. Security Considerations 4
is explicit that without recomputing the digest against the referenced VRC, a
VWC "should not be treated as evidence of which edge was witnessed".

## Suggested fix

1. Build VWCs through `new_vwc` on whatever path is meant to issue them.
2. On receipt, recompute the digest against the referenced VRC and compare
   decoded bytes.
3. `taskContext` is REQUIRED on the VWC specifically — see #1065, which is a
   prerequisite rather than a parallel task.

Conformance audit finding **F8**.

title: feat(persona)!: derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#582 (design note
docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.7).

Provenance::Derived { source, derived_at }: a value taken from a source
the holder connected or supplied — a code-hosting profile, an uploaded
CV — that nobody signed. Previewed as `derived` at the whole rung, never
as attested, and it correlates as a typed value does, since there is no
issuer signature to link. `source` is the kind of source, never a handle
or URL, because provenance reaches the verifier.

Attribute.endorsements: vault ids of credentials in which a third party
endorses the value. Inventory, not evidence — it never touches
provenance and is not disclosed with the value. attribute/put checks
every id against the vault and refuses one it does not hold (a
soft-deleted credential does not count) with `endorsementNotFound`.

`pnm persona attribute put --provenance derived --source <kind>
[--derived-at]` and `--endorsement <credential-id>`. The provenance flags
are gathered into ProvenanceFlags, and a flag the chosen provenance
ignores is still refused.

The design note records a gap found here: attribute/put's rule that a
credentialBacked provenance's credential is resolved at write
(`credentialNotFound`) is not implemented.

title: fix(cnm): vetting, audit and backup authenticate to a VTC with its own DID as audience
body:
`cnm vetting`, `cnm audit verify` and `cnm backup` could not sign in to a
VTC. All three took a token from `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated`, whose
audience is not a parameter: it is always the session's bound *VTA* DID, and
the DIDComm authenticate envelope it builds is encrypted to that DID's
key-agreement key. A VTC holds only its own keys, cannot open the envelope,
and refuses the login. `cnm vetting` then also built its `VtcClient` with the
VTA's DID as the community's DID. main connected to the VTA first, so without
`--url` the requests went to the VTA's REST URL too.

They now authenticate the way `cnm did-log install` does (#1632):
`VtcClient::connect(base, vtc_did, client_did, key)` with the profile's DID
and key, and the VTC's DID as the audience. They are exempt from
`requires_auth`, so no VTA connection is made first.

Where the VTC's DID comes from: `--vtc-did` (env `CNM_VTC_DID`), else a new
optional `vtc_did` on the community profile, set with
`cnm community set-vtc <did>`. The DID is never read from the server (for
example the VTC's `/health`): it is the audience the sign-in is signed for,
and a server allowed to name it could name another community's DID and
relay the signed document there. Discovery runs from DID to URL, as it does
for a VTA: `--url` if given, otherwise the `VTCRest` service in the DID's
document, matched on `type` and checked by the same endpoint guard as a
VTA's advertised REST URL.

The root cause is a generic "token for this base URL" helper sitting on a
session bound to one audience. `cnm`'s `auth::ensure_authenticated` wrapper
is removed, so nothing in `cnm` can reach the VTC through the VTA session
again, and `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` now documents that it
authenticates to the session's VTA only. Nothing else in the workspace
used `SessionStore` against a VTC.

When the VTC refuses the sign-in, `cnm` prints the fix with the DID filled
in: `vtc --config <config.toml> acl add --did <DID> --role admin --label cnm`,
or Access control, Add entry in the console. A VTC answers every
authentication failure the same way (VTI-SES-007), so the message names the
usual cause rather than claiming it.

Routing these through a live VTC exposed two more faults on the same paths,
fixed here:
- `cnm backup export` saved the `{ envelope }` response (the export shape
  since #1059) instead of the envelope, so the file printed `(none)` for
  its source DID and could not be imported. `VtcClient::export_backup`
  returns the envelope, and accepts a pre-#1059 bare one.
- `cnm audit verify` read the signed-checkpoint result from the top level,
  but #1110 moved it under `ext["org.openvtc"]`. Every report therefore
  looked like it had no checkpoint result, and a truncated log that the
  community key contradicts passed as long as its hash chain did. It reads
  both places now, and fails on any checkpoint status it does not know
  rather than passing it.

vtc-client gains `audit_verify`, `export_backup`, `import_backup`,
`REST_SERVICE_TYPE` and `api_base_from_did_document`, plus the three task
URIs. All are additive.

Tests: `vtc-service/tests/cnm_vtc_admin_live.rs` runs the audit, backup
(export then import preview) and vetting paths against a `MockVtc` over
HTTP. It also checks that a DID with no ACL row is refused in the shape
`cnm` keys its guidance on, and that the old VTA-session login fails where
the VTC-audience login succeeds. `cnm-cli/src/vtc.rs` asserts that the
authenticate document `cnm` sends names the VTC's DID as its `recipient`,
and that the refusal prints the `vtc acl add` command.

Docs: the bootstrap runbook gains the super-admin row `cnm` needs.
community-lifecycle.md and credentials.md listed `cnm join`, `cnm members`,
`cnm policies`, `cnm credentials`, `cnm endorsement-types` and `pnm vtc`
commands that do not exist. They now point at the admin console and REST
routes, and list what `cnm` does provide.


## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4748 passed, 0 failed, 50 ignored. The slow `self_hosted_did` 304 test passed after more than 60 s.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (admin UI built): 1779 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Left open

- The VTC's (and the VTA's) DI-signed `auth/authenticate/0.1` path does not check the document's `recipient`. The DIDComm path is audience-bound by encryption, but the REST path is not, so the server side of the audience binding is missing. Out of scope here.
- `VtcClient::upload_policy` sends `{purpose, regoSource}` to a `deny_unknown_fields` body expecting `{name, module, …}`. Untouched.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.15
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory ([#582](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/582))

Design note (VTI docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md) §5.7.

  Provenance gains `derived` {source, derivedAt}: a value taken from a
  source the holder connected or supplied — a code-hosting profile, an
  uploaded CV — that the holder did not type and no issuer signed. It is
  the holder's claim that the source said so, and a consumer must not
  present it as attested. `source` names the KIND of source (`github`,
  `cvUpload`), never a handle or URL: provenance reaches the verifier, and
  a handle there would disclose an identifier the holder never chose to
  share. For how strongly a disclosed value identifies the holder the
  kinds rank credentialBacked > derived > selfAsserted. The preview's
  provenance enum gains `derived`.

  Attribute gains `endorsements`: vault ids of credentials in which a
  third party endorses the value. Inventory, not evidence — a vouched
  self-assertion is still self-asserted, and folding a vouch into
  provenance would render it as attested. Not disclosed with the value.
  attribute/put takes it and refuses an id the vault does not hold
  (`endorsementNotFound`).

- **spec**: Vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1 — get an invitation to the DID it admits ([#581](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/581))

Keyring VTI-21 and VTI-32. `vtc/invitations/issue` returns the signed
  invitation to the inviter once, and nothing carried it further: an
  invitee was reached only by whatever the inviter improvised, and the
  credential is too large for a QR code.

  This task delivers an issued invitation over the credential-exchange
  family the framework already has. On `message` the community sends a
  `credential-exchange/offer` to the invited DID over a transport it
  advertises (`noRoute` if none); on `offer` it returns the OID4VCI offer
  for the inviter to hand over — small, because it names the credential
  rather than containing it. Either way the invitee redeems with
  `credential-exchange/request`, and the credential is released only for a
  key-binding proof by the invited DID's key, so a photographed QR code
  admits no one else. At most one offer per invitation is live; the
  invitation credential never appears in this task's response.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

title: test(vtc): every declared error code must be shown emitted, or baselined (#1600)
body:
The conformance ledgers witness the success path only (#1600). A spec could
declare extended codes, the service could emit none of them, and every gate
stayed green. `withdraw/0.1` shipped that way: its handler answered both
declared codes through the generic `app_error_to_reject` as a bare
`taskFailed`.

Since trust-tasks-rs 0.21.13 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#575), the
bindings carry each specification's declared `errorCodes`, as `ERROR_CODES`, a
per-task `error_codes` module, and `schema_index::error_codes_for`. The
workspace already requires 0.21.14 (#1635); this derives a census from those
codes.

`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/error_code_census.rs` takes its scope from the
same bound ∩ published `spec/vtc/*` set as `conformance.rs`, and gets the
declared codes from `error_codes_for`. No code strings are written by hand.
Every declared code must either have a `witness!` row naming the integration
test that asserts the service emits it, or appear in a typed, shrink-only

title: feat(persona): derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory (#582)
body:
feat(persona): derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory (#582)

Design note (VTI docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md) §5.7.

Provenance gains `derived` {source, derivedAt}: a value taken from a
source the holder connected or supplied — a code-hosting profile, an
uploaded CV — that the holder did not type and no issuer signed. It is
the holder's claim that the source said so, and a consumer must not
present it as attested. `source` names the KIND of source (`github`,
`cvUpload`), never a handle or URL: provenance reaches the verifier, and
a handle there would disclose an identifier the holder never chose to
share. For how strongly a disclosed value identifies the holder the
kinds rank credentialBacked > derived > selfAsserted. The preview's
provenance enum gains `derived`.

Attribute gains `endorsements`: vault ids of credentials in which a
third party endorses the value. Inventory, not evidence — a vouched
self-assertion is still self-asserted, and folding a vouch into
provenance would render it as attested. Not disclosed with the value.
attribute/put takes it and refuses an id the vault does not hold
(`endorsementNotFound`).

title: feat(persona)!: where a face may be worn, where it is, and what it has done
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#577 (design note
docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.4, §9.6).

Face reach. A pool face carries `reach` — FaceReach::Anywhere (default)
or Only { context_ids } — an enum rather than a context list, so
unrestricted and nowhere cannot be confused (#746/#769/#770).
binding/set refuses a face outside its reach (`outsideReach`);
profile/put refuses to narrow it past a context the face is worn in
(`boundOutsideReach`, naming them). An omitted reach on profile/put keeps
the face's current one: a client written before reach existed must not
lift a restriction by saving an edit.

persona/profile/usage — where a face is worn now, each binding's
`until`, and the reach beside them.

persona/profile/timeline — one face's history, oldest first: composed,
worn, unworn, expired, disclosed, valueChanged, promoted, retired,
reinstated. A binding taken off left no trace, so each face now has an
append-only event log (`pft:`, agent-scoped, ULID-keyed so recording
never takes the write lock), written after the change it describes and
never failing it; the timeline joins it with the disclosure records. A
face from before the log reports its composition from createdAt. A
promoted face keeps its log; a deleted one loses it. FaceEvent has no
member a value or label could go in, and a test holds that none reaches
the wire.

profile/compose takes `until` (`untilNotFuture`).

`pnm persona profile usage|timeline`, `put --reach-only/--reach-anywhere`,
`compose --until`. Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14.

BREAKING: Profile gains `reach`; ComposeRequest gains `until` and
ComposeRefusal a variant; VtaClient::persona_profile_put takes `reach`;
PersonaProfilePutBody gains a member; vta-cli-common cmd_profile_put and
cmd_profile_compose take new arguments.



Verified locally with the CI set on trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14: `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` (4746 passed), `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (1757), clippy `-D warnings`, fmt.

title: feat(spec): vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1 — get an invitation to the DID it admits
body:
Adds **`vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1`**: a way to get an issued invitation to the DID it admits. This answers Keyring's VTI-21 (no channel delivers an invitation) and VTI-32 (an invitation is too large for a QR code).

## Why a task, and why so small

`vtc/invitations/issue` returns the signed invitation to the inviter **once**. Nothing carried it further, so an invitee was reached only by whatever the inviter improvised. The credential is also too large to fit in a QR code.

This task doesn't define new delivery machinery. It uses the **credential-exchange family the framework already has**:

- **`channel: "message"`:** the community sends a `credential-exchange/offer` to the invited DID, over a transport that DID advertises. If it advertises none, the answer is `noRoute`.
- **`channel: "offer"`:** the community returns the OID4VCI Credential Offer to the inviter, to hand over out of band. It's small enough for a QR code because it *names* the credential rather than containing it.

Either way, the invitee redeems it with `credential-exchange/request` and receives the credential in `credential-exchange/issue`.

## The property that matters

The offer's pre-authorized code redeems **only** for a `credential-exchange/request` whose key-binding proof is made with a key of the invited DID. So:

- a photographed QR code, a misdirected message or a logged offer admits no one else. That's why `exposure.discloses` is `metadata`, while `issue` is `secret`.
- the invitation credential itself never appears in this task's response; it reaches only the invitee.
- at most one offer per invitation is live, because a new delivery replaces the previous one.

## Checks

- `npm run validate` passes for all 472 specs. The validator caught a local `expired` code shadowing the standard §8.3 `expired`, so the spec now uses the bare standard code.
- The Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated, and `check-bindings` shows all four agree, 897 declared error codes included.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes with 923 tests and 0 failed.
- The negative examples run under `--features validate,vtc`: `request_example_1`, `response_example_1` and `rejects_invalid_examples` all pass.
- `npm run build` passes.
- No versions or CHANGELOGs are touched; release-plz owns those.

The implementation in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure follows once this is released. The VTC already has the OID4VCI offer store and key-binding verification (`credentials::exchange::{make_offer, redeem}`).

title: fix(acl): key-export and persona-holder, and a narrowing that means what it says
body:
Follow-up to VTI #1619, and a re-sync of `acl-capabilities.json`, which had fallen **two** capabilities behind vti-common 0.21.0.

## The snapshot

- **`key-export`** (VTI #1619) is derived by `admin` alone. Exporting a key is gated separately from using it (VTI-VTA-003), so `initiator` keeps `key-mint` and does not get this.
- **`persona-holder`** is *additive*: no role derives it, and the agent grants it only to entries that name it. The sync script now parses `ADDITIVE_CAPABILITIES` into the snapshot. It fails loudly if that list is missing, rather than writing a snapshot that says there are none.

## Fixed: the console disagreed with the agent's rule

The agent (`vti_common::acl::effective_capabilities`) narrows an entry only by its **non-additive** names, then adds the additive ones on top.

The console intersected the role with the *whole* list. So an entry granted only `persona-holder` computed as holding **nothing**, when the agent gives it the full role plus the pool. `checkNarrowing` also refused `persona-holder` because no role includes it. The agent skips that role check for additive names and instead checks the *granter* (super-admin only), which the console can't see.

## Fixed: the access pane's editor could do the opposite of what it said

- **"Narrow" with nothing ticked sent `[]`**, under a warning that the entry "would be able to do none of what the role allows". The agent reads `[]` as *clear the narrowing*, which means the whole role. So the button meant to take everything away actually restored everything. A narrowing to nothing can't be expressed, so the button is now disabled with an explanation, and the way to take a role's authority away is a role change.
- **"Clear narrowing" sent `[]`**, which silently revoked `persona-holder`. It also stayed enabled on an entry whose only stored name was additive, where there was nothing to clear.

Both now go through a new core function, `narrowingToSend(kept, stored, intent)`. It carries additive grants through, and refuses a narrowing to nothing. The pane edits only the role's own capabilities and shows additive grants on their own line.

## Tests

- New tests in `acl.capabilities.mjs`: the additive list matches the snapshot; no role derives an additive capability; `key-export` is admin's alone; effective sets are right with additive grants alone and alongside a narrowing; `narrowingToSend` keeps the grant, clears without revoking it, and refuses a narrowing to nothing (each refusal paired with the acceptance it borders).
- Whole workspace: `npm run build`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass (124 + 668 + 750 + 6 + 9 tests, 0 failed).

body:
### Added

- **rs**: Emit each specification's declared error codes ([#575](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/575))

A specification's `errorCodes` front matter (SPEC §7.3 item 9) never reached
  the Rust bindings, so an implementation could only spell a declared extended
  code as a string literal, and nothing checked the literal was a code the
  specification declares — or that the service emitted the codes it declares at
  all. Downstream, that let `vtc/join-requests/withdraw/0.1` ship answering both
  of its declared codes as a bare `taskFailed` with every gate green
  (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1600).

  `trust-tasks-codegen` now emits, for every generated module:

  - `pub const ERROR_CODES: &[DeclaredErrorCode]` — the declarations in order,
    empty when the specification declares none;
  - `pub mod error_codes` (when it declares any) — one `DeclaredErrorCode`
    constant per code, named for its local part in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE

title: feat(persona): where a face may be worn, where it is, and what it has done
body:
Design note (VTI docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md) §5.4 and
§9.6, and `until` on compose.

FaceReach — a pool face may carry `reach`: `{kind: anywhere}` (the
default, and what absent means) or `{kind: only, contextIds: [...]}`.
binding/set refuses to wear a face outside it (`outsideReach`), and
profile/put refuses to narrow it past a context the face is worn in now
(`boundOutsideReach`, naming them). A tagged object rather than a bare
context list, so "unrestricted" and "nowhere" cannot be confused: `only`
needs at least one context, and nowhere is a retired face.

persona/profile/usage/1.0 — where one face is worn now, with each
binding's `until` and the face's reach beside them. Holder-only: it is
the map of which personas are one face.

persona/profile/timeline/1.0 — one face's history joined, oldest first:
composed, worn, unworn, expired, disclosed, valueChanged, promoted,
retired, reinstated. Never a value and never a private label. A
maintainer records from now on what it would not otherwise keep — a
binding taken off leaves no trace in the one that replaces it — and may
omit what happened before and left no record.

profile/compose takes `until`, for the face composed at the door of a
conference; `untilNotFuture` refuses one in the past or without a
personaDid.

title: feat(vtc): a self-hosted community installs its own DID log over did-management/did/register
body:
Keyring VTI-35: *a VTC cannot advertise the TSP service it is able to serve.*

## What's actually wrong

`vtc setup` has offered `#tsp` at mint since #929, but only when a mediator is configured during setup. Adding it **later** depends on where the community's DID is hosted:

- **On a DID host** (`did:webvh:<scid>:<host>:<path>`): `pnm did-mgmt dids edit` on the VTA is enough, because the VTA publishes each new entry to the host itself.
- **Self-hosted, or "serverless"** (`did:webvh:<scid>:<host>`, Keyring's setup): the VTC serves `data/did/<host>.jsonl` itself. The VTA holds the keys that extend that log but has no way to reach the VTC's copy, and the VTC keeps no VTA credential after setup. So the new entry can only arrive by an operator copying the file by hand, which is what Keyring did. Their restart wasn't needed; the route reads the file on every request.

## The fix: the VTC answers `did-management/did/register/0.1` for its own DID

No new Trust Task. `register` is the task a DID owner sends a DID host, and its spec already treats a second register from the owner with a longer log as an update. A self-hosted community is a DID host for exactly one DID, so it answers `register` for that DID at the root slot `.well-known`, over `POST /v1/admin/did/register`. The route requires a super-admin. (A new spec, trust-tasks-tf#574, was drafted and closed as superseded.)

Before serving anything, `did_log_install::check` verifies:

1. **The whole log:** every entry's proof under the update keys in force, the SCID and the hash chain. `validate()` + `assert_complete()`, so a partly valid chain is refused rather than cut down.
2. **The DID** is the community's own.
3. **Every served entry** survives unchanged, byte for byte, at the start of the new log. This refuses a shorter, rewritten or forked log. `register` alone would accept those from the owner, so this stricter rule carries a code minted by the VTC, as SPEC §8.5 allows (`org.openvtc.vtc:didLogNotAnExtension`).

The file is then swapped atomically (a temporary file renamed over the old one, holding a lock), with no restart. Re-sending the log already served changes nothing. A DID with a path is refused as not self-hosted, because a copy stored here would never be what resolvers read.

**Authority covers delivery only.** The log authenticates its own entries, so an administrator, or someone holding a stolen admin token, can't publish an entry the key holder didn't sign, or move the served log backwards.

## Operator path

```sh
pnm did-mgmt dids edit <community-did> …                  # the VTA signs the new entry
pnm did-mgmt dids get-log <community-did> --out did.jsonl
cnm did-log install --file did.jsonl
```

`cnm did-log install` authenticates **directly to the community**, with the community's DID as the audience (`VtcClient::connect`). It doesn't use the profile's VTA session, whose `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` uses the *VTA's* DID as the audience, which a VTC refuses. The same problem affects `cnm vetting`, `cnm audit` and `cnm backup` against a VTC, and is left for a separate fix. The operator's DID needs a super-admin entry in the VTC's ACL (`vtc acl`).

## Also

- `VtcClient::install_did_log`, and a `vtc_client::did_register` re-export of the generated types.
- `vta_sdk::openapi::{DidRegister01Payload, DidRegister01Response}` wrap the generated types. The OpenAPI snapshot and the admin console's `wire.ts` are regenerated.
- A new `AuditEvent::CommunityDidLogInstalled` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is additive).
- `didwebvh-rs` becomes a regular vtc-service dependency instead of setup-only.
- `MockVtc::start_with(TestVtc)`, so a test can serve a VTC it built itself.
- The redeploy hint #1624 prints for a DID the VTA manages but doesn't serve now names `cnm did-log install`.

## Tests

- `did_log_install`, 9 tests: an extension signed by the key holder, idempotent reinstall, a shorter log, a fork signed with the same key, a tampered entry, another DID's log, garbage input, the atomic swap on disk leaving nothing behind (and a refusal leaving the served file untouched), and no served log.
- `tests/did_register.rs`, 6 tests: the extension is served afterwards; a non-admin gets 403; a shorter log gets 409; another slot gets 400; a community whose DID has a path gets 404; and **a live test** that authenticates with `VtcClient::connect` and installs over real HTTP.
- `cnm` helpers: the DID is derived from the log, and the API URL from the DID.
- Whole workspace (excluding vtc) 4721 passed / 0 failed; vtc-service + vtc-client 1742 / 0; `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt` pass.

title: fix(vta)!: contexts/secrets requires KeyExport (VTI-VTA-003)
body:
`vta/contexts/secrets/1.0` (`get_context_secrets`) released a context DID's
private keys to any `Application`-role caller in that context. Its only gate
was the role floor (`require_write`, which also admits `Initiator`) plus the
context scope. VTI-VTA-003 says an export of derived key material "MUST be
gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key, and MUST
be audited". The audit was already there; the separate capability was not.
An `Application` can *use* its context's keys through the signing oracle, and
under the old gate that also let it *take* them. That is the case the
requirement exists for: keys that were taken stay with the caller after its
authority is withdrawn.

## The gate

`get_context_secrets` now requires `Capability::KeyExport`, the same
capability `keys/export-secret` requires. It reads the caller's **entry**,
like `ensure_may_mint` (#1619), so a narrowing that removes `key-export` from
an admin stops the next fetch. With no entry, the role decides. A store error
refuses the call. The gate replaces the `require_write` role floor. The
existing `require_context` scope check and the per-key `key.secret_export`
audit are unchanged.

`KeyExport` stays exactly as #1619 left it: derived by `admin` alone, and not
grantable to any other role. So the service that operates a context's DID
must be an admin **scoped to that context**. Integrations onboarded through
`provision-integration` already have that grant: the mediator, did-hosting
and the VTC. They are not affected.

## Who is affected

Any `application` or `initiator` entry that fetches its context's secrets
through `VtaClient::fetch_did_secrets_bundle` or
`vta_sdk::integration::startup`. The known one is **room-host**, whose
enrolment instructions granted `--role application`. After upgrading, such a
caller gets `permissionDenied`, which the SDK surfaces as
`VtaError::Forbidden` on REST, DIDComm and TSP. The message names the command
that fixes it for that caller's entry:

- an existing non-admin scoped to the context:
  `pnm acl change-role --did <did> --from application --to admin`
  (this keeps the entry's contexts);
- an entry with no contexts: `pnm acl update <did> --contexts <CONTEXT>`
  first. The fix never suggests promoting an unscoped entry, because that
  would mint a super-admin;
- an admin narrowed without `key-export`:
  `pnm acl update <did> --capabilities <existing>,key-export`
  (the narrowing is restated, never `--capabilities-all`);
- no entry: `pnm acl create --did <did> --role admin --contexts <CONTEXT>`.

## Also changed

- room-host's `grant_instructions` and its missing-DID help now grant a
  context-scoped admin (`vta import-did --role admin --context <C>` /
  `pnm acl create --role admin --contexts <C>`).
- `vti-secrets` gains `OnboardingTicket::admin_import_did_command`. Its module
  docs now separate integrations that only call the VTA (`application`) from
  those that load their DID's keys (context-scoped `admin`).
- Doc comments on the task constant, the handler, the SDK method and
  `get_context_secrets`. `docs/02-vta/integration-guide.md` gains a
  "Who may fetch a context's secrets" section.

## Tests (VTI-VTA-003)

- The `operations/export.rs` tests that asserted the old loosening are
  rewritten.
- New tests cover these cases: an Application is refused, an Initiator is
  refused, a context admin gets the bundle, an admin narrowed without
  `key-export` is refused, an admin of another context is refused, an
  unscoped non-admin is told to scope first, and a reader is refused. The
  entitlement-before-existence non-leak test now runs against both gates.
- A handler-level test checks that the refusal is `permissionDenied` and
  carries the fix command.

Closes #1625


## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`vta-service/src/operations/device.rs::split_capabilities` lists an entry's *stored* capability list whenever it is non-empty, instead of `effective_capabilities`. So an entry holding only an additive grant (today `persona-holder`) under-reports everything its role derives. This is unrelated to this change and is left for its own PR.

The TS console's role table (`acl-capabilities.json`) is not affected: `KeyExport`'s derivation is unchanged since #1619.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4725 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 1726 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

These ran against 5decb937. The branch was then rebased onto 1099d7b2 (#1627, which only adds VTC docs).

title: contexts/secrets releases a DID's private keys without KeyExport (VTI-VTA-003)
body:
## Summary

`vta/contexts/secrets/1.0` hands a context DID's **private keys** to any caller with the `Application` role in that context. It doesn't check the `KeyExport` capability. VTI-VTA-003 says any export of key material must be gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key, and must be audited. The bundle path is audited, but it isn't gated separately, and I can't find a divergence entry for it in the spec's Appendix F.

## Where

- `vta-service/src/operations/export.rs` → `get_context_secrets`: the role floor is `auth.require_write()` (Application or higher) plus `require_context` inside `build_did_secrets_bundle`. There's no capability check.
- By contrast, `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/keys.rs` → `handle_export_secret` (`keys/export-secret/0.1`) requires `Capability::KeyExport` and cites VTI-VTA-003 in its comment.
- Both paths reach `get_key_secret`, so each released key is audited (`key.secret_export`).

## The design reasoning is sound, but it isn't recorded as a divergence

The doc comment on `get_context_secrets` explains the intent. A service the VTA holds an identity for has to hold that DID's private keys to decrypt what's addressed to it. Reading "the keys of the DID you already operate is not an administrative act", and the context scope is enforced twice.

That's a reasonable position. But as written, VTI-VTA-003 covers *any* export of derived key material. VTI-VTA-002 goes further: operate on keys rather than export them. The rationale given for VTA-003 is that a caller holding a key keeps it after revocation. An `Application` principal that fetches a bundle keeps those keys after its role or scope is revoked, which is exactly the case the requirement targets.

## Options

1. **Record it** in Appendix F as a divergence from VTI-VTA-003, keeping the current behaviour and its justification (service DIDs must decrypt locally, and the VTA has no remote key agreement). Or amend the requirement so it distinguishes "a service loading the keys of the DID it operates" from export.
2. **Gate it** on a capability: either `KeyExport`, or a narrower one such as "operate this context's DID". That way granting `Application` doesn't imply export.
3. **Longer term (VTI-VTA-002):** a remote key-agreement / decrypt operation, so a service never needs the raw key-agreement secret.

## Context

This came up while designing `pnm messaging console` (a mediator console that runs as a VTA-managed DID). That feature will use per-key `keys/export-secret` (gated by `KeyExport` and audited) so it meets VTI-VTA-003 as written. So it doesn't depend on how this issue is resolved.

that fixes it for that caller's entry:

- an existing non-admin scoped to the context:
  `pnm acl change-role --did <did> --from application --to admin`
  (this keeps the entry's contexts);
- an entry with no contexts: `pnm acl update <did> --contexts <CONTEXT>`
  first. The fix never suggests promoting an unscoped entry, because that
  would mint a super-admin;
- an admin narrowed without `key-export`:
  `pnm acl update <did> --capabilities <existing>,key-export`
  (the narrowing is restated, never `--capabilities-all`);
- no entry: `pnm acl create --did <did> --role admin --contexts <CONTEXT>`.

## Also changed

- room-host's `grant_instructions` and its missing-DID help now grant a
  context-scoped admin (`vta import-did --role admin --context <C>` /
  `pnm acl create --role admin --contexts <C>`).
- `vti-secrets` gains `OnboardingTicket::admin_import_did_command`. Its module
  docs now separate integrations that only call the VTA (`application`) from
  those that load their DID's keys (context-scoped `admin`).
- Doc comments on the task constant, the handler, the SDK method and
  `get_context_secrets`. `docs/02-vta/integration-guide.md` gains a
  "Who may fetch a context's secrets" section.

## Tests (VTI-VTA-003)

- The `operations/export.rs` tests that asserted the old loosening are
  rewritten.
- New tests cover these cases: an Application is refused, an Initiator is
  refused, a context admin gets the bundle, an admin narrowed without
  `key-export` is refused, an admin of another context is refused, an
  unscoped non-admin is told to scope first, and a reader is refused. The
  entitlement-before-existence non-leak test now runs against both gates.
- A handler-level test checks that the refusal is `permissionDenied` and
  carries the fix command.

Closes #1625

title: fix(vta): warn at boot when approval rules exist but policy enforcement is off
body:
Refs #1608 (KR-22)

## Problem

`policy.enforcement` defaults to `false`. With it off, a rule written with `pnm approvals require` (or a hand-authored `pnm policy upsert` row) is stored, listed and explained, then gates nothing. Nothing tells the operator that. Keyring hit this as "consent policies inert by default".

## Decision

The default **stays off**. Turning it on would make every policy that was written but not meant to be in force a gate in every existing deployment at upgrade. The defect was the silence, so this PR adds a warning and documentation. Behaviour does not change.

## Change

- **vta-policy**: `unenforced_policies()` returns an `UnenforcedPolicies` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, new type, additive) with two parts:
  - how many approval rules are on the enabled declarative `approvals` row
  - the ids of enabled hand-authored rows

  It does not count the boot-installed `default` baseline, disabled rows, or a declarative row that holds approver sets but no rules. None of those would gate a task even with enforcement on.
- **vta-service** (`server::run`, after the policy seed): if enforcement is off and the result is non-empty, the VTA logs one `WARN`. The warning names what is being ignored and the fix: set `enforcement = true` under `[policy]` in config.toml, then restart. It is advisory only. If reading the rows fails, that is logged too, and boot never stops because of it. The enforcement flag is copied out of the config lock before the keyspace read, so the lock is not held across an await (R1.3).
- **docs/02-vta/approvals.md**: a callout at the top says approvals are opt-in and off by default. The Enforcement section now has the TOML snippet, explains why the default stays off, and shows the boot warning.

Example output:

```
WARN policy.enforcement is off, so 1 approval rule (`pnm approvals list`) is stored but NOT enforced — every task runs on the caller's own authority. Enforcement is opt-in: set `enforcement = true` under `[policy]` in config.toml and restart the VTA to apply it. See docs/02-vta/approvals.md#enforcement.
```

## Tests

- `vta-policy` `defaults::tests::kr22_*` (3): the baseline alone is not reported; approval rules and enabled operator rows are reported and disabled rows are not; approver sets without rules are not reported.
- `vta-service` `server::unenforced_policy_tests::kr22_warning_names_the_rules_and_how_to_enable_enforcement`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --no-default-features --features rest --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --no-default-features --features setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4724 passed, 0 failed, 50 ignored.
  - This run skipped one test, `routes::self_hosted_did::tests::if_none_match_with_current_etag_returns_304_without_body`, which hangs on my local macOS machine even when run alone.
  - The hang is unrelated to this diff, which touches no routes and no rate limiting. The same test passes in CI on this PR's base commit (run 35656644744, `Test (workspace)` success).
- VTC job not run: nothing on the VTC side changed.

title: feat(vtc): serve a member's credential bodies and show them in the admin console
body:
Closes #1215

## What

Admins can now read a member's credential bodies. It works through the new route `GET /v1/members/{did}/credentials`, bound to `vtc/members/credentials/0.1`, and through a Credentials card on the member-detail page in the admin console. The upstream task (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#336) is closed, and the generated module is already in the locked `trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.11, so this needs no dependency bump.

### Service
- **Route**: `AdminAuth`, with a Trust-Task header binding in `routes/mod.rs`. It sits under `/v1/members/{did}/`, before the `/{did}` catchall, like `relationships`.
- **What it reads**: the four fields #1213 keeps on the member row. No new storage and no new verification. `memberVmcBound` is the value stored at receipt.
- **Wire type**: the generated `specs::vtc::members::credentials::v0_1::Response`, documented by a new `vta_sdk::openapi::MemberCredentials01Response` wrapper (the pattern the census requires). There is no local mirror type.
- **Pairing rule**: `memberVmcReceivedAt` goes out only together with `memberVmc`, because the spec says a maintainer MUST NOT send one without the other. A row from before #1213 has the id and the receipt time but no body, so neither is sent.
- **Not found**: an unknown member gets a 404 with `{"error": "...", "code": "vtc/members/credentials:notFound"}`. That is the spec's only declared error code. The `error` member and the status are unchanged from every other VTC 404, so clients that read the status keep working. "Unknown" is judged the same way `members/show` judges it (member row **and** ACL row), so a tombstoned member is not found. A member who holds nothing gets a 200 with `memberVmcBound: false`, which the spec says is a real answer and not a failure.
- **Audit**: the spec says a maintainer SHOULD record the read, so each read writes a new `MemberCredentialsRead` event in `vti-common`. The event lists which documents were disclosed and never includes their contents. The write happens before the response. `AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant is additive and needs no `!`.
- **Conformance witness**: in `trust_tasks/conformance.rs`. It projects through the handler's own `credentials_response`, over a row filled by the real `record_issued_credentials` / `record_member_vmc`, rather than using a transcribed fixture.
- **Snapshots**: `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated.

### Console (`plugins/members.tsx`)
- The existing Credentials card now lists the grant, the acknowledgement and the role VEC, using the `<details>` + copy-JSON pattern from the published-relationships list.
- When `memberVmcBound` is false, the card shows the grant on record next to the digest the acknowledgement names (WD02 `credentialSubject.digestMultibase` or WD01 `credentialSubject.digest`). It also names the case: no acknowledgement, no digest, no grant body held, or never checked. All of this sits right above **Request member VMC**. The console does not recompute a digest; the daemon's `memberVmcBound` is the only verdict.
- The logic for reading those details lives in `lib/member-credentials.ts` and has vitest coverage.
- `MemberCredentialsRead` now has a label in the audit viewer.

### Docs
- New section in `docs/03-vtc/credentials.md`: "Reading a member's credentials".

## Tests
- `tests/members_crud.rs`, 7 new tests:
  - success: bodies come back as stored, and exactly one audit row is written, naming the disclosed documents
  - a member holding nothing: 200 and unbound
  - an unknown member: 404 with the declared code and no audit row
  - a departed member: 404
  - no token: 401
  - a non-admin: 403
  - the header of another task (`members/show`): refused
- Unit tests for the projection, including the pairing rule both ways.
- `vti-common` round-trip test for the new audit variant.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vti-common -p vta-sdk --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (admin-UI build **not** skipped): 1738 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p vti-common --lib audit`: 106 passed
- `vta-sdk` `generated_wire_types_census`: passed
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean
- admin-ui: `npm run lint` (`wire:check` + `tsc`) clean, `vitest run` 168 passed (20 files)

title: Serve a member's credential bodies, and show them in the admin console
body:
## The gap

The admin console can tell an operator that a member holds a membership credential. It cannot show them what it says.

#1213 made every issuance path keep the bodies — `Member::current_vmc`, `current_role_vec`, `member_vmc`, plus `member_vmc_bound` — so the data is all on the row. Nothing reads it out. `members/show/0.1` carries only the identifiers, and its response is `additionalProperties: false` with its own schema saying *"The credential body is not echoed here"*, so this cannot be fixed by adding a field locally: the conformance harness would reject it, correctly.

That leaves three questions unanswerable from the console:

- **What did we issue this member?** Only the ids are visible.
- **What exactly did they acknowledge?** The member-issued VMC is stored and never rendered.
- **Why is this edge incomplete?** The member-detail page says *incomplete* and cannot show the digest that failed to bind, or the grant it was checked against.

## Blocked on upstream

trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#336 proposes `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` — a per-member, admin-gated read returning the membership pair's bodies plus `memberVmcBound`. `MemberResponse` is shared by show/list/update, so bodies belong in a new task rather than on it; the issue has the reasoning.

Nothing here can land until that task is published and `trust-tasks-rs` is bumped. Per the stack-refresh discipline, that bump is not incremental downstream — two `trust-tasks-rs` versions in one graph fail to compile rather than warn — so verify with a path `[patch.crates-io]` over the TDK workspace before the publish.

## Work once unblocked

**Service** — `GET /v1/members/{did}/credentials`, `AdminAuth`, bound to the new URI in `routes/mod.rs`. Reads the four fields already on the row; no new storage, no new verification. `every_bound_canonical_task_exists_in_the_registry` confirms the URI resolves once the crate lands.

**Console** — a Credentials card on member detail, using the `<details>` + copy-JSON pattern the published-relationships list already uses (`plugins/members.tsx`). Worth rendering the digest comparison explicitly where `memberVmcBound` is false: the operator's next action is *Request member VMC*, and showing which grant the acknowledgement names makes it obvious why.

## Why it matters beyond ergonomics

DTG Core Credentials, *Membership Edge Completion*:

> A community asserting an entity's membership MUST be able to produce the member-issued VMC that completes the edge.

We hold that credential and have no way to produce it. Today that is a console gap; the same route is what a future protocol-level answer would read from.

## Related

- #1213 — stored the bodies and the binding state; this is the read side
- trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#336 — the upstream task this waits on

title: fix(vtc): a witness credential is personhood evidence only when its digest binds
body:
Refs #1068. This covers item 2 (the personhood `assert` path) and fixes a digest defect in #1161 that item 1's round-trip test found. Item 1 (issuing VWCs through `new_vwc`) is left open because the specifications do not make the VTC a VWC issuer. The reasons are below.

## A defect in #1161

`credentials::witness` could not verify a VWC built to the specification, for two separate reasons, and neither one caused a test failure:

1. **Wrong member.** It read `credentialSubject.digest`, the Working Draft 01 name. WD02 renamed the member to `digestMultibase`, which is what `DTGCredential::new_vwc` writes. So a VWC built by the catalog resolved `Absent`.
2. **Wrong coverage.** It recomputed with `ingress::digest_multibase`, the Trust Task framework digest, which includes the `proof`. DTG Credentials §Digest Encoding step 1 excludes the top-level `proof`. `ingress.rs` already warns against using one of these functions in place of the other. Stored VRCs are signed, so even with the right member name it would have resolved `Unresolved`.

The fix is to read `digestMultibase` first (the WD01 name is still accepted, as `dtg-credentials` accepts it), recompute with `dtg_credentials::digest_multibase_json`, and decode with `dtg_credentials::decode_digest_multibase`, plus a check that the digest is 32 bytes. Producer and verifier now use one implementation. The join/ceremony path calls the same `resolve_binding`, so this fix applies there as well.

## Personhood `assert` now uses the binding verdict

- `witness::annotate_vp_claims` writes the host's `WitnessBinding` onto every `WitnessCredential` entry in `vp_claims`. It uses the key (`witness_binding`) and shape (`{state, relationship_id}`) that the ceremony `Credential` fact uses, so a policy reads both the same way. The key belongs to the host: it is overwritten on witness entries and removed from all other entries, so a presenter cannot supply the verdict. If storage fails, the verdict is `Unresolved`, which is the same choice the join path makes.
- The default `personhood.rego` witness rule now requires `witness_binding.state == "bound"`. `unresolved` is not forgery (the edge may belong to another community), but this community cannot see the edge, so the default does not accept it. The operator doc shows the one-line change for an operator policy that should accept it.
- **Existing deployments.** `install_defaults` only fills missing pointers, so without an upgrade every VTC that is already running would keep the permissive default. `upgrade_unbound_witness_personhood_default` runs at boot. It replaces the active personhood policy only if **both** of these are true: the author is `DEFAULTS_AUTHOR`, and the policy *allows an unbound witness probe*. Like `upgrade_legacy_ceremony_defaults`, it checks what the policy does rather than comparing source hashes. The replacement is a new revision and the old revision is kept. An operator-authored policy is never replaced, even when its source is byte-identical to the old default (a test covers this).

## Why item 1 (issuance) is not done here

I read the specifications to find the path that should issue a VWC:

- **DTG Credentials WD02 §VWC:** the `issuer` is "a member, or a VTA acting according to VTC policy". The glossary says the same: a person, or "the VTA for a VTC who applies the VTC's policies for witnessing". The VTC is never the issuer in its own right. vtc-service signs as the community DID, and the spec says the community's identifier must be `public`. The spec only requires the witness identifier to be `directed` at minimum.
- **The issuing path the spec defines** is the Trust Task pair `witness/session/0.1` + `witness/session/submit/0.1` (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, already generated into `trust_tasks_rs::specs::witness`). The witness is the recipient. It opens a per-party session, verifies the party's VP against the session challenge, and delivers the VWC in `submit#response` together with `vwcDigestMultibase`. Nothing in VTI implements either task, and the witness role belongs to a member's or VTA's agent, not to the community service.
- **That path also requires a member that `new_vwc` cannot produce.** `witness/session/submit` Conformance item 1: the VWC's `taskDigestMultibase` **MUST** be the task digest of the `witness/session` document (framework §4.9.3). It says this member's schema "belongs to DTG Core Credentials". DTG Credentials WD02 does not define `taskDigestMultibase`, and `dtg-credentials` 0.9.1 has no parameter or field for it. A VWC built through `new_vwc` today therefore cannot conform to the only issuing flow the specifications define.

So issuance has to start upstream: `taskDigestMultibase` in dtgwg-cred-spec, then `dtg-credentials`, then a witness-role implementation of `witness/session{,/submit}` in the component that plays the witness (a VTA or member agent, not vtc-service). The `taskContext` requirement from #1065 is already met by construction, because `new_vwc` takes `task_context: String` as a required argument.

What this PR does for item 1: it pins `new_vwc` against the verifier. `a_catalog_built_vwc_binds_to_the_signed_vrc_it_witnessed` builds a VWC with `new_vwc` and `DTGCredential::digest_multibase` over a signed VRC stored the way publication stores it (with the framework digest in the column, so a verifier that matched on the column fails the test). The test fails on `main` for both reasons above. A second test checks that the same VWC carries `taskContext` and passes `ingress::classify_dtg`.

## Also noticed, not changed

The personhood assert route does not verify the proofs of embedded credentials (step 5 has noted this since the D2 review). The binding verdict establishes *which edge* a witness names. It does not establish that the named witness actually issued the credential. That gap is the same as before this PR and is out of scope here.

## Tests

- `witness.rs`: catalog round-trip (`new_vwc` → verifier → `Bound`); one VWC per direction binds its own edge; the digest excludes `proof`; `digestMultibase` is read before `digest`; a truncated or WD01 hex digest is `Malformed`; `annotate_vp_claims` touches witness entries only; a presenter-supplied verdict is overwritten.
- `personhood.rs` (VP → projection → shipped default policy): accepts a bound witness; refuses a witness naming an edge not held here, a digest over the wrong coverage, no digest, and a non-multihash; ignores a presenter-supplied `bound`.
- `policy/default.rs`: the rego rules for each state; the upgrade replaces the old default once, is idempotent, and never replaces an operator policy; the shipped default refuses the upgrade probe.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (admin UI built, `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` unset): 1402 passed, 0 failed
- Only `vtc-service` and docs changed, so the workspace job was not re-run.

The witness-digest verifier from #1161 read the Working Draft 01 member

framework digest, which includes the `proof`. DTG Credentials WD02
§Digest Encoding names `digestMultibase` and excludes the top-level proof,
so a VWC built by `DTGCredential::new_vwc` to the specification resolved

still accepts the WD01 name. It recomputes with `digest_multibase_json` and

onto every witness entry of `vp_claims`, using the key and shape of the

overwritten or removed. The default policy allows only `bound`.

`install_defaults` never revisits a filled pointer, so a VTC first booted

title: feat(pnm): pick which DID to open the mediator console as
body:
Two fixes to \`pnm messaging console\` (#1626), both found in use.

## 1. \`no mediator for <did>\` for a DID that publishes one
```
✗ Error: no mediator for did:webvh:QmUcyd…:webvh.storm.ws: pass one explicitly or publish a DIDCommMessaging service
```
The DID publishes its mediator in the array form, \`[{ "uri": "did:webvh:…:mediator" }]\`. \`affinidi-did-common\` 0.4.2 on crates.io returned that \`uri\` JSON-quoted. The fix had been merged in the TDK but never released, because the version wasn't bumped. affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#860 released it as **0.4.3**, and **\`affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin\` 0.1.1** also accepts the quoted form. This PR moves \`Cargo.lock\` to both; there are no manifest changes.

## 2. Choosing among several DIDs in a context
The console offered only a context's own DID (\`ContextRecord.did\`). It now offers every DID whose keys are in a context:
- **How DIDs are found:** from the key records alone (\`list_keys\`, active, per context), by the same \`{did}#…\` rule \`select_secret_kid\` uses. Nothing is exported to build the list. It covers every DID method, and exactly the DIDs whose keys the console could load.
- **Order:** the context's own DID comes first. A context DID with no keys in the context isn't offered, since it couldn't be loaded.
- **Labels:** when a context holds several DIDs, each choice shows its DID.
- **\`--did <DID>\`:** picks directly, alone or with \`--context\`.
- **\`--context\` with several DIDs and no \`--did\`:** asks among that context's DIDs.
- **Nothing narrowed:** asks among every choice, pnm's own session included, unless there's exactly one context DID.

Key export for the chosen DID is unchanged: per-key \`keys/export-secret\`, KeyExport-gated and audited (VTI-VTA-003).

## Tests
- **Unit:** picking by context, DID, or both; the no-match error names what was asked for; a key's DID comes from its id or its verification-method label, and a decorative label is ignored (#337); the context DID is listed first.
- \`cargo clippy -p pnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings\` and \`cargo fmt --all --check\` are clean.

No version fields are edited.

title: feat(persona)!: retire a face, warn before deleting one, and let a binding end on its own
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#570 (design note
docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.4, §9.5).

persona/profile/retire and persona/profile/reinstate, for pool and
context-local faces. Retire marks the face before clearing its bindings,
so an interrupted retire leaves a face that cannot be newly worn and a
repeat finishes the clearing; the cleared bindings come back in
`unbound`. binding/set and local/binding/set refuse a retired face
(`profileRetired`), profile/list leaves retired faces out unless
`includeRetired`. Reinstate binds nothing. Profile gains `status` and
`retiredAt`.

Binding `until` on binding/set and local/binding/set, returned by
binding/get and binding/list; `untilNotFuture` refuses one in the past or
on a cleared binding. A lapsed binding reads as cleared at once — every
binding read decodes through BindingRecord::into_read, and present
refuses a preview whose persona no longer wears a face — whether or not
the sweeper has run. The storage-thread sweeper (expire_bindings,
audited as persona.binding.expire) makes the clear durable and retires a
face the expiry left worn nowhere; never one still worn elsewhere, and
never deletes.

profile/get and profile/delete return `disclosedTo` {partyCount,
contextCount}; `pnm persona profile delete` says "deleting does not
un-tell them". Disclosure records now carry the face they were made
through; an older record is attributed through its binding where that
still wears the face.

`pnm persona profile retire|reinstate`, `list --include-retired`,
`binding set --until`, `local binding set --until`. Retire is
Destructive for the MCP guard (it withdraws access everywhere at once),
reinstate Mutating; both RetrySafe.

Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.12.

BREAKING: PersonaStore::set_binding and set_local_binding take `until`;
Profile, Binding, BindingSummary and DisclosureRecord gain members;
VtaClient::persona_binding_set and persona_local_binding_set take
`until`, persona_profile_list takes `include_retired`;
PersonaBindingSetBody, PersonaLocalBindingSetBody and
PersonaProfileListBody gain members.



Verified locally with the CI set after rebasing on main: `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` (4728 passed), `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (1726), clippy `-D warnings`, fmt.

title: Add the Vetting Card as a first r-card profile (initial draft)
body:
## What

This is the first content for this specification, marked as an **initial draft** throughout. It fills only what is needed to carry one profile:

- **Introduction:** scope, quoting the VDS definition from `dtgwg-cred-spec`.
- **Vetting Card** (normative, draft): an r-card profile that an applicant signs and presents to one vetter during an identity vetting session. It defines:
  - the card's members;
  - a Data Integrity `eddsa-jcs-2022` proof by the publisher;
  - audience, challenge and domain binding, a 15-minute validity window, and the checks a verifier applies;
  - `identityCommitment` and `commitmentSalt`, with one salt per application;
  - the card digest, taken over the exact form received;
  - what a card never carries: document numbers, document images, portraits.
- **Security, Privacy and Conformance** for the profile, plus references.
- **Glossary:** VDS and r-card (taken from the DTG Credentials spec), and vetting card.

## Left as template placeholders

Editors, contributors, document status, DOI, abstract, the IPR working group name, the Governance, Internationalization and Accessibility sections, and the appendices. None of these values were invented.

## Please look at

- **Commitment construction.** It commits only `type` and `value`, not `provenance`, so a claim later backed by a credential keeps the same commitment. Claims are ordered by `type`, with at most one claim per committed type. These are proposals and carry an editor's note.
- **Base r-card structure.** This spec doesn't define it yet, so the `claims` element shape is illustrative.
- **Card digest.** It follows the DTG Credentials Digest Encoding (JCS, `proof` excluded), taken over the card as received rather than a re-serialisation.

## Context

- This comes from the OpenVTC design `docs/design/vetting-process.md` (DRAFT v2; PR in `OpenVTC/openvtc` opened separately), sections 9.2 and 13.4 and decisions D2, D11 and D17.
- The statement a vetter issues after checking a card is a VEC, described in the identity-vetting endorsement profile proposed in trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#49.
- Related Trust Task specs, including the vetting session that carries the challenge and domain, are being proposed in `trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf`.

## Validation

`npm run collectExternalReferences` (the command `render-and-deploy.yml` runs) exits 0. Compared with `main`, the only new console line is `Dangling Definitions: VTC`: the template's example VTC term is no longer referenced once the placeholder body is replaced, and I left that term file untouched. All internal anchors resolve, the JSON example parses, and the commit carries a DCO sign-off.

title: Conformance ledger witnesses the success path only — declared error codes are never checked
body:
## The gap

The conformance ledgers (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/conformance.rs`, and the
VTA's equivalent from #857) witness the **success** path only. Of 71 witnesses
in the VTC table, **zero** carry an error code, and nothing anywhere else in
the workspace checks one either — a grep for `extended_code` or any `*_ERR_*`
constant across `vtc-service/tests` and `vta-sdk/tests` finds no census.

So a specification can declare extended error codes under SPEC §8.5, the
service can emit none of them, and every gate in the repo stays green.

This is precisely the defect class the file was written for, applied to the
other half of the wire. Its own module docs say:

> a VTC response could diverge arbitrarily from the schema its URI names and
> every gate in the repo stayed green

That is now true of the error response.

## It is not hypothetical — it shipped this week

`vtc/join-requests/withdraw/0.1` (#1591) declares two extended codes,
`withdraw:notFound` and `withdraw:alreadyDecided`. The handler returned
through the generic `app_error_to_reject`, which flattens `NotFound` and
`Gone` into a bare `taskFailed` carrying only English prose. **Neither
declared code was ever emitted**, and the ledger was green — the success
witness conformed, because the success path was fine.

It was caught only because I happened to add a dispatcher-level test asserting
the codes. Nothing required that test, and nothing would have noticed its
absence. The same shape recurred immediately afterwards on
`submit:requestAlreadyOpen` (#1592) and the three `supplement:*` codes
(#1593), each caught the same ad-hoc way.

Worth noting what this costs externally: telling `notFound` from
`alreadyDecided` without parsing prose is the entire reason a spec declares
two codes, and Keyring's KR-27 — auth refusal answered untyped — is a finding
of exactly this class that we received from outside rather than caught here.

## Why this is not a one-line census

The obvious fix is a derived census: for every witnessed task, assert the
service can emit each error code its specification declares. **The declared
codes do not reach the Rust bindings.** `errorCodes` lives in spec front
matter and in the upstream `registry.json`; `trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.6 emits no
`error_codes` constant, no `ErrorCode` type, and nothing in `schema_index`
exposes them. Our extended-code constants are hand-written string literals in
`vta-sdk` (`JOIN_REQUEST_WITHDRAW_ERR_NOT_FOUND = "vtc/join-requests/withdraw:notFound"`).

So there are two routes, and the cheap one is the wrong one:

1. **Hand-maintain the list in the ledger.** Cheap, and it reintroduces
   exactly the failure mode this file's design deliberately avoids — its URI
   census is "derived, not hand-maintained" for a reason, and the
   trust-tasks-tf CLAUDE.md documents four separate defects shipped by
   hand-maintained lists drifting from the tree.
2. **Have `trust-tasks-codegen` emit the declared codes**, then derive the
   census from them the way the URI census is derived. Upstream work in
   dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first, then a census here. This also removes the
   hand-written literals in `vta-sdk`, which today can silently disagree with
   the spec that defines them — nothing checks that
   `"vtc/join-requests/withdraw:notFound"` is a code the specification
   actually declares.

Route 2 is the one worth doing. Route 1 is worth considering only as a stopgap
if route 2 is blocked, and should carry a comment saying so.

## Scope note, so this is not closed prematurely

Two further limits are **stated** in the file and are not part of this issue,
but are worth keeping visible in the same place:

- the VTC ledger covers `spec/vtc/*` only; the 36 shared
  `spec/{acl,audit,auth,config,policy}/*` URIs it also binds are uncovered,
  pending a decision on which daemon's response shape is canonical;
- a witness is a fixture the author writes. Only 7 of 17 `to_v` witnesses
  project through production code (e.g. `routes::join_requests::manifest::
  response_v0_1`); the rest are transcribed by hand, so they assert that a
  shape the author believes in conforms, not that the service emits it.

The second is the point the plan's execution step 5 was making: the ledger
measures fixtures, not the running service. Filing it here so it is not closed
along with KR-09.

title: docs(vtc): bootstrap runbook for the first admin and vetter, and credential delivery
body:
Two Keyring findings (KR-01, KR-11 and KR-25; indexed in #1608) needed
documentation, not code.

## KR-01 and KR-11: bootstrap order

New: docs/03-vtc/bootstrap-runbook.md. Every step in it comes from the code.

- A fresh VTC's ACL is empty, including for the admin DID that setup prints.
  Setup records that DID only in the install token. The admin ACL entry is
  written in one place, POST /v1/admin/bootstrap, which is the last step of
  the install claim. Until the claim runs, /v1/auth/ answers 403.
- The runbook gives two paths. Path A: claim the install URL (or mint a fresh
  one with `vtc admin invite --did`). Path B, with no browser: seed the entry
  offline with `vtc acl add` or `vtc create-did-key --admin`.
- It records an ordering trap. admin/bootstrap refuses with 409 once any admin
  entry exists, and the install page treats that 409 as success. So adding an
  admin entry for another DID before the claim leaves the setup's admin DID
  with a passkey and no ACL entry.
- The first vetter has to be a separate identity. A vetter grant needs a
  Member row. An admin's ACL entry blocks it from being invited (409) and
  from joining (the admit effect refuses a duplicate ACL row). The default
  join.rego lets nothing bypass a vetting criterion. So the order is: admit
  the vetter-to-be (by invitation or moderator approval), grant the role, and
  only then add the vetting criterion.

getting-started.md, non-interactive-setup.md, vetting.md, the docs index and
the see-also lists now link to the runbook. getting-started Step 3 also
claimed the install page hands out a credential bundle for
`cnm auth login <bundle>`. It does not, and that command takes
--credential-bundle <sealed file>. Both claims are corrected.

## KR-25: the card is delivered, not returned inline

New: docs/03-vtc/credential-delivery.md, with a migration note for clients
built against the 0.28-era stack.

On admission, the VTC delivers the MembershipCredential and the role
EndorsementCredential as two credential-exchange/issue/0.1 DIDComm messages:

- typed as the task, not in the binding envelope;
- on a fresh thread each, in no guaranteed order;
- with body {credential_response: {credential}};
- sent through the durable outbox, which retries for 24 hours.

A client that waits only for the reply to its submit, or that unwraps only
the binding envelope, ends the join with nothing and sees no error.

What to rely on: treat `allow` as the decision, and keep an inbox for the
deposits. The VerdictWith contract (#541) says that over DIDComm the
credentials are delivered in a follow-up message, and the inline
verdict.with.vmc / roleVec copy may be omitted. The REST admin decision still
returns both inline.

History: separate delivery arrived in #279 and #317 and became durable in
#679. All three predate both the 0.28 pin and VTI-Eucalyptus-RC-0. The
current VTC still fills verdict.with.vmc / roleVec on every transport. No
commit between the two measured revisions (53a7cde4 and 460e0ebb) changes
the verdict's content. The note therefore documents the contract clients
should build on. It does not attribute the change to a single commit.

Refs #1608 (KR-01, KR-11, KR-25)
