title: fix(trust-tasks): name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error (#1609)
body:
fix(trust-tasks): name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error (#1609)

A `ServiceError` at 502/504 — a DID-hosting server or other peer that did
not answer or refused — fell into the catch-all arm and went out as an
opaque `internalError`. An openvtc join that failed because the hosting
server's replies were refused by its mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`)
showed the user "internal error: the consumer could not complete this
task", pointing at their own VTA.

It now goes out as `taskFailed` with `details.reason` =
`upstream_unavailable` and fixed text. The cause (peer, URL, its body)
stays in the operator's log, as the framework requires. The SDK recovers
the reason as `VtaError::Server { status: 502 }`, the variant REST
already produces for the same failure.

## [0.21.9](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/compare/trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.8...trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.9) — 2026-09-21 ### Added - **vtc**: A community can ask an applicant to tell it about themselves ([#543](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/543)) From the persona context-first design note (verifiable-trust-infrastructure, docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.2): a join manifest could ask only for credentials, so a community wanting a display name and a country had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and nothing connected the join ceremony to the applicant's persona. All additive, no new versions: - vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2: optional `requestedAttributes` -- claim types (never values), each `required` (default true) with a `purpose` shown to the applicant. Outside every criterion, so no requirementsDigest covers it. Answers are self-asserted: a community MUST NOT describe one as verified or decide as if it were; a community needing an attested value asks for a credential instead. - vtc/join-requests/submit/0.2: optional `attributes` -- [{type, value}], bound to the applicant by the document proof. New codes attributesMissing (a required one is absent) and attributesUnrequested (a type the manifest does not request -- refused rather than stored, so an over-sharing client cannot leave data with a community that never asked). SHOULD be sent through the applicant's own disclosure path so their record of what they told whom includes it. - vtc/_shared JoinRequest: optional `attributes`, so show and list carry the answers to reviewers, as the applicant's own statement. Bindings regenerated in Rust, TS, Go and Dart.

title: Define outcome evidence for a cited exchange
body:
The Trust Tasks half of splitting [trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#18](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/pull/18) across the three specifications, following the scope guidance in [dtgwg-cred-tf#39](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf/discussions/39) and the review on #18. The full redistribution map is in the credentials PR.

| Part | PR |
|---|---|
| Trust Tasks (this PR) | this one |
| Credentials | trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#56 |
| VTI | trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#33 |

**Merge order: this PR first.** dtgwg-cred-spec#56 links directly to the `#evidence-that-a-cited-exchange-completed` anchor this PR creates; merging it before this one leaves a dead link in a published Working Draft. The credentials and VTI PRs can merge in either order once this is in.

@talltree @sankarshanmukhopadhyay — tagging you as the authors of the #39 scope guidance this split implements. @stormer78 — item 20 below is where your three follow-ups from the trust-tasks-tf#173 closing comment land.

## Why here

Trust Tasks 0.5.0 already absorbed most of #18's reasoning through trust-tasks-tf#173: naming the innermost exchange by its initiating `id`, the task digest, `inResponseTo`, the document lifecycle. What it does not define is whether a **cited exchange completed**. That rule lives today in #18 and, separately, in `witness/session/submit/0.1` and `vetting/session/0.1` — none of which generalizes on its own.

Under the #39 scope guidance, a credential specification defines its types, properties and high-level requirements and references the specifications that define the rest; processing, ceremony and evidence requirements belong here.

## What this adds

- **Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed** — four checks: the citation binds the initiating document; the terminal's `threadId` pairs through the initiating document; the terminal's type is the **declared** outcome-evidence response; it is signed by the initiating document's **`recipient`**.
- **Specification Requirements item 20** — a citable specification declares its outcome-evidence response, with a payload schema, proof REQUIRED, `issuedAt` required, and `durable` retention. This is where Glenn's three follow-ups from the #173 closing comment land: the `cancelled` terminal state, items 17 and 18, and the empty `#response`.
- **Privacy Considerations item 6**, the **outcome evidence** term, and VTI as an informative reference.

## Evidence

[Keyring `ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing`](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/c3a7f1d2a547d7a602cf93b87f5672d7a158d4c1/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing) runs seven exchanges — witness, vetting, a minted thread, a cancellation, a self-signed response, an error, a counterfeit — through the witness spec's rule, Keyring's verifier, #18's text, and this rule, using real Trust Task documents and `eddsa-jcs-2022` proofs. Only this rule gets all seven right.

| Exchange | witness spec | Keyring | #18 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| witness ceremony | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ false negative | ✓ |
| vetting ceremony | ✗ (out of scope) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| minted `threadId` | ✗ (out of scope) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| cancelled (control `#response`) | ✗ | ✓ false positive | ✗ | ✗ |
| holder-signed `#response` | ✗ | ✓ false positive | ✗ | ✗ |
| error / counterfeit | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

The two false positives are a Keyring bug, tracked on our side, not a change proposed here.

## Notes for review

- `witness/session/submit` and `vetting/session` stay consistent with this section for their own exchanges; the registry specs are not edited here. `witness/session/submit/0.1` still states its own pairing rule ("evidence issuer = credential issuer"), which agrees with this general rule only because the witness case makes issuer and recipient coincide — a follow-up issue on dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf will propose it cite this section instead.
- **No Document Status bump** — bumps have been their own PR. A follow-up will bump it and fill in the minimum-version notes that dtgwg-cred-spec#56 and dtgwg-vti-spec#33 currently record as pending.
- Rendered with `npm run render` — no errors.
- Reviewed internally on our fork before proposing here; @bmiller59 is credited as co-author for the material carried over from his review.

title: Define outcome evidence for a cited exchange, once (#15)
body:
Define outcome evidence for a cited exchange, once (#15)

Binding a Citation to the Document It Names fixes which exchange a citation
names, but not whether that exchange completed. The DTG credential
specification's taskContext binding depends on that second question, and the
rules for it currently live in cred-spec PR #18 and, separately, in the
witness/session/submit and vetting/session task specifications. This moves
the generic rule into the framework, as the working group's scope guidance
places ceremony and evidence requirements here.

- New section, Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed: the four checks a
  consumer relying on a citation performs — the citation binds the initiating
  document; the terminal document's threadId pairs through the initiating
  document (so a minted threadId does not orphan evidence); its type is the
  declared outcome-evidence response (so a control response, error, or
  next-step never reads as completion); and it is signed by the initiating
  document's recipient (so a self-signed response does not pass, and vetting,
  where the responder is not the credential's issuer, still does).
- Specification Requirements item 20: a specification whose exchanges may be
  cited declares its outcome-evidence response, with a payload schema, proof
  REQUIRED, issuedAt required, and durable retention — the declarations Glenn
  Gore identified on trust-tasks-tf#173 as belonging to this profile.
- Privacy Considerations item 6: outcome evidence discloses the exchange's
  correlators, so unlinkability is assessed across the composition.
- New term, outcome evidence; VTI added as an informative reference.

The non-normative note records why each check is needed. Every case in it is
exercised against real Trust Task documents and proofs in Keyring's
tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing.

Refs trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#18, trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#11,
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#173.

title: vta-service-v0.37.0
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Keep a pinned value through an edit, and let the holder purge it ([#1606](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1606))

Implements the retention half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538
  (design note docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.1).

  A pin ({ref, pinVersion}) is for the counterparty who verified a value
  and must keep being shown it -- after a name change, the bank that has
  not been told yet. The store did not keep the version an edit replaced,
  so a pin resolved stale from the first edit onward: pinning worked only
  until the one event it exists for.

  Retained by reference (new vta-persona `retention` module, `pav:` keys):
  - An edit keeps the version it replaces when a face pins it, and a pin
    is served from that copy.
  - A kept version is reaped the moment no face pins it (after profile put
    and delete); an edit nothing pins keeps nothing.
  - Deleting the attribute drops every kept version with it.
  - Attribute.retained_versions lists what is kept and the faces pinning
    it, on attribute/list; filled on read, never stored.
  - A face pinning a kept version still presents that value, so the
    correlation index counts it among what the face carries, and a face's
    own analysis treats such a pin as carried rather than as the live
    attribute.

  The holder's override: persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0 removes kept
  versions (named, or all), re-pushes and names every face that pinned one
  (stalePins). Those faces present the entry as stale -- never the current
  value, which the holder did not choose for that counterparty. The current
  version is refused (currentVersion); that is attribute/delete. New
  PersonaStore::purge_versions, VtaClient::persona_attribute_purge_version,
  `pnm persona attribute purge-version`.

  profile/put now refuses a pin to a version neither current nor kept with
  the spec's pinnedVersionUnavailable code, naming the pins, instead of
  storing a face that presents nothing for that entry.

- **persona**: Say which entry is a face's name — entry slots ([#1605](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1605))

* build: require trust-tasks-rs 0.21.8 for persona slots and kept versions

  0.21.8 publishes trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538: the optional
  ProfileEntry and ResolvedClaim `slot`, Attribute.retainedVersions, the
  duplicateSlot codes, and persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0.



### Fixed

- **did-webvh**: Serialize versionTime log updates ([#1599](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1599))

* fix(did-webvh): serialize versionTime log updates

  Use one current-time policy for TEE genesis and runtime did:webvh
  updates. Wait for the next valid whole-second boundary, rechecking
  after wall-clock rollback, instead of backdating entries.

  Serialize same-DID log appends within a VTA process and add regression
  coverage for rapid updates, concurrent appends, legacy timestamps, and
  TEE genesis followed by an immediate validated update.

title: feat(vtc): a community can ask an applicant to tell it about themselves
body:
From the persona context-first design note in verifiable-trust-infrastructure (`docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md` §5.2), discussed in trustoverip/dtgwg-htx-tf#11.

A join manifest could only ask for credentials. A community that wants a display name and a country had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and nothing connected the join ceremony to the applicant's persona.

All changes are additive; no new versions:

### `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2` — `requestedAttributes`
- Claim types from the persona claim-type registry, never values.
- Each entry has `required` (default true) and a `purpose` shown to the applicant before anything is disclosed.
- It sits outside every criterion, so no `requirementsDigest` covers it.
- **Answers are self-asserted.** A community MUST NOT describe one as verified or decide as if it were. A community that needs an attested value asks for a credential in a criterion instead.

### `vtc/join-requests/submit/0.2` — `attributes`
- `[{type, value}]`, bound to the applicant by the document proof.
- New error code `attributesMissing`: a required attribute wasn't answered. Details name the missing types.
- New error code `attributesUnrequested`: a type the manifest didn't ask for. Refused rather than stored, so an over-sharing client can't leave data with a community that never asked for it.
- A producer SHOULD send the values through the applicant's own disclosure path, so the applicant's record of what they told whom includes them.

### `vtc/_shared/0.1` `JoinRequest` — `attributes`
Carries the answers through `show` and `list` to reviewers, as the applicant's own statement.

### Checks
- `npm run validate`
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs`
- Bindings regenerated in Rust, TS, Go and Dart

title: feat(persona)!: keep and show what a community may call a face
body:
Adopts `vta-sdk` 0.45 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1597).

### What changes
- **The label is carried forward.** `persona/binding/set` replaces the whole binding, label included, and OpenVTC has no way to set a label. Without this, changing a face from OpenVTC would silently erase the name the holder gave the community in `pnm` or the console. So `persona::binding::set` now reads the current label and sends it back. If that read fails, the write fails too, rather than defaulting to no name.
- **Both names are shown.** The panel line now reads `wears: <your name> (N attributes) — known here as “<label>”`. The agent now gives the face's own name only to the holder (which OpenVTC is), and gives the community the label.

### Dependencies
- `vta-sdk` 0.43.1 → 0.45.0, and the `vta-service` dev-dependency 0.32 → 0.36, so the graph resolves a single `vta-sdk`.
- The lockfile also updates the VTI subsystem crates and `vtc-client` to releases that require `vta-sdk ^0.45`. `vtc-client` 0.6.7 was keeping a second copy, `vta-sdk` 0.42, in the graph.
- `did-git-sign` still pulls `vta-sdk` 0.42.1, as it did before this PR.
- A test fixture gains the `sub_contexts` field that `vta-sdk` 0.44 added.

### Checks
Everything in `ci.yml` except bench, coverage and the plain `cargo check`:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1459 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`
- `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`
- `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`

New test: `a_labelled_binding_says_what_the_community_is_told`.

### Update
- Takes `vta-sdk` 0.45.1 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1602). 0.45.0 reported a declared `vta/contexts/get:notFound` as a protocol error, which failed `community_context_e2e` under coverage (`--include-ignored`).
- Re-run locally:
  - `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored`: 1478 passed, 0 failed
  - `--no-default-features` and `dev-overrides` test runs pass
  - clippy clean in both configurations

title: feat(persona): a face says which name is its own; old values kept for a pin, and removing them
body:
Uses `@openvtc/trust-tasks` 0.19.14 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538). The agent side is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1605 (slots) and #1606 (kept versions, `purge-version`). **Merge after those land and are released:** an agent without #1606 doesn't route `purge-version`.

### Face editor — "Calls itself"
- Pick which of the attributes a face shows is the face's own name; this sets the entry's `displayName` slot.
- Only attributes the face shows are offered.
- A name typed only into the face is kept unless the holder picks a different one.
- `composeEntriesWithSlots` carries every slot through an edit. `profile/put` replaces the whole face, and rebuilding live entries as bare `{ref}` would have dropped the name on the first save.
- The NAME hint no longer says contexts see the face's name. Since VTI #1597, a context sees only the label the holder picks when a persona wears the face.

### Attribute strip — kept values
- When the agent keeps an earlier value because a face is pinned to it, the strip says so and names the faces.
- **Remove the old value for good** calls `persona/attribute/purge-version`, after a confirmation that says:
  - the pinned faces will show *nothing* for it, not the current value;
  - anyone already shown the old value keeps it.
- The model is `manager/kept-versions.ts`.

### Wiring
- `personaAttributePurgeVersion` in core admin.
- The URI is added to both CI holder-only guards (the console carries it; no wallet surface does), and the count in the guard's message is updated.
- `task-surface.json` resynced from `vta-sdk` 0.45.1.
- Recorded coverage moves 205 → 206, with the reason noted beside it.
- `@openvtc/trust-tasks` ^0.19.14 at the root and in core. The lockfile changes that one package only.

### Checks
- `npm run lint`
- `npm test`: 1547 passed, 0 failed. New:
  - slot composition tests
  - `manager-kept-versions.test.mts`
  - a rendered test that the kept-value note appears and that purge asks before calling
  - a core `purge-version` client test
- `npm run build`, plus both persona guards run locally against `dist/`.

title: vta-cli-common-v0.20.0
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Keep a pinned value through an edit, and let the holder purge it ([#1606](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1606))

Implements the retention half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538
  (design note docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.1).

  A pin ({ref, pinVersion}) is for the counterparty who verified a value
  and must keep being shown it -- after a name change, the bank that has
  not been told yet. The store did not keep the version an edit replaced,
  so a pin resolved stale from the first edit onward: pinning worked only
  until the one event it exists for.

  Retained by reference (new vta-persona `retention` module, `pav:` keys):
  - An edit keeps the version it replaces when a face pins it, and a pin
    is served from that copy.
  - A kept version is reaped the moment no face pins it (after profile put
    and delete); an edit nothing pins keeps nothing.
  - Deleting the attribute drops every kept version with it.
  - Attribute.retained_versions lists what is kept and the faces pinning
    it, on attribute/list; filled on read, never stored.
  - A face pinning a kept version still presents that value, so the
    correlation index counts it among what the face carries, and a face's
    own analysis treats such a pin as carried rather than as the live
    attribute.

  The holder's override: persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0 removes kept
  versions (named, or all), re-pushes and names every face that pinned one
  (stalePins). Those faces present the entry as stale -- never the current
  value, which the holder did not choose for that counterparty. The current
  version is refused (currentVersion); that is attribute/delete. New
  PersonaStore::purge_versions, VtaClient::persona_attribute_purge_version,
  `pnm persona attribute purge-version`.

  profile/put now refuses a pin to a version neither current nor kept with
  the spec's pinnedVersionUnavailable code, naming the pins, instead of
  storing a face that presents nothing for that entry.

or merges, and the document is **edited in place**: VTI-31 gained a "Fixed
upstream" note, and a retraction of its own proposed fix, between our first
read and our second. So the findings are restated here rather than linked.

Tier 1 is closed (10 shipped, 3 already fixed before we read the report). This
issue covers what remains. Split an item into its own issue when someone picks
it up; this is the index, not the work.

Full triage and reasoning: `design-docs/keyring-remediation-plan.html`.

---

## Tier 2 — accepted, not yet scheduled

- **KR-15 — `VTCRest` endpoint omits `/v1`.** The template emits a bare
  `{URL}`; its status-list sibling already carries `/v1`. Fix the template,
  and accept both forms on the resolver side for DIDs already minted.
- **KR-21 — no channel delivers an invitation to its invitee.** Admission is
  push-shaped with no join ceremony — a known shape, not a surprise. Needs a
  delivery path to the invitee, not only to the admin.
- **KR-32 — an invitation is too large for the channel it must travel on.**
  An `InvitationCredential` link is 6,331 bytes; QR byte mode tops out at
  2,953, and base64url's `-`/`_` rule out alphanumeric mode. **Do this with
  KR-21, not separately** — they are one problem seen from each end, and
  invite-by-reference (a short identifier the client resolves, as it already
  resolves a manifest) answers both.
- **KR-23 — manager operations require admin.** Folds into the existing ACL
  capability-narrowing work; `keys.rs:229` already calls `require_admin` a
  "role floor", so the least-privilege path is a known gap.
- **KR-17 · KR-18 — provisioning leaves a DID unusable.** One issue, not two:
  re-provision binds to a dead hostname, and a self-managed mint produces a
  DID with no services the VTA will accept.
- **KR-08 — worker stack overflow creating a context.** Debug-build only, with
  a 32 MiB workaround, so it does not block them — but a stack that deep is
  worth understanding rather than papering over.
- **KR-07 · KR-16 · KR-20 — three small operational fixes.**
  `functions_file` resolved against cwd; admin invite needing the daemon
  stopped; a persona mint printing instructions that do not apply. Cheap,
  unglamorous, and each cost them an afternoon.

## Tier 3 — answered in prose, not code

- **KR-01 · KR-11 — bootstrap order is undocumented.** A fresh VTC cannot
  authenticate its own admin, and the first vetter has no documented path.
  Both are real sequences that simply are not written down. A setup runbook is
  the deliverable, and it is the cheapest high-value item in the whole set for
  the next integrator.
- **KR-22 — consent policies inert by default.** The default stays off:
  flipping it would silently turn every written-but-not-intended policy into a
  gate across existing deployments. Document it as opt-in **and** add a
  startup warning when policy rows exist while `policy.enforcement` is false —
  the missing warning is the actual defect they hit.
- **KR-25 — card delivered, not returned inline.** A deliberate change on
  Eucalyptus that was never written up. Changelog entry and a migration note.

## Not in this issue

- **Declined or re-scoped** (KR-02, KR-10, KR-12, KR-13) — each answered with
  a written reason in the plan; no work queued.
- **KR-06** — blocked until their configuration reproduces it.
- The conformance-ledger gap is #1600.

title: feat(persona)!: keep a pinned value through an edit, and let the holder purge it
body:
Rebased onto `main` now that #1605 has merged; the file tree is identical to the one tested.

Implements the retention half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538 (`trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.8). Design note §9.1.

### The defect
A pin (`{ref, pinVersion}`) is for a counterparty who verified a value and must keep seeing it — after a name change, the bank that hasn't been told yet. The store never kept the version an edit replaced, so every pin went stale at the first edit. Pinning stopped working exactly when it was needed.

### Retained by reference
New `vta-persona` `retention` module, stored under `pav:` keys.
- **Kept and served.** An edit keeps the version it replaces if some face pins it, and the pin is served from that copy.
- **Reaped.** A kept version is dropped as soon as no face pins it, checked after every profile put and delete. An edit that nothing pins keeps nothing.
- **Deleted with the attribute.** Deleting the attribute drops every kept version too.
- **Visible to the holder.** `attribute/list` fills `Attribute.retained_versions` with the kept versions and the faces pinning them. It's computed on read and never stored.
- **Still correlated.** A face pinned to a kept version still presents that value, so the correlation index counts it among the values the face carries.

### The holder's override: `persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0`
- **What it removes:** the named kept versions, or all of them.
- **Stale pins:** every face that pinned a removed version is re-pushed to its contexts and named in `stalePins`. Those faces then present the entry as stale, never as the current value, which the holder didn't choose for that counterparty.
- **Current version:** refused with `currentVersion`; removing it is `attribute/delete`'s job.
- **Where it's wired:**
  - task URI, dispatch table, reach table (holder), retry-safety census (`RetrySafe`) and conformance witness
  - `vta-mcp` guard, classified as destructive
  - `VtaClient::persona_attribute_purge_version`
  - `pnm persona attribute purge-version`

### Also
`profile/put` now refuses a pin to a version that is neither current nor kept, using the spec's `pinnedVersionUnavailable` code and naming the pins. Previously it stored a face that presented nothing for that entry.

**Breaking:** `vta_persona::Attribute` gains `retained_versions`, and a pin to a version the store doesn't hold is now refused rather than stored.

### Tests
- `vta-persona`: pin survives an edit, retention by reference, purge leaves pins stale, delete drops kept versions, a kept value is still correlated.
- Wire test `a_pinned_name_survives_a_rename_until_the_holder_purges_it`, checked against the published schema for `attribute/list` and `purge-version`.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4674 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: fix(vtc): a caller-visible failure reaches the client typed, and an internal one says nothing
body:
Two defects in `vtc-service`'s Trust Task reject mapping, both of which
`vta-service` fixed long ago and this service never did. Found by following
#1602, which fixed the client half of the first one for a single code.

## Every NotFound, Conflict and Gone arrived as an opaque string

§8.3 defines no `notFound` / `conflict` / `gone`, so all three ride out under
`taskFailed`. That is the correct wire code and it is not enough on its own: a
caller cannot tell "the row you asked for is absent" — very often a *normal*
state it knows how to handle — from "this operation genuinely failed".

The VTA puts the discriminator in `details.reason`, and
`VtaClient::trust_task_error` reads it back into the same typed `VtaError` the
REST and problem-report paths produce. The VTC passed `details: None`, so
every one of these collapsed into `Protocol(String)` — the exact failure
`CLAUDE.md` names by name ("never collapse a Conflict into a string").

#1602 recovered `NotFound` for extended codes whose local part is literally
`notFound`. That leaves everything else, including four of the six codes added
this week (`submit:requestAlreadyOpen`, `supplement:notAwaitingEvidence`,
`supplement:alreadyDecided`, `withdraw:alreadyDecided`) and the pre-existing
`vetting/vetters/resend:notGranted`, which is a `NotFound` underneath whose
local part is not `notFound`.

`reject_with_code_because` carries both. A client that knows the extended code
gets the precise reason; one that does not falls back to `taskFailed` per
SPEC §8.5 and still recovers the right typed variant from the marker. The
marker is **merged** into `details` rather than replacing it, because the
spec'd annex members (`requestId`, `status`) are what the applicant's client
acts on — a marker that overwrote `requestId` would take away the thing they
need to withdraw.

## An internalError sent its cause to the caller

Framework 0.5.0, *What a `message` May Not Say*: a `message` MUST NOT reveal
consumer-internal state. The catch-all arm was
`RejectReason::InternalError { reason: message }` with `message =
err.to_string()`, so an unauthenticated caller received things like
`vtc_did not configured`, `audit_writer not initialised`, or a raw fjall or
serde failure — the deployment's shape and which invariant just broke.

The producer needs one fact from an `internalError`: the failure was not its
document's doing. The cause is what the *operator* needs, and now goes to the
log. Every other arm describes the caller's own request back to it, which is
not internal state, and passes through unchanged.

## Tests

Three, each verified to fail when its fix is reverted:

- `an_internal_error_does_not_send_its_cause` — two causes of different
  shapes, because the leak was in a catch-all rather than in `Internal` alone.
- `caller_visible_failures_carry_their_reason_marker` — all four variants.
- `a_coded_reject_carries_the_reason_marker_a_client_reads` — end to end
  through the dispatcher, asserting the spec'd annex survives the merge.

title: fix(did-webvh)!: serialize versionTime log updates
body:
## Summary

- Replace backdated did:webvh `versionTime` generation with a shared
  wait-until-valid whole-second policy.
- Apply the policy to both regular and TEE genesis paths.
- Serialize same-DID update execution within one VTA process so rapid
  callers append consecutive log entries safely.
- Document replacement-document concurrency semantics and add regression
  coverage for wall-clock rollback, concurrent updates, and TEE
  genesis-to-update validation.

## Notes

The per-DID lock is process-local by design, matching VTA's
single-process ownership model. Multi-replica coordination remains out
of scope.
author: yaroslava-kurash

title: fix(did-webvh)!: serialize versionTime log updates (#1599)
body:
fix(did-webvh)!: serialize versionTime log updates (#1599)

* fix(did-webvh): serialize versionTime log updates

Use one current-time policy for TEE genesis and runtime did:webvh
updates. Wait for the next valid whole-second boundary, rechecking
after wall-clock rollback, instead of backdating entries.

Serialize same-DID log appends within a VTA process and add regression
coverage for rapid updates, concurrent appends, legacy timestamps, and
TEE genesis followed by an immediate validated update.

Signed-off-by: Yaroslava Kurash <yaroslava.k@affinidi.com>

* fix(did-webvh): bound the versionTime wait and refuse a stale replacement document

Three defects in the versionTime and serialisation change.

`wait_until_not_future` compared a whole-second `target` against a
truncated clock, so the comparison could never reach zero for a target
carrying a sub-second remainder. Production never hit it —
`plan_version_time` only ever yields a whole second — but
`waits_again_after_a_backward_clock_adjustment` builds its own target
and hung forever, taking the workspace test job down with it, and with
it every target ordered after vta-support: vta-tee's three new genesis
tests never ran at all. Compare against the raw clock instead.
`target <= now` is exactly the condition `didwebvh-rs` checks, it
terminates for any target, and it drops up to a second of needless
waiting per collision.

The wait was unbounded. A previous entry stamped well ahead of this
host's clock — a chain minted elsewhere, or a backwards NTP step here —
parked the request, and everything queued behind it, for the whole skew
with no error and no log line. Cap the accumulated sleep at
`MAX_WAIT_SECONDS`; past it stamp `previous + 1s` anyway and warn.
Strict increase is the invariant that must not bend, and a transiently
future-dated entry resolves once clocks agree. Transient beats terminal.

The per-DID lock turned a caught conflict into a silent lost update.
`document` is a whole replacement built from a head the caller read
earlier, and every in-tree caller that supplies one — `agent_name_op`
and the `operations::protocol::*` service patchers — passes no
`expected_version_id`. Before the lock, such a caller captured its
`RecordSnapshot` at the old `log_entry_count` and the check before the
final write refused it. The reload inside the lock re-bases that
snapshot on the newer head, so the check passes and the stale document
is appended, discarding the intervening edit with no error anywhere.
Refuse explicitly, against the head as it stood before queueing.
Updates carrying no document (rotation, witnesses, watchers, ttl) still
compose onto whichever head they find, which is the serialisation the
lock exists to provide.

Also hold the lock registry by `Weak`, so idle entries are reclaimed
instead of accumulating one per DID for the life of the process; and
record in the module docs that dropping the backdate leaves no
clock-skew slack on the verifying side, since `didwebvh-rs` rejects a
future `versionTime` with no grace window.

title: feat(persona)!: say which entry is a face's name — entry slots
body:
Implements the slot half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538, published in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.8. Design note §3.1 and §5.5.

A face may hold several names, for example a legal one and the one it goes by. Entries carried no role, so a consumer rendering "what does this face call itself" had to guess from claim types, and guessed wrong whenever there were two. This is the Alice-and-Bob question from trustoverip/dtgwg-htx-tf#11: the data model already allowed two names, but nothing said which one was the face's.

### Changes
- **Slot on every entry.** `ProfileEntry` (in both `vta-persona` and `vta-sdk`) gains an optional `slot` on all four forms: ref, pinned, override and inline. `LocalProfileEntry` gains one too.
- **Duplicates refused.** A face repeating a slot is rejected with `persona/profile/put:duplicateSlot` or `persona/local/profile/put:duplicateSlot`, naming the slot. The store refuses it as well, so no write path can store one.
- **Resolved reads.** `ResolvedClaim` gains `slot`, and `profile/get` with `resolve` returns it.
- **CLI.**
  - `pnm persona profile put --display-name <attribute-id>` marks the entry the face calls itself by.
  - `--entries-file` accepts `"slot"`.
- **Round-trip tests** now cover every slotted form in both crates, plus a slotted pin that must stay a pin. `slot` sits on every form, so it can't tell the forms apart; `deny_unknown_fields` still has to do that.

**Breaking:** every `ProfileEntry` variant gains `slot`, as do `LocalProfileEntry` and `ResolvedClaim`.

### Tests
- Wire test `a_face_names_itself_by_slot_and_only_once`, checked against the published schema.
- `vta-persona`, `vta-sdk` and `pnm-cli` unit tests: 1169 passed.
- Persona wire tests: 31 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- The full workspace suite ran on the stacked retention branch, which includes this commit: 4674 passed, 0 failed. It hasn't run on this branch on its own.

The next PR (kept versions and `purge-version`) is stacked on this one.

title: feat(persona): a face says which name is its own; old values kept for a pin, and removing them
body:
feat(persona): a face says which name is its own; old values kept for a pin, and removing them

Uses @openvtc/trust-tasks 0.19.14 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538).

Face editor -- CALLS ITSELF: pick which of the attributes a face shows
is its own name (the entry's `displayName` slot). A face can show a legal
name and the one it goes by; this says which is the face's. The choice is
offered only from what the face shows, and a name typed into the face
itself is kept unless the holder picks another.

composeEntriesWithSlots keeps every slot through an edit. profile/put
replaces the face, so rebuilding live entries as bare {ref} -- what
composeEntries does -- would strip the name on the first save.

The NAME hint no longer says contexts see the face's name: since
verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1597 a context sees only the label the
holder chooses when a persona wears the face.

Attribute strip -- kept values: when the agent keeps an earlier value
because a face is pinned to it (Attribute.retainedVersions), the strip
says so and which faces are the reason. "Remove the old value for good"
calls persona/attribute/purge-version after a confirmation that says the
pinned faces will show nothing -- not the current value -- and that
anyone already shown the old value keeps it. Model in kept-versions.ts.

Wiring: personaAttributePurgeVersion in core admin; the URI added to
both CI holder-only guards; task-surface.json resynced (vta-sdk 0.45.1)
and the recorded coverage moved 205 -> 206 with the reason.

title: vta-sdk-v0.45.1
body:
### Fixed

- **sdk**: A task's declared `:notFound` is VtaError::NotFound ([#1602](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1602))

#1580 made the contexts family answer its specification's error codes,
  so a missing context now arrives as `vta/contexts/get:notFound`. The
  client recovered NotFound only from the `details.reason` marker, which
  those codes do not carry, so the rejection became a flat
  Protocol("trust task failed [vta/contexts/get:notFound]: …").

  Every Trust-Task caller that treats an absent context as a normal state
  -- look it up, create it if missing -- therefore failed instead. OpenVTC's
  community_context_e2e tests are the ones that caught it, on the bump to
  vta-sdk 0.45 (OpenVTC/openvtc#362). The same applies to app-state's and
  the persona family's declared :notFound.

  Match the local part `notFound` on any extended code, as the client
  already does for `transportUnavailable`. A different local code that
  merely contains the word (`parentNotFound`) stays a Protocol error.

- **sdk**: Honour an explicit --url on every transport, not only forced REST ([#1601](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1601))

Keyring finding VTI-14: pointing `cnm` at a host had no effect, because the
  community was resolved from the DID document instead. With VTI-15 this made
  the CLI unusable against their stack, and is why their repository carries its
  own admin client — an adoption cost, not just a bug.

title: feat(persona): honest pins, purge-version, and entry slots
body:
Second spec change from the persona context-first design note in verifiable-trust-infrastructure (`docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md` §3.1, §5.5, §9.1; discussed in trustoverip/dtgwg-htx-tf#11).

### `persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0` (new)
Lets the holder override retention. After a name change, the old value is kept only while some face pins it, for example the bank that must keep seeing the name it verified. This task removes such a value anyway; a deadname is the case that makes it necessary.

- Removes the named retained versions, or all of them.
- Returns `stalePins`, naming every profile that pinned a removed version.
- Those entries then present as stale. They do **not** fall back to the current value, because a pin exists so a counterparty isn't shown a value the holder didn't choose for them.
- Refuses the current version (`currentVersion`); that's what `attribute/delete` is for.
- Destructive. Holder-authorized and unscoped.

### Retention by reference
- `attribute/put`: a maintainer that keeps prior versions MUST keep them only while some profile pins them, and MUST list them in the new `Attribute.retainedVersions` (`version`, `updatedAt`, `pinnedBy`, no values).
- `profile/put`: a pin to a version that is neither current nor retained MUST be refused with the existing `pinnedVersionUnavailable` code.

### Slots
- Optional `slot` on every `ProfileEntry` form, on the local profile entry, and on `ResolvedClaim`.
- `displayName` answers "what does this face call itself", which a flat entry list couldn't do once a face held several names.
- Well-known slots: `displayName`, `primaryEmail`, `primaryPhone`, `primaryAddress`, `avatar`.
- Unique within a profile. New `duplicateSlot` codes on `profile/put` and `local/profile/put`.

Every new member is optional. `slot` is added to all four `ProfileEntry` forms together, so each form stays distinguishable from the others.

### Checks
- `npm run validate`: 454 specs.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs`.
- Bindings regenerated in Rust, TS, Go and Dart. Dart was formatted with SDK 3.13.4 stable.

title: spec(vtc/join-requests/supplement): vetting travels in the presentation, so it is replaced with it
body:
#526 stated that vetting attestations are "attached to the request, not to the
presentation", and that a consumer MUST NOT discard them when the presentation
is replaced. That is wrong, and I found it while implementing the consumer
side.

A community counts vetting by reading the attestations **out of the
presentation** it was handed — in the reference implementation,
`vetting_credentials(vp)` filters the VP's `verifiableCredential` array. The
per-request vetting record that does exist is a *record*: it answers the admin
view, the vetter sweep, and the question of which admissions a later-withdrawn
statement counted toward. No decision reads it. So there is nothing on the
request for a consumer to decline to discard, and a supplement whose
presentation omits the attestations is one with no vetting.

The claim was also internally inconsistent with the rule immediately above it.
Carrying forward attestations from a superseded presentation is accumulation —
it decides the request on evidence the applicant is no longer presenting, which
is exactly the defect the replace-not-merge rule exists to prevent. It merely
arrives by a different route, so the corrected text forbids it explicitly.

What survives is the promise underneath, which is the part that mattered: a
vetting attestation is a credential the **applicant** holds, so re-presenting
it costs the vetter nothing and no one attests twice. The obligation this puts
on a deferring community is now stated — name the attestations in the
`presentationDefinition` alongside everything else required.

The Correlation subsection carried the same error ("it is what lets vetting
survive") and is corrected to what the linkage actually buys: the applicant
keeps their place rather than starting again.

Prose only, in place, per SPEC §5.2's draft rule — no schema change, so the
bindings are untouched.

title: chore(deps)!: move to trust-tasks-rs 0.11, and fix the wire drift it exposed
body:
Started as "did the sibling release fix the duplicate `trust-tasks-rs`?" — yes.
But the upgrade turns on schema validation for 22 tasks that previously had
none, and **three of them were sending non-conforming payloads**.

## The graph

`trust-tasks-https` / `-didcomm` / `-proof` / `-tsp` / `-capability-client` /
`-didcomm-v1` now all require `^0.11`, and `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.19.9 /
`-mediator` 0.18.20 followed. Until every one agreed, bumping the direct
dependency put **two** `trust-tasks-rs` nodes in the graph and the types crossed:

```
error[E0308]: expected `MediatorAcl`, found a different `MediatorAcl`
note: there are multiple different versions of crate `trust_tasks_rs`
```

Refreshing the lock to the versions that agree collapses it to one node.

## Three live defects, all the same class as #919

They were shipping before this PR. Nothing failed only because neither end had a
schema to check against.

1. **`CreateDidWebvhRequest` serialized snake_case.** Canonical wire is camelCase
   (R3.1) and the schema is `additionalProperties: false`. It worked solely
   through `CreateDidWebvhBody`'s back-compat aliases — which is exactly what made
   it invisible.
2. **`update_context` sent `null`** for unset members, where the schema types them
   as optional *strings*. Now built from `UpdateContextBody`, which skips `None`.
3. **`WebvhPathMode` emitted `auto_assign`** where the schema pins `autoAssign`
   with a `const` per `oneOf` branch.

**Number 3 is the one worth your attention.** The drift was in a *discriminant
value*, not a member name — so it slipped past every review and every convention
that watches member casing. And it was only reachable after fixing #1: the payload
had to get past the field-name check before the value check could fail. One drift
was hiding another.

Aliases keep the retired spellings accepted, so a peer built against the old shape
still parses; only what we **emit** moves. A round-trip test pins both directions,
and the REST test that posts the old spelling is annotated as the back-compat
coverage it now is — please don't let anyone "modernise" it.

## Four census guards, all shrinking

Every debt list in the workspace fired, each in the good direction:

| Guard | Change |
|---|---|
| manifest debt (`UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK`) | 36 → 14 |
| conformance witnesses | +22, each schema-validated with the mandatory non-vacuity check |
| `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` | −22 |
| producer-payload `UNPUBLISHED` | −2 |

I **de-rotted one test rather than re-pinning it**. `an_unspecced_task_proceeds_by_default`
hard-coded `webvh/dids/create` as its unspecced example — which this PR publishes,
so it failed for the best possible reason. It now derives one from the debt list at
runtime, so it follows the debt down instead of breaking every time a spec lands,
and returns early with a note to delete itself when the list empties.

## Follow-up I'd propose rather than bolt on

The 22 new witnesses use hand-written `json!`, which proves *the schema accepts a
shape*. Where a typed body exists (`CreateDidWebvhBody`, `UpdateContextBody`, …),
`to_v(typed)` is strictly stronger — it asserts **our types** conform, which is
what caught all three defects here. That's a second audit pass and will likely
surface more drift, so it deserves its own PR.

## BREAKING CHANGE

`WebvhPathMode` serializes as `wellKnown` / `autoAssign` instead of `well_known` /
`auto_assign`. Deserialization accepts both, so this breaks only a consumer that
string-matches on what we emit. Title carries `!`; expect the advisory semver job
to report it.

## Pre-merge

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` — **4514 passed, 0 failed** across 145 binaries
- [x] No `version =` edits, no changelog file

title: feat(rooms): a `host` feature, so a room's member half reaches wasm
body:
`vti-rooms` already had two halves and no name for them:

| Consumer | Imports |
|---|---|
| `vta-service` (a member) | `mls`, `sealed`, `wire` |
| `vtc-service`, `room-host`, `vti-rooms-dtg` (hosts) | `storage`, `authz`, `audit`, `wire` |

This names the second half `host`, on by default, and makes `vti-common`
optional behind it.

`vti-common` describes itself as server-side infrastructure and pulls axum,
fjall and tokio — it was the whole of what kept a room's member code off
`wasm32-unknown-unknown`. With it optional, `--no-default-features --features
mls` builds there, which is what lets a browser hold a room's keys itself rather
than ask an agent to. Design: #1344.

**The member half needed no source changes.** That is a property of `error.rs`,
which deliberately does not use `vti_common::error::AppError` because key
material is not a service's concern — a decision made for its own reasons that
paid for itself here.

`lifecycle` is deliberately left ungated. Only hosts consume it today, but it
needs nothing from `vti-common`, and a member computing a room's lifecycle state
to explain it on screen should not need a host's dependencies.

## The wasm plumbing, and why it is per-target

Three things, each of which reports as a `compile_error!` that reads like an
unsupported target and is not:

- **OpenMLS 0.9 has a first-class `js` feature** — `web-time` for the
  `SystemTime` wasm lacks, plus getrandom's JS backend. Declared per-target
  rather than as a feature of this crate, so building for wasm just works with
  nothing for a consumer to remember. Verified wasm-only: `web-time` is in the
  wasm dependency tree and absent from the native one.
- **Two getrandom majors are in the graph.** The 0.4 is ours; the 0.2 arrives
  transitively under `openmls_rust_crypto` through RustCrypto's elliptic-curve
  stack, so no feature declared here could reach it. `getrandom_02` is a feature
  shim, not a dependency this crate calls — done here rather than left to each
  artifact crate because the choice is target-specific and on wasm32 there is
  only one right answer.
- **No `RUSTFLAGS` are needed.** With both declared per-target with their
  features, `--cfg getrandom_backend="wasm_js"` is unnecessary.

## Guards

Two steps in CI's `features` job, so neither property rots silently:

- clippy on the member half with no host (`-D warnings`);
- a wasm32 `--lib` check.

## Note for the version bump

Possibly breaking for an external consumer that already sets
`default-features = false` on `vti-rooms 0.1.x`: they previously got
`storage`/`authz`/`audit` and now get the member half. Consumers on default
features are unaffected — `default = ["host"]` gives them exactly what
`default = []` did. cargo-semver-checks builds with default features, so it will
not see this; flagging it rather than touching a `version =` field.

## Verified locally

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — clean
- `cargo test -p vti-rooms` — 81 passed
- `cargo clippy -p vti-rooms --no-default-features --features mls --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo check -p vti-rooms --lib --no-default-features --features mls --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` — clean

title: fix(vtc): return the endorsement-type delete body the OpenAPI document declares
body:
**`Test (VTC)` is red on `main`.** This is the one-handler fix.

## What broke

#1587 replaced the hand-written `{ typeUri }` with the generated
`vtc/endorsement-types/delete/0.1` response and documented the route with
`EndorsementTypeDelete01Response` — the `vta_sdk::openapi` wrapper that renders
the specification's own schema, because `utoipa::ToSchema` cannot be derived on
a foreign type. The handler kept returning the generated type *inside* that
wrapper, so `openapi_response_census` failed:

```
endorsement_types.rs::delete
    declares: EndorsementTypeDelete01Response
    returns:  Json<DeleteTaskResponse>
```

Nothing was wrong on the wire. The wrapper is `#[serde(transparent)]`, so the
bytes are identical either way — which is the whole reason that census compares
*names*. `admin-ui/openapi.json` generates `admin-ui/src/lib/wire.ts`, so an
annotation that drifts from its handler ships a console typed against the wrong
shape and nothing says so: the generated TypeScript typechecks against itself.

## The fix

The handler builds the generated type — the builder's `try_into` is what checks
the value against the schema — and returns the wrapper. Hoisted into a `let`,
because `.try_into()` inside `From::from(...)` has nothing to infer from.

The explanation sits in a plain comment, not the doc comment: utoipa copies a
handler's doc comment into the API document, so putting it there would have
changed `openapi.json` (and required regenerating `wire.ts`) in order to explain
one of our own censuses to API consumers. **The API document is unchanged** —
the diff is one file.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (the `Test (VTC)` job's command) —
  63 targets, 0 failures
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_response_census` — 6 pass
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_snapshot` — 4 pass, document
  unchanged
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` —
  clean

## Why this sat unnoticed

`cargo test` stops at the first failing target. Until #1587 landed, the first
failure in the tree was the generated-wire-types census — in the *other* job —
so this one never got to run. Worth remembering that the two VTI test jobs
exclude each other (`Test (workspace)` excludes `vtc-service` and `vtc-client`;
`Test (VTC)` is only those two), so a change that touches shared crates needs
both run locally, not one.

title: chore(rooms)!: dtg-credentials 0.6 → 0.8
body:
Two breaking releases at once, and the second is why this is worth doing now rather than
eventually.

## 0.8 — a VAC is not a bearer credential

`verify_chain` now **requires the presenter to be the leaf's subject**, refusing otherwise
with `NotThePresenter`. Before, it used `presenter` for one thing — comparing it against
the leaf's *optional* `audience` — so a leaf without one was accepted from **anybody**, and
a captured presentation was a bearer token.

**Both hand-written copies of that rule are deleted.** That is the payoff.
`vti-rooms-dtg`'s chain verifier and its nomination check had each written it
independently, after hitting the gap separately, each with a comment explaining why they
had to:

> `verify_chain` uses `claimant` only for the audience check; it does not require the grant
> to name them. Without this a nomination would be a bearer token, and anyone who ever
> observed one could take the room the moment it went dormant.

Two copies of a rule is one place for it to be forgotten, and the duplicate is the one
nobody updates.

**The tests that pinned the property stay exactly where they were.** A chain presented by
the wrong party is still refused; which layer refuses it is no longer this crate's
business. Their assertions move to the library's wording, which is better — it names both
parties rather than only the rule:

> the chain's leaf grants to `did:key:z6Mkfr2…`, but it was presented by `did:key:z6Mkn5Z…`

`audience` is gone from the credential. `room_oracle::present` still accepts the
`rooms/keys/present/0.1` payload member and ignores it, so every existing caller keeps
working — the CLI names its host there. Removing it from the schema is proposed in
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#414. Accepting a request that is not wrong beats refusing
it, and both beat pretending the value still binds something.

## 0.7 — digests, and a required expiry

`validUntil` became required on `new_vac`. `rooms/owner/issue-authority` now **refuses** a
request without one rather than defaulting: nothing about a subject's standing is consulted
when a chain is verified, so authority that does not expire is authority nobody can
withdraw by waiting — and picking a lifetime here would put the room's most consequential
number somewhere its owner never looks.

The same rule made `Option` dead in two test fixtures. Every caller already passed a value,
and "a nomination that never expires" is now a state no test can construct, so both
signatures lose the `Option`.

## Ordering, for anyone else upgrading

Filed as OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#22. A **new issuer against an old verifier** reports a
broken chain rather than a version skew — `names parent zQm…, but was presented after
urn:uuid:…`, with nothing to say those are different kinds of identifier. That is the
direction a client-first upgrade hits, and it is how this whole thread started: a
browser-native room member on 0.7 talking to `room-host` on 0.6.

## Verified

| | |
|---|---|
| `vti-rooms` | 78 + 13 passed |
| `vti-rooms-dtg` | 19 passed |
| `room-host` | 23 passed |
| `vtc-service` rooms | 26 passed |
| `vta-service` rooms | 11 passed |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Marked `!`: `rooms/owner/issue-authority` now refuses a request it previously accepted, and
`AuthorityPresentation`'s `audience` no longer binds anything.

title: fix(sdk): a task's declared `:notFound` is VtaError::NotFound
body:
### Regression
#1580 made the contexts family answer with its specification's error codes, so a missing context now arrives as `vta/contexts/get:notFound`. The client only recovers `VtaError::NotFound` from the `details.reason` marker, which those codes don't carry. The rejection therefore became a flat `Protocol("trust task failed [vta/contexts/get:notFound]: …")`.

Any Trust Task caller that treats a missing context as normal (look it up, create it if missing) fails as a result. OpenVTC's `community_context_e2e` tests caught it on the bump to `vta-sdk` 0.45 (OpenVTC/openvtc#362, coverage job, which runs `--include-ignored`). The app-state and persona families declare `:notFound` codes that hit the same gap.

### Fix
Any extended code whose local part is `notFound` now maps to `VtaError::NotFound`, the same local-part match the client already does for `transportUnavailable`. A different local code that merely contains the word, such as `parentNotFound`, stays a `Protocol` error.

### Verification
- New `a_declared_not_found_code_is_not_found` covers contexts, app-state and persona, plus the `parentNotFound` negative case.
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client --lib`: 525 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --all-targets --features client -- -D warnings`: clean.
- With this branch patched into openvtc, `cargo test -p openvtc-core --test community_context_e2e -- --include-ignored` goes from 2 failed to 2 passed.

After release, openvtc#362 picks it up by bumping `vta-sdk`.

title: fix(sdk): a task's declared `:notFound` is VtaError::NotFound (#1602)
body:
fix(sdk): a task's declared `:notFound` is VtaError::NotFound (#1602)

#1580 made the contexts family answer its specification's error codes,
so a missing context now arrives as `vta/contexts/get:notFound`. The
client recovered NotFound only from the `details.reason` marker, which
those codes do not carry, so the rejection became a flat
Protocol("trust task failed [vta/contexts/get:notFound]: …").

Every Trust-Task caller that treats an absent context as a normal state
-- look it up, create it if missing -- therefore failed instead. OpenVTC's
community_context_e2e tests are the ones that caught it, on the bump to
vta-sdk 0.45 (OpenVTC/openvtc#362). The same applies to app-state's and
the persona family's declared :notFound.

Match the local part `notFound` on any extended code, as the client
already does for `transportUnavailable`. A different local code that
merely contains the word (`parentNotFound`) stays a Protocol error.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(sdk): honour an explicit --url on every transport, not only forced REST
body:
Keyring finding VTI-14: pointing `cnm` at a host had no effect, because the
community was resolved from the DID document instead. With VTI-15 this made
the CLI unusable against their stack, and is why their repository carries its
own admin client — an adoption cost, not just a bug.

## The cause is a layer below where it is felt

The finding is filed against `cnm`'s vetting subcommands, and that is where an
operator meets it: `vetting::connect` builds its `VtcClient` from
`VtaClient::rest_url()`, so a discarded override sends it to the host the DID
document advertises while the operator watches the host they named stay idle.

But the discard happens in `session::connect_with_transport`. `url_override`
was honoured on exactly two paths — forced `--transport rest`, and the
priority-1 config `mediator_did` hint. The priority-2 path, which is what a
DID with an advertised endpoint actually takes, destructured `rest_url` out of
`resolve_vta_endpoint` and threaded that through, dropping `--url` on the
floor. So this affected **every** authenticated command that later reads
`rest_url()`, not only vetting.

## The fix, and what it deliberately does not do

`VtaEndpoint::with_rest_override`, applied once where the endpoint is resolved
rather than at each of the places `rest_url` is threaded. An operator who
names a host means it.

The transport choice is untouched. `--url` names a REST base; it is not a
statement about whether to speak TSP or DIDComm, and an operator who wants
that says `--transport rest`. Rewriting the mediator selection from a REST
flag would be a second, larger behaviour change smuggled in behind a bug fix.

## Tests

Two, and the second is the one that matters. The first asserts the override
survives on every variant — `Tsp` included, since that is what a
dual-transport VTA resolves to and therefore the arm most deployments take.
The second asserts that with **no** override the resolved endpoint is
unchanged: a fix that always rewrote `rest_url` would pass the first test and
break every operator relying on the advertisement.

Both live in `session.rs`, which is behind `#[cfg(feature = "session")]` —
`cargo test -p vta-sdk` compiles 380 tests and none of them. The workspace run
picks it up through feature unification, which is what CI runs.

title: feat(persona): who holds an old value, where an edit landed, what a context may call a face
body:
Adds UI for the persona lifecycle fields published in `@openvtc/trust-tasks` 0.19.13 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#533). The agent side is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1597. Against an agent without that change, the new fields are simply absent and every screen falls back to saying nothing new.

### Released
- **Per claim:** each disclosed claim now shows whether the verifier's copy is still current.
- **Out-of-date parties:** above the table, a list of everyone holding a value the holder has since changed.
  - Grouped by verifier, context and persona.
  - Only the latest disclosure to each counts, so someone already sent the new value isn't listed.
- **`removed` is kept separate from `changed`.** There's nothing newer to send, and the verifier keeps what it received.
- **`unknown` is never shown as current.** It comes from an older agent or a record made before fingerprints existed.
- **Model:** `manager/disclosure-currency.ts`. The pane only draws.
- **Not included — a one-tap "send them the new value" button.** A disclosure is a context-side preview → present step, which the console doesn't perform. The copy says to present the new value again from that context.

### Attribute save
- Says where the edit landed, from `refreshed` / `heldByPin`: how many places and contexts now show the new value, and how many faces pin the earlier one.
- The note is `accent` unless it also carries a correlation warning.

### Wearing a face
- New field for what the context may call the face. The copy says the context never sees the holder's own name for it.
- The form loads the existing label. `binding/set` replaces the whole binding, so a face change would otherwise wipe the label. A rendered test pins this; I checked it fails with the load removed.
- `personaBindingSet` gains `label`.

### Dependency
`@openvtc/trust-tasks` is raised to `^0.19.13` at the root and in core, so only one copy is installed. The lockfile changes that one package and nothing else. A local npm re-resolve had dropped the `libc` fields on native optional dependencies, which Linux installs use to pick the right native package, so I edited it by hand and checked it with `npm ci`.

### Checks
- `npm run lint`
- `npm test`: 1536 passed, 0 failed. New:
  - `manager-disclosure-currency.test.mts` (5 tests)
  - a core `label` payload test
  - a rendered label-preservation test
- `npm run build`

title: ZKP working draft: trust-graph implementation guide and construction catalogue
body:
> **Status (15 September 2026):** ready for review. Two commits — the draft as opened on 8 September and a second commit on 14 September (`e1afc3f`) folding the review since: fifteen construction records (nine primitive, six composed), Implementation Guide steps 4–5, integration, Research and Book notes, Appendix E review-notes index. Round 1 (shape review) runs to 22 September on the task-force thread [#23](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-tf/discussions/23) (the 8 September anchor; a duplicate opened on 15 September for the working-group call was deleted the same day). Merged 16 September; the review of that date is answered in [PR #11](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-spec/pull/11). The description below is as opened; the counts it gives are the 8 September ones.

This draft introduces an implementation-oriented ZKP specification for decentralized trust graphs. It starts with the outcome an application needs—membership eligibility, a private relationship, selective disclosure, common control, accepted status or delegated authority—and connects it to credential inputs, constructions, verifier checks and reproducible evidence. Personhood and liveness are important use cases and sources, rather than the specification's entire scope.

The contribution contains twelve construction records, the ADR-001 crosswalk, four proving-system entries and portable conformance generation. Records remain informative at their existing evidence states. ADR-001 is the flagship community-anchored use case; a credential-bound membership presentation is proposed as the first implementation milestone supporting it. Existing component tests do not establish the complete composition.

The reading order now leads with an implementation guide and trust-graph lifecycle. Detailed cryptographic background follows the operational material. The book explains construction fit and paper relationships from the same technical records. Explicit WG review notes mark proposals, open technical questions and evidence requests; they do not imply ratification.

The draft clarifies private witness custody, credential authenticity, offline voucher linkage, distinct members versus distinct people, root authority, transcript encoding and the separation of proof verification, policy acceptance and action completion. It documents the lab's domain-separated, length-prefixed transcript hash and BN254 conversion, with a comparison vector. Strict transcript types and semantic checks remain proposed implementation work, rather than claims about the current lab validator.

Near the end, an informative maintenance note describes how surveys of related DTG, Trust over IP, VTC and First Person Project work may produce traceable updates. An agent handoff lists twelve verification tasks with use-case fit, dependencies and expected evidence. The companion research/verifier-worklist.json makes that queue reusable.

Validation performed locally: all 17 conformance files validate; generated sections and terms match regeneration; Spec-Up-T renders with its two configured external glossary sources; the framed/plain transcript comparison digests were separately reproduced. Existing record states and histories were preserved. These checks are not a circuit audit or independent reproduction of the complete proof.

Review requested: general scope and first milestone; credential/witness contracts; canonical wire profile; construction comparisons; book organization; and the evidence required for future recommendations or adoption.

The author’s CC BY 4.0 grant for the adapted background is recorded in Appendix A. The renderer’s Windows branch-metadata fallback remains a known local rendering limitation. The draft also leaves exact cross-repository implementation baselines and several wire-profile decisions open. No construction or proving system is proposed as adopted merely by opening this PR.

### Added

- **vtc**: Implement vtc/join-requests/supplement/0.1 — answer a deferral in place ([#1593](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1593))

Closes the second half of Keyring's KR-03, the one `join-requests/withdraw`
  ([#1591](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1591)) left open. A community that cannot decide a request on what it was
  given defers it and says what more it needs — and the applicant had nowhere to
  put the answer. The request stays open, the dedup guard refuses a second
  application, and the only exits were withdrawing (losing your place) or waiting
  for a retention sweep neither party controls. A deferral was a dead end dressed
  as a question.

  Spec'd upstream first (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #526, corrected by #531, shipped in
  trust-tasks-rs 0.21.6) and implemented here against the generated types.

title: fix(persona)!: carry the holder's label into resolved claims
body:
Implements §3.3 of `docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md`.

`persona/profile/get` with `resolve` returns `ResolvedClaim`. Its published schema already defines `label`: "from the override where one is given and from the pool attribute otherwise". The maintainer returned no label at all. On top of that, `resolve_profile` dropped `OverrideValue.label`, even though the form's own doc comment says an override replaces value *and* label. A holder who named an override lost that name everywhere they'd look for it.

`ResolvedClaim` gains `label`, taken from the first of these that has one:
1. the override's label
2. the pool attribute's label
3. the inline entry's label

The handler emits it. Materialised claims are unchanged, so the label is never disclosed.

**Breaking:** `vta_persona::ResolvedClaim` gains a public member.

### Tests
- New `profile::tests::a_resolved_claim_carries_the_holders_label` covers all three sources and override precedence.
- `cargo test -p vta-persona`: 119 passed.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test persona_trust_task`: 27 passed. Resolved responses still pass the response-conformance layer.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: feat(persona)!: say who holds an old value, where an edit landed, and what a context may call a face
body:
Server side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#533, published in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.7. Implements §3.4, §9.2 and §9.3 of `docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md`.

### `disclosure/history` — `claimCurrency`
`present` records a keyed hash of each value that leaves. History compares that hash at read time with what the same persona presents now, in the same context, and reports one of:

- `current` — the verifier holds what the persona still presents
- `changed` — the persona now presents a different value, so the verifier's copy is out of date
- `removed` — the persona no longer presents that claim type
- `unknown` — a predicate, or a record written before fingerprints existed; never reported as `current`

This reads nothing above the boundary, and records no value, pool identifier or store-wide version below it. `changed` rows are the re-present list: parties holding a value the holder has since changed.

**Also fixed:** history rows were serialised from the store's `DisclosureRecord`. Its `claims` pairs and `citedContactRevisions` aren't members of the published row, so any non-empty history failed response validation. The only test read an empty one. Rows are now built to the schema.

### `attribute/put` — `refreshed`, `heldByPin`
`refreshed` lists the bindings an edit re-pushed. `heldByPin` lists the faces that pin the attribute and so didn't follow the edit. New `PersonaStore::attribute_reach`.

### `binding/set`, `local/binding/set` — `label`
`label` is what the context may call the face worn there. `binding/get` and `binding/list` return it. `profileName` — the holder's own name for the face — is now returned only to a holder-authorized caller; before this, every caller in the context was given it. New CLI flag: `pnm persona [local] binding set --label`.

### Breaking
- `PersonaStore::set_binding` and `set_local_binding` take a label.
- `VtaClient::persona_binding_set` and `persona_local_binding_set` take a label.
- `PersonaBindingSetBody`, `PersonaLocalBindingSetBody`, `BindingSummary` and `DisclosedClaim` each gain a member.
- `vta_cli_common` `cmd_binding_set` and `cmd_local_binding_set` take a label.
- `trust-tasks-rs` requirement raised to `0.21.7`.

**Downstream:** openvtc's `persona::binding::set` calls `persona_binding_set` and will need the new argument once it takes this `vta-sdk`.

### Tests
- `a_name_change_is_answerable_end_to_end`: a wire test that checks responses against the published schema. It covers:
  - the context sees the label and never the face name
  - the edit reports `refreshed` and `heldByPin`
  - history moves from `current` to `changed`
- `vta-persona` unit tests:
  - all four currency states
  - a cleared binding keeps no label
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4652 passed, 0 failed. This ran against the unreleased spec via a local `[patch]`. After switching to the published 0.21.7 I re-ran only the persona tests (`vta-persona` and `persona_trust_task`), which pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: docs(persona): design note for context-first identity and face lifecycle
body:
Adds `docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md`: a review of the persona / faces / worlds model against the UX discussion in trustoverip/dtgwg-htx-tf#11, and the plan that follows from it.

**What it proposes**
- **Context-first authoring:** keep the agent-scoped pool, but compose faces from a context arrival, local by default. Promoting a value to the pool is the explicit act of sharing it.
- **Worlds (facets) are suggested, never authored.** A context is not a subset of a world.
- **Findings, with evidence:**
  - correlation was blind to override and inline values
  - `OverrideValue.label` was dropped
  - the holder's private face name crossed the context boundary
  - super-admin bypasses `PersonaHolder`
  - pins cannot be honoured
- **Lifecycle:**
  - name changes, handled by retaining old versions while something references them, with an explicit holder purge
  - disclosure currency: who still holds an outdated value
  - edit reach: where an edit landed
  - retire versus delete, and binding expiry that retires
  - a per-face timeline
  - face templates that share the manifest-criterion schema

**Decisions recorded**
- Retained versions are acceptable, bounded by reference, with purge as the holder's override.
- Binding expiry retires rather than deletes.
- §9.2 was revised during implementation: disclosure currency uses a fingerprint of the disclosed value rather than a version number, because a version would expose store-wide write activity below the boundary.

**Already implemented from it**
- Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#533
- VTI: #1594, #1596, #1597
- Plugin: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#263, #264

**Still open:** §7 questions 1–4.

title: fix(persona): correlate values faces carry, and honour profileId
body:
Implements §5.1 of `docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md`, the first item in its sequencing. The design note lands separately on `docs/persona-context-first`.

### The defect
`persona/correlation/analyze` could not see a value a face carries itself. Its index is keyed on pool attributes. An `override` replaces a pool value for one face, and an `inline` entry never enters the pool — the two forms a holder reaches for when they want a face to be *different*. So the same throwaway address typed into two context-local faces produced no finding, even though that's the linkage the guard exists to report. The context-first flow proposed in the note would have steered every user onto that unindexed path.

### The fix
- **New index.** One agent-scoped edge per (value, face) under a new `pxf:` prefix (`vta-persona/src/face_values.rs`). The four face writers maintain it under the write lock. Each writes the index before the record, so a crash can only over-warn.
- **Local faces are indexed agent-scoped, deliberately.** What crosses is a keyed hash, and only holder-reach tasks can address it. A per-context index couldn't see the same value in two contexts.
- **Backfill.** Faces written before the index existed are indexed once, on the first analysis. It's idempotent and restartable.
- **Findings.**
  - `sharedWith` now names faces that carry the value.
  - A value held only by faces is reported as a finding without `attributeId`.
  - `why` counts both attributes and faces.

### Fixed on the way
- **`profileId` was accepted and ignored**, so `pnm persona correlate --profile-id` analysed the whole pool. It now confines the analysis to that face, pool or context-local (new `PersonaStore::analyze_face_correlation`).
- **`Finding.attributeId` serialised `None` as `null`**, which the response schema refuses. So every *candidate* analysis that found a match returned 500 — the guard failed exactly when it had something to say.

### Related
- Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#533 adds the corresponding MUSTs to `correlation/analyze`. No wire shape changes, so this doesn't wait on a `trust-tasks-rs` release.
- UX: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#263 (merged) renders face-only findings on the identity map.

### Tests
- `vta-persona`: six new tests in `face_values::tests`:
  - two local faces sharing a value
  - an override equal to another attribute
  - no self-sharing
  - edges dropped on rewrite and delete
  - backfill
  - face-scoped analysis
- `vta-service/tests/persona_trust_task.rs`: two wire tests, schema-validated against the published response type — local faces plus `profileId` narrowing, and a matching candidate.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4657 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `vtc-service` / `vtc-client` not run: neither depends on `vta-persona`.

title: feat(persona): who holds an old value, where an edit landed, what a context may call a face
body:
feat(persona): who holds an old value, where an edit landed, what a context may call a face

Uses the persona lifecycle members published in @openvtc/trust-tasks
0.19.13 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#533), served by the agent from
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1597.

Released view: each disclosed claim says whether it is still current
(claimCurrency). Above the table, the parties holding a value the holder
has since changed -- grouped by verifier, context and persona, and
decided by the latest disclosure to each, so a party already sent the
new value is not listed. `removed` is kept apart from `changed`: there
is nothing newer to send. `unknown` (an older agent, or a record from
before fingerprints) is never read as current.
disclosure-currency.ts holds the model; the pane only draws.

Attribute save: says where the edit landed -- places and contexts
refreshed, and faces that pin the earlier value -- from the agent's
refreshed / heldByPin. An older agent's answer claims nothing.

Wearing a face: a field for what the context may call it, with copy that
the context never sees the holder's own name for the face. The form
loads the existing label, because binding/set replaces and a face change
would otherwise clear it; a rendered test pins that and fails without
it. personaBindingSet gains `label`.

@openvtc/trust-tasks requirement raised to ^0.19.13 at the root and in
core so one copy is installed. The lockfile is edited for that one
package only; a local npm re-resolve dropped the libc fields of the
native optional dependencies, which Linux CI relies on.
